Rabbi Chizkiyah was sitting before Rabbi Elazar and asked him: “How many lights were created before the world was created?” He answered: “Seven. They are the light of Torah, the light of Gehinnom, the light of Gan Eden, the light of the Throne of Glory, the light of the Beis HaMikdash, the light of repentance, and the light of Mashiach. These were created before the world was created.”

Is that so? Did Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish not say: The wicked do not repent even at the entrance to Gehinnom, as it says: “They shall go out and see the corpses of the people who rebel against Me”? It does not say “who rebelled,” but “who rebel”—they continue rebelling forever! There is no difficulty: the former statement concerns the sinners of Israel, and the latter concerns the sinners of the nations of the world.

What, then, of the verse “Those who pass through the valley of weeping”? It refers to those who are liable to Gehinnom at that moment; Avraham our father comes, raises them up, and receives them, except for an Israelite who had intercourse with a gentile woman, whose foreskin is drawn forward so that he does not recognize him.

For “uncircumcision” is used as a designation for the nations, as it is said: “All the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised of heart.” And it says: “This uncircumcised Philistine,” an

This is why he was informed here of the exile in Egypt, and at its end, “Afterward they shall go out with great possessions.” “Great” points to the attribute of Atik: they are bound to the root. These are the great possessions they brought out of Egypt, for there they were refined through the ten plagues in all ten attributes. Through each plague Israel emerged from one attribute in the husk, for there are also ten of these, one opposite the other, and entered one attribute in holiness.

Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Neḥemya, Rabbi Yehuda says: “Go you [lekh lekha]” – twice, one from Aram Naharayim and one from Aram Naḥor. Rabbi Neḥemya says: “Lekh lekha” – twice, one from Aram Naharayim and Aram Naḥor, and one when He flew him from [the Covenant] between the Pieces and brought him to Ḥaran. That is what is written: “Your people [amekha] will volunteer on your day of battle [ḥeilekha]” (Psalms 110:3) – I was with you [imekha] when you volunteered on My behalf to descend into the fiery furnace. “On your day of battle” – when you assembled for Me all the hosts [haḥayalot] and masses. “
: ‘May God give you Of the dew of heaven and the fat of the earth, Abundance of new grain and wine.’

The levels differ greatly. For concerning Jacob it is written, “May God give you of the dew of heaven.” This is the supernal dew flowing from the Ancient of Days, called the dew of heaven—the upper heaven—dew flowing through the level of heaven, and from there to the field of holy apples. “Of the fatness of the earth”: this is the supernal earth, the land of life. Concerning Esau it is written, “of the fatness of the earth”; concerning Jacob, “of the fatness of the earth” means the supernal land of life. He inherited the earth above and the heaven above, whereas Esau received the earth here be
Your dead shall live; my corpses shall arise. Awake and sing, dwellers in the dust! For Your dew is a dew of lights, and the earth shall cast forth the dead.

He said to him: I expound another verse, for it is written: “Your dew is a dew of lights, and the earth shall cast forth the dead.” Whoever makes use of the light of Torah is revived by the light of Torah; whoever does not make use of the light of Torah is not revived by the light of Torah.

Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi also said: With every utterance that came from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, the souls of Israel departed, as it is said: “My soul departed when he spoke.” Since their souls departed at the first utterance, how did they receive the second? He brought down the dew with which He will revive the dead and revived them, as it is said: “You showered abundant rain, O God; when Your inheritance was weary, You established it.”

“A great light”—the light created on the first day, which the Holy One, blessed be He, hid away for those who toil in the Oral Torah by day and by night. Through their merit the world endures, as it is said: “Thus says the Lord: Were it not for My covenant by day and night, I would not have established the laws of heaven and earth.” Which covenant is observed by day and by night? This is Talmud.

“Like scarlet,” kashanim? It should have said kashani! Rabbi Yitzḥak said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: Even if your sins are like these years that have been arranged and have proceeded from the six days of Creation until now, they shall become white as snow.

Rabbi Abbahu said: From the beginning of the world’s creation, the Holy One, blessed be He, foresaw the deeds of the righteous and the deeds of the wicked, as it is written: “For the Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked shall perish.” “The earth was unformed and void”—these are the deeds of the wicked. “God said, Let there be light”—these are the deeds of the righteous. But I do not know which He desires, the deeds of these or of those. Since it is written, “God saw that the light was good,” He desires the deeds of the righteous and does not desire the deeds of the wi

Besides, the words of the Torah can best sink into the soul there in the desert, for there is no light except that which issues from darkness, for when that “other side” is subdued the Holy One is exalted in glory. In fact, there can be no true worship except it issue forth from darkness, and no true good except it proceed from evil. And when a man enters upon an evil way and then forsakes it the Holy One is exalted in glory. Hence the perfection of all things is attained when good and evil are first of all commingled, and then become all good, for there is no good so perfect as that which iss

So, too, you: If you are astonished at the reward I paid that wicked man for four steps he ran for My honor, how much more when I pay the reward of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who ran before Me like horses! Thus it is written: “Concerning the prophets, my heart is broken within me; all my bones tremble. I have become like a drunken man, like a man overcome by wine, because of the Lord and because of His holy words.”
But he is citing a verse! The verse teaches us Abraham’s alacrity.

Consider further: just as alacrity results from inward ardor, so inward ardor is also born of alacrity. When a person feels himself performing a mitzvah, as he hastens his outward movement, he thereby causes his inward movement to burn as well, and his longing and desire continue to grow stronger. But if he moves his limbs sluggishly, the movement of his spirit will also sink and be extinguished. Experience bears witness to this. You already know that what is most desired in serving the Creator, blessed be His Name, is the heart’s desire and the soul’s longing. This is what King David celebrat

Therefore they said that the soul of the soul awakens a person through fear and wisdom; the soul awakens a person through understanding, as it is written: “He said to man: Behold, fear of the Lord is wisdom,” and so forth. The soul awakens through repentance, which is called understanding and is called Sarah. The spirit is the voice and is called knowledge; it awakens a person to raise his voice in Torah, and is called the Written Torah. From the intellectual soul, good deeds are awakened.

There is a person who, after regretting his sins and repenting, engages in Torah with fear and love of the Holy One, blessed be He, and not in order to receive a reward. He merits the letter vav, which is the son of yod-heh; on its account it is called binah. This causes vav to return to heh. Thus the word teshuvah means: vav returns to heh. Neither heh nor vav ever rests upon a person without fear and love, which are yod-heh; we certainly call them fear and love. From there Torah and mitzva are given, which are son and daughter. Because Israel fulfills Torah and mitzva, they are called childr

As soon as Israel, the holy people, emerges from exile by itself, concerning the river that had been desolate and dry it is immediately said: “A river goes out from Eden”—this is vav—“to water the garden.” The river is the middle column. “Goes out from Eden”—this is the supernal Mother. “To water the garden”—this is the lower Shekhina.

What is the difference between the lower Eden and the upper? Like the advantage of light over darkness. The lower Eden is called the feminine Eden; the upper Eden is called the masculine Eden. Concerning it is written: “No eye has seen, O God, besides You.” This lower Eden is called a garden in relation to the Eden above; this garden is called Eden in relation to the garden below. Those who are in the lower garden enjoy this Eden above them every Sabbath and every new moon, as it is written: “From new moon to new moon, and from Sabbath to Sabbath.”
Abram went as the Lord had spoken to him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.

The Lord smelled the pleasing aroma, and the Lord said in His heart: “I will not again curse the ground because of man, for the inclination of man’s heart is evil from his youth; nor will I again strike every living thing as I have done.”

He said to them: Is it not written, “For the inclination of the human heart is evil from his youth”? Rabbi Yudan said: It is written “from his shaking”—from the time he stirs and comes out into the world.

Antoninus asked our Rabbi: From when is the evil inclination placed in a person—from when he leaves his mother’s womb, or before he leaves it? He replied: Before he leaves his mother’s womb. He said: No; if it were in him while he was in his mother’s womb, he would dig through her innards and come out. Rabbi conceded to him, for he had accorded with Scripture’s meaning, as it is said: “For the inclination of the human heart is evil from his youth.” Rabbi Yudan said: It is written “from his shaking”—from the time he stirs to emerge from his mother’s womb.

One who truly loves the Creator, blessed be His Name, will not strive and aim merely to discharge his obligation through what is already well known as the duty incumbent on all Israel. Rather, he will act like a son who loves his father: if his father reveals even a little of his wish for something, the son will already do as much as he can in that matter and that action. Even though his father said it only once, and in half a sentence, that is enough for the son to understand the direction of his father’s wishes and to do even what he did not expressly tell him, whenever he can infer for hims
What is the reason? Rava said: So that he will select a fine portion for the Sabbath and a fine portion for the festival.

Rabbi Shimon said: His father did not teach him, and he had no teacher. From where, then, did he learn Torah? The Holy One, blessed be He, provided his two kidneys as two teachers, and they welled forth and taught him Torah and wisdom. Thus it is written: “I bless the Lord who counseled me; even at night my kidneys instruct me.”

Secrets of Torah: “After these things,” and so forth—these are words of Torah, as it is written: “These words the Lord spoke to your entire assembly.” Just as there they are words of Torah, so here they are words of Torah. After a person engages in these things in this world, the Holy One, blessed be He, gives him good tidings and first greets his soul with peace: “Do not fear, Abram; I am your shield”—from all the evil kinds of Gehinnom.
“He mustered his trained men, born in his household”: Rav said, He poured Torah into them. Shmuel said, He poured gold upon them.

He began to grieve over breaking the tablets. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: Do not grieve over the first tablets, for they contained only the Ten Commandments. With the second tablets I give you laws, exposition, and aggadot. Thus it is written: “He would tell you the secrets of wisdom, for wisdom is doubled.” Moreover, you are informed that I have forgiven your sin, as it is said: “Know that God overlooks some of your iniquity.”

The totality of the entire Torah is certainly this: Torah is the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. The Written Torah is what is written as the Lord; the Oral Torah is what is written as God. Since Torah is the mystery of the holy name, it is called thus. The Written Torah and the Oral Torah: this is the general and that is the particular. The general needs the particular, and the particular needs the general. They unite with one another and all becomes one. Therefore the totality of Torah embraces above and below, for this name is above and that name is below: this is the mystery of the upper

At the end of forty years, during which they engaged in all those commandments of Torah that Moses taught them, both those practiced in the land and those practiced outside the land, he then taught them in a particular way. Thus it is written: “Know today and take it to your heart”—“today” specifically, what had not been permitted beforehand. “That the Lord is God”—this is in a particular way. In this matter are many mysteries and secrets. This and the first are all one matter: this in general and this in particular.

Rabbi Yehuda says: When Israel heard “I am the Lord your God,” Torah study was fixed in their hearts; they would learn and would not forget. They came to Moses and said: “Moses our teacher, serve as an intermediary, a messenger between us,” as it is said: “You speak with us, and we shall hear,” and “Now, why should we die?” What benefit is there in our destruction? They again began learning and forgetting. They said: Just as Moses is mortal and passes away, his teaching passes away. Immediately they returned to Moses and said: “Moses our teacher, if only He would reveal Himself to us a second

They shall no longer teach one another, each his neighbor and each his brother, saying, “Know the Lord,” for all of them shall know Me, from the least of them to the greatest, declares the Lord; for I will forgive their iniquity and no longer remember their sin.

We have learned: The Torah gives a person six hundred and thirteen kinds of counsel, so that he may be complete with his Master, for his Master wishes to benefit him in this world and in the World to Come.

Rav Adda son of Rabbi Ḥanina said: Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Joshua, for it contains the arrangement of the Land of Israel. What is the reason? “For in much wisdom is much vexation.”

Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: “I will make you a great nation”—this is when we say, “God of Abraham.” “I will bless you”—this is when we say, “God of Isaac.” “I will make your name great”—this is when we say, “God of Jacob.” Could the blessing conclude with all of them? Scripture says, “Be a blessing”: with you it concludes, and it does not conclude with all of them.

Rabbi Jochanan said: All heathens who come to Israel are circumcised by their own freewill and with their consent, and in the fear of Heaven are they circumcised. We do not believe a proselyte until seven generations (have passed), so that the waters should not return to their source. But slaves are circumcised both by their freewill and with their consent as well as without their consent, and no confidence is placed in slaves. Likewise with all the slaves who were circumcised with our father Abraham, they did not remain true (converts) in Israel, neither they nor their seed, because it is sai

: ‘Abram took his wife Sarai and his brother’s son Lot, and all the wealth that they had amassed, and the persons that they had acquired in Haran; and they set out for the land of Canaan. When they arrived in the land of Canaan,’

: ‘Reside in this land, and I will be with you and bless you; I will assign all these lands to you and to your heirs, fulfilling the oath that I swore to your father Abraham.’

Another matter: “Jacob settled…” – Abraham converted proselytes. That is what is written: “Abram took Sarai his wife…[and the people that they had made in Ḥaran]” (Genesis 12:5). Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra: Were all who entered the world to assemble, they would be unable to create even a small gnat, and you say: “And the people that they had made in Ḥaran”? Rather, these are the proselytes that Abraham converted. Why, then, did it say “made” and did not say “converted”? It is to teach you that anyone who draws a proselyte near, it is as though he created him. Lest y
: ‘Isaac sowed in that land and reaped a hundredfold the same year. GOD blessed him,’
Gold comes from the north; upon God is awesome majesty.

Rabbi Yitzḥak said: One who wishes to become wise should turn south, and one who wishes to become wealthy should turn north. Your sign is that the table was in the north and the menorah in the south. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: One should always turn south, for by becoming wise he becomes wealthy, as it is said: “Length of days is in her right hand; in her left, riches and honor.”
: ‘and the man grew richer and richer until he was very wealthy:’

They begin and say: “For you are our father.” Isaac says to them: Instead of praising me, praise the Holy One, blessed be He. Isaac points out the Holy One, blessed be He, before their eyes. Immediately they raise their eyes on high and say: “You, Lord, are our Father; our Redeemer from eternity is Your name.”

That is, he should at least contemplate in his mind the greatness of the blessed Infinite One and His kingship, which is “the kingship of all worlds,” higher and lower. He “fills all worlds” and “encompasses all worlds,” as it is written, “Do I not fill heaven and earth?” Yet He sets aside the higher and lower worlds and directs His kingship particularly toward His people Israel as a whole, and toward this person individually, for a person is obligated to say, “For my sake the world was created.” He, for his part, also accepts His kingship upon himself: that He should be King over him, and tha

Another interpretation: “From new moon to new moon.” How is it possible for all flesh to come to Jerusalem every month and every Sabbath? Rabbi Levi said: Jerusalem is destined to become like the land of Israel, and the land of Israel like the entire world. How will they come on the new moon and Sabbath from the end of the world? Clouds will come, carry them, and bring them to Jerusalem, where they will pray in the morning. This is what the prophet praises: “Who are these that fly like a cloud,” and so forth.
Behold, I was formed in iniquity, and in sin my mother conceived me.

Another matter, “when a woman conceives” – that is what is written: “I was generated in iniquity” (Psalms 51:7). Rabbi Aḥa said: Even if one would be the most pious of the pious, it is impossible that he will not have one aspect of iniquity. David said before the Holy One blessed be He: ‘Master of the universe, did my father Yishai intend to produce me; was his intention not for his pleasure? Know that it is so, for after they have fulfilled their needs, this one turns his face to here and that one turns her face to there, and you insert each and every drop that is in him.’ That is what David

Therefore Moses was the beginning in the world. If you ask who is the completion, since Moses was the beginning: the completion is the Messiah, for then completeness will be found in the world, such as there had not been for generations. At that time completeness will be found above and below, and all the worlds will be in one union. Then it is written: “On that day the Lord shall be one and His name one.”
He restores my soul; He leads me in paths of righteousness for His name’s sake.

Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: A person’s inclination overpowers him every day and seeks to kill him, as it is said: “The wicked watches the righteous and seeks to kill him.” Were it not for the Holy One, blessed be He, who helps him, he could not overcome it, as it is said: “The Lord will not leave him in his hand, nor condemn him when he is judged.”
He stores sound wisdom for the upright; He is a shield for those who walk in integrity.
If you do well, shall it not be lifted up?

The Gemara interprets this verse. The phrase: “If You will bless me indeed,” means that he prayed for a blessing with regard to Torah. “And enlarge my border,” means that he prayed for a blessing with regard to students. “And that Your hand be with me,” that my studies not be forgotten from my heart. “And that You will work deliverance from evil [mera’ati],” that I will find friends [re’im] like me. “That it may not pain me,” that the evil inclination should not grow stronger and prevent me from studying Torah. Othniel further prayed: If You do so, good; and if not, I will go depressed [linsis
Wood whose light does not rise: strike it, and it will shine. A body in which the soul’s light does not rise: strike it, and the soul’s light will rise; they will unite with one another to shine.

“Every support of bread”—these are the masters of Talmud, as it is said: “Come, eat of my bread and drink of the wine I have mixed.” “Every support of water”—these are the masters of aggada, who draw a person’s heart like water through aggada.
: ‘Chastise me, O ETERNAL One, but in measure; Not in Your wrath, lest You reduce me to naught.’

This is the counsel offered in the holy Zohar, where the head of the academy in Gan Eden said: “Wood in which the light does not rise is struck,” and so forth; “a body in which the soul’s light does not rise is struck,” and so forth. “The soul’s light” means that the light of the soul and intellect does not shine sufficiently to rule over the body’s material coarseness. Although he intellectually understands and contemplates Hashem’s greatness, it does not take hold and become attached in his mind strongly enough to enable him to rule over the heart’s materiality, because of its materiality an
: ‘The way of God is perfect; the word of the ETERNAL is pure. [God] shields all who seek refuge.’
But you, Israel My servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, offspring of Abraham who loved Me.

“Jacob was very frightened and distressed. He divided the people who were with him, and the flocks, and the cattle, and the camels, into two camps” (Genesis 32:8). “Jacob was very frightened and distressed” – Rabbi Pinḥas in the name of Rabbi Reuven: The Holy One blessed be He made a promise to two people, but they were afraid; the chosen of the patriarchs, and the chosen of the prophets. The chosen of the patriarchs – this is Jacob, as it is stated: “For the Lord has chosen Jacob for Himself” (Psalms 135:4). The Holy One blessed be He said to him: “Behold, I am with you” (Genesis 28:15), but

Rabbi Abba said: “Command deliverances for Jacob”—for those in exile, that redemption may be found for them in their exile. Come and see: Jacob was the glory of the patriarchs, and without Isaac, Jacob would not have come into the world. Therefore “command deliverances for Jacob” refers to Isaac, for when Isaac was saved, Jacob’s deliverances came to be.

So Abraham was sentenced by Nimrod to be burned. The Holy One, blessed be He, foresaw that Jacob would arise from him and said: Abraham is worthy of being saved through Jacob’s merit. Thus it is written: “Therefore, thus says the Lord concerning the house of Jacob, who redeemed Abraham”—Jacob redeemed Abraham.
The first commandment is called Anokhi, from the side of Keter, which is ayin from “our God.” Anokhi contains kaf—Keter—and it contains ayin.

We learned: An action below awakens an action above. If a person acts properly below, a corresponding power is awakened properly above. If a person performs kindness in the world, kindness is awakened above, rests upon that day, and crowns it on his account. If a person conducts himself mercifully below, mercy is awakened upon that day, and it is crowned with mercy on his account. Then that day stands over him as an advocate on his behalf when he needs it.
: ‘Fear not, for I am with you, Be not frightened, for I am your God; I strengthen you and I help you, I uphold you with My victorious right hand.’
: ‘GOD appeared to him by the terebinths of Mamre; he was sitting at the entrance of the tent as the day grew hot.’

“After my skin, this was struck; and from my flesh I will behold God.” Avraham said: After I circumcised myself, many converts came to attach themselves to this covenant. “And from my flesh I will behold God”: Had I not done this, how would the Holy One, blessed be He, have appeared to me? “Hashem appeared to him.”
: ‘This, after my skin will have been peeled off. But I would behold God while still in my flesh,’

“Avram fell upon his face”: Out of awe of the Divine Presence. Before he was circumcised, he lacked the strength to stand while the holy spirit rested upon him. This is what is said of Bilam, “Falling, with eyes uncovered,” in the teaching of Rabbi Eliezer.
Hashem appeared to Avram and said, “To your descendants I will give this land.” He built an altar there to Hashem, Who had appeared to him.
When He finished speaking with him, God ascended from above Avraham.

That is, he sees and recognizes that Hashem is before him. David HaMelech calls this “Your holy spirit” and “the joy of Your salvation.” For they said in Bereishis Rabbah, at the beginning of Vayeira, concerning “From my flesh I shall behold God,” that guarding the covenant of the flesh is immediately followed by vision: “Hashem appeared.”

“I am asleep regarding redemption, but the heart of the Holy One, blessed be He, is awake to redeem me.” Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said: Where do we find that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called the heart of Yisrael? From this verse, as it is written: “The Rock of my heart and my portion is God forever.”
My flesh and my heart fail; God is the Rock of my heart and my portion forever.

“Bereishis”: within it are “two,” and within it is “Shabbos,” as in “beis-reishis” and “bara shis.” These are two Shabboses. Of them it is said, “The Children of Israel shall keep Shabbos, to make Shabbos ….” Shabbos is mentioned twice here, corresponding to the upper and lower Shechinah. “Throughout their generations”: what does this mean? Fortunate is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbos in the two chambers of the heart, from which the evil inclination, which is desecration of Shabbos, is cleared away. “An eternal covenant”: this is the righteous one, upon whom both rest—one to fill

When the Shechinah is in exile, it is said of her, “The dove found no resting place …,” except on Shabbos and festivals. At that time she unites with her husband, and many additional souls descend with her to dwell among Israel. This is what is written: “The Children of Israel shall keep Shabbos throughout their generations.”

Shabbos is the Shechinah. The master of her house is the middle pillar. He breaks and portions a piece of bread, which is a drop, and gives it to the guest, who is righteous and poor. The guest blesses the master of the house with “in all,” “from all,” and “all,” which are the three patriarchs, with the blessings with which they were blessed.

Therefore it is written, “Between Me and the Children of Israel.” Because the whole of faith is found in Shabbos, a person is given another soul, a supernal soul, a soul containing every completeness, corresponding to the World to Come. Therefore it is called Shabbos. What is Shabbos? The Name of the Holy One, blessed be He—a Name complete on every side.
For the ETERNAL’s portion is this people; Jacob, God’s own allotment.

Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosei: Whoever delights Shabbos is given an inheritance without boundaries, as it says: “Then you will delight in Hashem; I will make you ride upon the heights of the earth, and I will feed you the inheritance of Yaakov your father ….” Not like Avraham, of whom it is written, “Arise, walk through the land, through its length …”; and not like Yitzchak, of whom it is written, “For to you and your descendants I will give all these lands”; but like Yaakov, of whom it is written, “You will spread out westward, eastward, northward, and southward.”
“An additional soul”: His mind is broadened for eating and drinking.
“An additional soul”: An expansiveness of heart for rest and joy, to be open to abundance, so that he may eat and drink without his soul being repelled by it.

Therefore it is written, “Between Me and the Children of Israel.” Because the whole of faith is found in Shabbos, a person is given another soul, a supernal soul, a soul containing every completeness, corresponding to the World to Come. Therefore it is called Shabbos. What is Shabbos? The Name of the Holy One, blessed be He—a Name complete on every side.
On Shabbos they would say, “A psalm, a song for the day of Shabbos”: a psalm and song for the future, for the day that is entirely Shabbos, rest for eternal life.
On the seventh day they would say, “A psalm, a song for the Shabbos day”—for the day that is entirely Shabbos.

Five things are one sixtieth of something else: fire, honey, Shabbos, sleep, and a dream. Fire is one sixtieth of Gehinnom; honey is one sixtieth of manna; Shabbos is one sixtieth of the World to Come; sleep is one sixtieth of death; a dream is one sixtieth of prophecy.

Rav would regularly say: The World to Come is unlike this world. In the World to Come there is neither eating nor drinking, neither procreation nor commerce, neither jealousy nor hatred nor rivalry. Rather, the righteous sit with their crowns upon their heads and enjoy the radiance of the Divine Presence, as it says: “They beheld God, and ate and drank.”
He did not stretch out His hand against the nobles of the children of Yisrael; they beheld God, and they ate and drank.

On this Shabbos day, every sorrow, every anger, and every distress is forgotten throughout the world, because it is the day of the King’s celebration, when additional souls are given, in the likeness of the World to Come.

On Shabbos and festivals, souls, spirits, and life-souls descend upon them by way of emanation; these are the holy spirit from the ten sefiros. Each appointed angel pleads merit for his birds, which are the souls that fly into human beings. When Israel fulfills this commandment, each appointed angel pleads merit for his birds.

There are three levels, and all are called Shabbos: the supernal Shabbos, the Shabbos of the day, and the Shabbos of the night. They are all one, and the whole is called Shabbos. Each one, when it rules, takes its companions and invites them to join in its rule. When this one comes into the world, all of them come and are invited with it.

Shin: the great Shabbos is Binah; the small Shabbos is Malchus. Beis: the two arms, Greatness and Might. Tav: Tiferes. Through it Shabbos is equivalent to the entire Torah. The three crowns of shin are the three upper sefiros. All are included in repentance, which is the upper Shechinah, of whom it is said, “The prayer of every mouth.”

There are two chambers in the heart: one emits breath, and the other emits breath. These are the upper heh and the lower heh, in the two chambers of the heart, corresponding to the First and Second Temples.
: ‘A sage’s mind tends toward the right hand, a fool’s toward the left.’

Rabbi Shimon arose and said: “She continued to bear his brother Hevel.” Woe to the world: they have eyes but do not see, ears but do not hear the secrets of Torah, and they pursue the profits of this world. Come and see: Kayin is the evil inclination; Hevel is the good inclination. Hevel is the heart, and they are the two chambers of the heart, as it is written: “The heart of the wise is to his right, and the heart of the fool is to his left.”
: ‘Her feet go down to Death; Her steps take hold of Sheol.’

Come and see: there are days and there are days. The ordinary days, as stated, stand outside for the nations. The days of Shabbos, which are the days of the week, stand for Israel. When this point rises, everything is concealed, and it rises; once it rises, it is called Shabbos. What is Shabbos? If you say it is because of cessation, as it is written, “For on it He ceased,” that is correct. But the mystery of the matter is this: once this point rises and light shines, it is crowned with the patriarchs. Once crowned with the patriarchs, it joins and unites with them to become one, and the whole
: ‘All who are linked to My name, Whom I have created, Formed, and made for My glory—’

All who are linked to My name, whom I have created, formed and made for My glory” (Isaiah 43:7), And it says: “The Lord shall reign for ever and ever” (Exodus 15:18). Said Rabbi Hananiah ben Akashya: It pleased the Holy Blessed One to grant merit to Israel, that is why He gave them Torah and commandments in abundance, as it is said, “The Lord was pleased for His righteousness, to make Torah great and glorious
: ‘GOD made everything for a purpose, Even the wicked for an evil day.’
Rav Yehudah said: The Holy One, blessed be He, created His world only so that people should fear Him, as it says: “God has acted so that they should fear Him.”
: ‘I realized, too, that whatever God has brought to pass will recur evermore: Nothing can be added to it And nothing taken from it—and God has brought to pass that mortals feel reverence.’

you shall be free to set a king over yourself, one chosen by the ETERNAL your God. Be sure to set as king over yourself one of your own people; you must not set a foreigner over you, one who is not your fellow Israelite.
How have we scorned Your name?

Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai: From the day that the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, no person called the Holy One, blessed be He, “Master,” until Avraham came and called Him Master, as it says: “He said: My Master, Hashem, how shall I know that I shall inherit it?”
: ‘From there he moved on to the hill country east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel on the west and Ai on the east; and he built there an altar to GOD and invoked GOD by name.’

“The Lord, God of heaven, who took me from my father’s house”: He did not say “and God of the earth,” whereas above he said, “I will make you swear,” and so forth. He said to him: Now He is God of heaven and God of the earth, because I have made Him familiar in people’s mouths. But when He took me from my father’s house, He was God of heaven and not God of the earth, because the inhabitants of the world did not recognize Him and His Name was not familiar on earth.
I will make you swear by Hashem, God of heaven and God of earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites among whom I dwell.

Rav Yehudah would remove his shoes and rain would come, whereas we cry out and no one pays attention to us. Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, desires the heart, as it is written: “Hashem sees into the heart.”

What do those people of faith say? “If Hashem desires us … He will give it to us.” When a person strives toward the Holy One, blessed be He, with the desire of his heart, He requires of us only the heart, and that they guard that holy mark, as it is written: “Your people are all righteous; they will inherit the land forever.”

A mystery of mysteries for those who know wisdom: fortunate are they when this spirit is aroused. This spirit is an extension of this point; it issues from it and spreads through the world. That is the mystery of Shabbos that rests below. Therefore keeping is written concerning it: “The Children of Israel shall keep Shabbos.” As explained, it does not say merely “Shabbos,” but “es haShabbos,” to include that spirit which rests upon all. It must be guarded, since it abides with a person; therefore it is written, “Everyone who keeps Shabbos from profaning it.” Within this mystery is another myst

Rava said: What does the verse mean, “There will be a radiance like light; rays issue from His hand, and there His strength is concealed”? To what are the righteous comparable before the Divine Presence? To a lamp before a torch.
Hashem God formed the human being from dust of the ground, breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the human being became a living soul.

Shabbos is the sanctity that is fixed and enduring from Hashem; Israel does not sanctify it, for it was already sanctified at the beginning of Creation. It was, however, a precious gift in His treasury, which He concealed from the wicked so that they would not benefit from this sanctity, and gave to Israel. Concerning this it says, “To know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you,” as our Sages said in Shabbos 10b. This is the sanctity from Above with which the Holy One, blessed be He, sanctifies a person of Israel on Shabbos: he merits an additional soul through the flow of sanctity from Above, a
Grace is deceptive, Beauty is illusory; It is for her fear of GOD That a woman is to be praised.

: ‘And if anyone sets out to pursue you and seek your life, the life of my lord will be bound up in the bundle of life in the care of GOD—who will fling away the lives of your enemies as from the hollow of a sling.’

What is the meaning of “and He was refreshed”? It teaches that the day of Shabbos sustains all souls, as it says, “and He was refreshed.” Another interpretation: it teaches that souls fly forth from there, as it says, “and He was refreshed.”
it shall be a sign for all time between Me and the people of Israel. For in six days GOD made heaven and earth, [before] ceasing from work and being refreshed on the seventh day.

Perhaps you will say: What reward does anyone who observes Shabbos receive? Scripture teaches: “Happy is the man who does this, and the son of man who holds fast to it, who guards Shabbos from desecrating it and guards his hand from doing any evil.” Thus we learn that anyone who observes Shabbos despite hardship is saved from transgression.
Fortunate is the person who does this, and the human being who holds fast to it: who keeps Shabbos from profaning it, and guards his hand from doing any evil.

“The son of David does not come until the souls in the body are exhausted.” If you ask: They could nevertheless be exhausted through the children born to idolaters! Rabbi Elchanan says that the souls of Israel and of idolaters are not in one body. As for the statement that in the days of Mashiach a woman will give birth every day, perhaps one may say that there will be a new body and new souls.
Rav Yosef challenged this: His wife is permitted, and another person need not even be mentioned? On the contrary: his wife is like his own body, while another person is not like his own body.
“Those who fear My name”—those who keep Shabbos.
: ‘But for you who revere My name a sun of victory shall rise to bring healing. You shall go forth and stamp like stall-fed calves,’

Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonasan: What does the verse mean, “Why is there a price in the hand of a fool to acquire wisdom when he has no heart”? Woe to the enemies of Torah scholars—a euphemism for the scholars themselves—who engage in Torah but have no fear of Heaven.
What good is money in the hand of a fool To purchase wisdom, when that person has no mind?
: ‘Moreover, I have assigned to him Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan; and I have also granted skill to all who are skillful, that they may make everything that I have commanded you:’

To incline your ear to wisdom, turn your heart toward understanding. For if you call to discernment and raise your voice to understanding; if you seek it like silver and search for it like hidden treasures—then you will understand the fear of Hashem and find the knowledge of God.
: ‘Make the heart of this people dull, make its ears heavy, and seal its eyes, lest it see with its eyes, hear with its ears, understand with its heart, return, and be healed.’

Rava would regularly say: The goal of wisdom is repentance and good deeds, so that a person should not read Scripture and study Mishnah yet rebel against his father, his mother, his teacher, or someone greater than he in wisdom and number, as it says: “The beginning of wisdom is fear of Hashem; good understanding belongs to all who practice them.” It does not say “to those who act,” but “to those who practice them”—to those who act for its own sake, and not to those who act for an ulterior purpose. Anyone who acts for an ulterior purpose would have been better off not being created.
: ‘The beginning of wisdom is reverence toward GOD; all who practice it gain sound understanding. Praise of [God] is everlasting.’

“Fortunate is the man who fears Hashem.” Is a man fortunate, but not a woman? Rav Amram said in the name of Rav: Fortunate is one who repents while still a man in his strength. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Fortunate is one who overcomes his inclination like a man.
: ‘Hallelujah. Happy are those who fear GOD, who are ardently devoted to God’s commandments.’

Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonasan: What does the verse mean, “The utterance of David son of Yishai, and the utterance of the man who was raised on high”? The utterance of David son of Yishai, who established the yoke of repentance.

Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani said: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi explained it to me personally: An ordinary person bows as we have said; the Kohen Gadol bows at the beginning of every blessing; the king, once he bows, does not straighten up again, as it says: “When Shlomo finished praying … he arose from before the altar of Hashem, from kneeling upon his knees.”

Rabbi Chanan said: Even if the master of dreams tells a person that he will die tomorrow, he should not withhold himself from seeking mercy, as it says: “For amid many dreams, vanities, and abundant words, fear God.”
For amid many dreams, vanities, and abundant words, fear God.

It was also taught thus: The devoted ones would finish its recitation at sunrise, so that they could join redemption immediately to prayer and thus pray during the day. Rabbi Zeira said: What verse supports this? “They will fear You with the sun, and before the moon, throughout all generations.”
Let them fear You as long as the sun shines, while the moon lasts, generations on end.

The root of Amalek within the heart is the absence of awareness of the One before Whom one stands, as it is written in Midrash Tanchuma at the end of Ki Seitzei: The Name is not complete and the Throne is not complete until Amalek is erased. The completeness of the Name is as stated in Pesachim 50a: “I am not read as I am written.” In this world it is not fully evident to the eye how Hashem was, is, and will be, and brings everything into being, which is the meaning of the Name Havayah. The Throne is providence: He sits as a king upon a throne, and His kingship rules over everything. “When Has

“Cain departed [vayetze] from the presence of the Lord, and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden” (Genesis 4:16). “Cain departed from the presence of the Lord” – from where did he depart? Rabbi Yudan said in the name of Rabbi Aivu: He cast the words behind him and departed, as though deceiving the Most High. Rabbi Berekhya said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Rabbi Shimon: He departed as one who shows a split hoof, and as one who deceives his Creator. Rabbi Ḥama said in the name of Rabbi Ḥanina bar Rabbi Yitzḥak: He departed joyfully, just as it says: “Here he is going out [yotze] to meet yo
: ‘A psalm. A song; for the sabbath day.’
: ‘Why should My beloved be in My House, Who executes so many vile designs? The sacral flesh will pass away from you, For you exult while performing your evil deeds.’
: ‘they must be circumcised, homeborn and purchased alike. Thus shall My covenant be marked in your flesh as an everlasting pact.’
: ‘The impurity from his discharge shall mean the following—whether his member runs with the discharge or is stopped up so that there is no discharge, his impurity means this:’

: “But to draw the light and radiance of the Shechinah also upon his body and his animal soul—which is the vital soul actually clothed within his body—he must fulfill practical mitzvos performed through the body itself. Then the actual bodily power involved in this action is included in Hashem’s light and will and united with Him in complete unity; this is the third garment of the divine soul.

Avram was called Avraham. Yitzchak was called Avraham, as it is written: “These are the generations of Yitzchak son of Avraham: Avraham.” Yaakov was called Yisrael, as it is written: “Your name shall no longer be called Yaakov, but Yisrael.” Yitzchak was called Yisrael, as it is written: “These are the names of the sons of Yisrael who came to Egypt with Yaakov.” Avraham was called Yisrael. Rabbi Nasan said: This is a profound matter: “The dwelling of the children of Yisrael who dwelled in Egypt, in the land of Canaan, and in the land of Goshen was thirty years and four hundred years.”

Therefore we have learned: What is the meaning of “He reveals deep things from darkness”? Rabbi Yose says: If you say that they are revealed from concealed darkness, we see that all those supernal crowns are hidden, and we call them “deep things.” What, then, does “reveals” mean? Rather, all those supernal hidden things are revealed only through that darkness which belongs to the mystery of night.
He reveals deep things from darkness and brings the shadow of death into light.

Rava expounded: What does the verse mean, “How beautiful are your steps in sandals, daughter of a generous one”? How beautiful are the feet of Israel when they ascend for the pilgrimage festival! “Daughter of a generous one”: the daughter of Avraham our father, who is called generous, as it says: “The generous ones of the nations gathered, the people of the God of Avraham.” “The God of Avraham,” but not the God of Yitzchak and Yaakov? Rather, “the God of Avraham,” because he was the first of the converts.
: ‘Your people come forward willingly on your day of battle. In majestic holiness, from the womb, from the dawn, yours was the dew of youth.’

“Yours is the dew of your youth.” Our father Avraham was afraid and said: Perhaps I bear the sin of worshipping idols all those years. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: “Yours is the dew of your youth.” Just as this dew disappears, so your sins disappear. Just as dew is a sign of blessing for the world, so you are a sign of blessing for the world.
A maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite.

David wrote the Book of Psalms through ten elders. Should Eisan the Ezrachite not also be counted? Rav said: Eisan the Ezrachite is Avraham. Here it is written, “Eisan the Ezrachite,” and there it is written, “Who aroused righteousness from the east …?”

Therefore it is written: “Every native in Yisrael shall dwell in sukkos.” Everyone who is of the holy root and stock of Yisrael shall dwell in sukkos, beneath the shade of faith. Whoever is not of the holy stock and root of Yisrael does not dwell in them, and removes himself from beneath the shade of faith.
I am GOD’s,” Another shall use the name of “Jacob,” Another shall mark his arm “of GOD” And adopt the name of “Israel.

Rabbi Abba bar Zavda said in the name of Rav: A mourner is obligated in all the commandments stated in the Torah except for tefillin, for they are called “splendor,” as it says: “Bind your splendor upon yourself.”

How do we know that tefillin are strength for Israel? For it is written: “All the peoples of the earth will see that the name of Hashem is called upon you, and they will fear you.” It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says: These are the tefillin upon the head.
: ‘And all the peoples of the earth shall see that GOD’s name is proclaimed over you, and they shall stand in fear of you.’

: ‘And who is like Your people Israel, a unique nation on earth, whom You, God, went and redeemed as Your people, winning renown for Yourself for great and marvelous deeds, driving out nations before Your people whom You redeemed from Egypt.’
You are My servant, Israel in whom I glory.
And your people, all of them righteous (ve-amekha khulam tzaddikim), shall inherit the land forever; the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, wherein I may be glorified.

Rabbi Yehudah bar Simon said: This is like someone who was sitting and making a crown for a king. Someone passed him and asked, “What are you doing?” He answered, “I am making a crown for the king.” He said: “Set in it as many precious stones and pearls as you can; set emeralds, set pearls. Why? Because it will be placed on the king’s head.” So the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moshe: “Praise Yisrael as much as you can. Magnify them and adorn them. Why? Because I will take pride in them,” as it is stated: “He said to me: You are My servant, Yisrael, in whom I take pride.”

When all the congregations have finished all their prayers, the angel appointed over the prayers takes all the prayers offered in all the congregations, makes them into crowns, and places them upon the head of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is stated: “To You all flesh shall come.” “To You” is interpreted as an ornament, as it is stated: “You shall wear them all as an ornament.” It also says: “Yisrael, in whom I take pride,” for the Holy One, blessed be He, crowns Himself with the prayers of Yisrael, as it is stated: “And a crown of glory upon your head.”
: ‘all humankind comes to You, You who hear prayer.’
You will be a crown of splendor in the hand of Hashem, and a royal diadem in the palm of your God.
“And he binds crowns for his Creator”: He makes crowns from the prayers of the righteous.

And why is all this? They said to him: Because the Holy One, blessed be He, always desires the prayers of the righteous and crowns Himself with their prayers. As we have said, the angel appointed over the prayers of Yisrael, whose name is Sandalfon, takes all those prayers and makes them into a crown for the Life of the worlds, as they have explained. All the more so the prayers of the righteous, which the Holy One, blessed be He, desires: they become a crown, so that the Holy One, blessed be He, may crown Himself with those prayers. If you ask: Since holy camps were accompanying him, why was
: ‘I foretell the end from the beginning, And from the start, things that had not occurred. I say: My plan shall be fulfilled; I will do all I have purposed.’
: ‘Behold, as the eyes of servants look unto the hand of their master, as the eyes of a maiden unto the hand of her mistress, so our eyes look unto the Lord our God, until He be gracious unto us.’
God said, “Let there be light”; and there was light.

The Rabbis taught: One who sees the sages of Israel says, “Blessed … Who has apportioned of His wisdom to those who fear Him.” Upon seeing sages of the nations of the world, one says, “Blessed … Who has given of His wisdom to flesh and blood.”
But there are only nine occurrences of “He said” in the account of creation! “In the beginning” is also an utterance, as it is written: “By the word of Hashem the heavens were made.”
[God] made darkness a screen—pavilions of dark thunderheads, dense clouds of the sky all around.
But, see, this I did find: God made human beings plain, but they have engaged in too much reasoning.
Such is the story of heaven and earth when they were created. When the ETERNAL God made earth and heaven—
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korchah said: “When they were created”—read “through Avraham”: through the merit of Avraham.

When it says, “These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created,” read “when they were created” as “He created them with the letter heh.” Why was this world created with a heh? Because it resembles a portico, so that whoever wishes to go out may go out. Why is its leg suspended? So that if a person returns in repentance, they can bring him in.

The other opened and said: “From my flesh I shall behold God.” Why “from my flesh”? It should say “from myself.” Rather, from my flesh literally. What is this? It is written, “Holy flesh shall pass from you,” and it is written, “My covenant shall be in your flesh.” For it was taught: Whenever a person is marked with this holy inscription of this sign, from it he beholds the Holy One, blessed be He—from it literally—and a holy soul cleaves to him.
From the breath of God they perish, and from the spirit of His anger they are consumed.
Let us make humankind in our image, after our likeness. They shall rule the fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, the cattle, the whole earth, and all the creeping things that creep on earth.
: ‘she lusted for concubinage with them, whose members were like those of donkeys and whose organs were like those of stallions.’

Rav Yehuda said: Opposite a naked gentile, it is forbidden to recite Shema. The Gemara asks: Why did Rav Yehuda discuss particularly the case of a gentile? Even with regard to a Jew it is also prohibited. The Gemara replies: Opposite the nakedness of a Jew, it is obvious that it is prohibited; however, opposite the nakedness of a gentile, it was necessary for him to say. Lest you say that since it is written about gentiles: “Their flesh is the flesh of donkeys” (Ezekiel 23:20), say that his nakedness is like that of a mere donkey and does not constitute nakedness. Rav Yehuda taught us that the

As he was leaving, that man said to him: “Does the Merciful One perform a miracle for liars in this way?” He said to him: “Wicked one, are they not called donkeys? For it is written, ‘Whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys.’”
If you wish, say: “Their flesh is the flesh of donkeys.” And if you wish, say: “Their mouth speaks falsehood, and their right hand is a right hand of deceit.”

“The weight of my hand is upon me ….” The Rabbis taught: If one says, “The weight of my hand,” or “the weight of my foot is upon me,” Rabbi Yehudah says: He brings a barrel and fills it with water. He inserts his hand as far as the elbow, or his foot as far as the knee. He weighs donkey flesh, sinews, and bones, and places them inside until the barrel is full again. Although there is no proof for the matter, there is a remembrance of it, as it says: “Whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys.”

A pregnant woman: from when her pregnancy becomes recognizable. How long until pregnancy becomes recognizable? Sumchos says in the name of Rabbi Meir: Three months. Although there is no proof for the matter, there is a remembrance of it, as it says: “It was after about three months ….” A remembrance of it? A verse is written, and it is a great proof! Because some women give birth at nine months, and some give birth at seven.

“The night was for us a watch.” This is difficult: In Berachos 2b, concerning the emergence of the stars, we say that it is night; although there is no proof, there is an indication, as it is written, “The night was for us a watch.” Why is it not a complete proof, as the verse is used here? The answer is that there the aim is to establish that the time for lying down, concerning the recitation of Shema, is the emergence of the stars. Therefore it says there that this is not a complete proof: Although it is night at that time, it is nevertheless not the time when everyone lies down.

Rav said: All agree that a slave has no recognized lineage, for it is written: “Remain here with the donkey”—a people likened to the donkey. They raised an objection: “Tziva had fifteen sons and twenty slaves”! Rav Acha bar Yaakov said: This is like the expression “a bull, son of cattle.”
You stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go up there; we will worship and we will return to you.

Rav Pappa said: If an ox gores a maidservant and she miscarries, its owner pays the value of the offspring. What is the reason? It is treated as damage to a pregnant she-donkey, for Scripture says: “Remain here with the donkey”—a people likened to the donkey.

Rabbi Yirmiyah said to Rabbi Zeira: It is taught that one may buy animals, male slaves, and maidservants from them. Does this mean an Israelite slave, or perhaps even a gentile slave? He said to him: It is reasonable that it means an Israelite slave; for what need is there to permit buying a gentile slave? When Ravin came, Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: Even a gentile slave, because one thereby brings him under the wings of the Divine Presence.

Rabbi Abba bar Mamal challenged: If so, when someone gives a coin to his maidservant and says, “You are betrothed to me after I free you,” would the betrothal also take effect? How can the cases be compared? There, initially she had the status of an animal, whereas now she is an independent person.
The Rabbis hold: Every offspring in the womb of a Canaanite maidservant is treated like an offspring in the womb of an animal.

Rav Yehudah said to Shmuel: “Even in the presence of mice?” He said to him: “Sharp one, no! Rather, it refers to the household of so-and-so, who engage in marital relations in the presence of their male and female slaves.” What interpretation do they rely upon? “Remain here with the donkey”—a people likened to the donkey.

“Anyone with whom betrothal cannot take effect ….” From where do we know this concerning a Canaanite maidservant? Rav Huna said: Scripture says, “Remain here with the donkey”—a people likened to the donkey. We have found that betrothal does not take effect with her.

§ Similarly, Rav Adda bar Ahava said: A person who has a transgression in his hand, and he confesses but does not repent for his sin, to what is he comparable? To a person who holds in his hand a dead creeping animal, which renders one ritually impure by contact. As in this situation, even if he immerses in all the waters of the world, his immersion is ineffective for him, as long as the source of ritual impurity remains in his hand. However, if he has thrown the animal from his hand, once he has immersed in a ritual bath of forty se’a, the immersion is immediately effective for him.

Rabbi Elazar said: What is the meaning of “She opens her mouth with wisdom, and the Torah of kindness is upon her tongue”? Is there a Torah of kindness and a Torah that is not of kindness? The rabbis established: ‘An unlearned person cannot be pious.’ For the Torah was given from the right side of the Holy One, which is Chesed, and therefore one who engages in Torah is called pious… If you say that many unlearned people perform kindness, they explained: Who is pious? One who acts with kindness toward his Maker, like David, who would unite. What would he unite? He would unite the supernal Torah with the Holy One. Therefore: ‘Guard my soul, for I am pious.’

Rabbi Yehuda of the West, Eretz Yisrael, and some say Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, taught: It is permitted to flatter wicked people in this world, as it is stated concerning the future: ‘The vile person shall no longer be called generous, nor shall the churl be said to be noble’ (Isaiah 32:5). Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said: The angel appeared to him as a gentile, for the Master said: An Israelite whom a gentile joins on the road should keep the gentile to his right. When Esau returned from outside, he would say to his father, “Father, is salt liable to tithing?” Isaac would marvel and say, “See how meticulous this son of mine is about the commandments!” His father would ask him, “My son, where were you today?” He would answer, “In the house of study. Is this not the law in such-and-such a matter? Is this not its prohibition, and is this not its permission?” Through these words he ensnared him with his mouth; therefore Isaac loved him. ‘He appeared as a Torah scholar’—Jacob accorded him honor as though he were his teacher, placing him at his right so that Jacob would be on the angel's left.

Rava said: You do not find a Torah scholar who renders practical rulings unless he comes from the tribe of Levi or the tribe of Issachar. Levi, for it is written, “They shall teach Your ordinances to Jacob”; Issachar, for it is written, “Of the children of Issachar, those who understood the times, to know what Israel should do.” But say that Judah too is included, for it is written, “Judah is My lawgiver”! I am speaking of bringing a discussion to its conclusion in accordance with the halakhah.

Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak strongly objects to this: If that is so, does an animal, with regard to whom vayyitzer is not written with a double yod, not have an inclination? Don’t we see that it causes damage and bites and kicks? Rather, interpret the double yod homiletically, in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, as Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said: This alludes to the difficulty of human life; woe unto me from my Creator (yotzri) and woe unto me from my inclination (yitzri). If one opts to follow either his Creator or his inclination, woe unto him from the other.

R. Simeon used always to say when the time of the Sabbath meal arrived: ‘Prepare ye the meal of the supernal Faith! Make ready the meal of the King!’ Then he would sit with a glad heart. Rabbi Abbahu opened: “Those who sit at the gate speak about me”—these are the nations of the world who sit in theaters and circuses. “And the songs of those who drink strong drink”—after they sit and eat, drink, and become drunk, they sit and speak about me and mock me. … They say: “These Jews observe Shabbat. The Gemara returns to the verse of Jacob wrestling with the angel. The verse states: ‘And Jacob was left alone; and a man wrestled with him until the breaking of the day’ (Genesis 32:25). Rabbi Elazar says: The reason Jacob remained alone was that he remained to collect some small pitchers that had been left behind. From here it is derived that the possessions of the righteous are dearer to them than their bodies. And why do they care so much about their possessions? It is because they do not stretch out their hands to partake of stolen property.
Yaakov remained alone, and a man wrestled with him until daybreak.

§ Since the halakhot of the descendants of Noah have been mentioned, a full discussion of the Noahide mitzvot is presented. The Sages taught in a baraita: The descendants of Noah, i.e., all of humanity, were commanded to observe seven mitzvot: The mitzva of establishing courts of judgment; and the prohibition against blessing, i.e., cursing, the name of God; and the prohibition of idol worship; and the prohibition against forbidden sexual relations; and the prohibition of bloodshed; and the prohibition of robbery; and the prohibition against eating a limb from a living animal.

With regard to the instruction: Do not go out alone at night, the Gemara states that this is as it was taught in a baraita: One should not go out alone at night, neither on Tuesday nights nor on Shabbat nights, i.e., Friday nights, because the demon Agrat, daughter of Maḥalat, she and 180,000 angels of destruction go out at these times. And as each and every one of them has permission to destroy by itself, they are all the more dangerous when they go forth together.

The Gemara above mentioned that Abraham refused to accept property that did not belong to him. With regard to this, Rabbi Abba says: Difficult is the return of theft that has been consumed, as even the perfectly righteous are unable to return it, as it is stated: ‘That I will not take a thread nor a shoe strap nor anything that is yours…except only that which the young men have eaten with me’ (Genesis 14:23–24). Even the righteous Abraham was unable to return that which the young men had already consumed.
I am excluding myself; only what the lads have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me, Aneir, Eshkol and Mamrei, they may take their portion.

MISHNA: If customs collectors took one’s donkey and gave him a different donkey that was taken from another Jew in its stead, or if bandits took his garment and gave him a different garment that was taken from a Jew in its stead, these items are now his because the owners despaired of retrieving them when they were stolen, and they may therefore be acquired by another. In a case of one who salvages items from a river, or from a troop (hagayis) of soldiers, or from bandits, if the owners of the items despaired of retrieving them, they are his, i.e., they belong to the one who salvaged them. Rav Ashi said: Is it written in the Torah: No man shall carry out (yotzi), indicating a prohibition against carrying objects from one domain to another on Shabbat? ‘No man shall go out (yetze)’ is written. Everyone agrees that there is no death penalty administered by the court in overstepping the Shabbat limit.

‘A prohibition serving as the warning for a court-imposed death penalty.’ Rashi explains it as ‘one shall not carry out,’ deriving the prohibition of carrying from one domain to another. The answer is that ‘one shall not go out’ is written; there is no expression here of carrying a load.

Bereshit: “Fear Shabbat”—you shall hold My Shabbatot in awe; fear Torah, fear the covenant. Just as the covenant must be guarded so that one does not enter it into an alien domain, so a person must guard Shabbat, not taking something out of the private domain and bringing it into the public domain. The private domain is the Shechinah: its width is four, corresponding to the four letters of the divine Name, and its height is ten, corresponding to the Name’s expanded letters. The public domain is the serpent, the woman of harlotry, the poison of the other god, Samael, who comprises the seventy n

The acts of taking out on Shabbat are two that are four for one inside, and two that are four for one outside. How so? The poor person stands outside and the householder inside. If the poor person extends his hand inside and places something into the householder’s hand, or takes something from it and brings it out, the poor person is liable and the householder is exempt. If the householder extends his hand outside and places something into the poor person’s hand, or takes something from it and brings it in, the householder is liable and the poor person is exempt.
