Abaye said that we have a tradition: A poor person is only one lacking in intelligence, in agreement with the opinion of Rav Naḥman. In the West, Eretz Yisrael, they say: One who has this attribute, intelligence, in him has everything in him. One who does not have this attribute in him, what is in him? If he acquired this, what else is lacking? If he has not acquired this, what has he acquired?

“The poor person extended his hand”—with a basket or hamper in it, in which he receives loaves from the householder. The Mishnah therefore describes carrying in terms of a poor person and a wealthy person, incidentally teaching us that a mitzvah accomplished through a transgression is forbidden and incurs liability.

The Gemara asks: Let us say that this mishna is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis and not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Ḥidka. The Gemara rejects that approach: Even if you say that it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Ḥidka, the mishna can be understood, as we can say to him: That which you want to eat on Shabbat eve, Friday afternoon, eat at night on Shabbat instead. The Gemara asks: And do we have a person sit and fast all day on Shabbat eve? According to this suggestion, he would not eat at all on Friday. Rather, we must say: In accordance with whose opinion i

Rava explains: They would put a hump-like stroke on the roof of the letter ḥet as if to thereby say: The Holy One, Blessed be He, lives (ḥai) in the heights of the universe. And they would suspend the left leg of the letter heh, as Rabbi Yehuda Nesia asked Rabbi Ami: What is the meaning of that which is written: ‘Trust in the Lord forever, for in the Lord (beYah) is God, an everlasting (olamim) Rock’ (Isaiah 26:4)? Rabbi Ami said to him: Anyone who puts their trust in the Holy One, Blessed be He, will have Him as his refuge in this world and in the World-to-Come. This is alluded to in the word

Rabba said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: The Holy One will raise Jerusalem three parasangs upward, as it is said, ‘It shall be raised and inhabited in its place.’ What does ‘in its place’ mean? According to its original place. How do we know that its original place measured three parasangs? Rabba said: An elderly man told me: I myself saw the first Jerusalem, and it measured three parasangs.

David wrote the Book of Psalms through ten elders. Should Ethan the Ezrahite not also be counted? Rav said: Ethan the Ezrahite is Abraham. Here it is written, “Ethan the Ezrahite,” and there it is written, “Who roused from the east the one whom righteousness meets at his feet?”

Yaakov arrived safely at the city of Shechem, which is in the Land of Canaan, when he came from Padan Aram. He encamped before the city. He bought the part of the field where he had spread his tent, from the sons of Chamor, father of Shechem, for one hundred kesitahs.

‘He purchased the tract of the field where he had pitched his tent from the possession of the children of Hamor, father of Shekhem, for one hundred kesita’ (Genesis 33:19). ‘He purchased the tract of the field where he had pitched his tent…for one hundred kesita’ – Rabbi Yudan bar Simon said: This is one of three places that the nations of the world cannot deride Israel and say: ‘They are stolen (property) in your hands,’ and these are: The Cave of Makhpela, the Temple, and Joseph’s tomb. The Cave of Makhpela, as it is written: ‘Abraham heeded Efron, and Abraham weighed for Efron (the money…)’

True, it is written, ‘Come ye, buy wine and milk without money and without price’ (Isa. 55, 1), and this in reference to work on behalf of the Holy One. But this only indicates that, whereas knowledge of the Holy One and of His Torah can be acquired without price or fee, the doing of good works for the sake of Heaven requires sacrifice and must be ‘paid for’ with full price; otherwise the doer is not worthy to draw down unto himself the spirit of holiness from above.

The verse states: ‘And Rehoboam went to Shechem; for all Israel came to Shechem, to make him king’ (I Kings 12:1). It was taught in the name of Rabbi Yosei: Shechem is a place ordained for calamity. In Shechem, they tormented and raped Dinah, in the outskirts of Shechem the brothers sold Joseph, in Shechem the kingdom of the house of David was divided.
His brothers were jealous of him but his father kept the matter in mind.

Abaye said: Murderers are also common in Shechem, as it is written: ‘And as troops of robbers wait for a man, so does the band of priests; they murder in the way toward Shechem, yes, they commit enormity’ (Hosea 6:9). What is the meaning of ‘the band of priests’? Rabbi Elazar says: It means that the people would band together to kill people, like those priests who band together to distribute teruma among themselves in the granaries.
And as troops of robbers wait for a man, so does the company of priests; they murder on the way to Shekhem: for they commit lewdness.

The young men who had grown up with him spoke to him, saying, “Thus shall you say to this people who spoke to you, saying, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy; now you lighten it for us.’ Thus shall you speak to them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s loins.’”

And what is the meaning of the phrase ‘and this was the cause that he lifted his hand against the king’? Rav Naḥman says: He removed his phylacteries before Solomon, thereby demonstrating that he does not consider Solomon his superior. Rav Naḥman says: The arrogance that existed in Jeroboam drove him from the World-to-Come, as it is stated: ‘And Jeroboam said in his heart: Now shall the kingdom return to the house of David. If this people go up to offer sacrifices in the House of the Lord in Jerusalem, then shall the heart of this people turn again to their lord, even to Rehoboam, king of Jude

‘He purchased the tract of the field where he had pitched his tent from the possession of the children of Hamor, father of Shekhem, for one hundred kesita’ (Genesis 33:19). ‘He purchased the tract of the field where he had pitched his tent…for one hundred kesita’ – Rabbi Yudan bar Simon said: This is one of three places that the nations of the world cannot deride Israel and say: ‘They are stolen (property) in your hands,’ and these are: The Cave of Makhpela, the Temple, and Joseph’s tomb. The Cave of Makhpela, as it is written: ‘Abraham heeded Efron, and Abraham weighed for Efron (the money…)’

True, it is written, ‘Come ye, buy wine and milk without money and without price’ (Isa. 55, 1), and this in reference to work on behalf of the Holy One. But this only indicates that, whereas knowledge of the Holy One and of His Torah can be acquired without price or fee, the doing of good works for the sake of Heaven requires sacrifice and must be ‘paid for’ with full price; otherwise the doer is not worthy to draw down unto himself the spirit of holiness from above.

But the spirit of holiness is not so: it demands a full price and strenuous effort, purification of one’s self and one’s dwelling, devotion of heart and soul; and even so one will be lucky to win it to take up its abode with him. Therefore one must beware and walk straitly according to the paths and ways of righteousness, turning neither to the right hand nor to the left; for otherwise, even if it had entered into a man, it will straightway depart from him, and thereafter it will indeed be passing hard to recall it again.
Speak to the B’nei Yisrael and have them take for Me a terumah-offering. From every man whose heart impels him to generosity shall you take My terumah-offering.

And the king said to Aravna, No; but I will surely buy it of thee at a price: neither will I offer burnt offerings to the Lord my God of that which costs me nothing. So David bought the threshingfloor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.

It is also stated with regard to the spies: ‘And they went up into the south, and he came to Hebron’ (Numbers 13:22). Why is the phrase ‘and he came’ written in the singular form? The verse should have said: And they came. Rava says: This teaches that Caleb separated himself from the counsel of the other spies and went and prostrated himself on the graves of the forefathers in Hebron. He said to them: My forefathers, pray for mercy for me so that I will be saved from the counsel of the spies.
Thou prevailest for ever against him, and he passes: Thou changest his countenance, and sendest him away.
They shall spread upon them a cloth of crimson thread and they shall cover it with a covering of tachash -hide and put its (carrying) poles (in place).

… Know that the firstborn were sacrificing until the tribe of Levi arose; take proof from the beginning of the creation of the world. Adam the first man was the firstborn of the world. When he sacrificed his offering, as it is stated: ‘May it please the Lord more than a bull with horns and hooves’ (Psalms 69:32), he donned the vestments of the High Priest, as it is stated: ‘The Lord God made for Adam and for his wife hide tunics, and clothed them’ (Genesis 3:21). They were praiseworthy garments, and the firstborn would perform the service in them. When Adam died, he bequeathed them to Seth. …

‘The Lord God made for Adam and for his wife garments of hide (or), and clothed them’ (Genesis 3:21). In Rabbi Meir’s Torah, they found that ‘garments of or’ was written. These are the garments of Adam the first man, that were similar to the common rue, broad at the bottom and narrow at the top. Rabbi Yitzḥak Ravya says: They were as smooth as a fingernail and as pretty as jewels. Rabbi Yitzḥak said: It was like the thin linen garments that come from Beit She’an. (And they were called) garments of hide because they adhered to the skin. Rabbi Elazar said: Goat hides. Rabbi Aivu said: Garments t

… ‘He purchased the tract of the field where he had pitched his tent…for one hundred kesita’ – Rabbi Yudan bar Simon said: This is one of three places that the nations of the world cannot deride Israel and say: ‘They are stolen (property) in your hands,’ and these are: The Cave of Makhpela, the Temple, and Joseph’s tomb. The Cave of Makhpela, as it is written: ‘Abraham heeded Efron, and Abraham weighed for Efron (the money…)’ (Genesis 23:16). The Temple, as it is written: ‘David gave to Ornan for the place (six hundred shekels worth of gold)’ (I Chronicles 21:25). Joseph’s tomb – ‘he purchased
Hate the evil, and love the good, and establish justice in the gate: it may be that the Lord God of hosts will be gracious to the remnant of Yosef.
Yaakov arrived safely at the city of Shechem, which is in the Land of Canaan, when he came from Padan Aram. He encamped before the city.

Rabbi Shimon said: Since a miracle has occurred for me, I shall go and repair something, as it is written, “Jacob came whole.” Rav said: Whole in his body, whole in his wealth, whole in his Torah. “He encamped before the city”—Rav said: He established coinage for them. Shmuel said: He established marketplaces for them. Rabbi Yochanan said: He established bathhouses for them.
You are to love Adonoy, your God, with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your possessions.

‘Jacob arrived intact’ – intact in his body. Because it is written: ‘He was limping because of his hip’ (Genesis 32:32); nevertheless, intact in his body. Intact in his children; because it is written in his regard: ‘If Esau will come upon the one camp, and smite it, the remaining camp will survive’ (Genesis 32:9); nevertheless, here, intact in his children. Intact in his wealth; although, Rabbi Avun said in the name of Rav Aḥa: Our patriarch Jacob would give Esau that same gift for nine years; nevertheless, here, intact in his wealth. Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Intact in his studies, but Joseph forg

The mishna articulates a general principle: One is obligated to recite a blessing for the bad that befalls him just as he recites a blessing for the good that befalls him, as it is stated: ‘And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might’ (Deuteronomy 6:5). The mishna explains this verse as follows: ‘With all your heart’ means with your two inclinations, with your good inclination and your evil inclination, both of which must be subjugated to the love of God. ‘With all your soul’ means even if God takes your soul. ‘And with all your might’
The spirit of man is the candle of the Lord, searching all the inward parts of the belly.
Thy word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.

The Gemara asks: And is the light of a torch not bright enough for searching? But didn’t Rava say: What is the meaning of that which is written, ‘And a brightness appears as the light; He has rays at His side; and there is the hiding of His power’ (Habakkuk 3:4), which indicates that God will provide rays of glory for the righteous in the future? The Sages explained this verse by means of a parable: To what are the righteous comparable before the Divine Presence? They are comparable to a lamp in the face of a torch. This statement indicates that the light of a torch is significantly greater th

We learned in our mishna the explanation of the verse: ‘And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul and all your might’ (Deuteronomy 6:5). This was elaborated upon when it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Eliezer says: If it is stated: ‘With all your soul,’ why does it state: ‘With all your might’? Conversely, if it stated: ‘With all your might,’ why does it state: ‘With all your soul’? Rather, this means that if one’s body is dearer to him than his property, therefore it is stated: ‘With all your soul’; one must give his soul in sanctification of God. And if one’s

“Jacob was left alone.” Rabbi Elazar said: He remained behind for small vessels. From here we learn that the possessions of the righteous are dearer to them than their bodies. Why so much? Because they do not stretch out their hands to take what is stolen.

The Sages continued to ask Abba Ḥilkiyya about his unusual behavior. What is the reason that the entire way the Master did not wear his shoes, but when he reached water he put on his shoes? He said to them: The entire way I can see and take care where I walk, and therefore there is no need for me to wear out my shoes, but in the water I cannot see. Therefore, I put on my shoes to avoid hurting myself. They asked: What is the reason that when the Master reached shrubs and thorns, he lifted up his clothes? He said to them: This flesh will heal if it is scratched by thorns, but this garment will

… ‘You shall say: Moreover, here is your servant Jacob, behind us’ – that is what is written: ‘The earth is given into the hand of the wicked one; he covers the faces of its judges…’ (Job 9:24). ‘He placed them in the charge of the servants, each drove by itself’ – why did he not introduce them intermingled? It was in order to astonish him with his gift. Why did he not introduce them all at once? It was in order to satiate the eyes of the wicked one. He came to end it, but he said: ‘Receive’; He came to end it, but he said: ‘Receive.’ ‘The gift went before him and he stayed that night in the c
The present passed on ahead of him, but he spent the night in the camp.

‘I shall repair something’—in the manner of Jacob when he was saved from Esau's hand. ‘Whole in his Torah’—he had not forgotten his learning because of the weariness of the journey. ‘Whole in his body’—he had been healed of his limp.
Yaakov arrived safely at the city of Shechem, which is in the Land of Canaan, when he came from Padan Aram. He encamped before the city.

‘Whole’—whole in his body, for he was healed of his limp; whole in his possessions, for he lacked nothing despite the gift he had given; whole in his Torah, for he had not forgotten his learning in Laban’s house.

The verse states: ‘And the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him on the way, and he was clad in a new (ḥadasha) garment, and the two were alone in the field.’ What is taught by the phrase ‘in a new garment’? Rav Naḥman says: It was like a new garment; just as a new garment has no imperfection, so too, the Torah studies of Jeroboam at that time had no imperfection. Alternatively, ‘a new garment’ teaches that they introduced (sheḥideshu) matters that no ear had ever heard.

Gehazi was a man mighty in Torah, but he had three faults: a begrudging eye, licentiousness, and denial of the resurrection of the dead. A begrudging eye: When Elisha sat teaching, Gehazi would sit at the door. The students saw him and said: Gehazi has not entered; shall we enter? Thus his teaching was being delivered, but no one benefited from it.

Even Achiyah the Shilonite erred and signed. For Jehu was a great righteous man, as it is written, “Hashem said to Jehu: Because you have done well in doing what is upright in My eyes, and have done to the house of Ahab according to all that was in My heart, your descendants to the fourth generation shall sit upon the throne of Israel.” Yet it is also written, “Jehu did not take care to walk in the Torah of Hashem, God of Israel, with all his heart; he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam, who caused Israel to sin.” What caused this? Abaye said: A covenant is made with the lips, for Jeh

And that is what Rava said: To those who are right-handed in their approach to Torah, and engage in its study with strength, good will, and sanctity, Torah is a drug of life, and to those who are left-handed in their approach to Torah, it is a drug of death. Alternatively, why are matters of Torah referred to as royal? Because to each and every utterance that emerged from the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He, two crowns are tied. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: What is the meaning of that which is written: ‘My beloved is to me like a bundle of myrrh that lies between my breasts’ (Song of Son

Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥman began: ‘A song of ascents. I lift my eyes to the mountains (heharim)’ (Psalms 121:1) – I lift my eyes to the parents (hahorim), to my teachers, and to those who raised me. ‘From where will my help come?’ (Psalms 121:1) – Eliezer, when he went to bring Rebecca, what is written in his regard: ‘The slave took ten camels…’ (Genesis 24:10), but I (Jacob) do not have even one nose ring or one bracelet. Rabbi Ḥanina said: He (Isaac) sent him empty-handed. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: He sent with him, but Esau arose and took it from him. He then said: ‘What, will I lose my co
When she had finished giving him to drink, she said, I will also draw water for your camels, until they will have finished drinking.

Likewise, the Holy One, blessed be He, brings the soul, casts it into the body, and judges them together, as it says, ‘He summons the heavens above and the earth to judge His people.’ ‘He summons the heavens above’—this is the soul. ‘And the earth to judge His people’—this is the body.

§ The Sages taught: There are three partners in the creation of a person: The Holy One, Blessed be He, and his father, and his mother. His father emits the white seed, from which the following body parts are formed: The bones, the sinews, the nails, the brain that is in its head, and the white of the eye. His mother emits red seed, from which are formed the skin, the flesh, the hair, and the black of the eye. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, inserts into him a spirit, a soul, his countenance (ukelaster), eyesight, hearing of the ear, the capability of speech of the mouth, the capability of wal

When the Tabernacle is completed with its thigh, it is written of Jacob, ‘Jacob came whole.’ Jacob is the likeness of the Central Column from its outward aspect. Moses was there, but from the inward aspect: this one is the body and that one is the soul. Thus the two thighs of the Central Column, Netzach and Hod, are complete.

… Just as there, the term ‘this’ is referring to the New Moon, so too, here the term is referring to the New Moon. And similarly, everyone agrees that the Torah was given to the Jewish people on Shabbat, as it is written here in the Ten Commandments: ‘Remember the Shabbat day to keep it holy’ (Exodus 20:8), and it is written there: ‘And Moses said to the people: Remember this day, in which you came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage, for by strength of hand the Lord brought you out from this place; there shall be no leaven eaten’ (Exodus 13:3). Just as there, the mitzva of remembrance

AND GOD FINISHED BY MEANS OF THE SEVENTH DAY: this is the Oral Law, which is the ‘seventh day’, and through which the world was completed and the whole is preserved. HIS WORK WHICH HE HAD MADE, but not the whole of HIS work, because it was the Written Torah which produced the Whole through the power of the Writing which issued from Wisdom.

With regard to the wealthy of other countries, where there are no Sages, by what virtue do they merit their wealth? He said to him: Because they honor Shabbat, as Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said: One time I was hosted at the home of a homeowner in Laodicea and they brought before him a table of gold that was so heavy it required sixteen people to carry it, and there were sixteen chains of silver attached to it, and there were bowls and cups and pitchers and flasks attached to it, and there were all sorts of food, and delicacies, and fragrant spices on it. And when they placed it there they would say
A Psalm of David. The earth is the Lord’s, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell in it.
The blessing of the Lord, it makes rich, and he adds no sorrow with it.

“God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it.” It is written, “The blessing of Hashem makes rich, and He adds no sorrow with it.” “The blessing of Hashem makes rich”—this is Shabbat, as it is said, “God blessed the seventh day.” “And He adds no sorrow with it”—this is mourning, as it is said, “The king was grieved over his son.”
He went ahead of them, and he prostrated himself to the earth seven times, until he approached his brother.
for a just man falls seven times, and yet rises up again: but the wicked stumble into mischief.

“He bowed himself to the ground seven times.” Why seven? Because it is said, “A righteous person falls seven times and rises.” Another explanation: Why seven? He said to him: Consider yourself as though you were sitting in judgment behind seven barriers, while I stand before you to be judged, and be filled with compassion for me. Rabbi Chanina bar Yitzchak said: He did not cease bowing and advancing, bowing and advancing, until he brought the attribute of judgment into the attribute of mercy.
He (the man) said, No longer will your name be spoken of as Yaakov, but as Yisrael, for you have contended with God(ly beings) and with men, and you have won.
He will deliver thee in six troubles: and in seven no evil shall touch thee.

… Although Israel sinned and the Holy One blessed be He delivered them into the hand of the nations of the world due to their iniquities, they (the nations) did not emerge unscathed as, ultimately, the Holy One blessed be He will judge the nations of the world into whose hand He delivered them, just as He did with Egypt and Babylon. This is why ‘to whom’ is written six times – corresponding to the six exiles that Israel was exiled among the nations, and they were all punished on their account. They are: Egypt first, and then Assyria, Babylon, Media, Greece, and Edom. …
He who sits in the heavens laughs: the Lord has them in derision.
Yoseif recalled the dreams that he had dreamt about them, and said to them, You are spies. You have come to see where the land is exposed.

… ‘Tigris (Ḥidekel) (it is that which goes east of Ashur)’ – this refers to Greece, which was quick (kala) and harsh (ḥada) in its edicts, as it would say to Israel: ‘Write for yourselves on the horn of an ox that you have no share in the God of Israel.’ Rav Huna said: In three areas, the kingdom of Greece takes precedence over (they surpass) the Evil Empire: In its legal system, in its script, and in its language. Rav Huna said in the name of Rav Aḥa: All the kingdoms may be called after Ashur because they enrich themselves (mitasherot) through Israel. Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said: All the kin

… ‘It is that which encircles the entire land of Kush’ (Genesis 2:13), as it is stated: ‘From India to Kush’ (Esther 1:1). ‘The name of the third river is Ḥidekel’ (Genesis 2:14), this is Greece, which is sharp (ḥada) and swift (vekala) in their edicts against Israel, and says to them: ‘Write on the horn of the ox: Israel has no portion in the God of Israel.’ ‘It is that which flows east of Assyria’ (Genesis 2:14) – Rav Huna said: All the kingdoms are called Assyria, as they bolstered (me’ashrin) themselves at Israel’s expense. Rabbi Yosei ben Rabbi Ḥanina said: All the kingdoms are called Egy

youths in whom was no blemish, but well favoured, and skilful in all wisdom, and discerning in knowledge, and perceptive in understanding, and such as had ability in them to stand in the king’s palace, and whom they might teach the learning and the tongue of the Kasdim.
He will speak to the people for you. He will be your spokesman, and you will be his master.

They cried out to Hashem against the inclination for idolatry… They fasted for three days and three nights, and it was delivered into their hands. A fiery young lion came forth from the Holy of Holies. The prophet said to Israel: This is the evil inclination for idolatry… He said: Cast it into a lead container and cover its opening with lead, for lead absorbs sound, as it is written, ‘He cast her into the midst of the measure… and cast the lead stone upon its mouth.’

‘A cow’—this is Egypt, ‘Egypt is a beautiful heifer.’ ‘Red’—this is Babylon, ‘You are the head of gold.’ ‘Whole’—this is Media. Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said: The kings of Media were whole; the Holy One has no charge against them except the idolatry they inherited from their ancestors. ‘In which there is no blemish’—this is Greece… ‘Upon which no yoke has come’—this is wicked Edom, which did not accept the yoke of the Holy One.
The lads grew up. Eisov became a skilled trapper, a man of the field. Yaakov was a wholesome man, living in tents.

It was taught in a baraita, Rabban Gamliel said: In three aspects of their conduct, I like the Persians: They are a modest people; they are modest in their eating, they are modest in the lavatory, and they are modest in another matter, i.e., sexual relations.

The verse states: ‘In the evening she went, and in the morning she returned’ (Esther 2:14). Rabbi Yoḥanan said: From the implicit criticism of that wicked man, Ahasuerus, who cohabited with many women, we have incidentally learned his praise as well, that he would not engage in sexual relations during the day, but in a more modest fashion at night.

The Gemara asks: Why did he need to tell them to separate during the morning hours? Didn’t Rav Huna say: The Jewish people are holy and do not have relations during the day? It was not necessary to command them until night. The Gemara replies: It was necessary to tell them in the morning, as Rava said: If it was a dark house, it is permitted to have relations during the day. And similarly, Rava said, and some say that Rav Pappa said: A Torah scholar obscures the light in the room with his cloak and is thereby permitted to have relations during the day. When Rochel had given birth to Yoseif, Yaakov said to Lavan, Send me on my way, and I will go to my own place and to my homeland.

‘It was when Rachel bore Joseph, Jacob said to Laban: Release me, and I will go to my place and to my land’ (Genesis 30:25). ‘It was when Rachel bore Joseph’ – when Joseph was born, Esau’s adversary was born, as it is stated: ‘Jacob said to Laban: Release me, and I will go to my place and to my land,’ as Rabbi Pinḥas said in the name of Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥman: It is a tradition that Esau will fall only into the hand of the descendants of Rachel. That is what is written: ‘Will the young of the flock not drag them?’ (Jeremiah 49:20) – why does it call them ‘the young of the flock’? It is becaus
The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the Lord, and against his anointed, saying,
He went ahead of them, and he prostrated himself to the earth seven times, until he approached his brother.
Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and not be afraid: for the Lord God is my strength and my song; he also is become my salvation.

Rabbi Yehuda began: ‘Hashem is good, a stronghold on the day of trouble; He knows those who take refuge in Him.’ Fortunate is the person who holds fast to the Holy One, for His strength is true strength… ‘A stronghold’ is the power in which salvations reside, as it is written, ‘He is a stronghold of salvations for His anointed.’ ‘On the day of trouble’—when the other nations oppress Israel.

The Rabbis interpreted the verse regarding the New Year and Yom Kippur; ‘my light,’ (Psalms 27:1) on the New Year, ‘and my salvation’ (Psalms 27:1) on Yom Kippur. Whom shall I fear? Now of him who relaxes his hold of the Holy One, blessed be He, it is written: ‘If thou art faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is straitened’ (Prov. 24, 10), and the only way of holding firmly to God is to hold firmly to the Torah; for whosoever holds firmly to the Torah holds firmly to the tree of life, and, as it were, adds strength to the community of Israel.

‘Days were formed, and one of them was His’—this is the Shabbat day for Israel… The Holy One said to Israel: Did I not write for you in My Torah, ‘This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth’? Although you do work throughout the six days, Shabbat should be made entirely Torah. Therefore they said: A person should rise early and study on Shabbat, go to the synagogue and house of study, read Torah and study the Prophets, and afterwards go home to eat and drink.

Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: Anyone who observes Shabbat according to its law is forgiven, even if he served idols like the generation of Enosh, as it is written, “Happy is the person who does this … who guards Shabbat from desecrating it.” Do not read “from desecrating it,” mechalelo, but “he is forgiven,” machul lo.

… Did we not learn: Rabbi Shimon says: All the sefichin are permitted except for the sefichin of cabbage, as there is nothing like it in the vegetables of the field.’ He said to him: ‘But do my colleagues not disagree with me? You breached the fence of the Sages, and ‘one who breaches a fence, a serpent will bite him.’’ And so it was for him. Another matter, ‘and he encamped before the city’ – he entered on Friday near sunset, while it was still day, and established Shabbat boundaries while it was still day. That is to say: Jacob observed Shabbat before it was given.
All his sons and all his daughters rose to console him, but he refused to be consoled. He said, I will go down to the grave mourning for my son. His father wept for him.
The Midrash explains ‘to Sheol’ as Gehinnom. Jacob said: This sign was given to me by God: If none of my sons dies during my lifetime, I am assured that I shall not see Gehinnom.

Rabbi Shimon further said: We learned that Shabbat is a likeness of the World to Come; this is certainly so… The additional soul comes from the mystery of Remember upon this shelter of peace, which receives from the World to Come and gives this addition to the holy people. Through this addition they rejoice, and all weekday matters, all sorrows, and all troubles are forgotten, as it is written, ‘On the day Hashem gives you rest from your sorrow, your turmoil, and the hard service…’

‘He completed on the sixth day’—so that he would not say that He therefore performed work on Shabbat, for the verse says, ‘He completed on the seventh day.’ He would not accept the Sages' exposition: What did the world lack? Rest. Shabbat came and rest came, and this was its completion.

MISHNA: One may only stand and begin to pray from an approach of gravity and submission. There is a tradition that the early generations of pious men would wait one hour, in order to reach the solemn frame of mind appropriate for prayer, and then pray, so that they would focus their hearts toward their Father in Heaven. Standing in prayer is standing before God and, as such, even if the king greets him, he should not respond to him; and even if a snake is wrapped on his heel, he should not interrupt his prayer.

Rabbi Jeremiah said in Rabbi Elazar’s name: If one prayed without concentration and knows that he will concentrate the second time, he may pray again; otherwise he should not. Rabbi Chiyya the Great said: In all my days I never managed to concentrate; once I made an effort, and I thought: Who enters before the king first, the alqafta or the Exilarch? Shmuel said: I counted chicks. Rabbi Mana said: I am grateful to my head, for when I reach Modim it bows of its own accord.

Rabbeinu Tam explains ‘scrutiny of prayer’ here as in Bava Batra 164b: One of the three matters from which a person is not spared each day is praying without directing his heart, as in the Yerushalmi… However, it is not possible to explain our passage this way. Rather, it concerns one who strives to concentrate and trusts that his prayer must be answered… He thinks in his heart that his request should be fulfilled because he prayed with concentration, and comes to heartache when it is not fulfilled.

Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi said to Elijah: And is there anyone alive in this world who is comparable to them and can produce such efficacious prayers? Elijah said to him: There are Rabbi Ḥiyya and his sons. Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi decreed a fast, and the Sages brought Rabbi Ḥiyya and his sons down to the pulpit to pray on behalf of the congregation. Rabbi Ḥiyya recited the phrase in the Amida prayer: Who makes the wind blow, and the wind blew. Rabbi Ḥiyya recited the next phrase: Who makes the rain fall, and rain fell. When he was about to say the phrase: Who revives the dead, the world trembled.

Rabbi Jeremiah said in Rabbi Elazar’s name: If one prayed without concentration and knows that he will concentrate the second time, he may pray again; otherwise he should not. Rabbi Chiyya the Great said: In all my days I never managed to concentrate; once I made an effort, and I thought: Who enters before the king first, the alqafta or the Exilarch? Shmuel said: I counted chicks. Rabbi Mana said: I am grateful to my head, for when I reach Modim it bows of its own accord.

The Gemara returns to the topic of prayer. It was taught in a baraita that the tanna Abba Binyamin would say: All of my life I have taken great pains with regard to two things: That my prayer should be before my bed and that my bed should be placed north to south. Abba Binyamin’s statement requires explanation. With regard to his statement: That my prayer should be before my bed, the Gemara asks, what does before my bed mean? If you say that it literally means that he would stand before his bed and pray, it is difficult, as Rav Yehuda said that Rav said, and some say that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Le
‘Close to my bed’—all my days I took care, upon rising from my bed, not to perform work and not to engage in Torah until I had recited Shema and prayed.

‘Rather, say: close to my bed’—he would not perform work until he prayed. Rashi explains that even study is included, for studying before prayer is forbidden. I do not know the source for this. § The Gemara relates an incident related to the halakha of scouring and rinsing. Rav Yitzḥak bar Yehuda was initially accustomed to study Torah before Rami bar Ḥama. After some time, he left him and went to study before Rav Sheshet. One day Rami bar Ḥama met him and said to him colloquially: Did you assume, as many do, that when the chief of taxes (alkafta) grasped me by the hand, the fragrance of his hand came to my hand? Do you think that because you went away from me in order to study before Rav Sheshet, have you become like Rav Sheshet merely by association?

The Gemara relates that when Rav Ḥisda and Rav Sheshet would meet each other, Rav Ḥisda’s lips would tremble from the teachings of Rav Sheshet. Rav Sheshet’s fluency and expertise were such that Rav Ḥisda would be filled with awe in his presence. For his part, Rav Sheshet’s entire body would shake from Rav Ḥisda’s sharpness, i.e., from his brilliant, analytical mind.

‘Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it’—this is the mystery of the holy covenant. Because all the sources of the body's limbs are established through this covenant, it includes them all. Similarly, Shabbat comprises the whole Torah, and all the mysteries of Torah depend upon it. Keeping Shabbat is like keeping the whole Torah: one who guards Shabbat is as though he guarded the whole Torah.

Bereshit contains the letters of ‘two’ and ‘Shabbat.’ These are the two Shabbatot, concerning which it is said: ‘The children of Israel shall keep the Shabbat, to make the Shabbat…’ Shabbat is mentioned twice here, corresponding to the upper and lower Shekhinah. What does ‘throughout their generations’ mean? Fortunate is one who makes them a dwelling on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, so that the evil inclination, which is the desecration of Shabbat, departs from there. ‘An everlasting covenant’ is the righteous one, upon whom both rest: one to fill him and one to be filled from him.

There are also three books of Prophets whose appearance in a dream is meaningful: One who sees the book of Kings should anticipate greatness, royalty; one who sees the book of Ezekiel should anticipate wisdom, as the configuration of the Divine Chariot is described therein; one who sees the book of Isaiah should anticipate consolation; and one who sees the book of Jeremiah should be concerned about calamity, because Jeremiah prophesied extensively of impending calamity.

As Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, gives a person an additional soul on Shabbat eve, and at the conclusion of Shabbat removes it from him, as it is stated: ‘He ceased from work and was refreshed (vayinafash)’ (Exodus 31:17). Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish expounds the verse as follows: Since he ceased from work, and now Shabbat has concluded and his additional soul is removed from him, woe (vai) for the additional soul (nefesh) that is lost.

The term vayinefash (and He rested) (Ibid.) may be resolved into vai (woe), nefesh (soul), that is, woe to the soul forlorn! Now we may well argue that it should rather be woe to the body that loses the special spirit with the departure of the Sabbath. But the truth is that man possesses a certain nefesh (psyche) that attracts to itself the special spirit on the eve of Sabbath, so that that spirit takes up its abode and resides within it the whole of the Sabbath. It thus becomes a superior nefesh, with greater power and resources than it possessed before.

The unique character of the Sabbath is expressed in the words: ‘Between Me and the children of Israel.’ And because the Faith is centred in the Sabbath, man is given on this day an additional, a supernal soul, a soul in which is all perfection, according to the pattern of the world to come. What does the word ‘Sabbath’ mean? The Name of the Holy One, the Name which is in perfect harmony at all sides.’

This Speech is called Shabbat. Because Shabbat is called Speech, weekday speech is forbidden on Shabbat. The printed marginal gloss, Gilyon Maharshab, relates: Rabbi Shimon acted this way—when he saw his mother speaking, he would say to her, ‘Mother, be silent; it is Shabbat, and this is forbidden.’ For this Speech must rule, and no other. This Speech, coming from the side of darkness, reveals deep things from within it. That is the meaning of ‘from darkness’: specifically from that which comes from the side of darkness.

Rabbi Shimon said: This verse concerns the mystery of the unity of faith. ‘With me from Lebanon, bride’—Voice says to Speech, ‘With me,’ for Voice comes to Speech and leads her with it, so that they become one without any separation. Voice is the general principle and Speech the particular. Therefore the general requires the particular, and the particular requires the general: there is no Voice without Speech and no Speech without Voice.

If a person has not merited to ask for mercy that words of Torah enter his innermost being, he should at least ask for mercy that excessive eating and drinking not enter his innermost being… It happened that Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi said at his death: It is revealed and known before the Holy One that I labored in Torah with all ten fingers, and did not eat or derive pleasure in this world even with one of my small fingers… I made my eating and drinking serve only to sustain my life, and I engaged in Torah all my days.

When the Tree of Good and Evil has dominion—the ordinary things of purity and the ordinary things of impurity—those sages who resemble Shabbat and festivals have only what those ordinary ones give them. It is like the Shabbat day, which has only what is prepared for it during the weekdays.

The masters of the Mishnah therefore established: ‘Study is not the main thing, but action.’ For the Holy One is concealed in the secrets of Torah. Through what is He made known? Through the commandments, which are His Shekhinah, His likeness. As He is humble, His Shekhinah is humility; He is pious, and she is pious; He is mighty, and she rules over all the nations of the world. Rabbi Avira expounded—and some say Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: The evil inclination has seven names. The Holy One, blessed be He, called it “evil,” as it is written, “For the inclination of a person’s heart is evil from his youth.” Moses called it “uncircumcised,” as it is written, “Circumcise the foreskin of your heart.” David called it “impure,” as it is written, “Create for me a pure heart, O God”—implying that there is an impure heart.
Create in me a clean heart, O God and renew a steadfast spirit within me.

… This is assuredly the clean heart which David asked for. ‘And renew a steadfast spirit within me’ indicates the spirit spoken of in the passage: ‘and the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters’, this being, as has been pointed out, the spirit of the Messiah; the same is alluded to in the promise: ‘And a new spirit will I put within you’ (Ez. 36, 26). I was watching in the visions of the night, and behold, with the clouds of heaven came one like a son of man. He reached the Ancient of Days, and they brought him near before Him.

The Gemara asks: Does it refer to the repetition of the phrase: ‘And He said’ in Genesis? There are only nine such phrases, not ten. Arise, cry out in the night: in the beginning of the watches pour out thy heart like water before the face of the Lord: lift up thy hands towards him for the life of thy young children, that faint for hunger at the head of every street.

We have been taught that it behoves man always to rouse the good prompter against the evil prompter; if the latter departs, well and good, but if not, the man should study the Torah, as there is nothing so well calculated to crush the evil prompter as the Torah; if he departs, well and good, but if not, let the man remind him of the day of death so as thereby to subdue him.

R. Jose said: ‘When a man perceives that evil thoughts are assailing him, he should study the Torah, and that will drive them away.’ R. Eleazar said: ‘When the evil side comes to seduce a man, he should draw it towards the Torah, and then it will quit him.

Joseph walked through the valley of the shadow of death, having been brought down to Egypt, but the Shekinah was with him, as we read: ‘And the Lord was with Joseph’, and by reason of the presence of the Shekinah all that he did prospered in his hand; so much so that if he had something in his hand and his master wanted something of a different kind, it changed in his hand to the kind his master wanted. Hence, it says ‘made to prosper in his hand’, the reason being that the Lord was with him.

‘The Lord was with Joseph, and he was a successful man, and he was in the house of his master, the Egyptian’ (Genesis 39:2). ‘The Lord was with Joseph’ – but with the rest of the tribes, He was not? Rabbi Yudan said: (This is analogous) to an animal driver, who had twelve animals laden with wine before him. One of them entered the shop of an idolater; he forsook the eleven and followed after it. They said to him: ‘Why do you forsake eleven (animals) and follow the one?’ He said to them: ‘These are in the public domain, and I am not concerned lest (the wine) become libation wine.’ So, these (Jo
Adonoy was with Yoseif, and he was successful. He was (a servant) in the house of his master, the Egyptian.

… Rabbi Huna said in the name of Rabbi Aḥa: This is how our forefather Abraham sat and pondered that entire day. Rabbi Elazar said: Due to a promissory note. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Due to the shame. ‘But the righteous will be secure as a young lion’ – ‘Jacob settled.’
The wicked flee when no man pursues: but the righteous are bold as a lion.

All anger issues from the side of rigorous judgement, but in two directions, one referred to as blessed, the other as cursed. Similarly, from the side of Isaac there issued two sons, one of whom was blessed and the other cursed on high and below; the two separated, each going off towards his own side, the one making his abode in the Holy Land, the other on Mount Seir, being as he was ‘a cunning hunter, a man of the field’ (Gen. 25, 27). The latter had his home in the desert, in regions of waste and desolation, while the former ‘dwelt in tents’ (Ibid.), all being fitly ordained.

The total of this is the total of that, but he will not get anything from him, and in that way he makes a mockery of the one receiving the lashes. ‘He mocks at the undoing of the innocent’ (Job 9:23) – Rav Aḥa said: When the righteous live in tranquility and seek to live in tranquility in this

Rabbi Levi bar Chama said in Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish’s name: A person should always rouse his good inclination against his evil inclination, as it says, ‘Be stirred, and do not sin.’ If he overcomes it, well and good; if not, let him occupy himself with Torah, as it says, ‘Speak in your hearts.’ If he overcomes it, well and good; if not, let him recite Shema, as it says, ‘Upon your beds.’ If he overcomes it, well and good; if not, let him recall the day of death, as it says, ‘And be silent, selah.’

So too the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel: My children, I created an evil inclination, which is the wound, and I created Torah as its antidote. If you are engaged in Torah study you will not be given over into the hand of the evil inclination, as it is stated: ‘If you do well, shall it not be lifted up?’ (Genesis 4:7). One who engages in Torah study lifts himself above the evil inclination.

Rabbi Yochanan said to him: Granted, Torah and deeds of kindness atone, for it is written, “Through kindness and truth iniquity is atoned.” “Kindness” means deeds of kindness, as it is written, “One who pursues charity and kindness finds life, charity, and honor.” “Truth” means Torah, as it is written, “Acquire truth, and do not sell it.” But from where is the same derived concerning one who buries his children?

Rabbi Yoḥanan says in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai: Even if a person recited only the recitation of Shema in the morning and in the evening, he has fulfilled the mitzva of: ‘This Torah scroll shall not depart from your mouth.’ And it is prohibited to state this matter in the presence of ignoramuses (amei ha’aretz), as they are likely to get the impression that there is no need to study Torah beyond this. to execute vengeance upon the nations, chastisements upon the peoples;

As to the question, What about the anger of students of the Torah? that anger is good in all its aspects, since, as we have been taught, the Torah is fire, and it is she who kindles that holy anger in her devotees, as it is written, ‘Is not my word like as a fire? saith the Lord’ (Jer. 23, 29). Hence it is that there are two grades, ‘blessed’ and ‘cursed’, each ranged on its own side. From the one issue all blessings in the upper and the lower worlds, all beneficence, all light, all deliverance, all redemption; whilst the other is the source of all curses, all wars and bloodshed, all desolation and evil, and all defilement.

Immediately the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave the priesthood to Abraham, as it is stated: ‘The Lord says to my lord: Sit at My right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool’ (Psalms 110:1), and afterward it is written: ‘The Lord has sworn, and will not repent: you shall be a priest forever,

A person never took a penny from Job and needed to take from him a second time. ‘And you shall be a blessing (berakha)’ – read it as ‘a pool (berekha).’ Just as a pool purifies the impure, so, you draw the distant near and purify them for their Father who is in Heaven. Rabbi Berekhya said: ‘I will bless you’ is already written; why does the verse state (further): ‘And you shall be a blessing’? When the Tabernacle is completed with its thigh, it is written of Jacob, ‘Jacob came whole.’ Jacob is the likeness of the Central Column from its outward aspect. Moses was there, but from the inward aspect: this one is the body and that one is the soul. Thus the two thighs of the Central Column, Netzach and Hod, are complete.
The woman conceived and bore a son. She saw that he was (exceptionally) good, and she kept him hidden for three months.

‘She saw that he was good.’ It was taught: Rabbi Meir says that his name was Tov. Rabbi Yehuda says his name was Toviyah. Rabbi Neḥemya says he was suited for prophecy. Others say he was born circumcised. The Sages say: When Moses was born, the entire house filled with light. Here it says, ‘She saw that he was good,’ and elsewhere, ‘God saw that the light was good.’
For the commandment is a lamp; and Tora is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life:
Elohim saw that the light was good, and Elohim divided the light from the darkness.

‘May God give you’—may He give you divinity… Another explanation: ‘From the dew of heaven’—this is Scripture; ‘and from the fat of the earth’—this is Mishnah; ‘grain’—this is Talmud; ‘wine’—this is Aggadah.

… It will be when you need it. ‘May God give you’—may He give you divinity… Another explanation: ‘From the dew of heaven’—this is Scripture; ‘and from the fat of the earth’—this is Mishnah; ‘grain’—this is Talmud; ‘wine’—this is Aggadah.

Bereshit contains the letters of ‘two’ and ‘Shabbat.’ These are the two Shabbatot, concerning which it is said: ‘The children of Israel shall keep the Shabbat, to make the Shabbat…’ Shabbat is mentioned twice here, corresponding to the upper and lower Shekhinah. What does ‘throughout their generations’ mean? Fortunate is one who makes them a dwelling on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, so that the evil inclination, which is the desecration of Shabbat, departs from there. ‘An everlasting covenant’ is the righteous one, upon whom both rest: one to fill him and one to be filled from him.

Why did He set a time for darkness? Because as long as the evil inclination is in the world, there is darkness and the shadow of death in the world, as it is written: ‘The stone of thick darkness and the shadow of death’ (Job 28:3). Rabbi Acha said: Be’avon is written in full. Even the most pious of the pious cannot be without one aspect of iniquity. David said: Did Jesse intend to bring me into the world? He intended only his own need. Once they had fulfilled their need, one turned his face in one direction and the other in the other direction, while You gathered every single drop. This is what David said: “My father and my mother have abandoned me.”

Another matter, ‘when a woman conceives’ – that is what is written: ‘I was generated in iniquity (Psalms 51:7). Rabbi Aḥa said: Even if one would be the most pious of the pious, it is impossible that he will not have one aspect of iniquity. David said before the Holy One blessed be He: ‘Master of the universe, did my father Yishai intend to produce me; was his intention not for his pleasure? Know that it is so, for after they have fulfilled their needs, this one turns his face to here and that one turns her face to there, and you insert each and every drop that is in him.’ That is what David s

Jacob lived in the land of Egypt for seventeen years. The days of Jacob, the years of his life, were one hundred and forty-seven years.

Why did Jabez merit a life without suffering and without the evil inclination in this world, resembling what the Holy One will give the righteous in the future? Because he traveled throughout the places of Israel and taught Torah publicly for the sake of Heaven. Whoever teaches his fellow one verse, one law, or one utterance is as though he sets life before him… ‘If You will indeed bless me’—with Torah study; ‘and enlarge my border’—with students.

‘To guard the way’—this is proper conduct. ‘The Tree of Life’ teaches that proper conduct precedes the Tree of Life. The Tree of Life is none other than Torah, as it is said, ‘It is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it.’

We have been taught that it behoves man always to rouse the good prompter against the evil prompter; if the latter departs, well and good, but if not, the man should study the Torah, as there is nothing so well calculated to crush the evil prompter as the Torah; if he departs, well and good, but if not, let the man remind him of the day of death so as thereby to subdue him.

One must say ‘Savri maranan,’ and they respond ‘L’chaim,’ because they are attached to the Tree of Life, rather than the Tree of Death—the vine through which Adam sinned. One said it was wheat, and one said it was a vine; all are true. There are seven species: wheat, barley, grapevine, fig, pomegranate, olive oil, and honey… Grapevine: she squeezed grapes in another domain and made wine of idolatrous libation, and it became the Tree of Good and Evil.
Hashem God caused every tree pleasant to the sight and good for food to grow from the ground, with the Tree of Life in the midst of the garden and the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil.
Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine I have mixed.
Hashem God said, ‘Behold, the man has become like one of Us, knowing good and evil. Now, lest he stretch out his hand and take also from the Tree of Life, and eat and live forever!’

‘And now, he might extend his hand’ – Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: This teaches that the Holy One blessed be He opened for him an opportunity for repentance. ‘And now’ – ‘and now’ is nothing other than repentance, as it is stated: ‘And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God (ask of you? Only to fear the Lord your God, to walk in all His ways…)’ (Deuteronomy 10:12). But he (Adam) said: ‘Might (pen)’ – and pen is nothing other than no. The Holy One blessed be He said: ‘Will he now extend his hand and eat from the tree of life?’ It was a rhetorical question. And if he eats, he will live forever.
Abraham stretched out his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son.
But to the wicked God said: ‘What right have you to recount My statutes and take My covenant upon your lips, when you hate discipline and cast My words behind you?’
Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it.

And that is what Rava said: To those who are right-handed in their approach to Torah, and engage in its study with strength, good will, and sanctity, Torah is a drug of life, and to those who are left-handed in their approach to Torah, it is a drug of death.

Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, ‘Remain a widow in your father’s house until my son Shelah grows up,’ for he said, ‘Lest he too die like his brothers.’ Tamar went and dwelt in her father’s house.

The Gemara comments: Who is the tanna of the mishna? It is Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, who holds that a legal presumption (ḥazaka) is established after two occurrences. As it is taught in a baraita: If a woman circumcised her first son and he died as a result of the circumcision, and she circumcised her second son and he also died, she should not circumcise her third son, as the deaths of the first two produce a presumption that this woman’s sons die as a result of circumcision. This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: She should circumcise her third son, as there

Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says: If one confesses in subsequent years, all the more so is he praiseworthy, as he remembers his earlier sins and is thereby humbled, as it is stated: ‘For I know my transgressions; and my sin is ever before me’ (Psalms 51:5). But how do I establish the meaning of the verse: ‘Like a dog that returns to its vomit’? It may be established in accordance with the opinion of Rav Huna, as Rav Huna said: When a person commits a transgression and repeats it, it is permitted to him. The Gemara is surprised at this: Can it enter your mind that it is permitted to him because h

‘Remember’ is a place where there is no forgetfulness, and forgetfulness does not exist there. For there is no forgetfulness in the place of the supernal covenant, and all the more so above it. Below, however, there is forgetfulness: a place that requires remembrance. Concerning this it is written, ‘Let the iniquity of his fathers be remembered…’ There are appointed beings there who recall a person’s merits and his sins.
At the end of two full years, Pharaoh was dreaming, and behold, he was standing by the Nile.
Hashem lives! Blessed is my Rock, and exalted is the God of my salvation.
Of David. Blessed is Hashem, my Rock, who trains my hands for battle and my fingers for war.
Blessed is the Lord, day by day; He bears our burden—God is our salvation. Selah.

“It came to pass at the end.” Rabbi Elazar opened: “The Lord lives; blessed is my Rock, and exalted is the God of my salvation.” Elohei is written with a vav. This verse calls for contemplation. “The Lord lives” refers to the living righteous one, the foundation of the world, who is called the Life of the Worlds. “Blessed is my Rock” is as it is written, “Blessed is the Lord, my Rock”; this is the world sustained by that righteous one. “Exalted” refers to the upper world; Elohei, with a vav, refers to heaven, as in “The heavens are the Lord’s heavens.” Come and see: “Blessed is Adonai, day by

A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If I am a father, where is My honor? If I am a master, where is the fear of Me?—says Hashem of hosts to you, the priests who despise My name. Yet you say, ‘How have we despised Your name?’

The Congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the world, “I sleep” concerning the commandments, “but my heart is awake” to acts of kindness. “I sleep” concerning charity, “but my heart is awake” to perform it. “I sleep” concerning the offerings, “but my heart is awake” to the recitation of Shema and prayer. “I sleep” concerning the Temple, “but my heart is awake” to synagogues and houses of study. “I sleep” concerning the appointed end, “but my heart is awake” for redemption. “I sleep” concerning redemption, but the heart of the Holy One, blessed be He, is awake
My flesh and my heart fail; God is the Rock of my heart and my portion forever.
The God of Israel said; the Rock of Israel spoke to me: ‘A ruler over mankind—a righteous one, ruling in the fear of God.’

We learned: Rabbi Yehudah said, There is no sin in the world that does not admit repentance, except this one. There are no sinners who do not behold the face of the Shekhinah, except this one, as it is written, “Evil shall not dwell with You”—not at all. Rabbi Yitzchak said: Fortunate are the righteous in this world and the World to Come. Of them it is written, “Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.” What does “they shall inherit the land forever” mean? Rabbi Yehudah said: As it is written, “I shall walk before the Lord in the lands of the living.”

After turning to a bad course, Acher asked Rabbi Meir: What does “Gold and glass cannot equal it, nor can vessels of fine gold be exchanged for it” mean? He answered: These are words of Torah, difficult to acquire like vessels of gold and fine gold, but easily lost like glass vessels. Acher told him: “Rabbi Akiva your teacher did not explain it that way. Rather, just as vessels of gold and glass can be repaired after breaking, so a Torah scholar can be restored even after going astray.” Rabbi Meir told him: “Then you too should return.” He answered: “I have already heard from behind the curtai

They asked him, “Why do you call yourself Rav Huna?” He replied, “That is my name.” “Why, when they told you to sit upon the bed, did you sit?” He replied, “Whatever the master of the house tells you, do—except leave.”

quote: The general principle is that there is nothing that cannot be repaired through repentance. “Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him.” Rabbi Elazar opened: “Why should I fear in days of evil, when the iniquity of my heels surrounds me?” Come and see: there are three who fear without knowing what they fear, as has been explained. A person may fear without knowing why because of sins he does not recognize as sins and to which he pays no attention; he fears the days of evil. What are the days of evil? They are the days associated with that evil—the evil inclination, which is called evil. It has appointed days when it is given permission in the world to lead astray
Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of falsehood, and sin as with the ropes of a wagon!

For this is the evil inclination’s craft: today it says, “Do this,” and tomorrow it says, “Do that,” until it tells him to worship idols, and he goes and worships them. Rabbi Ami said: He is called a transgressor. Such is the evil inclination’s trade: Today it tells him, “Do this,” tomorrow, “Do this,” and eventually, “Go and worship an idol,” and he goes and does so. God saw the light, that it was good, and God separated the light from the darkness.

God said, ‘Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, separating water from water.’ God made the firmament and separated the waters below the firmament from the waters above the firmament, and it was so. Why is “it was good” not written concerning the second day? Rabbi Yochanan taught in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Rabbi Chalafta: Because Gehinnom was created on it, as it says, “For the inferno was prepared from yesterday”—the day that had a yesterday but no day before yesterday. Rabbi Chanina says: Because division was created on it, as it says, “Let it divide between water and water.” Rabbi Tavyomei said: If division that serves the world’s order and habitation is not called good, how much more so division that throws it into confusion. Rabbi Shmuel said: Because the work of the waters had n

Fortunate is the one who guards Shabbat’s dwelling, the heart, so that the sadness of the spleen and the anger of the gall do not approach it. That anger is the fire of Gehinnom, concerning which it is written, “Do not kindle a fire in any of your dwellings on the day of Shabbat.” Indeed, whoever becomes angry is as though he kindled the fire of Gehinnom.
You shall kindle no fire in any of your dwellings on the day of Shabbat.
In all toil there is gain, but talk of the lips leads only to lack.

Another interpretation: “In all distress there is gain.” Everything Joseph suffered with his mistress brought him a gain from her. Why? Because he married her daughter. “But talk of the lips leads only to loss”: because he said to the chief cupbearer, “Remember me” and “Mention me,” two years were added to his imprisonment, as it says, “It came to pass at the end of two years.”

Happy is the man who makes Hashem his trust and does not turn to the arrogant or to those who stray after falsehood.

The Gemara explains: What is the situation where Joseph sanctified God’s name in private? As it is written: ‘And it came to pass on a certain day, when he went into the house to do his work’ (Genesis 39:11). Rabbi Yoḥanan says: This teaches that both Joseph and Potiphar’s wife stayed in the house, as they intended to perform a matter of sin. With regard to the phrase ‘when he went into the house to do his work,’ Rav and Shmuel engage in a dispute with regard to its meaning. One says: It means that he went into the house to do his work, literally. And one says: He entered the house in order to

… Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥman said: In order to juxtapose the incident of Tamar to the incident of Potifar’s wife. Just as this one, (Tamar, acted) for the sake of Heaven, so too, that one, (Potifar’s wife, acted) for the sake of Heaven, as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: She saw through her astrology that she was destined to bring forth a child from him, but she did not know whether it would be from her or from her daughter. That is what is written: ‘(The astrologers, the stargazers,) who foretell by the new moons of that which will befall you’ (Isaiah 47:13). …

“The servant said to him.” This is what is written: “Canaan holds deceitful scales in his hand; he loves to oppress.” Canaan is Eliezer. “Deceitful scales in his hand”: he sat weighing whether his daughter was suitable or unsuitable. “He loves to oppress”: to take the beloved of the world, Isaac. He said, “Perhaps the woman will not consent,” and I will give him my daughter. Abraham said to him: You are cursed, and my son is blessed; one who is cursed does not cleave to one who is blessed.

Rabbi Yannai would examine the ferry before crossing. He acted according to his teaching: A person should never stand in a dangerous place saying that a miracle will be performed for him, for perhaps no miracle will be performed. Even if a miracle is performed, his merits are diminished. Rabbi Chanin said: What verse teaches this? “I have become small through all the kindnesses and all the truth that You have shown Your servant.”

Ten sefirot of nothingness, corresponding to the ten fingers: five opposite five, with the covenant of the Unique One aligned in the middle, in the word of the tongue and in the circumcision of the procreative organ.
Until the time his word came, the utterance of Hashem refined him.
He sets an end to darkness, and searches out every limit—the stone of gloom and the shadow of death.

AND IT CAME TO PASS AT THE END. R. Hiya expounded the word ‘end’ from the text: He setteth an end for darkness, and he searcheth out to the furthest bound; a stone of thick darkness and the shadow of death (Job 28, 3). ‘The end here mentioned is’, he said, ‘an allusion to the ‘end of the left’, which, after roaming to and fro in the world, finally ascends and presents itself before the Holy One, blessed be He, to bring accusations against mankind. He ‘searcheth out to the furthest bound’ (takhlith— destruction), inasmuch as all his works are never for good, but always for destruction and for t

‘It was at the conclusion of two years, and Pharaoh was dreaming: and, behold, he stood at the Nile’ (Genesis 41:1). ‘It was at the conclusion of two years.’ ‘He sets an end to darkness’ (Job 28:3) – He set a time for the world, how many years it would spend in darkness. Why did He set a time for darkness? Because as long as the evil inclination is in the world, there is darkness and the shadow of death in the world, as it is written: ‘The stone of thick darkness and the shadow of death’ (Job 28:3). If the evil inclination is removed from the world, there is no darkness and shadow of death in
If you indeed forget Hashem your God and follow other gods, serving them and bowing to them, I testify against you today that you will surely perish.

Rami bar Abba said: What is meant by “A small city, with few men in it”? “A small city” is the body; “few men in it” are the limbs; “a great king came against it and besieged it” is the evil inclination; “he built great siegeworks against it” are sins. “There was found in it a poor wise man” is the good inclination; “he delivered the city through his wisdom” is repentance and good deeds. “No one remembered that poor man”: when the evil inclination prevails, no one remembers the good inclination.
When the storm passes, the wicked one is no more; but the righteous one is the foundation of the world.

Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Even for one righteous person the world exists, as it is stated: “But the righteous is the foundation of the world” (Proverbs 10:25). Rabbi Ḥiyya himself said: The proof is from here, as it is stated: “He will keep the feet of His pious ones” (I Samuel 2:9), meaning that God maintains the world due to the pious people. The Gemara questions this proof; “pious ones” indicates many rather than a single righteous person. Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: Although the text is vocalized in the plural, it is written in the singular: “His pious one”; God m
Light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright of heart.
The light of the righteous rejoices, but the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.
A wise person’s heart is at his right, and a fool’s heart at his left.
Joseph saw Benjamin with them and said to the one in charge of his house, ‘Bring the men into the house, slaughter an animal, and prepare, for the men will eat with me at noon.’
“The men took … Joseph saw … and prepare.” “Prepare” refers specifically to Shabbat, as it says, “On the sixth day they shall prepare.” This teaches that Joseph observed Shabbat before it was given.
He sent portions to them from before him, and Benjamin’s portion was five times as large as any of theirs. They drank and became intoxicated with him.
Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine I have mixed.

Meanwhile an elder approached him and said: Faithful Shepherd, prepare a table for your Master, for Him and the Matron, with every kind of delight, to fulfill “This is the table that is before the Lord.” Until now, all have delighted in the King’s table, as it is written, “Come, eat of My bread.” This is the bread of the Written Torah and the wine of the Oral Torah. There are many delicacies there—the different meanings of Torah—which are sweeter than all the foods and delights of the world and of a king.

‘May God give you’—may He give you divinity… Another explanation: ‘From the dew of heaven’—this is Scripture; ‘and from the fat of the earth’—this is Mishnah; ‘grain’—this is Talmud; ‘wine’—this is Aggadah.

The expounders of metaphor say: Do you wish to recognize the One who spoke and brought the world into being? Learn haggadah. For if you do so, you will come to recognize the Holy One Blessed be He and cleave to His ways. And if you do yours, then I will do Mine, (Devarim 11:23) "and the L-rd will drive out, etc."

Happy is the person who does this, and the son of man who holds fast to it: who guards Shabbat from desecrating it and guards his hand from doing any evil.

If you ask: What reward does one who keeps Shabbat receive? Scripture says, ‘Happy is the person who does this… who guards Shabbat against desecrating it, and guards his hand against doing any evil.’ We have therefore learned that whoever keeps Shabbat even under hardship is saved from transgression.

quote: Thus there is no person who does not receive an addition to his nefesh, ruach, and neshamah, according to the portion allotted to him. A person must direct his intention so that some of this addition will remain with him for the weekdays. Through this his ways will be established, if he directs his intention properly; he is assured that he will not sin, that sins will not come about through him, and that the evil inclination will not accuse him. Everything depends upon his intention.
Pharaoh sent and summoned Joseph, and they hurried him from the pit. He shaved, changed his garments, and came before Pharaoh.
Hashem takes pleasure in those who fear Him, in those who hope for His kindness.

Who are “those who await His kindness”? Those who engage in Torah at night and join themselves to the Shekhinah. When morning comes, they await His kindness. We have explained that when a person engages in Torah at night, a thread of kindness is drawn over him by day, as it says, “By day the Lord commands His kindness, and at night His song is with me.” Therefore it says, “The Lord favors His fearers,” rather than “takes pleasure in His fearers”: like someone who seeks another with goodwill and wishes to become reconciled with him. In this way Joseph was sorrowful in spirit and heart because h
Hashem builds Jerusalem; He gathers the outcasts of Israel. He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.

A baraita teaches: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave Israel three good gifts, all of them through suffering: Torah, the Land of Israel, and the World to Come. What is the source for Torah? “Happy is the man whom You discipline, God, and teach from Your Torah.” For the Land of Israel: “As a man disciplines his son, Hashem your God disciplines you,” followed by, “For Hashem your God brings you to a good land.” For the World to Come: “The commandment is a lamp and Torah is light; the way of life is the reproof of discipline.”
Yochana and Mamre said to Moses: Are you bringing straw to Afarayim? He replied: People say, “Bring vegetables to a town of vegetables.”
But I will also judge the nation they serve; afterward they will go out with great wealth.

Reish Lakish said: May I be an atonement for Rabbi Chiyya and his sons. When Torah was first forgotten from Israel, Ezra came up from Babylonia and reestablished it. When it was again forgotten, Hillel the Babylonian came up and reestablished it. When it was again forgotten, Rabbi Chiyya and his sons came up and reestablished it.

Rav Yehudah said in Shmuel’s name: All the clusters of scholars who arose for Israel from the days of Moses until Yosef ben Yoezer died learned Torah like Moses our teacher. From then onward, they did not learn Torah like Moses our teacher. But did Rav Yehudah not say in Shmuel’s name that three thousand laws were forgotten during the mourning for Moses? Those that were forgotten were forgotten; those they had learned, they knew like Moses our teacher. But was it not taught: After Moses died, if the majority declared something impure, they declared it impure; if the majority declared it pure,
Happy is the man whom You discipline, Yah, and whom You teach from Your Torah.

This is taught through an a fortiori inference from the law concerning the tooth and eye of a slave: The tooth and eye are each a single limb of a person and if his master damages either, the slave thereby obtains his freedom; suffering that cleanses a person’s entire body all the more so that one attains freedom, atonement, from his sins.

Rabbi Chama saw a blind man sitting and toiling in Torah. He said to him, “Greetings, free man.” The man replied, “Where did you hear that I was the son of slaves?” He answered, “No; I mean that you are free in the World to Come.” Rabbi Yudan said: It is written, “If he knocks out his male slave’s tooth or his female slave’s tooth, he shall send him free.” If, for these, which affect only one bodily member, the Torah says to send him free, how much more so for a person whose suffering affects his whole body. Rabbi Pinchas said in the name of Rabbi Hoshaya: It does not say, “Happy is the man wh

They are called according to this arrangement: Chesed is the right arm; Gevurah, the left arm; Tiferet, the body; Netzach and Hod, the two legs; Yesod is the body’s extremity, the sign of the holy covenant. Malchut is the mouth, which we call Oral Torah. Chochmah is the brain, the inward thought; Binah is the heart, and through it the heart understands. Of these two it is written, “The hidden things belong to the Lord our God.”

“They traveled three days in the wilderness and found no water.” Water means Torah, as it says, “All who thirst, come to the water.” Rabbi Yeisa asked: Who had given them Torah here? Torah had not yet been given to them. Rabbi Elazar said: They went out into the wilderness to behold Him. The Holy One, blessed be He, removed the radiance of His glory from there, and they went to behold Him but did not find Him. We have learned that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called Torah; water is none other than Torah, and Torah is none other than the Holy One, blessed be He.
For wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will be pleasant to your soul.

Rabbi Elazar asked his father: How are these meals arranged? He answered: Of Shabbat night it is written, “I will make you ride upon the heights of the earth.” That night the Matron and the entire Field of Apples are blessed; a person’s table is blessed and an additional soul is granted. That night is the Matron’s joy, and a person must rejoice in her joy and eat the Matron’s meal. Of Shabbat day, the second meal, it is written, “Then you shall delight above the Lord”—“above the Lord,” precisely. At that hour the Holy Ancient One is revealed, and all the worlds rejoice. We celebrate the perfec

“Remember” belongs to the masculine, and “Guard” belongs to the feminine. The Shabbat day is the mystery of all faith, extending from the highest head to the end of all levels; Shabbat is all of it. There are three levels, all called Shabbat: the supernal Shabbat, the daytime Shabbat, and the nighttime Shabbat. They are all one, and all are called Shabbat. Each, when it rules, takes its companions and invites them to be with it in its dominion; when it comes into the world, all come and are invited with it.

‘Happy is the man who has made the Lord his trust’ (Psalms 40:5) – this is Joseph. ‘And did not turn to the proud’ (Psalms 40:5) – because he said to the chief butler: ‘Remember me…and mention me,’ two years were added for him. ‘Happy is the man who makes the Lord his trust’ – Rabbi Yudan said: Many myriads of myriads tend after falsehood, woe unto anyone who puts his trust in them. ‘For a dream comes with a multitude of concerns’ (Ecclesiastes 5:2) – Pharaoh said: ‘Who stands over whom – I for my god, or my god over me?’ (Joseph) said to him: ‘You, over your god.’ That is what is written: ‘It

“Pharaoh sent and he called Joseph”: it should have said “to call Joseph.” Rather, “He called Joseph” refers to the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says, “Until the time his word came, the utterance of the Lord refined him.” “Until the time his word came”—this is “He called Joseph.” Here it is written, “He called Joseph,” and there, “He called to Moses.” “He shaved and changed his garments”—in honor of the king, as has been explained.
He called to Moses, and Hashem spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying:
He called his name Noah, saying, ‘This one will comfort us from our work and from the toil of our hands, from the ground that Hashem cursed.’
Afterward his brother came out, his hand grasping Esau’s heel, and he called his name Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them.

It is written, “He called et his name Noah,” whereas it is written, “He called his name Jacob.” Why is et not written there? There is one level there and another level here. Thus it is written, “I saw et the Lord”; it does not say, “I saw the Lord,” but “et the Lord.” So too, with Noah, “He called et his name Noah.” “He called his name Jacob” corresponds to Jacob’s own level: the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself called him Jacob. Here, however, et includes the Shekhinah.

When Joseph the righteous first descended to Egypt, he drew the Shekhinah after him, for the Shekhinah follows only the righteous. Therefore Joseph was first drawn to Egypt and properly gathered all the world’s wealth; afterward the Shekhinah descended to Egypt, with all the tribes. Because Joseph guarded the covenant, he merited to be crowned in its place and attained sovereignty above and sovereignty below.
