Thus, whoever guards the holy covenant is as though he fulfilled the entire holy Torah, for the covenant is equivalent to the whole Torah.
You will give truth to Jacob and kindness to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from days of old.

“Ask yourself an ot”—an actual letter, for all proceeded through the mystery of the letters. Similarly, what is written concerning Rahab? “Give me a sign of truth.” This is the letter vav, for it is called the letter of truth. Should you say that the other letters are not true? They are indeed; nevertheless, this letter is called the letter of truth.

Another interpretation: the peddler is Joseph the righteous. Just as a spice dealer holds all the bundles of spices and fragrant powders, so Joseph upholds Torah, because he fulfilled it; all Torah’s commandments are bound to guarding the holy covenant. Therefore the Shekhinah is bound to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; Jacob and Joseph are as one and have one likeness. This is what is written, “These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph.” Therefore it says, “with all the powders of the peddler,” for from the place of the river that flows forth everything is watered and all faces shine.

Thus says Hashem of hosts: The fast of the fourth month, the fast of the fifth, the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth will become joy, gladness, and good festivals for the house of Judah. Therefore love truth and peace.

It is written, “Dominion and fear are with Him; He makes peace in His heights.” The companions have explained this verse. “Dominion” is Abraham, of whom it is written, “You are a prince of God among us,” and “I will bless you and make your name great.” “Fear” is Isaac, as it is written, “The Fear of Isaac was with me.” “He makes peace in His heights” is Jacob, as it is written, “Give truth to Jacob,” and “Love truth and peace.” Truth and peace are bound to one another; therefore he is the perfection of all.

“These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph.” As has been explained, Jacob’s entire likeness was in Joseph; whatever happened to one happened to the other, and both proceed as one. This is the mystery of the letter vav spelled vav-vav: both proceed together, for they are one mystery and one likeness.
I have given you one portion beyond your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorite with my sword and my bow.

“Abram passed through the land as far as the place of Shechem.” This is the synagogue, the place where the Shekhinah dwells, as it is said, “I have given you one shechem.” This is the Shekhinah, which appeared to him because he was called righteous, for tzedek dwells only with the tzaddik. This is “as far as the place of Shechem.” “As far as Elon Moreh”—these are the houses of study, where Torah is learned and taught publicly.
Command the children of Israel and say to them: My offering, My bread for My fire-offerings, My pleasing fragrance—you shall take care to offer to Me at its appointed time.

He opened and said: Rabbi Elazar explained this verse, “Et My offering, My bread for My fire-offerings.” “Et My offering” is the mystery of the Congregation of Israel, for it says et—et precisely. “My offering” is the offering and the bond by which union is made. “My bread” is the sustenance that comes from above through the awakening below. “For My fire-offerings” includes the other hosts that must receive sustenance, each as befits it. “My pleasing fragrance” is the will and bond through which all are united in the mystery of the upper world.

“Remember” is the mystery of the masculine, which encompasses all the members of the upper world. “Et the Shabbat day” includes Shabbat’s entrance, which is night; this is et. “To sanctify it”: sanctity is required from the holy people, so that it may be crowned through them as is fitting.

Come and see: corresponding to those seven righteous ones, the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded in the Torah that an additional offering be brought on seven occasions during the year, to add delights and pleasures for them from the King’s house, so that the fathers be satisfied first and then the children. These are seven occasions and no more. On Shabbat, it corresponds to the righteous one, foundation of the world, who is called “All” and is called Shabbat, to add delights for him from the concealed mind. On Rosh Chodesh, it corresponds to the Congregation of Israel, which is called the mo
Pharaoh sent and summoned Joseph, and they hurried him from the pit. He shaved, changed his garments, and came before Pharaoh.
Hashem takes pleasure in those who fear Him, in those who hope for His kindness.
The deliverance on that day became mourning for all the people, for the people heard on that day that the king was grieved over his son.
The blessing of Hashem makes rich, and He adds no sorrow with it.

‘God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it.’ It is written, ‘The Lord’s blessing brings riches, and He adds no sorrow with it.’ ‘The Lord’s blessing brings riches’ refers to Shabbat, as it says, ‘God blessed the seventh day.’ ‘He adds no sorrow with it’ refers to mourning, as in the verse, ‘The king was grieved over his son.’

A certain heretic asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha: Do you not say that the Holy One, blessed be He, foresees what will happen? He replied: Yes. The man asked: Then why is it written, “He grieved in His heart”? Rabbi Yehoshua asked him: Has a son ever been born to you? He replied: Yes. What did you do? I rejoiced and made everyone rejoice. Did you not know that he would eventually die? He replied: At a time of joy, joy; at a time of mourning, mourning. Rabbi Yehoshua said: So it was before the Holy One, blessed be He. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: The Holy One, blessed be He, mourned His world
Hashem regretted that He had made mankind on the earth, and He was grieved in His heart.
Hashem builds Jerusalem; He gathers the outcasts of Israel. He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.
He swallowed wealth and will vomit it out; God will drive it out of his belly.
He counts the number of the stars; He calls them all by names. Great is our Lord and abundant in power; His understanding is beyond number.
For we must surely die, like water poured on the earth that cannot be gathered again. Yet God does not take away a soul; He devises plans so that the banished one will not remain banished from Him.

Rabbi Yitzchak said: What the prophets would prophesy in every generation, they received from Mount Sinai. Thus Moses says to Israel, “Those who are here with us standing today, and those who are not here with us today.” It does not say that the latter are “standing with us today,” but simply “with us today.” These are the souls destined to be created, which had no tangible existence, so that “standing” is not said of them. Although they did not exist at that time, each received his portion. Thus it says, “The burden of the word of the Lord to Israel by the hand of Malachi”—not “in the days of
Joseph saw Benjamin with them and said to the one in charge of his house, ‘Bring the men into the house, slaughter an animal, and prepare, for the men will eat with me at noon.’
“The men took … Joseph saw … and prepare.” “Prepare” refers specifically to Shabbat, as it says, “On the sixth day they shall prepare.” This teaches that Joseph observed Shabbat before it was given.

So too the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel: My children, I created an evil inclination, which is the wound, and I created Torah as its antidote. If you are engaged in Torah study you will not be given over into the hand of the evil inclination, as it is stated: ‘If you do well, shall it not be lifted up?’ (Genesis 4:7). One who engages in Torah study lifts himself above the evil inclination.

Why are the nations tainted? Because they did not stand at Mount Sinai. When the serpent came upon Eve, it implanted pollution in her. Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, had their pollution cease; the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai, did not have their pollution cease. Rav Aha, Rava’s son, asked Rav Ashi: What about converts? He answered: Though they themselves were not there, their heavenly roots were there, as it says, “Those standing here with us today before the Lord our God, and those who are not here.” This disagrees with Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, who said: The pollution did not ce
Such is the way of an adulterous woman: she eats, wipes her mouth, and says, ‘I have done no wrong.’

“Who passes by us continually”: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said in Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov’s name: Whoever hosts a Torah scholar in his home and lets him benefit from his possessions is regarded by Scripture as though he offered the daily offerings.
Rabbi Berechyah said: One who wishes to pour wine upon the altar should fill the throats of Torah scholars with wine, as it is written, “To you, men, I call.”

Did Rabbi Elazar say that one who fasts is called holy? Did he not say: A person should always consider himself as though a holy presence dwells within his innards, as it is written, “The Holy One is in your midst, and I will not come into the city”? There is no contradiction: one teaching concerns a person able to endure self-affliction; the other concerns a person unable to endure it.
I will not carry out My fierce anger; I will not return to destroy Ephraim. For I am God and not a man, the Holy One in your midst, and I will not enter the city.
On the third day Joseph said to them, ‘Do this and live, for I fear God.’
Speak to the whole congregation of the children of Israel and say to them: You shall be holy, for I, Hashem your God, am holy.

“Speak to the entire congregation of the children of Israel and say to them, You shall be holy”: This teaches that the section was proclaimed to the assembled congregation. Why was it proclaimed in an assembly? Because most of the Torah’s essential laws depend upon it. “You shall be holy”—you shall be separate. “For I, the Lord your God, am holy”: If you sanctify yourselves, I account it to you as though you sanctified Me; if you do not sanctify yourselves, I account it to you as though you did not sanctify Me. Could this mean that I am holy only if you sanctify Me? Scripture says, “For I am h

Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai taught: Because all matters depend upon Rachel, Israel is called by her name: ‘Rachel weeps for her children.’ Not only by her name, but also by her son’s name: ‘Perhaps Hashem, God of hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.’ And not only by her son’s name, but by her grandson’s name: ‘Is Ephraim a precious son to Me?’
Hate evil, love good, and establish justice in the gate. Perhaps Hashem, God of hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.

§ Rabbi Avira, and some say Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, taught: The evil inclination has seven names. The Holy One, Blessed be He, called it evil, as it is stated: ‘For the inclination of a man’s heart is evil from his youth’ (Genesis 8:21). Moses called it uncircumcised, as it is stated: ‘And circumcise the foreskin of your hearts’ (Deuteronomy 10:16). David called it impure, as it is stated: ‘Create for me a pure heart, O God’ (Psalms 51:12); by inference, there is an impure heart that is the evil inclination.

Hashem smelled the pleasing fragrance, and Hashem said in His heart, ‘I will not again curse the ground because of mankind, for the inclination of the human heart is evil from youth. Nor will I again strike every living thing as I have done.’

‘Joseph, seventeen years old…’ – and you say he was a lad? It is because he would perform the actions of a lad – he would groom his eyes, lift his heels, and curl his hair. ‘Was herding…Joseph brought evil report of them to their father’ – what did he say? Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehuda, and Rabbi Shimon: Rabbi Meir says: Your sons are suspected of eating the limb of a living animal. Rabbi Shimon says: They are directing their glances at the girls of the land. Rabbi Yehuda says: They are demeaning the sons of the maidservants and calling them slaves. Rabbi Yehuda bar Simon said: He was punished for
He fell upon the neck of his brother Benjamin and wept, and Benjamin wept upon his neck.

“He fell upon his brother Benjamin’s necks.” How many necks did Benjamin have? Rabbi Elazar said: He wept over the two Temples that would stand in Benjamin’s portion and would be destroyed. “Benjamin wept upon his neck”: he wept over the Tabernacle of Shiloh, which would stand in Joseph’s portion and would be destroyed.

They asked Rav Huna, son of Rav Natan: Why did you drink the cup in two draughts? He answered: It was taught, One who drinks his cup in one draught is a glutton; in two draughts is proper conduct; in three is among the haughty.

Rabbi Abbahu said: Scripture says, “Joseph is a fruitful son, a fruitful son by a spring.” The eye that did not wish to feed upon or enjoy what was not its own shall merit to eat as far as its eyes can see. Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said: “The favor of Him who dwells in the bush”: the eye that did not wish to enjoy what was not its own shall merit to eat among those who hate him.
I will give grass in your field for your animals, and you will eat and be satisfied. Guard yourselves, lest your heart be enticed and you turn aside, serve other gods, and bow down to them.

Rabbi Avdimi of Haifa said: Before a person eats and drinks, he has two hearts; after he eats and drinks, he has only one heart. For it is written, “A hollow man becomes two-hearted,” and it is written, “Hollow, of boards,” which we translate as “hollow boards.”
You shall love Hashem your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.

A person must bless for misfortune just as he blesses for good fortune, as it is said, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.” “With all your heart”—with both your inclinations, the good inclination and the evil inclination. “With all your soul”—even if He takes your soul. “With all your might”—with all your wealth. Another interpretation: with every measure He measures out to you, thank Him exceedingly.

The sustenance higher than all is the sustenance of the companions who engage in Torah: they eat the sustenance of spirit and soul, and do not eat the sustenance of the body at all. It comes from the exalted place, most precious of all, called Chochmah. Therefore the companions’ bodies are weaker than those of other people, for they do not eat bodily sustenance; they eat the sustenance of spirit and soul from that remote, exalted place, most precious of all. This food is therefore the most subtle of the subtle. Fortunate is their portion! This is what is written, “Wisdom gives life to its poss
For wisdom provides shelter, as money provides shelter; but the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom gives life to those who possess it.
Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine I have mixed.

Meanwhile an elder approached him and said: Faithful Shepherd, prepare a table for your Master, for Him and the Matron, with every kind of delight, to fulfill “This is the table that is before the Lord.” Until now, all have delighted in the King’s table, as it is written, “Come, eat of My bread.” This is the bread of the Written Torah and the wine of the Oral Torah. There are many delicacies there—the different meanings of Torah—which are sweeter than all the foods and delights of the world and of a king.
I desire to do Your will, my God; Your Torah is within my innermost being.

Although Rabbi Akiva said, “Make your Shabbat like a weekday rather than depend on others,” nevertheless a person should take a little meat and a little wine, without excessive meat and wine. If he indulges excessively, Scripture testifies against him: “Do not be among wine-drinkers, among those who gorge on meat, for the drunkard and glutton will become poor.” If a person has not merited to ask for mercy that words of Torah enter his inward parts, he should at least ask for mercy that excessive food and drink not enter them, as it says, “I have refined you, but not as silver; I have chosen yo

Rabba bar Rav Huna visited the house of Rabba bar Rav Nahman. They served him three se’a of cakes prepared with rich oil. He asked them: Did you know I was coming? They replied: Are you more important to us than Shabbat?
He sent portions to them from before him, and Benjamin’s portion was five times as large as any of theirs. They drank and became intoxicated with him.
“Five portions”: his own portion together with his brothers, and the portions of Joseph, Asenath, Manasseh, and Ephraim.
Of Benjamin he said: The beloved of Hashem will dwell securely beside Him. He shelters him all the day, and between his shoulders He dwells.

The tannaim differ: “He shelters him” refers to the First Temple; “all the day” refers to the Second Temple; “and between his shoulders He dwells” refers to the messianic era. Rabbi says: “He shelters him” refers to this world; “all the day” refers to the messianic era; “and between his shoulders He dwells” refers to the World to Come.
The soul of man is the lamp of Hashem, searching all the chambers of the belly.
Only be strong not to eat the blood, for the blood is the life; you shall not eat the life with the flesh.
A wise person’s heart is at his right, and a fool’s heart at his left.

Likewise Metatron pleads the merit of his birds—the spirits that fly within human beings. From the Throne come the neshamot; from this living creature, the ruchot; and from the ofan, the nefashot. These belong to Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah. On Shabbat and festivals, neshamot, ruchot, and nefashot descend upon them by way of Atzilut, the holy spirit from the ten sefirot. Each appointed angel pleads the merit of his birds—the souls that fly within human beings. When Israel fulfill this commandment, each appointed angel pleads the merit of his birds.

If you were to say that “At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps” expresses a leniency—that God will not search Jerusalem by the very bright light of a torch, but by a smaller lamp, so that great sins will be found but small sins will not—come and hear: “The soul of man is the lamp of the Lord, searching all the chambers of the belly.”

We have been taught that it behoves man always to rouse the good prompter against the evil prompter; if the latter departs, well and good, but if not, the man should study the Torah, as there is nothing so well calculated to crush the evil prompter as the Torah; if he departs, well and good, but if not, let the man remind him of the day of death so as thereby to subdue him.

Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: “Master of the universe, You tell us to kindle light before You, yet You are the light of the world, and light dwells with You, as it says, ‘Light dwells with Him.’ Yet You say, ‘Toward the face of the menorah’!” The Holy One, blessed be He, said: “It is not that I need you, but that you should give light for Me as I gave light for you. Why? To exalt you before the nations, so that they will say: See how Israel gives light for the One who illuminates the whole world.” This is like a sighted man and a blind man walking together. The sighted man sa
For the lips of a priest should guard knowledge, and Torah should be sought from his mouth, for he is a messenger of Hashem of hosts.

The purpose of this aggadah is to interpret the section as an allusion to the dedication of the lamps in the Second Temple through Aaron and his sons—that is, the Hasmonean high priest and his sons. I found it in these words in Rabbeinu Nissim’s Megillat Setarim, which cites this aggadah: “I saw in a Midrash: When the twelve tribes brought their offerings and the tribe of Levi did not bring an offering, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: Speak to Aaron and say to him, There is another dedication with the kindling of lamps. Through your descendants I will perform miracles and bring sal

What is Shabbat? If you say it is because of cessation, as it says, “For on it He ceased,” that is correct. But the mystery is this: when this point ascends and the light shines, it is crowned with the Patriarchs. Once crowned with them, it joins and unites with them as one, and all is called Shabbat: shin–bat. Shin, as has been explained, is the mystery of the three Patriarchs, who unite with the only daughter. She is crowned with them, and they with the World to Come; all is one. This is shin–bat: that all should be one.

The tenth commandment: ‘The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat.’ The Shekhinah is called Shabbat from the side of the three upper levels: shin, with three crowns—Keter, Chokhmah and Binah. She is bat, daughter, the fourth with them. The six days, from Chesed through Yesod, are those in which work is done, for building begins with Chesed, as in ‘The world is built through kindness.’ From Binah upward, however, there is rest, delight and cessation from all work.

Rabbi Shimon said: We see that Chochmah encompasses all. Supernal Chesed issues from Chochmah; Gevurah, which is severe judgment, issues from Binah. Jacob brings the two sides to perfection. The Patriarchs encompass all, and Jacob encompasses the Patriarchs.

There is a further mystery in what we learned: the world was created through ten utterances. Upon examination, they are three, through which the world was created: Chochmah, Tevunah, and Daas. The world was created only for Israel. When He wished to establish the world, He made Abraham in the mystery of Chochmah, Isaac in the mystery of Tevunah, and Jacob in the mystery of Daas. Of this it says, “Through knowledge the chambers are filled.” Then the entire world was perfected. When Jacob’s twelve tribes were born, everything was perfected according to the pattern above.

The soul is called by five names: nefesh, ruach, neshamah, yechidah, and chayyah. Nefesh is the blood, as it says, ‘For the blood is the nefesh.’ Ruach ascends and descends, as it says, ‘Who knows whether the spirit of human beings ascends upward?’ Neshamah is one’s disposition, as people say, ‘His disposition is good.’ It is called chayyah because all the limbs are lifeless, while it lives within the body; and yechidah because all the limbs come in pairs, while it is alone within the body.
Command the children of Israel and say to them: My offering, My bread for My fire-offerings, My pleasing fragrance—you shall take care to offer to Me at its appointed time.

It is taught in another baraita with regard to the verse: “And the children of Israel ate the manna forty years” (Exodus 16:35). But did they really eat it for forty years? But didn’t they eat it for forty years less thirty days? The manna began to fall on the sixteenth of Iyyar in the first year in the wilderness, and they stopped eating it on the sixteenth of Nisan in the fortieth year. Rather, this verse comes to tell you that they tasted the taste of manna in the unleavened cakes that they took out from Egypt on the fifteenth of Nisan in their first year, and this sustained them until the

Come and see: When Israel entered and cleaved to the Holy King through the revelation of the holy mark, they then merited to eat another, higher bread, beyond what they had before. At first, when Israel left Egypt, they entered into the bread called matzah. Now they merited to enter and eat another, higher bread, from a higher place, as it is written, “Behold, I shall rain bread upon you from heaven”—from heaven itself. At that time this was available to Israel from that place. The companions who engage in Torah are nourished from another, still higher place. What is it? As it is written, “Wis

The Holy One, blessed be He, said: If I lead them by the direct route, each will now take possession of a field and a vineyard and neglect Torah. Instead, I will lead them through the wilderness; they will eat the manna and drink the water of the well, and Torah will become settled within their bodies.
Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it.
I am Hashem your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slaves. You shall have no other gods before Me.

Rabbi Yehuda says: When Israel heard “I am the Lord your God,” Torah study became fixed in their hearts. They learned without forgetting. They came to Moses and said: Moses our teacher, become an intermediary between us, as it says, “You speak with us, and we shall hear,” and, “Now, why should we die? What benefit is there in our destruction?” They reverted to learning and forgetting. They said: As Moses is flesh and blood and passes away, so his teaching passes away. They immediately returned to Moses, saying: Moses our teacher, would that He reveal Himself to us a second time! “Would that He

You shall speak to the children of Israel, saying: Nevertheless, you shall keep My Shabbatot, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.
Your people are all righteous; they will inherit the land forever—the shoot of My planting, the work of My hands, in which to be glorified.
The colleagues said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: They permitted it in honor of Shabbat… Rabbi Bibi said in Rabbi Chanina’s name: The awe of Shabbat is upon him, and he speaks truth.

ref: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath 17
quote: From the companions: At every Shabbat meal, including the meal after Shabbat, one should say, “These are the meals of perfect faith.” On Shabbat night one arranges twelve loaves upon the table and says, “This is the meal of the Field of Apples, and Zeir Anpin and the Holy Ancient One come to dine with her.” This is Isaac’s meal: he is the master of the meal and directs them. Whoever delights in this meal is saved from the birth pangs of the Messiah. At the morning meal one arranges eight loaves and says, “This is the meal of the Holy Ancient One, and Zeir Anpin and the Holy Field of Apples com
Joseph saw Benjamin with them and said to the one in charge of his house, ‘Bring the men into the house, slaughter an animal, and prepare, for the men will eat with me at noon.’
“The men took … Joseph saw … and prepare.” “Prepare” refers specifically to Shabbat, as it says, “On the sixth day they shall prepare.” This teaches that Joseph observed Shabbat before it was given.
On the sixth day they shall prepare what they bring in, and it will be double what they gather each day.

Caesar said to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya: Why does a Shabbat dish give off such a fragrance? He replied: We have a certain spice called Shabbat; we put it into the food, and its fragrance spreads. Caesar said: Give us some of it. He replied: It is effective for one who observes Shabbat; for one who does not observe Shabbat, it is ineffective.

Rabbi Elazar said in Rabbi Yosei’s name: For the sake of the fastidious, He blessed Shabbat with delicacies. Rabbi prepared a Shabbat meal for Antoninus and brought him cold cooked dishes; he ate and enjoyed them. On a weekday Rabbi prepared another meal and brought hot dishes. Antoninus said: Those pleased me more than these. Rabbi replied: These lack a certain spice. Antoninus asked: Is the king’s storehouse lacking anything? Rabbi replied: They lack Shabbat. Do you have Shabbat?

“They gathered a double portion of bread”: When they measured what they had gathered in their tents, they found it doubled—two omers for each person. An aggadic interpretation reads lechem mishneh as bread that was changed: on that day it changed for the better in fragrance and taste.
On the sixth day they gathered a double portion of bread, two omers for each person. All the leaders of the congregation came and told Moses.

Why did the princes bring offerings in this form? The Rabbis said: Although they all brought the same offering, they offered it in reference to great matters, and each offered according to his own understanding. Nachshon began and offered in reference to kingship, as his father had appointed him king over his brothers: “Judah, your brothers shall praise you”; “Judah is a lion’s cub”; and, “Judah prevailed among his brothers, and from him came the ruler.” The sages and great men of Judah’s tribe held a tradition from our father Jacob of everything destined to happen to each tribe until the days
The likeness of their faces was a human face; the four had the face of a lion on the right, the four had the face of an ox on the left, and the four had the face of an eagle.

How do we know that the showbread is from the King’s table? For it is written, “He spoke to me: This is the table that is before the Lord.” Zeh—“this”—signifies twelve faces. Likewise, whoever has the means should prepare and arrange four loaves upon his table at each Shabbat meal, making twelve faces for the three meals.

The Faithful Shepherd arose and said: Aaron the priest, rise from your sleep to slaughter bulls, sheep, lambs, birds, and all the kinds needed for the King’s meal. The showbread corresponds to the two tablets of Torah, of which it says, “They were written on this side and on that.” Zeh—“this”—signifies twelve faces: “The Lord bless you,” “The Lord shine upon you,” “The Lord lift His face toward you.” The second zeh is Adonai, Adonai, Adonai: twelve living creatures, of whom it is said, “The face of a lion on the right for all four, the face of an ox on the left for all four, and the face of an
From within it came the likeness of four living creatures. This was their appearance: they had a human likeness.

“They had a human likeness”: This is puzzling, for they also had the likeness of an ox, a lion, and an eagle. It appears to me that because this is the primary form of them all, the prophet praised the Chariot by it. It is the likeness of the face of our father Jacob.
He sent portions to them from before him, and Benjamin’s portion was five times as large as any of theirs. They drank and became intoxicated with him.
Its libation shall be a quarter of a hin for each lamb; in the holy place pour out a libation of strong drink to Hashem.

Reish Lakish said: When wine is poured upon the altar, they plug the drains, to fulfill “In the holy place pour a libation of strong drink to the Lord.” How does this imply that? Rav Pappa said: Shekhar denotes drinking, satiety, and intoxication. Rav Pappa said: Learn from this that when a person is satisfied with wine, his satisfaction comes through his throat. Rava said: A young Torah scholar who has little wine should swallow it in large draughts. Rava himself would swallow the cup of blessing in large draughts.

The heavens and the earth and all their host were completed. On the seventh day God completed His work that He had made, and on the seventh day He rested from all His work that He had made. God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, for on it He rested from all His work that God had created to do.
For I said: A world shall be built through kindness; in the heavens You establish Your faithfulness.
These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created, on the day that Hashem God made earth and heavens.
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said: Behibare’am, ‘when they were created,’ may be read be’Avraham, ‘through Abraham’: they were created in Abraham’s merit.

“The Lord said to Abram: Go forth from your land.” Rabbi Yitzchak began: “Listen, daughter, see, and incline your ear; forget your people and your father’s house.” Rabbi Yitzchak said: This is like someone traveling from place to place who saw a burning palace. He said, “Could this palace be without a master?” The owner of the palace looked out at him and said, “I am the owner of the palace.” So our father Abraham said, “Could this world be without a master?” The Holy One, blessed be He, looked out at him and said, “I am the Master of the world.” “The king will desire your beauty, for he is yo

When the Holy One, blessed be He, told Moses to make a Mishkan, Moses immediately said to Israel, “They shall take an offering for Me.” As Moses worked on the Mishkan, Israel’s scoffers said, “Could the Shekhinah dwell through the son of Amram?” Rabbi Yochanan said: He was occupied with the Mishkan for six months: they made it for three months and kept it folded for three months. Even so, they mocked him: “It has been made! Did Moses not say that God would cause His Shekhinah to dwell among us?” But the Holy One, blessed be He, intended to erect the Mishkan in the month in which our father Isa
On the third day Abraham raised his eyes and saw the place from afar.
God said to Abraham, ‘Do not let it be evil in your eyes concerning the boy and your maidservant. Whatever Sarah says to you, listen to her voice, for in Isaac shall offspring be called yours.’
Isaac went out to meditate in the field toward evening. He raised his eyes and saw, and behold, camels were coming.
Come, my beloved, let us go out to the field; let us lodge in the villages.

Rather, not like Abraham, of whom “mountain” is written, as it says, “As it is said today: On Hashem’s mountain He will be seen”; and not like Isaac, of whom “field” is written, as it says, “Isaac went out to converse in the field”; but like Jacob, who called it a “house,” as it says, “He called the name of that place Bethel.”
A truthful lip will endure forever, but a lying tongue only for a moment.
The Jews had light, gladness, joy, and honor.

“The Jews had light, joy, gladness, and honor.” Rav Yehuda said: “Light” means Torah, as it says, “For a commandment is a lamp, and Torah is light.” “Joy” means a festival, as it says, “You shall rejoice on your festival.” “Gladness” means circumcision, as it says, “I rejoice over Your word.” “Honor” means tefillin, as it says, “All the peoples of the earth will see that the name of Hashem is proclaimed upon you, and they will fear you.” Rabbi Eliezer the Great teaches that this refers to the tefillin worn on the head.

“They stood at the foot of the mountain.” Rav Avdimi bar Hama bar Hasa said: This teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, held the mountain over them like a vat and said: If you accept the Torah, well and good; if not, there will be your burial. Rav Aha bar Yaakov said: From here there is a weighty declaration of coercion regarding Torah. Rava said: Nevertheless, they accepted it again in the days of Ahasuerus, for it says, “The Jews established and accepted”: They established what they had already accepted.

Until this point the prophets prophesied through the holy spirit. From this point onward, “Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise,” as it says, “For it is pleasant if you keep them within you,” and, “That your trust may be in the Lord”; also, “Have I not written for you thirty teachings,” and, “To make known to you the truth.” Likewise it says, “Ask your father and he will tell you; your elders, and they will say to you.” Could this mean ordinary elders in the marketplace? Scripture says, “They will say to you.” You thus learn that an elder is one who has acquired wisdom.
Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise, and set your heart upon my knowledge.

Rav Shmuel bar Inya said: What is the meaning of “I will take pleasure in it and be glorified”? The word is written without a heh but read with a heh. Why is the heh missing? It signifies the five things that distinguished the First Temple from the Second: the Ark, its cover and cherubs; the heavenly fire; the Shekhinah; the holy spirit; and the Urim and Tummim. The sages answered: The heavenly fire did exist in the Second Temple, but it did not assist in consuming the offerings.
We learned there: “One who makes use of the crown passes away.” Reish Lakish taught: This means one who makes use of someone who studies halakhot, the crown of Torah.
For the lips of a priest should guard knowledge, and Torah should be sought from his mouth, for he is a messenger of Hashem of hosts.
Your people are all righteous; they will inherit the land forever—the shoot of My planting, the work of My hands, in which to be glorified.
“They were involved in that miracle”: The Greeks decreed that all virgins who were to marry must first submit to intercourse with the governor, and the miracle was brought about through a woman.

He implanted defilement in her. For Rabbi Yochanan said: When the serpent came upon Eve, he implanted defilement in her. Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, had their defilement cease; the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai, did not have their defilement cease.
Therefore say: Behold, I give him My covenant of peace.
He said of his father and mother, ‘I have not seen him’; he did not recognize his brothers and did not know his children, for they guarded Your word and kept Your covenant.
My covenant with him was life and peace; I gave them to him for reverence, and he feared Me and stood in awe before My name.
He sent portions to them from before him, and Benjamin’s portion was five times as large as any of theirs. They drank and became intoxicated with him.
“The men took … Joseph saw … and prepare.” “Prepare” refers specifically to Shabbat, as it says, “On the sixth day they shall prepare.” This teaches that Joseph observed Shabbat before it was given.

Rabbah bar bar Chanah said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: They taught this only regarding Shabbat and festivals, since a person establishes his meal around wine. On other days of the year, however, he recites a blessing over each cup. It was also stated: Rabbah bar Mari said in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s name: They taught this only regarding Shabbat and festivals, when a person comes from the bathhouse, and after bloodletting, since a person establishes his meal around wine on these occasions. On other days of the year, he recites a blessing over each cup.
It is not for kings, Lemuel, not for kings to drink wine, nor for princes to seek strong drink.

“It is not for kings, Lemuel; it is not for kings to drink wine.” His mother said to him: What have you to do with kings who drink wine, become drunk, and say, “Why do we need God?” “Nor for rulers, strong drink”: Should one to whom all the world’s mysteries are revealed drink wine and become drunk? Some say: Should one at whose door all the world’s rulers rise early to wait drink wine and become drunk?
Rava said: A person is obligated to become intoxicated on Purim until he cannot distinguish between “Cursed is Haman” and “Blessed is Mordechai.”
He saw Amalek, took up his parable, and said: Amalek is the first of the nations, but its end is utter destruction.
Hashem will be King over all the earth. On that day Hashem will be one and His name one.

'In the beginning God created': this verse calls out for interpretation, as our sages expounded: for the sake of Torah, which is called 'the beginning of His way,' and for the sake of Israel, who are called 'the beginning of His produce.'
Pharaoh said to Joseph, ‘Since God has made all this known to you, there is none as discerning and wise as you.’

“All the land of Egypt grew hungry”—“Whatever he tells you, do.” Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: He compelled them to circumcise themselves. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said: It does not say chiyyitanu, but hecheyitanu—“You have kept us alive”: You have given us life in this world and life in the World to Come.

Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: Had Israel observed the first Shabbat, no nation or tongue would have ruled over them, for it says, “On the seventh day some of the people went out to gather,” and afterward, “Amalek came.” Rabbi Yochanan said in Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s name: If Israel would observe two Shabbatot according to their laws, they would immediately be redeemed, as it says, “Thus says the Lord to the eunuchs who observe My Shabbatot,” followed by, “I will bring them to My holy mountain.”
They said to one another, ‘Indeed, we are guilty concerning our brother, for we saw the distress of his soul when he pleaded with us, and we did not listen. Therefore this distress has come upon us.’
Joseph could not restrain himself before all those standing by him, and he cried, ‘Send everyone out from before me!’ No one stood with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.

The correct explanation in my view is that many members of Pharaoh’s household and other Egyptians were present and implored him to forgive Benjamin, because their compassion had been stirred by Judah’s pleas. Joseph could not hold firm against them all, and he called to his servants, “Remove every outsider from me, for I will speak with them.” They went out, and as they left he raised his voice in weeping. The Egyptians and the members of Pharaoh’s household who had just gone out heard him, for they were still in the outer courtyard.
Sing and rejoice, daughter of Zion, for behold, I am coming and will dwell in your midst, declares Hashem.

What, then, is meant by “Those passing through the valley of weeping”? It concerns those who are at that time liable to Gehinnom. Abraham comes, raises them out, and receives them—except an Israelite who had relations with a gentile woman: his foreskin extends, and Abraham does not recognize him.

After praying, Rabbi Alexandri would say: “Master of the worlds, it is revealed and known before You that we desire to do Your will. What prevents us? The leaven within the dough and subjection to foreign kingdoms. May it be Your will to rescue us from their power, so that we may return to fulfill the statutes of Your will with a whole heart.”
The goat shall bear upon itself all their iniquities to a cut-off land, and he shall send the goat into the wilderness.

‘The goat shall bear upon itself’ refers to Esau, as it says, ‘Esau my brother is a hairy man.’ ‘All their iniquities,’ avonotam, can be read as ‘the iniquities of the blameless man,’ avonot tam, as it says, ‘Jacob was a blameless man.’
His soul clung to Dinah, Jacob’s daughter. He loved the young woman and spoke to her heart.

“They took Dinah”: Rabbi Yudan said, They dragged her out. Rav Huna said: A woman who has had relations with an uncircumcised man finds it difficult to separate. Rav Huna said: She said, “Where shall I carry my shame?” until Shimon swore that he would take her. This is what is written, “Shaul, son of the Canaanite woman”—the son of Dinah, who had been violated by a Canaanite. Rabbi Yehudah said: He acted as the Canaanites act. Rabbi Nechemyah said: She had been violated by a Hivite, who is included among the Canaanites. The Rabbis said: Shimon took her and buried her in the land of Canaan.
Joshua had sons who took wives unfit for the priesthood, and he was standing before the angel.

Why was Joshua the High Priest punished? Rav Pappa said: His sons married women unfit for the priesthood, and he did not protest. For it says, “Joshua was wearing filthy garments.” Was it Joshua’s habit to wear filthy garments? Rather, this teaches that his sons married women unfit for the priesthood, and he did not protest.

Joshua was clothed in filthy garments and stood before the angel. He answered and said to those standing before him, ‘Remove the filthy garments from him.’ He said to him, ‘See, I have removed your iniquity from you, and I will clothe you in fine robes.’ I said, ‘Let them place a pure turban upon his head.’ They placed the pure turban upon his head and clothed him in garments, while the angel of Hashem stood by.
Sudara—the scholar’s head covering—alludes to “The secret of the Lord is for those who fear Him.”
The secret of Hashem is for those who fear Him, and His covenant is to make it known to them.

He said to me, ‘What do you see?’ I said, ‘I see a menorah entirely of gold, with its bowl on top, its seven lamps upon it, and seven and seven channels for the lamps on its top. Beside it are two olive trees, one to the right of the bowl and one to its left.’
The one who breaks through goes up before them. They break through, pass through the gate, and go out by it. Their king passes before them, and Hashem is at their head.

Another interpretation: “A bowl is upon its head”—“Their king will pass before them, and the Lord at their head.” “Its seven lamps upon it” signifies the merit of Shabbat, which Israel observe once in seven days. “Seven and seven channels”: seven correspond to the seven days of creation—“She has hewn her seven pillars”—and seven correspond to the seven fathers: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Kehat, Amram, Moses, and Aaron.
He answered and said to me: ‘This is the word of Hashem to Zerubbabel: Not by might and not by power, but by My spirit, says Hashem of hosts.’

A king is not saved by a great army; a mighty warrior is not rescued by great strength. The horse is a false hope for salvation; with all its power it cannot deliver. Behold, the eye of Hashem is upon those who fear Him, upon those who hope for His kindness.

Rabbi Levi bar Chiya said: One who leaves the synagogue, enters the study hall, and occupies himself with Torah merits receiving the Shekhinah, as it says, “They go from strength to strength; each appears before God in Zion.” Rabbi Chiya bar Ashi said in Rav’s name: Torah scholars have no rest, either in this world or in the World to Come, as it says, “They go from strength to strength; each appears before God in Zion.”

Rav Huna and Rav Chisda were sitting when Geneiva passed by. One said to the other, “Let us stand before him, for he is a Torah scholar.” The other answered, “Shall we stand before a contentious person?” Meanwhile Geneiva approached and said, “Peace to you, kings; peace to you, kings!” They asked, “How do you know that the sages are called kings?” He answered, “For it is written, ‘Through me kings reign.’”
Through me kings reign, and rulers decree justice.

We have been taught that it behoves man always to rouse the good prompter against the evil prompter; if the latter departs, well and good, but if not, the man should study the Torah, as there is nothing so well calculated to crush the evil prompter as the Torah; if he departs, well and good, but if not, let the man remind him of the day of death so as thereby to subdue him.

Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: A person’s inclination grows stronger against him every day and seeks to kill him, as it says, “The wicked watches the righteous and seeks to kill him.” If the Holy One, blessed be He, did not help him, he could not overcome it, as it says, “The Lord will not abandon him into its hand, nor condemn him when he is judged.”

You too: If you marvel at the reward I paid that wicked man for four steps he ran in pursuit of My honor, how much more so when I pay the reward of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who ran before Me like horses! This is the meaning of “Concerning the prophets, my heart is broken within me, all my bones tremble; I have become like a drunken man, like a man overcome by wine, because of Hashem and because of His holy words.”
For wisdom provides shelter, as money provides shelter; but the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom gives life to those who possess it.

Abaye heard a man say to a woman, “Let us rise early and travel together.” He said, “I will go and keep them from transgression.” He followed them three parasangs through a marsh. When they parted, he heard them say, “The road was long, and our company pleasant.” Abaye said, “If it had been someone I hate”—meaning himself—“he could not have restrained himself.” He went and leaned against a doorpost, distressed. An elder came and taught him: Whoever is greater than another has a greater evil inclination.

Thus says Hashem: Let the wise person not boast of his wisdom; let the mighty not boast of his might; let the wealthy not boast of his wealth. Rather, let one who boasts boast of this: understanding and knowing Me, that I am Hashem, who acts with kindness, justice, and righteousness on the earth, for in these I delight, declares Hashem.
For wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will be pleasant to your soul.
Who are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you shall become a plain. He will bring forth the top stone amid cries of ‘Grace, grace to it!’

R. Judah expounded: In the future, the Holy One, blessed be He, will bring the evil inclination and slaughter it before the righteous and the wicked. To the righteous it appears like a high mountain, and to the wicked like a strand of hair. Both groups weep. The righteous weep and say, “How were we able to conquer such a high mountain?” The wicked weep and say, “How were we unable to conquer this strand of hair?” The Holy One, blessed be He, also marvels with them, as it says, “Thus says Hashem of Hosts: Though it is wondrous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, it will als

Rabbi Chiya saw the moon still visible on the morning of the twenty-ninth. He took a clod of earth, threw it toward it, and said, “We need to sanctify you this evening, and you are still here? Go and conceal yourself!” Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi said to Rabbi Chiya: “Go to Ein Tav, sanctify the month, and send me the signal: David, king of Israel, lives and endures.”

The descendants of Nachshon wished to establish one pillar, but that Edomite would not allow them. The members of the assembly nevertheless gathered and established a pillar in the month in which Aaron the priest died. They could calculate it, but they did not disclose it. How does “pillar” signify a month? For it is written, “Solomon had twelve officers over all Israel, who sustained the king and his household, each for one month of the year.” But it is also written, “One officer was in the land.” Rav Yehudah and Rav Nachman disagreed: One said that one officer was appointed over all of them;

He asked them, “Why, when I declare something impure, do you declare it pure, and when I forbid it, do you permit it?” They answered, “Because you intercalate years and establish months outside the Land of Israel.” He said, “Did not Akiva son of Joseph intercalate years and establish months outside the Land?” They answered, “Leave Rabbi Akiva aside: he had left no one like himself in the Land of Israel.” He said, “I too left no one like myself there.” They answered, “The kids you left have become horned goats. They sent us to you with this message: If he listens, well and good; if not, let him
Israel is holy to Hashem, the first of His produce. All who devour him incur guilt; evil will come upon them, declares Hashem.

Rabbi Avun said: “I call to God Most High, to God who fulfills on my behalf.” If a girl is three years and one day old and the court decides to intercalate the year, her signs of virginity return; if not, they do not return.
This month shall be for you the head of the months; it is the first for you of the months of the year.
The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes, leaping over the mountains, bounding over the hills.

Rabbi Yehudah says: “The voice of my beloved! Here he comes”—this is Moses. When he told Israel, “You are being redeemed this month,” they said: Moses our teacher, how can we be redeemed? Did the Holy One, blessed be He, not tell Abraham, “They shall enslave and afflict them for four hundred years,” yet we have only two hundred and ten? He replied: Since He desires your redemption, He does not look at your calculations, but “leaps over the mountains.” The mountains and hills here signify appointed times and added periods: He leaps over calculations, appointed times, and added periods. You are

Rabbi Alexandri said: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi raised a contradiction. It is written, “In its time,” and it is written, “I will hasten it.” If they merit, “I will hasten it”; if they do not merit, “in its time.”
The small one will become a thousand, and the young one a mighty nation. I, Hashem, will hasten it in its time.
The peoples heard and trembled; anguish seized the inhabitants of Philistia.

For we heard how Hashem dried up the waters of the Sea of Reeds before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two Amorite kings across the Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom you utterly destroyed.

Or has a god ever attempted to come and take for himself a nation from the midst of another nation, through trials, signs, wonders, war, a mighty hand, an outstretched arm, and great terrors, like all that Hashem your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?

When Israel reached the sea and the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to split the Sea of Reeds for them, Rahab, the appointed ruler of Egypt, came and demanded judgment before Him. He said: “Master of the world, why do You wish to judge Egypt and split the sea for Israel? They are all guilty before You, and all Your ways are justice and truth. These worship stars and constellations, and so do those; these practice sexual transgression, and so do those; these shed blood, and so do those.” At that hour it was difficult before Him to set aside the course of judgment. Israel were traveling toward t

The Rabbis taught: A man’s wife died, leaving a nursing child, and he could not afford a wet nurse. A miracle was performed for him: his breasts opened like a woman’s, and he nursed his son. Rav Yosef said, “See how great this man is, that such a miracle was performed for him!” Abaye answered, “On the contrary, see how deficient this man is, that the order of creation was changed for him.” Rav Yehudah said: See how difficult a person’s sustenance is, that the order of creation was changed for him. Rav Nachman said: Know that this is so, for a miracle occurred, yet sustenance was not created.

Rabbi Yannai would examine the ferry before crossing. He acted according to his teaching: A person should never stand in a dangerous place saying that a miracle will be performed for him, for perhaps no miracle will be performed. Even if a miracle is performed, his merits are diminished. Rabbi Chanin said: What verse teaches this? “I have become small through all the kindnesses and all the truth that You have shown Your servant.”

Rav Mari, son of Shmuel’s daughter, said: I was standing on the bank of the Pappa River and saw angels appearing as sailors. They brought sand, filled boats with it, and it became fine flour. Everyone came to buy it. I said to them: “Do not buy this, for it is the product of miracles. Tomorrow boats of wheat will arrive from Parzina.”

There were four kings, and what one requested another did not: David, Asa, Jehoshaphat, and Hezekiah. David said, “I will pursue my enemies and overtake them.” The Holy One, blessed be He, answered, “I will do so,” as it says, “David struck them from twilight until the evening of the following day.” … Asa arose and said, “I have no strength to kill them; I will pursue, and You act.” He answered, “I will act,” as it says, “Asa pursued them, for they were broken before the Lord and before His camp.” It does not say “before Asa,” but “before the Lord and before His camp.” Jehoshaphat arose and sa

What is a conspiracy of the wicked? Shevna taught thirteen myriads, while Hezekiah taught eleven myriads. When Sennacherib came and besieged Jerusalem, Shevna wrote a note and shot it out on an arrow: “Shevna and his followers have made peace; Hezekiah and his followers have not,” as it says, “Behold, the wicked bend the bow; they prepare their arrow upon the string.” Hezekiah feared: “Perhaps, Heaven forbid, the Holy One, blessed be He, will follow the majority; since the majority surrender, we too will be surrendered.” A prophet came and told him, “Do not call a conspiracy everything this pe
On that night the king’s sleep was disturbed. He ordered the book of remembrances, the chronicles, to be brought, and they were read before the king.
He said to me, ‘What do you see?’ I said, ‘I see a menorah entirely of gold, with its bowl on top, its seven lamps upon it, and seven and seven channels for the lamps on its top.’
From the north comes gold; awesome majesty surrounds God.
Place the table outside the curtain, and the menorah opposite the table on the southern side of the Tabernacle; place the table on the northern side.
The faithfulness of your times will be a store of salvations, wisdom, and knowledge; fear of Hashem is his treasure.

David said: “Fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever.” What does this mean? A person may study Midrash, halakhot, and aggadot, yet if he lacks fear of sin, he possesses nothing. This is like a man who says to his friend, “I have a thousand measures of grain, a thousand of oil, and a thousand of wine.” His friend asks, “Do you have storehouses in which to put them? If so, everything is yours; if not, you have nothing.” So a person studies everything, and they tell him: If you have fear of sin, everything is yours, as it says, “The faithfulness of your times…fear of the Lord is His treasure.”
“Joab sent to Tekoa and brought a wise woman from there.” Why specifically Tekoa? Rabbi Yochanan said: Because they regularly use olive oil, wisdom is common among them.
Grace is false and beauty is vain; a woman who fears Hashem is to be praised.

All blessings above and below depend upon the seventh day. Why was no manna found on the seventh day? Because all six supernal days are blessed from that day, and each gives its sustenance below on its own day from the blessing received on the seventh day. Therefore one who abides in faith must arrange his table and prepare a meal on Shabbat night, so that his table may be blessed throughout the six days. At that time blessing is available for all six weekdays, and blessing does not rest upon an empty table. Therefore one must arrange his Shabbat-night table with bread and food.
Beside it are two olive trees, one to the right of the bowl and one to its left.

Happy is the man who has not walked in the counsel of the wicked, stood in the way of sinners, or sat in the company of scoffers. Rather, his delight is in the Torah of Hashem, and in his Torah he meditates day and night.

Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi expounded: “Happy is the man who has not walked”—to the theaters and circuses of the nations; “nor stood in the path of sinners”—who has not stood at their hunting spectacles; “nor sat in the company of scoffers”—who has not sat among their schemes. Lest someone say, “Since I have not gone to theaters or circuses and have not stood at their spectacles, I shall go and indulge in sleep,” Scripture says, “He shall meditate upon His Torah day and night.”
I am Hashem your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slaves.
He said, ‘These are the two sons of oil who stand by the Lord of all the earth.’
“The two sons of oil”: the eminence of priesthood and kingship, whose holders are anointed with the anointing oil.

The teli in the world is like a king on his throne; the wheel in the year, like a king in his province; the heart in the soul, like a king at war. God made everything one opposite the other: good opposite evil, good from good and evil from evil. Good distinguishes evil, and evil distinguishes good. Good is reserved for the good, and evil for the evil.
For the lips of a priest should guard knowledge, and Torah should be sought from his mouth, for he is a messenger of Hashem of hosts.
He said, ‘These are the two sons of oil who stand by the Lord of all the earth.’

Rabbi Oshaya said: What is the meaning of “I took two staffs, naming one Pleasantness and the other Wounders”? “Pleasantness” refers to Torah scholars in the Land of Israel, who treat one another pleasantly in halakhic discussion; “Wounders” refers to scholars in Babylonia, who wound one another in halakhic discussion. “He said to me, These are the two sons of oil…two olive trees upon it.” Rabbi Yitzchak said: “Oil” refers to the scholars of the Land of Israel, who are agreeable to one another in halakhah like olive oil; “two olive trees” refers to the scholars of Babylonia, who are bitter tow

If a matter of judgment is too difficult for you—between blood and blood, between claim and claim, between affliction and affliction, matters of dispute within your gates—you shall arise and go up to the place that Hashem your God will choose. You shall come to the priests, the Levites, and to the judge who will be in those days; inquire, and they will tell you the matter of judgment. You shall act according to the word they tell you from that place which Hashem will choose, taking care to do all that they instruct you. According to the Torah they teach you and the judgment they tell you, you

What is meant by “With enemies at the gate”? Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba said: Even a father and son, a teacher and student, who study Torah at one gate become enemies to one another. Yet they do not leave there until they become loving friends, as it says, “Vahev in Supha”: Read the phrase as “Love at its end.”
Therefore it is said in the Book of the Wars of Hashem: ‘Vahev in Suphah, and the streams of Arnon.’
The words of the wise are like goads, and like firmly planted nails are the masters of assemblies; they were given by one Shepherd.

“Masters of assemblies” are Torah scholars who sit in groups and occupy themselves with Torah: some declare impure and some declare pure, some forbid and some permit, some disqualify and some validate. A person might say, “How, then, can I study Torah?” Scripture says, “They were all given by one Shepherd.” One God gave them; one leader proclaimed them, from the mouth of the Master of all deeds, blessed be He, as it says, “God spoke all these words.”

Rabbi Abba said that Shmuel said: For three years Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel disagreed. These said: The halakha is in accordance with our opinion, and these said: The halakha is in accordance with our opinion. Ultimately, a Divine Voice emerged and proclaimed: Both these and those are the words of the living God. However, the halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Beit Hillel.
If one person can be overpowered, two can stand against the attacker; a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
A truthful lip will endure forever, but a lying tongue only for a moment.
For Hashem’s portion is His people; Jacob is the cord of His inheritance.

Rabbi Salmoni said in Reish Lakish’s name: He showed Jacob a Throne of Glory with three legs. Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin said in Rabbi Levi’s name: You are the third leg. This accords with Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin’s statement in Rabbi Levi’s name: “For the Lord’s portion is His people; Jacob is the cord of His inheritance.” Just as a cord is not woven with fewer than three strands, so the Patriarchs are no fewer than three.

What is “heaven”? This is the mystery of the Patriarchs; and the mystery of the Patriarchs is Jacob, who encompasses them all. For Jacob is the glory of the Patriarchs, and he stands to illuminate the world.
You will give truth to Jacob and kindness to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from days of old.

Could the first tithe also cease in the third year? Scripture says, “Speak to the Levites and say to them: When you take from the children of Israel the tithe that I have given you from them as your inheritance.” Scripture compares it to an inheritance: Just as an inheritance has no interruption, so the first tithe has no interruption.

Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says: Whoever has tefillin on his head and arm, tzitzit on his garment, and a mezuzah at his doorway is strengthened against sin, as it says, “A threefold cord is not quickly broken,” and, “The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear Him and rescues them.”

What is Shabbat? If you say it is because of cessation, as it says, “For on it He ceased,” that is correct. But the mystery is this: when this point ascends and the light shines, it is crowned with the Patriarchs. Once crowned with them, it joins and unites with them as one, and all is called Shabbat: shin–bat. Shin, as has been explained, is the mystery of the three Patriarchs, who unite with the only daughter. She is crowned with them, and they with the World to Come; all is one. This is shin–bat: that all should be one.

There are three prayers on Shabbat, and the fourth is Musaf. The evening prayer is “You sanctified”: this is the lower Shekhinah, which belongs to the left side, where the Levites are, of whom it is said, “You shall sanctify the Levites.” The morning prayer is “Moses rejoices in the gift of his portion”: this is “The soul of every living being,” the supernal Mother, of whom it is said, “If you lie among the sheepfolds”—read not im, “if,” but em, “Mother.” Of her it is said, “He lay down in that place”: she lies in the place of the twenty-two letters of Torah. Fortunate is the mouth of Torah in
But as for me, my prayer is to You, Hashem, at a time of favor. God, in the abundance of Your kindness, answer me with the truth of Your salvation.
Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Sunshine on Shabbat is charity for the poor, as it says, “For you who fear My name, a sun of charity will rise, with healing.”
He said, “Do not stretch out your hand against the boy, and do not do anything to him, for now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only one, from Me.”

Had the God of my father—the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac—not been with me, you would now have sent me away empty-handed. God saw my affliction and the toil of my hands, and He gave judgment last night.

Rabbi Yehudah said: Whenever the engravings of the supernal King are properly ordered in their places, all the worlds rejoice, and all deeds are established in their enduring order, as it says, “The work of the Lord, for it is awesome.” What does “awesome” mean? Rabbi Elazar said: The perfection of all, as it says, “The great, mighty, and awesome God.” What is “awesome”? This is Jacob, of whom it says, “Jacob was a tam man”—as the Targum renders it, a complete man, complete in everything. Likewise, all the deeds of the Holy One, blessed be He, are perfect, with complete and enduring perfection
When he sees his children, the work of My hands, in his midst, they will sanctify My name; they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob and stand in awe of the God of Israel.

You shall speak to the children of Israel, saying: Nevertheless, you shall keep My Shabbatot, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.
This month shall be for you the head of the months; it is the first for you of the months of the year.

Rabbah bar Shmuel taught: Might one think that just as a year is intercalated when necessary, a month is likewise extended when necessary? Scripture says, “This month shall be for you”—see it like this and sanctify it. Rava said: There is no difficulty. One case concerns extending the month, the other sanctifying it. The teaching means: Might one think that just as a year and a month are extended when necessary, the month may also be sanctified early when necessary? Scripture says, “This month shall be for you”—see it like this and sanctify it.

The head of the court says, “Sanctified,” and all the people respond, “Sanctified, sanctified.” Whether the new moon was seen at its proper time or later, they sanctify the month. Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok says: If it was not seen at its proper time, they do not sanctify it, because Heaven has already sanctified it. The Gemara asks: From where is the head of the court’s declaration derived? Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda said in Rabbi Yose ben Shaul’s name, in Rabbi’s name: Scripture says, “Moses declared the appointed times of the Lord”; this teaches that the head of the court says, “Sanctifie

Rabbi Shimon said: It is written, “From new moon to new moon and from Shabbat to Shabbat.” Why are these equated? They all ascend to one level, and one unites with the other. Their joy in one another is found only when the Holy Ancient One is revealed; then there is joy for all. We learned: “A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day”—for the Shabbat day itself; it is praise with which the Holy One, blessed be He, is praised. Then joy is found and an additional soul is granted, for the Ancient One is revealed and union is prepared. So too, when the moon is renewed: the sun illuminates her with the jo
Hashem is God, and He has given us light. Bind the festival offering with cords, to the horns of the altar.
The middle bar, within the boards, shall pass through from end to end.

Rabbi Shimon said: “The middle bar within the boards, passing from end to end”—this is holy, perfect Jacob, as we have explained from “Jacob was a complete man, dwelling in tents.” It does not say “dwelling in a tent,” but “in tents”: two, for he grasps this one and that one. So here, “The middle bar within the boards, passing from end to end,” grasps both. We learned: What is “a complete man”? As the Targum renders it, whole—whole in everything, whole on both sides, with the Holy Ancient One and with Zeir Anpin; whole with supernal Chesed and supernal Gevurah, bringing both to perfection.

Bereshit bara: “house” and “head”—these are Father and Mother. Bara, in Aramaic, means “son”: this is the middle pillar, of which it is said, “A river issues from Eden.” There is Eden and there is Eden, as it says, “You give them drink from the river of Your Edens”—“Your Edens,” indeed. There is the supernal Eden, the supernal Keter; the lower Eden is yud; and there is a further lower Eden, the supernal Mother, who is dalet. She is Eden in relation to the river beneath her, as it says, “A river issues from Eden to water the garden.”
A river goes out from Eden to water the garden; from there it divides and becomes four heads.

What is written? “Joseph gathered all the money.” This is fitting, for that river which flows forth gathers everything, and all wealth abides in it. This is the mystery of “God placed them in the firmament of heaven.” Everything is as it should be: certainly Joseph must rule over the kingdom.

As soon as Israel, the holy people alone, leave exile, the river that had been parched and dry will immediately be described as “a river issues from Eden”—this is vav—“to water the garden.” “A river” is the middle pillar; “issues from Eden” refers to the supernal Mother; “to water the garden” refers to the lower Shekhinah.
We are all sons of one man; we are honest. Your servants have never been spies.
They said, “Your servants are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan. Behold, the youngest is with our father today, and the one is no more.”

What is written? “We are all sons of one man”—nachnu. It should have said anachnu. Why is the alef missing? Because the mystery of the covenant was not present with them, the alef departed from there, for alef is masculine. Bet is feminine, and alef masculine. Thus the alef departed, and they remained feminine in relation to the Shekhinah. Afterward they said, “We are honest”—anachnu—with the alef added. They spoke without knowing what they were saying: because Joseph was present there, they completed the word and said anachnu. How do we know? It is written, “Your servants are twelve brothers,

All the miracles and mighty deeds performed for Israel, when the radiance of the Holy Ancient One shines in His crowns, are engraved and inscribed in az, in the alef.… When the light of the alef joins and reaches the zayin—what is zayin? “The Lord has a sword, filled with blood”—then He performs miracles and mighty deeds, because alef is joined with zayin. This is song, song from every side; this is “Then Moses sang.”

Come and see: corresponding to those seven righteous ones, the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded in the Torah that an additional offering be brought on seven occasions during the year, to add delights and pleasures for them from the King’s house, so that the fathers be satisfied first and then the children. These are seven occasions and no more. On Shabbat, it corresponds to the righteous one, foundation of the world, who is called “All” and is called Shabbat, to add delights for him from the concealed mind. On Rosh Chodesh, it corresponds to the Congregation of Israel, which is called the mo

ref: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath 17
quote: From the companions: At every Shabbat meal, including the meal after Shabbat, one should say, “These are the meals of perfect faith.” On Shabbat night one arranges twelve loaves upon the table and says, “This is the meal of the Field of Apples, and Zeir Anpin and the Holy Ancient One come to dine with her.” This is Isaac’s meal: he is the master of the meal and directs them. Whoever delights in this meal is saved from the birth pangs of the Messiah. At the morning meal one arranges eight loaves and says, “This is the meal of the Holy Ancient One, and Zeir Anpin and the Holy Field of Apples com
Jacob slaughtered an offering on the mountain and called his kinsmen to eat bread. They ate bread and spent the night on the mountain.

Come and see: all Jacob’s deeds were for the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He. Therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, was always with him, and the Shekhinah never departed from him. When Isaac called his son Esau, Jacob was not there; the Shekhinah informed Rebecca, and Rebecca informed Jacob.
Jacob went on his way, and angels of God met him.
“Angels of God encountered him”: Angels of the Land of Israel came to meet him and escort him into the Land.

Why must tefillin and mezuzot be written in their original language? Because it is written concerning them, “They shall be”—they shall remain as they are. But what case of “Aramaic written in Hebrew” can there be? In the Torah, admittedly, there is yegar sahaduta; but here, in tefillin and mezuzot, what Aramaic is there?
Laban called it Yegar-sahadutha, and Jacob called it Gal-ed.

Rabbi Yosei says: The Persian kingdom lasted thirty-four years while the Temple stood; the Greek kingdom, one hundred and eighty; the kingdom of the Hasmonean house, one hundred and three; and the kingdom of Herod, one hundred and three. From then onward, count from the Temple’s destruction. In the diaspora they write the Greek era in documents.

I saw, and behold, a storm wind was coming from the north, a great cloud and flashing fire, with radiance surrounding it; and from its midst, from the midst of the fire, came something like the appearance of chashmal.
Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the summit of Pisgah, which faces Jericho. Hashem showed him all the land, Gilead as far as Dan.
For thus said Hashem concerning the house of the king of Judah: “You are Gilead to Me, the summit of Lebanon; yet surely I will make you a wilderness, cities uninhabited.”

The Gemara raises an objection from what was taught in the following baraita: Four people died due to Adam’s sin with the serpent, in the wake of which death was decreed upon all of mankind, although they themselves were free of sin. And they are: Benjamin, son of Jacob; Amram, father of Moses; Yishai, father of David; and Kilab, son of David. And all of them were learned through tradition, except for Yishai, father of David, with regard to whom there is an explicit verse interpreted homiletically, as it is written: ‘And Absalom placed Amasa in charge of the army in place of Joab, and Amasa wa
Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity, and in sin my mother conceived me.

Another matter, ‘when a woman conceives’ – that is what is written: ‘I was generated in iniquity (Psalms 51:7). Rabbi Aḥa said: Even if one would be the most pious of the pious, it is impossible that he will not have one aspect of iniquity. David said before the Holy One blessed be He: ‘Master of the universe, did my father Yishai intend to produce me; was his intention not for his pleasure? Know that it is so, for after they have fulfilled their needs, this one turns his face to here and that one turns her face to there, and you insert each and every drop that is in him.’ That is what David s
Jacob said to Laban, “Give me my wife, for my days have been fulfilled, so that I may come to her.”

“My days are fulfilled”: the days my mother told me. Also, my days are fulfilled, for I am eighty-four years old; when shall I establish the twelve tribes? This is why he said, “That I may come to her.” Even the most frivolous person would not speak this way! Rather, he said it for the sake of producing offspring.
I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you. I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh, and give you a heart of flesh.

Rabbi Acha bar Yaakov said: Come and see what is written: “Isaac entreated the Lord on behalf of his wife, for she was barren.” Why was she barren? Because the evil inclination is not present in its power in the world; thus procreation is not found except through prayer. What is written? “The Lord answered his entreaty, and Rebecca his wife conceived.” When the inclination is aroused, procreation becomes possible. Rabbi Yosei said: If so, what difference is there between this world and that future time? Moreover, Scripture says that the Holy One, blessed be He, will do this. Rabbi Acha answere
The two of them were naked, the man and his wife, and they were not ashamed.

After they finished eating, Rabbi Yitzḥak told Rav Naḥman: Rabbi Yoḥanan said that our father Jacob did not die. He replied: Was it then for nothing that the mourners mourned him, the embalmers embalmed him, and the buriers buried him? Rabbi Yitzḥak answered: I am interpreting a verse: “Do not fear, My servant Jacob, declares Hashem, and do not be dismayed, Israel, for I will save you from afar, and your offspring from the land of their captivity.” The verse compares Jacob to his offspring: Just as his offspring are alive, so he too is alive.
Some say that Moses did not die. Here it is written, “He died there,” and elsewhere, “He was there with Hashem.” Just as there he stood ministering, so here too he stands ministering.
: “To Machir I gave Gilead.”

Rava said: This follows Rav Chananel’s teaching in Rav’s name: In the future, the righteous will revive the dead. Here it is written, “The lambs shall graze as promised,” and elsewhere, “They shall graze in Bashan and Gilead as in days of old.” Bashan means Elisha, who came from Bashan, as it says, “Yaanai and Shaphat in Bashan,” and, “Here is Elisha son of Shaphat, who poured water over Elijah’s hands.” Gilead means Elijah, as it says, “Elijah the Tishbite, of the inhabitants of Gilead, said.”

Another interpretation: “An ox, a sheep, or a goat”—this is “What has been already is.” Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Nechemyah discussed this. Rabbi Yehudah says: If someone tells you that had Adam not sinned and eaten from that tree, he would have lived and endured forever, answer him: Elijah already existed; he did not sin, and he lives and endures forever.

“Founded upon sockets of fine gold”: their foundation was three excellent things, unequaled in the world. This is “The Lord founded the earth through wisdom, established the heavens through understanding; through His knowledge the depths were split”—this is the sea. Wisdom is fear of the Lord, as it says, “Fear of the Lord is wisdom, and turning from evil is understanding.” Knowledge means one who recognizes his Creator, as it says, “There is no knowledge of God in the land,” and, “Understanding and knowing Me.”
'Wisdom': what a person hears from others and learns. 'Understanding': discerning something in one’s own heart from things one has learned. 'Knowledge': the holy spirit.
I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in every kind of craft.

Who said those teachings, and delivered them from one place to the other? Was it not Elijah the Prophet, who traveled from Sura to Pumbedita by way of a miraculous leap through the air above ten handbreadths from the ground, who said them? Apparently, the prohibition of Shabbat limits does not apply above ten handbreadths, for Elijah would not have transgressed this prohibition. The Gemara rejects this argument: This is no proof; perhaps Yosef the demon, who does not observe Shabbat, reported these teachings and brought them from Sura to Pumbedita.
