It is a sign between Me and the children of Israel forever, for in six days Hashem made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed.

If one vows, “Benefit from the uncircumcised is forbidden to me,” he may benefit from uncircumcised Israelites but may not benefit from circumcised members of the nations. If he vows against benefit from the circumcised, he may not benefit from uncircumcised Israelites, but may benefit from circumcised members of the nations. For the designation “uncircumcised” is applied to the nations, as it says, “All the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in heart.” It also says, “This uncircumcised Philistine,” and, “Lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest
This month shall be for you the head of the months; it is the first for you of the months of the year.

Rabbi Akiva said to Rabbi Yehoshua: “My teacher, permit me to say one thing before you that you taught me.” He answered, “Speak.” He said: “The word otam, ‘them,’ is stated three times. Read it as atem, ‘you’: you—even if you err; you—even if you act deliberately; you—even if you are misled.” He answered in these words: “Akiva, you have comforted me; you have comforted me.”
These are the appointed festivals of Hashem, holy convocations, which you shall proclaim at their appointed times.
You shall keep My statutes. You shall not breed your animal with a different kind; you shall not sow your field with mixed kinds; and a garment of mixed kinds, shaatnez, shall not come upon you.

Shmuel said: “You shall observe My statutes”—statutes I have already established for you. “You shall not crossbreed your animal; you shall not sow your field with mixed kinds”: just as the rule concerning your animal concerns crossbreeding, so the rule concerning your field concerns grafting. And just as the rule concerning your animal applies both in the Land and outside the Land, so the rule concerning your field applies both in the Land and outside the Land.
God saw the light, that it was good, and God separated the light from the darkness.

Rav Judah said in Rav’s name: Adam was a heretic, as it says, “Hashem God called to the human being and said to him, Where are you?”—where has your heart turned? R. Isaac said: He drew his foreskin forward. Here it says, “Like Adam, they transgressed the covenant,” and elsewhere it says, “He has broken My covenant.”

Why is Havdalah included in the blessing “Who grants knowledge”? Rav Yosef said: Because distinguishing is an act of wisdom, they placed it in the blessing of wisdom. The Sages say: Because Havdalah concerns the weekday, they placed it in the first weekday blessing.
Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who make darkness into light and light into darkness, who make bitter into sweet and sweet into bitter.
Of the children of Issachar, men who understood the times, to know what Israel should do: their chiefs were two hundred, and all their brothers were at their command.
The king spoke to the wise men who knew the times, for such was the king’s practice before all who knew law and judgment.

“The king said to the wise men”—who were the wise men? The Sages. “Those who knew the times”—those who knew how to intercalate years and establish months. He said to them, “Judge her for me.” They said: “What shall we do? If we tell him to kill her, tomorrow he will be sober and demand her from us. If we tell him to leave her, she has shown contempt for the monarchy.” They told him: “Since the Temple was destroyed and we were exiled from our land, counsel has been taken from us, and we no longer know how to judge capital cases. Go to Ammon and Moab, who remain settled in their places like wine

“The king said to the wise men, those who knew the times.” Who were they? Rabbi Simon said: This was the tribe of Issachar, as it is written, “The children of Issachar, who understood the times, to know what Israel should do.” … “Their heads were two hundred”: these were the two hundred heads of courts that the tribe of Issachar supplied. “All their brothers followed their word”: all agreed with their halakhic judgment as with a law given to Moses at Sinai.

Rava said: You will not find a Torah scholar who issues authoritative rulings unless he comes from Levi or Issachar. Levi: “They shall teach Your ordinances to Jacob.” Issachar: “The children of Issachar, who understood the times, to know what Israel should do.” But say Judah too, for it is written, “Judah is My lawgiver”! I am speaking of reaching the conclusion that accords with the halakhah.

R. Yohanan said: A gentile who engages in Torah incurs the death penalty, as it says, “Moses commanded us the Torah as an inheritance”—an inheritance for us, not for them. Why is this not counted among the seven commandments? According to the reading “inheritance,” he is stealing it; according to the reading “betrothed,” his judgment is like that of violating a betrothed young woman, which is stoning. They raised an objection: R. Meir used to say: From where do we know that even a gentile who engages in Torah is like a High Priest? It says, “Which a human being shall perform and live through t

“Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it”: this is the mystery of the holy covenant. All the sources of the body’s members abide in this covenant, which encompasses everything. Similarly, Shabbat encompasses Torah, and all Torah’s mysteries depend upon it. Observing Shabbat is like observing the entire Torah; one who guards Shabbat is as though he guarded the whole Torah.

The Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: Did I not write for you in My Torah, “This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth”? Although you work throughout the six days, let Shabbat be devoted entirely to Torah. From here they said: A person should rise early on Shabbat and study, go to the synagogue and house of study, read Torah and study the Prophets, and afterward go home, eat, and drink, fulfilling, “Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a good heart.” For the Holy One, blessed be He, finds rest only with those who practice Torah, as it says, “All these My hand has
May the pleasantness of the Lord our God be upon us; establish the work of our hands for us, and establish the work of our hands.

This noam is the pleasantness issuing from the World to Come. From the World to Come all lamps shine and spread in every direction. That goodness and light of the World to Come, from which the Patriarchs draw, is called pleasantness. Another interpretation: the World to Come is itself called pleasantness. When it is awakened, all joy, goodness, light, and freedom in the world are awakened; therefore it is called pleasantness. We have therefore learned: when Shabbat enters, all the condemned in Gehinnom rest and enjoy freedom and repose. When Shabbat departs, we must awaken supernal joy upon ou

He opened and said: “Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace.” “Her ways are ways of pleasantness”—these are the paths of Torah. Upon one who walks in the paths of Torah, the Holy One, blessed be He, causes the pleasantness of the Shekhinah to rest, never to depart from him. “All her paths are peace”: all the paths of Torah are peace—peace for him above and below, peace in this world and in the World to Come.
Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace.
For a mitzvah is a lamp, and Torah is light, and the reproofs of discipline are the way of life.
The heavens recount the glory of God, and the firmament tells of the work of His hands.

Then, when Heaven enters the bridal canopy and comes to illuminate her, all the companions who adorned her are mentioned there by name. This is “The firmament declares the work of His hands.” “The work of His hands” refers to those who uphold the covenant with the bride. These masters of the covenant are called “the work of His hands,” as it says, “Establish the work of our hands”: this is the enduring covenant sealed in a person’s flesh.

So too, Torah scholars, the children of the King and Matron, are called Shabbatot and festivals. They have no means of their own, for they are not tradesmen like the other servants, the people of the weekdays. Their reward in this world and the World to Come is that they should be delighted with every kind of food and drink, and honored with beautiful clothing, as with Shabbat, of which it is said, “Honor it with clean garments.” Everything a person does for Shabbat and festivals, he should do for them.

At that time the Shekhinah is called Tosefta, an addition, from the side of the Shabbat day. Many additions descend with her to Torah scholars; these are called additional souls, as it says, “The soul of every living being shall bless Your Name, Lord our God.” Those additions granted to the holy people on Shabbat eve are inherited by Torah scholars during the weekdays. Through them, the weekday becomes holy. These are the additions descending from Tosefta, for the Shekhinah is indeed the adornment of the body of the Holy One, blessed be He.

“They guarded”—this is the Shekhinah, which guards those who observe Shabbatot and festivals. Therefore the Shekhinah does not depart from Israel on any Shabbat or festival, or even on the “Shabbatot of weekdays”; rather, she is closed and enclosed within them. In every prayer she ascends toward the Lord, until she reaches the chariot of the supernal Patriarchs—Gedulah, Gevurah, and Tiferet—which have twelve faces corresponding to the twelve tribes. In accordance with the merit she pleads for these masters of prayer and good deeds, through each commandment of Torah, so they encamp upon their m
Yehudah approached him and said: Please, my lord, let your servant speak a word in my lord’s ears, and do not let your anger burn against your servant, for you are like Pharaoh.

Yehudah said: What can we say to my lord? What can we speak, and how can we justify ourselves? God has found your servants’ guilt. Here we are, slaves to my lord—both we and the one in whose hand the goblet was found.
The one among your servants with whom it is found shall die, and we too will become slaves to my lord.

Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says: Since the world is judged according to its majority, and the individual is judged according to his majority, if he performs one mitzvah, fortunate is he, for he has tipped himself and the whole world toward merit. If he commits one transgression, woe to him, for he has tipped himself and the whole world toward guilt, as it says, “One sinner destroys much good.” Through the one sin he committed, much good is lost to him and to the whole world.
He said to Avram: Know with certainty that your seed will be strangers in a land that is not theirs, and they will enslave them and afflict them for four hundred years.
This is how I was: by day scorching heat consumed me, and frost by night; sleep fled from my eyes.
We said to my lord: We have an elderly father and a young child of his old age. His brother is dead, and he alone remains of his mother, and his father loves him.
They said, “Your servants are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan. Behold, the youngest is with our father today, and the one is no more.”
“His brother is dead”: He uttered an untruth out of fear. He said to himself: If I tell him that Joseph is alive, he will say, “Bring him to me.”
Now, please let your servant remain in place of the boy as a slave to my lord, and let the boy go up with his brothers.
My lord asked his servants: Do you have a father or a brother?
The king said to me: What is it that you seek? And I prayed to the God of heaven.
I said to the king: If it is good in the king’s eyes, and if your servant is pleasing before you, send me to Yehudah, to the city of my fathers’ graves, so that I may rebuild it.

“Yehudah approached him.” Rabbi Yehudah, Rabbi Nechemyah, and the Rabbis differ. Rabbi Yehudah says: an approach for battle, as in “Yoav and the people with him approached for battle.” Rabbi Nechemyah says: an approach for conciliation, as in “The children of Yehudah approached Yehoshua,” to conciliate him. The Rabbis say: an approach for prayer, as in “Eliyahu the prophet approached and said: Hashem, God…” Rabbi Elazar explained it to them: “If for battle, I am coming; if for conciliation, I am coming; if for prayer, I am coming.”

“The remaining camp will escape”: against his will, for I will fight him. He prepared himself for three things: a gift, prayer, and battle. For a gift, as it says later, “The gift passed before him”; for prayer, “God of my father Avraham”; for battle, “The remaining camp will escape.”

I will tell you a principle that you should understand throughout the coming passages concerning Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov. It is a great matter that our Sages expressed briefly: “Everything that happened to the fathers is a sign for the children.” Therefore Scripture relates at length their journeys, the digging of wells, and their other experiences. A reader might think these details superfluous and without benefit, but they all come to teach about the future. When an event happens to a prophet from among the three patriarchs, he perceives through it what has been decreed to happen to hi

When Yosef saw their great shame, he said to them, “Come close to me,” and they came close. He kissed each one and wept over him, as it says, “He kissed all his brothers and wept over them.” Just as Yosef reconciled with his brothers only through weeping, so, when the Holy One, blessed be He, redeems Israel, He will redeem them through weeping: “With weeping they will come, and with supplications I will lead them. I will guide them to streams of water, on a straight path where they will not stumble, for I have become a father to Israel, and Ephraim is My firstborn.”
Therefore, on this day we must throw a bone to the dog. While it is gnawing, whoever wishes to enter may enter the King’s palace, and no one will prevent him. Afterward it will wag its tail for him.
Joseph could not restrain himself before all those standing by him, and he cried, ‘Send everyone out from before me!’ No one stood with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
The small one will become a thousand, and the young one a mighty nation. I, Hashem, will hasten it in its time.

“Yehudah approached him.” Rabbi Yehudah, Rabbi Nechemyah, and the Rabbis differ. Rabbi Yehudah says: an approach for battle, as in “Yoav and the people with him approached for battle.” Rabbi Nechemyah says: an approach for conciliation, as in “The children of Yehudah approached Yehoshua,” to conciliate him. The Rabbis say: an approach for prayer, as in “Eliyahu the prophet approached and said: Hashem, God…” Rabbi Elazar explained it to them: “If for battle, I am coming; if for conciliation, I am coming; if for prayer, I am coming.”
Yehudah approached him and said: Please, my lord, let your servant speak a word in my lord’s ears, and do not let your anger burn against your servant, for you are like Pharaoh.

“The remaining camp will escape”: against his will, for I will fight him. He prepared himself for three things: a gift, prayer, and battle. For a gift, as it says later, “The gift passed before him”; for prayer, “God of my father Avraham”; for battle, “The remaining camp will escape.”
He said: If Esav comes against the one camp and strikes it, the remaining camp will escape.
The king said to me: What is it that you seek? And I prayed to the God of heaven.
I said to the king: If it is good in the king’s eyes, and if your servant is pleasing before you, send me to Yehudah, to the city of my fathers’ graves, so that I may rebuild it.
A king’s heart is like streams of water in Hashem’s hand; He turns it wherever He desires.

“Israel said: Why have you dealt badly with me?” Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Chama bar Chanina: Yaakov our father never spoke an idle word. Yet the Holy One, blessed be He, said: “I am occupied with making his son king in Egypt, and he says, ‘Why have you dealt badly with me?’” This is what is written: “My way is hidden from Hashem, and my judgment passes away from my God.”
Yisrael said: Why did you do me this harm, telling the man that you had another brother?

Four hundred barrels of Rav Huna’s wine turned sour. Rav Yehudah, the brother of Rav Sala the Pious, and the Rabbis—or, according to others, Rav Adda bar Ahavah and the Rabbis—came to him and said: “Let the Master examine his conduct.” He said: “Am I suspect in your eyes?” They answered: “Is the Holy One, blessed be He, suspect of executing judgment without justice?”

Yosef shall not carry [my bier], for he is king, and you must accord him honor. Levi shall not carry it. Why? Because he bears the Ark, and one who bears the Ark of the Ever-Living One does not bear the coffin of the dead. If you carry my bier as I have commanded you, God will in the future arrange you in camps under banners.
His brothers also went and fell before him and said: Here we are, your slaves.
Why do you say, Yaakov, and speak, Yisrael: My way is hidden from Hashem, and my justice passes by my God?
My lord asked his servants: Do you have a father or a brother?
We said to my lord: We have an elderly father and a young child of his old age. His brother is dead, and he alone remains of his mother, and his father loves him.
You said to your servants: Bring him down to me, so that I may set my eyes upon him.
We said to my lord: The boy cannot leave his father; if he leaves his father, he will die.
You said to your servants: Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you shall not see my face again.
When we went up to your servant, my father, we told him my lord’s words.
“His brother is dead”: He uttered an untruth out of fear. He said to himself: If I tell him that Joseph is alive, he will say, “Bring him to me.”

Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai said: Great is peace, for the Torah spoke untrue words for the sake of peace. Which words? “Thus shall you say to Joseph: Please forgive your brothers’ wrongdoing and sin.” We do not find that he commanded any of these things. Rather, he knew Joseph’s piety and did not suspect him or regard him as one who would shed blood.

Thus shall you say to Yosef: Please forgive the wrongdoing of your brothers and their sin, for they dealt evil with you. And now, please forgive the wrongdoing of the servants of your father’s God. Yosef wept as they spoke to him.

“The dead know nothing”: these are the wicked, who are called dead even during their lifetimes, as it says, “And you, slain wicked prince of Israel.” Alternatively, it may be derived from “By the testimony of two witnesses or three witnesses the dead shall be put to death.” But he is still alive! Rather, he was already dead from the outset.
When he sees that the boy is not there, he will die, and your servants will have brought down the gray hair of your servant, our father, in grief to the grave.
Now, please let your servant remain in place of the boy as a slave to my lord, and let the boy go up with his brothers.

“For behold, the kings assembled; they passed together.” “The kings” are Yehudah and Yosef. “They passed together”: this one was filled with wrath against the other, and the other was filled with wrath against him. “They saw and were amazed”—“The men looked at one another in amazement.” “They were alarmed and hastened away”—“His brothers could not answer him.” “Trembling seized them there”: these are the tribes. They said: “Kings are contending with one another; what concern is it of ours? It befits a king to contend with a king.” “Yehudah approached him”—“One draws near to another”: Yehudah a
For behold, the kings assembled; they passed by together.

Therefore, “For behold, the kings assembled; they passed together”: they became angry together, and they became angry with one another over Binyamin. What is written? “They saw and were amazed; they were alarmed and hastened away. Trembling seized them there”—all those who were present.
They told him all the words Yosef had spoken to them, and he saw the wagons Yosef had sent to carry him; then the spirit of Yaakov their father revived.

Come and see: once Yosef was lost to his father, Yaakov lost the additional spirit he possessed, and the Divine Presence departed from him. Afterward, what is written? “The spirit of Yaakov their father revived.” Had he been dead until then? Rather, that additional spirit—the Divine Presence—had departed from him and was no longer within him, because his sorrow had caused this. Therefore it says, “The spirit of Yaakov their father revived.”

Reish Lakish said: Any person who becomes angry—if he is a sage, his wisdom departs from him; if he is a prophet, his prophecy departs from him. That a sage’s wisdom departs is learned from Moshe, for it says, “Moshe became angry with the officers of the army,” and afterward, “Elazar the priest said to the men of the army who had come to battle: This is the statute of the Torah that Hashem commanded Moshe.” This implies that the law had become hidden from Moshe.

If that person does not guard it, but uproots this supernal holiness from its place so that the Other Side can dwell there, he is certainly a person who rebels against his Master; it is forbidden to draw close to him or associate with him. This is “He tears his soul in his anger”: he tears and uproots his soul through his anger, and causes a foreign god to dwell within him. Therefore it is written, “Withdraw from the man whose soul is in his anger”: he tears and defiles that holy soul because of his anger. “Of what account is he?” That person is regarded as idolatry.
You who tear your soul in your anger—shall the earth be abandoned for your sake, or a rock be moved from its place?

Esther [was a prophetess], for it is written, “On the third day Esther clothed herself in royalty.” It should have said “royal garments”! Rather, the Divine Spirit clothed her. Here it says, “She clothed herself,” and elsewhere it says, “A spirit clothed Amasai.”

On the third day Esther clothed herself in royalty and stood in the inner court of the king’s house, opposite the king’s house. The king sat upon his royal throne in the royal house, opposite the entrance of the house.

We learned before the Master: What is holiness? The perfection of everything, called supernal wisdom. From that place springs and streams flow in every direction until they reach this Zot. When this Zot is blessed from that supernal place called holiness and wisdom, it is called the Holy Spirit: a spirit from that holiness above. When mysteries of Torah emerge and are aroused from it, it is then called the holy tongue.

What is repentance? The sinner must abandon his sin, remove it from his thoughts, and resolve in his heart never to do it again, as it says, “Let the wicked abandon his way.” He must also regret the past, as it says, “After I returned, I regretted.” The Knower of hidden things must testify concerning him that he will never return to this sin, as it says, “We will no longer call the work of our hands our god.” He must confess with his lips and articulate these matters that he has resolved in his heart.
Joseph could not restrain himself before all those standing by him, and he cried, ‘Send everyone out from before me!’ No one stood with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
The small one will become a thousand, and the young one a mighty nation. I, Hashem, will hasten it in its time.
Yehudah approached him and said: Please, my lord, let your servant speak a word in my lord’s ears, and do not let your anger burn against your servant, for you are like Pharaoh.
For behold, the kings assembled; they passed by together.

“For behold, the kings assembled; they passed together.” “The kings” are Yehudah and Yosef. “They passed together”: this one was filled with wrath against the other, and the other was filled with wrath against him. “They saw and were amazed”—“The men looked at one another in amazement.” “They were alarmed and hastened away”—“His brothers could not answer him.” “Trembling seized them there”: these are the tribes. They said: “Kings are contending with one another; what concern is it of ours? It befits a king to contend with a king.” “Yehudah approached him”—“One draws near to another”: Yehudah a
Who is a God like You, who bears iniquity and passes over transgression for the remnant of His inheritance? He does not maintain His anger forever, for He desires kindness.

“They passed together”: the mystery is that when they join together, then “they passed together,” for all the world’s sins do not pass away and become subdued until they unite. It is as it is written, “And passes over transgression.” Therefore, “They passed together”: those sins passed away and were atoned for, because then all faces shine and all sins are removed.

The Teli in the universe is like a king on his throne; the wheel in the year is like a king in his province; the heart in the person is like a king in battle. God made everything opposite its counterpart: good opposite evil, good from good and evil from evil. Good distinguishes evil, and evil distinguishes good. Good is kept for the good, and evil is kept for the wicked.

Some say that this is what [Bava ben Buta] told [Herod]: “He blinded the eye of the world, as it is written [of the sages], ‘If it be hidden from the eyes of the congregation.’ Let him go and occupy himself with the eye of the world [the Temple], as it is written, ‘Behold, I will profane My sanctuary, the pride of your strength, the delight of your eyes.’”
He sent Yehudah ahead of him to Yosef, to give direction before him toward Goshen, and they came to the land of Goshen.
Dominion and dread are with Him; He makes peace in His heights.

“He sent Yehudah ahead of him.” This is what Scripture says: “Dominion and dread are with Him; He makes peace in His heights.” “Dominion” is Michael, and “dread” is Gabriel. Michael is of water and Gabriel of fire, yet they stand before the Divine Presence and do not harm one another. Thus, “He makes peace in His heights.”
On the third day Joseph said to them, ‘Do this and live, for I fear God.’
The beginning of wisdom is fear of Hashem; good understanding belongs to all who practice them. His praise endures forever.
A wise person’s heart is at his right, and a fool’s heart at his left.

Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: What does “The utterance of David son of Yishai, the utterance of the man raised on high” mean? It is the utterance of David son of Yishai, who established the yoke of repentance.
These are David’s last words: the utterance of David son of Yishai, the utterance of the man raised on high, the anointed of the God of Yaakov and the sweet singer of Yisrael.
For there is no righteous person on earth who does good and does not sin.
Your people are all righteous; they will inherit the land forever—the shoot of My planting, the work of My hands, in which to be glorified.
The God of Israel said; the Rock of Israel spoke to me: ‘A ruler over mankind—a righteous one, ruling in the fear of God.’

For we learned: Whoever emits his seed in vain is called evil and does not behold the face of the Shechinah, as it is written, “For You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You.” And it is written, “Er, Yehudah’s firstborn, was evil.” … We learned: Rabbi Yehudah said, “There is no sin in the world for which there is no repentance except this one; and there are no sinners who do not behold the face of the Shechinah except this one, as it is written, ‘Evil shall not dwell with You’—at all.” Rabbi Yitzchak said: “Fortunate are the righteous in this world and in the Worl

After turning to a bad course, Acher asked Rabbi Meir: What does “Gold and glass cannot equal it, nor can vessels of fine gold be exchanged for it” mean? He answered: These are words of Torah, difficult to acquire like vessels of gold and fine gold, but easily lost like glass vessels. Acher told him: “Rabbi Akiva your teacher did not explain it that way. Rather, just as vessels of gold and glass can be repaired after breaking, so a Torah scholar can be restored even after going astray.” Rabbi Meir told him: “Then you too should return.” He answered: “I have already heard from behind the curtai
Return, wayward children; I will heal your waywardness. Here we are, we have come to You, for You are Hashem our God.

They asked him, “Why do you call yourself Rav Huna?” He replied, “That is my name.” “Why, when they told you to sit upon the bed, did you sit?” He replied, “Whatever the master of the house tells you, do—except leave.”

“Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites.” They said: Let us follow the established way of the world. Was not Canaan, who sinned, cursed to become a slave? This one too—“Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites.” “His brothers heeded him.”
Whoever disqualifies others is himself disqualified, and he never speaks in their praise. Shmuel said: He disqualifies others with his own blemish.
Yehudah recognized them and said: She is more righteous than I, because I did not give her to my son Shelah. He did not know her again.

“Yehudah approached him.” Rabbi Yehudah, Rabbi Nechemyah, and the Rabbis differ. Rabbi Yehudah says: an approach for battle, as in “Yoav and the people with him approached for battle.” Rabbi Nechemyah says: an approach for conciliation, as in “The children of Yehudah approached Yehoshua,” to conciliate him. The Rabbis say: an approach for prayer, as in “Eliyahu the prophet approached and said: Hashem, God…” Rabbi Elazar explained it to them: “If for battle, I am coming; if for conciliation, I am coming; if for prayer, I am coming.”
Now, please let your servant remain in place of the boy as a slave to my lord, and let the boy go up with his brothers.
Even when I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me. Your rod and Your staff—they comfort me.

The fourth said: “Why is the strap hanging there? Strike me with it.” This is David, as it says, “Of David: Judge me, Hashem.” Likewise Shlomo says, “One who loves discipline loves knowledge,” and David says, “Fortunate is the man whom You discipline, God.”
Joseph could not restrain himself before all those standing by him, and he cried, ‘Send everyone out from before me!’ No one stood with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
Yehudah approached him and said: Please, my lord, let your servant speak a word in my lord’s ears, and do not let your anger burn against your servant, for you are like Pharaoh.
One draws close to the other, and no breath can enter between them.

“For behold, the kings assembled; they passed together.” “The kings” are Yehudah and Yosef. “They passed together”: this one was filled with wrath against the other, and the other was filled with wrath against him. “They saw and were amazed”—“The men looked at one another in amazement.” “They were alarmed and hastened away”—“His brothers could not answer him.” “Trembling seized them there”: these are the tribes. They said: “Kings are contending with one another; what concern is it of ours? It befits a king to contend with a king.” “Yehudah approached him”—“One draws near to another”: Yehudah a

Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai taught: Since all matters depend upon Rachel, Israel are called by her name: “Rachel weeps for her children.” They are called not only by her name, but also by her son’s name: “Perhaps Hashem, God of Hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Yosef.” Not only by her son’s name, but also by her grandson’s name: “Is Ephraim My precious son?”
Hate evil, love good, and establish justice in the gate. Perhaps Hashem, God of hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.

“Yehudah, your brothers will acknowledge you”: your brothers acknowledge you, your mother acknowledges you, and I myself acknowledge you. Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai said: All your brothers will be called by your name. A person does not say, “I am a Reubenite,” or “I am a Simeonite,” but “I am a Jew.”
On the third day Joseph said to them, ‘Do this and live, for I fear God.’

Rav Chana bar Bizna said in Rabbi Shimon Chasida’s name: Yosef, who sanctified Heaven’s name in private, had one letter of the Holy One’s name added to his name. Yehudah, who sanctified Heaven’s name publicly, was named entirely after the name of the Holy One, blessed be He.
Rather, it is certainly chukkat, as we have explained: the letter He was originally Dalet, and this has already been discussed.
The beginning of wisdom is fear of Hashem; good understanding belongs to all who practice them. His praise endures forever.
He said to man: Behold, fear of the Lord—that is wisdom; and turning away from evil is understanding.

“A small city”: Egypt. “Few men within it”: Yosef’s brothers, as it says, “Yosef’s ten brothers went down.” “A great king came against it and surrounded it”: Yosef. “He built great siegeworks against it”: the three decrees he issued—that no slave should enter Egypt, that no person should enter with two donkeys, and that no one should enter without recording his own name and those of his father, grandfather, and grandmother. “A poor wise man was found in it”: Yehudah. “He delivered the city through his wisdom”: he said, “I will guarantee him,” and also said to Yosef, “Let your servant remain in
There was a small city with few men in it. A great king came against it, surrounded it, and built great siegeworks against it.
In it was found a poor, wise man, and he saved the city through his wisdom; yet no one remembered that poor man.
He sent Yehudah ahead of him to Yosef, to give direction before him toward Goshen, and they came to the land of Goshen.
Let your heart not envy sinners, but remain in fear of Hashem all the day.

These are the generations of Yaakov: Yosef, at seventeen years of age, was tending the flock with his brothers. He was a youth with the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, his father’s wives. Yosef brought an evil report of them to their father.

“He sent Yehudah ahead of him”: to establish a house of study for him, where he would give instruction and teach the tribes. Know that it was so: when Yosef left him, he knew the passage in which they had parted, for he had been teaching him. When Yosef’s brothers came and said, “Yosef is still alive,” his heart grew faint, for he did not believe them. Yaakov remembered that they had parted while studying the passage of the heifer whose neck is broken, and said: “Let him give you a sign of the passage in which we parted, and I will believe you.” Yosef too remembered it and gave them wagons. Wh
Yisrael journeyed with all that he had and came to Beersheva, and he offered sacrifices to the God of his father Yitzchak.
“To the God of his father Yitzchak”: A person is obligated to honor his father more than his grandfather. Therefore he associated [the sacrifice] with Yitzchak and not with Avraham.

“He offered sacrifices to the God of his father Yitzchak”: “A person is obligated to honor his father more than his grandfather; therefore he associated it with Yitzchak and not with Avraham”—these are Rashi’s words. They are insufficient, for it would have been appropriate to say “to the God of his fathers” without singling out anyone, just as he said, “The God before whom my fathers Avraham and Yitzchak walked.” In his prayer he said, “God of my father Avraham and God of my father Yitzchak.” Or it could simply say, “He offered sacrifices to Hashem,” as it says of Avraham, “He built an altar

Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Nechemyah differed [about the eshel Avraham planted]: one said it was an orchard, and the other said it was an inn. According to the one who said an orchard, “he planted” is understandable. But according to the one who said an inn, what does “he planted” mean? It is like the expression, “He shall plant his royal tents.”
He planted a tamarisk in Beersheva, and there he called in the name of Hashem, God of the world.

Rav Huna said: When Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi came to Tiberias, he asked Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish [why Yaakov offered sacrifices specifically to the God of his father Yitzchak]. Rabbi Yochanan said: A person is obligated to honor his father more than his grandfather. Reish Lakish said: He offered them on account of the covenant of the tribes.

Rava expounded: What does “How beautiful are your steps in sandals, daughter of the generous one” mean? How beautiful are Israel’s feet when they ascend for the pilgrimage festival. “Daughter of the generous one”: the daughter of Avraham our father, who is called generous, as it says, “The generous among the peoples have gathered, the people of the God of Avraham.” “The God of Avraham,” but not the God of Yitzchak and Yaakov? Rather, “the God of Avraham,” because he was the first of the converts.

ref: Mishneh Torah, First Fruits and other Gifts to Priests Outside the Sanctuary 4:3
quote: A convert brings [first fruits] and recites [the declaration], for Avraham was told, “I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.” He is thus the father of everyone in the world who enters beneath the wings of the Divine Presence. The oath that his children would inherit the land was first given to Avraham.
Your name shall no longer be called Avram; your name shall be Avraham, for I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.
Hear us, my lord: you are a prince of God among us. Bury your dead in the choicest of our graves; none of us will withhold his grave from you for burying your dead.

“To the Valley of Shaveh”: Rabbi Berechyah and Rabbi Chanina said in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name: There all the idolaters agreed together. They cut down cedars, made a great platform, and seated Avraham high upon it. They praised him and said, “Hear us, my lord.” They said: “You are king over us; you are prince over us; you are a god over us.” He answered them: “Let the world not lack its King, and let it not lack its God.”
The king of Sodom went out to meet him after his return from striking Kedorlaomer and the kings with him, at the Valley of Shaveh, which is the King’s Valley.
Yaakov dwelt in the land of his father’s sojourning, in the land of Canaan.

Yaakov made converts, as it is written, “Yaakov said to his household…” and “They gave to Yaakov…” We have not heard this of Yitzchak. Where do we hear it? Rabbi Yitzchak—and it was taught in the name of Rabbi Hoshaya the Great, in Rabbi Yehudah bar Simon’s name—said: Here it is written, “Yaakov dwelled in the land of his father’s sojournings.” What does “his father’s sojournings” mean? The conversions made by his father.
God said to Abraham, ‘Do not let it be evil in your eyes concerning the boy and your maidservant. Whatever Sarah says to you, listen to her voice, for in Isaac shall offspring be called yours.’

Rav Chiya bar Avin said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: A gentile inherits his father by Torah law, for it is written, “I have given Mount Seir to Esav as an inheritance.” But perhaps an apostate Israelite is different? Rather, the proof is from here: “I have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as an inheritance.”

Scripture says “sacrifices” to teach that these were not burnt offerings like those of his fathers, for Avraham offered burnt offerings. Our Rabbis said: “The descendants of Noach did not offer peace offerings; they offered burnt offerings.” Of Noach it is explicitly written, “He offered burnt offerings on the altar.” But Yaakov, out of fear of Hashem, offered peace offerings to bring all the divine attributes into harmony toward him, as they expounded: “Peace offerings—because they bring peace into the world.”

Was it not taught: “But not peace offerings—only burnt offerings”? Burnt offerings, yes; peace offerings, no! This follows the opinion that the descendants of Noach did not offer peace offerings. For Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina disputed this: one said that the descendants of Noach offered peace offerings, and the other said that they did not.

“He said: Because Hashem your God brought it before me.” Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish differed. One said: If the Holy One, blessed be He, provided for your sacrifice, as it says, “Avraham lifted his eyes and saw, and behold, a ram,” how much more so for your food!

Abaye said: At first I would study at home and pray in the synagogue. Once I heard what Rabbi Chiya bar Ami said in Ulla’s name—“Since the Temple was destroyed, the Holy One, blessed be He, has nothing in His world except the four cubits of halakhah”—I would pray only in the place where I studied.
Grace is false and beauty is vain; a woman who fears Hashem is to be praised.

Another Shabbat remained unmentioned, and it felt shame. It said before Him: “Master of the world, from the day You made me I have been called Shabbat, and a day cannot be without a night.” He said to it: “My daughter, you are Shabbat, and I call you Shabbat; but now I shall crown you with an additional supernal crown.” He issued a proclamation: “You shall fear My sanctuary.” This is the Shabbat of Shabbat eve, which is fear, and fear rests within it. What is it? The Holy One, blessed be He, included it and said, “I am Hashem.”

The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: Did I not write for you in My Torah, “This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth”? Although you work during all six days, let Shabbat be devoted entirely to Torah. Hence they said: A person should rise early and study on Shabbat, go to the synagogue and house of study, read the Torah and study the Prophets, and afterward go home to eat and drink, fulfilling “Go, eat your bread with joy and drink your wine with a good heart.” For the Holy One has rest only with those who practice Torah, as it says, “My hand made all these… But to this one I
My hand made all these things, and so all these things came to be, says Hashem. But to this one I will look: to the poor and broken in spirit, who trembles at My word.
Yehudah approached him and said: Please, my lord, let your servant speak a word in my lord’s ears, and do not let your anger burn against your servant, for you are like Pharaoh.

Behold, days are coming, says Hashem, when the plowman will overtake the reaper, and the one who treads grapes will overtake the sower of seed. The mountains will drip sweet wine, and all the hills will melt.

“Yehudah approached him.” “Behold, days are coming, says Hashem, when the plowman will draw near…” “The plowman” is Yehudah; “the reaper” is Yosef, as it says, “Behold, we were binding sheaves.” “The treader of grapes” is Yehudah, as it says, “I have bent Yehudah for Myself as a bow.” “The one who draws the seed” is Yosef, who drew his father’s descendants down to Egypt, as it says, “With human cords I drew them.” “The mountains will drip sweet wine”: these are the tribes, who said, “Kings are contending with one another; what concern is it of ours?”
Are you not like the children of the Cushites to Me, children of Yisrael? says Hashem. Did I not bring Yisrael up from the land of Egypt, the Philistines from Kaftor, and Aram from Kir?
When the storm passes, the wicked one is no more; but the righteous one is the foundation of the world.
Beautiful in elevation, the joy of all the earth, is Mount Zion, the northern heights, the city of the great King.

Rabbi Abba opened: “Beautiful in elevation, the joy of all the earth, Mount Zion, the recesses of the north, the city of the great King.” This verse is a mystery of faith. “Beautiful in elevation” is Yosef the righteous, of whom it is written, “Yosef was handsome in form and handsome in appearance.” “The joy of all the earth”: he is joy and gladness above and below. “Mount Zion, the recesses of the north”: because the Tabernacle of Shiloh stood in his portion. “Mount Zion” is Jerusalem. “The recesses of the north”: so it is indeed above and below.
He left all that he had in Yosef’s hand, and with him there he concerned himself with nothing except the bread that he ate. Yosef was handsome in form and handsome in appearance.

Because he ascended within the World to Come, a branch beautiful in appearance emerged from him, and all lights issue from it, together with all abundance and anointing oil to illuminate the earth. Who is this? Yosef the righteous, who provides abundance for the entire world, and from whom the world is sustained. Therefore, everything the Holy One, blessed be He, does in the world is all according to a supernal mystery, and everything is as it should be.
For behold, I command, and I will shake the house of Yisrael among all the nations as one shakes with a sieve, and not a pebble will fall to the earth.
Your people are all righteous; they will inherit the land forever—the shoot of My planting, the work of My hands, in which to be glorified.

Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: Sarah went down to Egypt and guarded herself against sexual immorality, and all the women guarded themselves through her merit. Yosef went down to Egypt and guarded himself against sexual immorality, and all the men guarded themselves through his merit. Rabbi Pinchas said in Rabbi Chiya’s name: The restraint against sexual immorality was itself sufficient for Israel to be redeemed from Egypt through its merit. What is the reason? “A locked garden is my sister, my bride.” What is written afterward? “Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates.”
For a righteous person falls seven times and rises, but the wicked stumble through calamity.
On that day I will raise up the fallen booth of David; I will repair its breaches, raise up its ruins, and rebuild it as in days of old.

Rav Nachman said to Rabbi Yitzchak: “Have you heard when Bar Nafli will come?” He asked: “Who is Bar Nafli?” He answered: “The Messiah.” “Do you call the Messiah Bar Nafli?” He said: “Yes, for it is written: On that day I will raise up the fallen booth of David.”

Since the Holy One, blessed be He, had already blessed him, why did his father bless him again, as it says, “Yitzchak called Yaakov and blessed him”? Yitzchak saw through the Holy Spirit that his descendants would be exiled among the nations. He said: “Come, let me bless you with blessings for the exiles, that the Holy One will return to you and gather you from the exiles.” What were those blessings? “From six troubles He will deliver you, and in seven no evil will touch you”; “You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, and will not fear destruction when it comes”; “At destruction and
From six troubles He will rescue you, and in seven no evil will touch you.

“Who has woe? Who has sorrow?” Although Israel sinned and the Holy One, blessed be He, delivered them into the hands of the nations because of their sins, the nations did not escape punishment. In the end the Holy One judges the nations into whose hands He delivered them, as He did with Egypt and Babylonia. Therefore “who” is written six times, corresponding to the six exiles in which Israel was exiled among the nations, all of whom were punished on their account. These are: Egypt first, then Assyria, Babylonia, Media, Greece, and Edom.

“And El Shaddai”: Why did Yaakov see fit to bless them with El Shaddai? To teach that many sufferings had passed over Yaakov. Even in his mother’s womb Esav struggled with him, as it says, “The children struggled within her.” … He fled from Esav to Lavan and spent twenty years there amid many troubles, as it says, “By day scorching heat consumed me.” After he left, Lavan pursued him to kill him. When he escaped him, Esav came and again sought to kill him, and he lost that entire gift on his account. When he escaped Esav, the trouble of Dinah came upon him; after Dinah’s trouble, Rachel’s troub

“And God Almighty”: He who has sufficient mercy and the power to grant it will grant you mercy; this is the plain meaning. Its midrashic interpretation is: May He who said “Enough” to the world say “Enough” to my troubles. I have had no rest since my youth: the trouble of Lavan, the trouble of Esav, the trouble of Rachel, the trouble of Dinah, the trouble of Yosef, the trouble of Shimon, and the trouble of Binyamin.
Jacob lived in the land of Egypt for seventeen years. The days of Jacob, the years of his life, were one hundred and forty-seven years.

Why did Yaakov merit a life without suffering and without the evil inclination in this world, of what the Holy One will give the righteous in the future? Because he sat in the house of study from his youth until his old age, and was proficient in Scripture and Mishnah, halakhot and aggadot, as it says, “Yaakov was a wholesome man, dwelling in tents.” … Immediately the compassion of the Holy One was stirred, and He gave Yaakov seventeen good years near the end of his life, resembling the World to Come. Hence they said: Anyone who experiences one good year near old age has a good sign; anyone wh
I will restore the fortunes of My people Yisrael. They will rebuild desolate cities and dwell in them; they will plant vineyards and drink their wine, and make gardens and eat their fruit.
I will plant them upon their land, and they shall no longer be uprooted from their land that I have given them, says Hashem your God.
He raised his voice in weeping; Egypt heard, and Pharaoh’s household heard.

“He raised his voice in weeping”: Just as Yosef reconciled with his brothers only through weeping, so the Holy One, blessed be He, redeems Israel only through weeping, as it says, “With weeping they will come, and with supplications I will lead them.”

Rabbi Yeisa opened with the verse: When the Holy One, blessed be He, raises the Community of Israel from the dust and wishes to exact vengeance from the idolatrous nations, then it is written, “Of the peoples no one was with Me.” Here it is written, “No man stood with him when Yosef made himself known to his brothers,” as it says, “He lifted them and carried them all the days of old.”
I trod the winepress alone, and of the peoples no one was with Me. I trod them in My anger and trampled them in My fury; their lifeblood spattered My garments, and I stained all My clothing.
Joseph could not restrain himself before all those standing by him, and he cried, ‘Send everyone out from before me!’ No one stood with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.

Come and see: every trouble that befell Yosef befell Zion. Of Yosef it is written, “Yisrael loved Yosef”; of Zion, “Hashem loves the gates of Zion.” Of Yosef, “They hated him”; of Zion, “She raised her voice against Me; therefore I hated her.” … And the good things that happened to Yosef happened to Zion. Of Yosef, “Yosef was handsome in form and handsome in appearance”; of Zion, “Beautiful in elevation, the joy of all the earth.” Of Yosef, “No one is greater in this house than I”; of Zion, “The glory of this latter house shall be greater.” Of Yosef, “Hashem was with Yosef”; of Zion, “My eyes

It was taught: Rabbi Meir used to say: Great is repentance, for on account of one individual who repents, the entire world is forgiven, as it says, “I will heal their waywardness; I will love them freely, for My anger has turned away from him.” It does not say “from them,” but “from him.”

Chizkiyahu said, “The living, the living—he shall thank You, as I do,” because the living draws close to the Living One. King David is alive, and his closeness is to the Life of all worlds. Whoever draws close to Him is alive, as it is written, “You who cleave to Hashem your God are all alive today.”

What did Shlomo do? Our Rabbis said: He brought David’s coffin and said, “Hashem God, do not turn away the face of Your anointed.” Rabbi Berechyah said in Rabbi Chelbo’s name: At that moment David came to life. You may derive it from David’s own words: “Hashem, You raised my soul from the grave; You kept me alive from descending to the pit.” Shlomo said: “Master of the worlds, act in this man’s merit,” as it says, “Remember the kindnesses of David Your servant.” Immediately he was answered.
Bring them close, one to the other, into one piece of wood, so that they become one in your hand.

The Rabbis said: He warned them against dissension. He told them: “All of you should be one assembly.” This is what is written, “You, son of man, take one piece of wood and write upon it… for the children of Israel…” “His companion” is written [in the singular]. When the children of Israel become one united band, prepare yourselves for redemption. What is written afterward? “I will make you one nation.”
I will make them one nation in the land, upon the mountains of Yisrael, and one king will be king over them all. They will no longer be two nations, nor will they be divided into two kingdoms again.

“I also established My covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan”—because they were circumcised. For everyone who is circumcised inherits the land, since only a righteous one inherits the land, and everyone who is circumcised is called righteous, as it says, “Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.” Everyone who is circumcised and guards this sign of the covenant is called righteous. See Yosef: throughout his life he was not called righteous until he guarded that covenant, the sign of the holy covenant. Once he guarded it, he was called righteous—Yosef the

“Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it”: this is the mystery of the holy covenant. Because all the sources of the body’s limbs are established in this covenant, it includes everything. Similarly, Shabbat comprises the Torah, and all the Torah’s mysteries depend upon it. Observing Shabbat is like observing the entire Torah: whoever keeps Shabbat is as though he kept the whole Torah.
All Israel have a share in the World to Come, as it says, “Your people are all righteous; they will inherit the land forever—the shoot of My planting, the work of My hands, in which to take glory.”

Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai taught: Shabbat said before the Holy One, blessed be He: “Master of the world, every day has a partner, but I have no partner.” The Holy One answered: “The Community of Israel is your partner.” When Israel stood before Mount Sinai, the Holy One told them: “Remember what I told Shabbat: The Community of Israel is your partner.” This is the commandment, “Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it.”
Remember the Shabbat day, to sanctify it.

Five things are one-sixtieth of another: fire, honey, Shabbat, sleep, and a dream. Fire is one-sixtieth of Gehinnom; honey is one-sixtieth of the manna; Shabbat is one-sixtieth of the World to Come; sleep is one-sixtieth of death; and a dream is one-sixtieth of prophecy.

Therefore it is written, “Between Me and the children of Israel.” Because all faith is found in Shabbat, a person is given another soul: a supernal soul, a soul containing every perfection, resembling the World to Come. Therefore it is called Shabbat. What is Shabbat? The name of the Holy One, blessed be He—a name complete in all its aspects.

Rabbi Chanina would wrap himself and stand as Shabbat approached, saying, “Come, let us go out to greet Shabbat the queen.” Rabbi Yannai would put on fine garments, wrap himself, and say, “Come, bride; come, bride.”
“Come, let us go out to greet the bride, the queen.” Some report his words as, “To greet Shabbat—the bride, the queen.” Rabbi Yannai would wrap himself, stand, and say, “Come, bride; come, bride.”
This day is a day of souls, not a day of the body, for the bundle of souls holds dominion. All those above and below stand in a single union, crowned with the additional supernal holy spirit.

When Rav Hamnuna the Elder would emerge from the river on the eve of Shabbat, he would sit for a moment, lift his eyes, and rejoice. He would say that he was sitting to behold the joy of the supernal angels: these ascending and those descending. On every Shabbat eve a person dwells in the world of souls. Fortunate is the one who knows the mysteries of his Master.

Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: Every day a heavenly voice goes forth from Mount Chorev and says: “The entire world is sustained on account of Chanina My son, while Chanina My son suffices with a kav of carobs from one Shabbat eve to the next.”

Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: Every day a heavenly voice goes forth and says: “The entire world is sustained on account of Chanina My son, while Chanina My son suffices with a kav of carobs from one Shabbat eve to the next.”

There was another incident involving Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa, who went to study Torah with Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai. Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai’s son became ill. He said to him: “Chanina, my son, pray for mercy for him, that he may live.” He put his head between his knees, prayed for mercy, and the child lived. Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai said: “Had Ben Zakkai pressed his head between his knees all day long, they would not have heeded him.” His wife asked: “Is Chanina greater than you?” He answered: “No; he is like a servant before the king, while I am like a minister before the king.”

What is [the Messiah’s] name? The school of Rabbi Sheila say: His name is Shiloh, as it says, “Until Shiloh comes.” The school of Rabbi Yannai say: His name is Yinnon, as it says, “May his name endure forever; before the sun, may his name flourish [yinnon].” The school of Rabbi Chanina say: His name is Chanina, as it says, “I will grant you no favor [chaninah].” Some say: His name is Menachem son of Chizkiyah, as it says, “For a comforter [menachem] who would restore my soul is far from me.” The Rabbis say: His name is the afflicted one of Rabbi’s household, as it says, “Surely he bore our ill
“His name is Yinnon”: like Yannai. Each one expounded according to his own name.
He said: I will make all My goodness pass before you, and I will proclaim the name of Hashem before you. I will show favor to whom I show favor, and have mercy upon whom I have mercy.

This disagrees with Rabbi Meir, for Rabbi Meir said: Two [requests] were granted to Moshe and one was not, as it says, “I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious”—even though he is unworthy; “and I will show compassion to whom I will show compassion”—even though he is unworthy.
He saw that there was no man, and was astonished that there was no intercessor. His own arm brought Him salvation, and His righteousness sustained Him.
One who pampers his servant from youth will have him become master in the end.
I said: You are divine beings, and all of you are children of the Most High.

You shall speak to the children of Israel, saying: Nevertheless, you shall keep My Shabbatot, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.
Your eyes saw my unformed substance, and in Your book they were all written: days were formed, and one of them is His.

“Days were fashioned, and one of them is His”: this is Israel’s Shabbat day. How so? A person works all six days and rests on the seventh, finding contentment with his children and household. Again, a person works before his enemies all six days and rests on the seventh, forgetting all the suffering he experienced. Such is the nature of a person: a good day makes him forget a bad day, and a bad day makes him forget a good day.

Rabbah said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: In the future the righteous will be called by the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says, “Everyone called by My name, whom I created for My glory, whom I formed and also made.” Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: Three are called by the name of the Holy One: the righteous, the Messiah, and Jerusalem.

The supernal crown is the crown of kingship. Of it is said, “Declaring the end from the beginning.” It is the skull of the tefillin. Within is the Name spelled Yod-He-Vav-He, which is the path of emanation.

Rava said: Life, children, and sustenance do not depend on merit; rather, they depend on mazal. For Rabbah and Rav Chisda were both righteous sages: when one prayed, rain came, and when the other prayed, rain came.

Bereshit: “Fear Shabbat,” which is the Shechinah, of whom it is said, “Those who profane it shall surely die.” Enemies entered her inner space, the Holy of Holies. Of them it is said, “He defiled the sanctuary of Hashem”; “He profaned the kingdom and its princes.” The maidservant entered the place of the mistress—she who is called menstruant, maidservant, foreign woman, and harlot—and defiled the place where the Shechinah had rested. A voice descended and said, “Fear Shabbat.” But she did not do so; rather, “He profaned the kingdom and its princes,” and the Shechinah fled from there.
Rabbi Yitzchak said: Sunshine on Shabbat is charity for the poor, as it says, “For you who fear My name, a sun of righteousness will shine, with healing in its wings.”

Rabbi Yochanan said in Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s name: If Israel were to observe two Shabbatot according to their laws, they would immediately be redeemed, as it says, “Thus says Hashem to the eunuchs who keep My Shabbatot,” and afterward it says, “I will bring them to My holy mountain.”

Rabbi Acha said in the name of Rabbi Tanchum son of Rabbi Chiyah: If Israel repented for one day, the son of David would come immediately. What is the reason? “Today, if you hear His voice.” Rabbi Levi said: If Israel kept one Shabbat properly, the son of David would come immediately. What is the reason? “Moshe said: Eat it today, for today is Shabbat to Hashem”—one day. And it says, “Through returning and rest you shall be saved”: through returning and resting you shall be redeemed.

Because Yosef guarded the covenant, he was saved from the pit and its snakes and scorpions. Moreover, he merited kingship. Of Israel, who guard Shabbat and the sign of the covenant of circumcision, it is said: “All Israel are children of kings.” If Israel guarded one Shabbat according to its law, they would immediately be redeemed.

Through this, the poison of death—the profaned woman—and her husband, the other god, the profanation of Shabbat, have no permission to draw near. Therefore the early Sages said: If Israel observed one Shabbat according to its law, they would immediately be redeemed.

“Today, if you listen to His voice.” Rabbi Levi said: If Israel observed even one Shabbat properly, they would immediately be redeemed, as it says, “Today, if you listen to His voice,” and it is written, “Keep the day of Shabbat to sanctify it.”

Rabbi Levi said: If Israel observe Shabbat properly, even for one day, the son of David will come. Why? Because it is equal to all the mitzvot, as it says, “For He is our God, and we are the people of His pasture and the flock of His hand—today, if you listen to His voice.” Rabbi Yochanan said: The Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: “Although I have fixed a time for the end, which will come at its appointed time whether they repent or do not repent, if they repent even for one day, I will bring it before its time.” Thus, “Today, if you listen to His voice.”

Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: I too say that not all are destined for light, and not all for joy. The righteous are destined for light, and the upright for joy. The righteous for light, as it says, “Light is sown for the righteous”; the upright for joy, as it says, “And joy for the upright of heart.”
The light of the righteous rejoices, but the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.

In Bereshit are trei, “two,” and Shabbat, thus: bet, reshit; bara shit. These are two Shabbatot, concerning which it is said, “The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat, to make Shabbat.” Shabbat is mentioned here twice, corresponding to the upper and lower Shechinah. “Throughout their generations”—what is ledorotam? Happy is the one who makes them a dwelling on Shabbat in the heart’s two chambers, and removes from there the evil inclination, which is desecration of Shabbat. “An everlasting covenant”—this is the Righteous One, upon whom both dwell: one to fill him, and one to be filled from hi
The children of Yisrael shall keep Shabbat, to observe Shabbat throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant.

On the day of your joy, on your appointed festivals, and at the beginnings of your months, you shall sound the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over your peace offerings. They shall be a remembrance for you before your God; I am Hashem your God.

“On your day of gladness”: these are the Shabbatot. Rabbi Natan says: These are the daily offerings. “On your appointed festivals”: these are the three pilgrimage festivals. “At the beginnings of your months”: as the words indicate.

Rav Yehudah said: A person should never ask for his needs in Aramaic. Rabbi Yochanan said: Whoever asks for his needs in Aramaic—the ministering angels do not attend to him, for the ministering angels do not understand Aramaic. A sick person is different, for the Divine Presence is with him.

The popular explanation that Kaddish is said in Aramaic because it is a beautiful prayer and great praise, and was therefore instituted in the language of the Targum so that the angels would not understand and become jealous of us, does not seem correct. There are many beautiful prayers in Hebrew. Rather, the explanation appears to be what we say at the end of Sotah: The world is sustained only by the order of Kedushah and by “May His great name be blessed” after the aggadic discourse. They were accustomed to say Kaddish after the discourse, where unlearned people were present who did not all

“Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it.” With what do you sanctify it? With Scripture and Mishnah, food and drink, clean clothing, and rest. Whoever delights in Shabbat is as though he honors the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says, “You shall call Shabbat a delight, the holy day of Hashem honored.” This teaches you: If you call Shabbat a delight, then the holy day of Hashem is honored.

Rabbi Tanchum son of Rabbi Chiya said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: It is written, “Sanctify My Shabbatot.” With what do you sanctify it? With food and drink and clean clothing. What is written there? “They shall be a sign between Me and you, that you may know that I am Hashem your God.” “I am Hashem”—I am faithful to pay you your reward. Thus, “He is entirely delightful.”
A river goes out from Eden to water the garden; from there it divides and becomes four heads.

As soon as Israel leave exile as the holy people alone, immediately the river that had been dried and parched is described by, “A river goes out from Eden”—this is the letter vav—“to water the garden.” The river is the central pillar. “Goes out from Eden”: this is the supernal Mother. “To water the garden”: this is the lower Divine Presence.

Rabbi Tanchum son of Rabbi Chiya said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: It is written, “Sanctify My Shabbatot.” With what do you sanctify it? With food and drink and clean clothing. What is written there? “They shall be a sign between Me and you, that you may know that I am Hashem your God.” “I am Hashem”—I am faithful to pay you your reward. Thus, “He is entirely delightful.”

“Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it.” With what do you sanctify it? With Scripture and Mishnah, food and drink, clean clothing, and rest. Whoever delights in Shabbat is as though he honors the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says, “You shall call Shabbat a delight, the holy day of Hashem honored.” This teaches you: If you call Shabbat a delight, then the holy day of Hashem is honored.

Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: The Holy One, blessed be He, gives a person an additional soul on Shabbat eve, and at the departure of Shabbat it is taken from him, as it says, “He ceased and was refreshed [vayinafash]”: once Shabbat has ceased, woe—the soul is lost.

“You shall honor it by refraining from your ways.” “You shall honor it”: your Shabbat clothing should not be like your weekday clothing, as Rabbi Yochanan called his garments “those that honor me.” “Refraining from your ways”: your Shabbat walking should not be like your weekday walking. “From pursuing your affairs”: your own affairs are forbidden, but the affairs of Heaven are permitted.

It is forbidden to afflict oneself on Shabbat. Rather, an Israelite must delight in it through food and drink and honor it with fine clothing and covering, as it says, “You shall call Shabbat a delight,” and “You shall honor it”—your Shabbat clothing should not be like your weekday clothing. For Rabbi Yochanan called the garments he wore on Shabbat “those that honor me.”

Adam, the first man, was the firstborn of the world. When he offered his sacrifice, as it says, “It will please Hashem more than a horned and hoofed ox,” he put on the garments of the High Priesthood, as it says, “Hashem God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife and clothed them.” They were garments of splendor, and the firstborn used them. When Adam died, he passed them to Shet.

When their priestly garments are upon them, their priesthood is upon them. When their garments are not upon them, their priesthood is not upon them. They are then considered non-priests, and the Master said: A non-priest who performs the Temple service is liable to death.

We learned before the Master: What is holiness? The perfection of everything, called supernal wisdom. From that place springs and streams flow in every direction until they reach this Zot. When this Zot is blessed from that supernal place called holiness and wisdom, it is called the Holy Spirit: a spirit from that holiness above.

Rabbi Zeira said in Rav’s name: Whoever teaches an unworthy student is like someone who throws a stone to Markulis, as it says, “Like binding a stone in a sling, so is one who gives honor to a fool,” and it is written, “Delight does not befit a fool.”
Like one who binds a stone in a sling, so is one who gives honor to a fool.

Elazar ben Poirah said to King Yannai: “King Yannai, is your treatment to be like that of an ordinary Israelite, when you are king and High Priest?” “What shall I do?” “If you listen to my advice, trample them.” “And what will become of the Torah?” “It is rolled up and lying in a corner; whoever wishes to learn may come and learn.” Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: At that moment heresy was cast into him, for he should have answered: “That may suffice for the Written Torah, but what of the Oral Torah?”

“Wash yourself, anoint yourself, and put on your garments”: Rabbi Elazar said: These are Shabbat garments. “Give to a wise person and he will become wiser still”: Rabbi Elazar said: This is Ruth the Moabite and Shmuel of Ramah.

Rav Ketina said: Even at the time of Jerusalem’s collapse, trustworthy people did not cease from among them, as it says, “A man will seize his brother in his father’s house: You have a garment; be our leader.” Matters that people conceal like a garment are in your possession.
On that day he will raise his voice and say: I will not be a healer; in my house there is neither bread nor clothing. Do not make me a ruler of the people.

Meanwhile an elder came to him and said: “Faithful Shepherd, prepare the table for your Master, for Him and for the Queen, with every kind of delight, to fulfill ‘This is the table that is before Hashem.’ Until now all have been delighting at the King’s table, as it is written, ‘Come, eat of My bread.’ This is the bread of the Written Torah and the wine of the Oral Torah. There are many delicacies there, varieties of the Torah’s meanings, sweeter than all the foods and delights of the world and of the king.”
Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine I have mixed.
“Things in which people cover themselves”: They hide so that people will not question them, because they are not proficient in these matters.
“A man will seize his brother”: When a man seizes his brother in his father’s house, saying: “You are rich in Torah, and it is clear in your hands like a garment.”
“They shall spread out the garment”: they shall make the matters clear like a garment. This is one of the things that Rabbi Yishmael expounded in the Torah figuratively.

Rabbi Abbahu said: “They shall spread out what he laid against her.” As it was taught: “They shall spread out the garment” teaches that this party’s witnesses and the other party’s witnesses come, and they clarify the matter like a new garment. Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says: The words are literal—an actual garment.

“He shall raise [his voice] on that day”: “raise” here means an oath. He will swear to them, “I will not be a binder”—I will not be one of those bound to the house of study. “In my house there is neither bread nor garment”: I possess neither an explanation of Mishnah nor an explanation of aggadah.
“They cover themselves in them as in a garment”: When people ask them these reasons of Torah, they act as though they are concealing their words, because they do not know how to answer.

What does “for covering the Ancient One” mean? This is one who conceals matters that the Ancient of Days concealed. What are they? The secrets of Torah. Others say: This is one who reveals matters that the Ancient of Days concealed. What are they? The reasons of the Torah.

“Achiyah the Shilonite prophet found him on the road, and he was covered in a new garment, and the two were alone in the field.” What is meant by “a new garment”? Rav Nachman said: Like a new garment. Just as a new garment has no flaw, so Yerovam’s Torah had no flaw. Another explanation: “A new garment”—they introduced teachings that no ear had ever heard.

Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak asked Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman: “Since I have heard that you are a master of aggadah, from where was light created?” He answered: “It teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, wrapped Himself in it like a garment, and the radiance of His splendor shone from one end of the world to the other.” He said this in a whisper. The other asked: “It is an explicit verse, ‘He wraps Himself in light like a garment,’ yet you tell it to me in a whisper?” He answered: “Just as I heard it in a whisper, so I have told it to you in a whisper.”
He wraps Himself in light like a garment, and stretches out the heavens like a curtain.

“A great light”: the light created on the first day, which the Holy One, blessed be He, stored away for those who toil in the Oral Torah by day and night, through whose merit the world endures, as it says, “Thus says Hashem: Were it not for My covenant day and night, I would not have established the laws of heaven and earth.” What covenant is practiced day and night? This is Talmud. Likewise it says, “If you annul My covenant of the day and My covenant of the night… My covenant with David My servant will also be annulled.” And it says, “His desire is in Hashem’s Torah, and he meditates on His

Esther [was a prophetess], for it is written, “On the third day Esther clothed herself in royalty.” It should have said “royal garments”! Rather, the Divine Spirit clothed her. Here it says, “She clothed herself,” and elsewhere it says, “A spirit clothed Amasai.”

On the third day Esther clothed herself in royalty and stood in the inner court of the king’s house, opposite the king’s house. The king sat upon his royal throne in the royal house, opposite the entrance of the house.

It is written, “On the third day Esther clothed herself in royalty”: she clothed herself in the likeness of that world. “Royalty” is the Holy Spirit, for the kingdom of Heaven sends forth a spirit from the breath of that world, and Esther clothed herself in it.

In this arrangement they are called: Chesed, the right arm; Gevurah, the left arm; Tiferet, the torso; Netzach and Hod, the two legs; Yesod, the body’s extremity, the sign of the holy covenant; Malchut, the mouth, which we call the Oral Torah. Chokhmah is the brain, inward thought. Binah is the heart, through which the heart understands. Of these two it is written, ‘The concealed things belong to the Lord our God.’ The upper Keter is the royal crown, of which it says, ‘Declaring the end from the beginning.’ It is the skull of the tefillin; another reading says, the skull that does not put on t
Mordechai went out from before the king in royal clothing of blue and white, with a great golden crown and a wrap of fine linen and purple; and the city of Shushan shouted and rejoiced.

“Which belonged to King Achashverosh.” Rabbi Yudan and Rabbi Levi said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: Wherever this Megillah says “King Achashverosh,” Scripture speaks of King Achashverosh. Wherever it says simply “the king,” it serves both sacred and ordinary meanings.

Rather, this is what it means: Although the prophecy of the prophets, consisting of visions and revelations, was taken away, the prophecy of the sages, which comes through wisdom, was not taken away. They know the truth through the Holy Spirit within them. For on occasion He causes His Divine Presence to rest even upon pious people who are not sages.

We learned that it is forbidden to gaze upon the Divine Presence. Therefore there is tekhelet, for tekhelet is the throne of the house of David and its adornment. This is fear before Hashem: to fear that place. Therefore, “You shall see it and remember all Hashem’s commandments.” This is the throne upon which judgments of life and death are adjudicated, as they explained: All colors are favorable in a dream except tekhelet, for it is the throne that ascends in judgment of life and death.
It shall be tzitzit for you: you shall see it, remember all the commandments of Hashem, and do them. You shall not stray after your heart and after your eyes, after which you go astray.
“White linen, fine cotton, and tekhelet.” What is chur? Rav said: openwork. Shmuel said: He spread white woolen cloth for them. “Karpas”: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said: cushions of fine fabric.
On the third day Joseph said to them, ‘Do this and live, for I fear God.’

“He passed before them.” This is what is written, “As a father has compassion upon children.” Rabbi Chiya taught: Like the most compassionate of the fathers. Who is the most compassionate of the fathers? Rabbi Yehudah said: Avraham, who said, “Far be it from You to do such a thing.” Rabbi Levi said: Yaakov—“He passed before them.” He said: “Better that he strike me than them.”

He said to him: The air of the Garden of Eden is the breath of the Holy Spirit, and the righteous are clothed in it as they were in this world. Afterward the Holy Spirit rests upon each one’s head, is formed into a crown, and becomes his crown. So it was with Mordechai, of whom it is written, “In royal clothing”—the likeness of that world. Afterward, “A great golden crown”: this is the crown that rests on the heads of the righteous in that world. When Israel received the Torah, it was so for them, until they sinned, as it is written, “The children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornamen

Rabbi Simai expounded: When Israel put “We will do” before “We will hear,” six hundred thousand ministering angels came and tied two crowns upon each Israelite, one corresponding to “We will do” and one to “We will hear.” When Israel sinned, one million two hundred thousand destructive angels descended and removed them, as it says, “The children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Chorev.”

I descended for your sake with thousands upon thousands and myriads upon myriads of angels, and entrusted two angels to each one of you: one girded him with his weapon, and one placed a crown on his head. Rabbi Yehudah of Tzippori said: He fastened belts upon them. Rabbi Simai said: He clothed them in royal purple upon which the explicit Divine Name was engraved. All the days they possessed it, no evil thing touched them—neither the Angel of Death nor anything else. When they sinned, Moshe told them, “Now remove your ornaments.”
For wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will be pleasant to your soul.
