What is Shabbat? If you say it is because of cessation, as it says, “For on it He ceased,” that is correct. But the mystery is that when this point ascends and the light shines, she is crowned with the patriarchs. When she is crowned with the patriarchs, she joins and unites with them to become one, and the whole is called Shabbat. Shabbat is shin-bat: shin, as they explained, is the mystery of the three patriarchs, who unite with the only daughter. She is crowned with them, and they with the World to Come; all is one. This is shin-bat, that all should be one.

There is a further mystery: We learned that the world was created with ten utterances, but when you consider it, there are three through which the world was created—wisdom, understanding, and knowledge. The world was created only for Israel’s sake. When He wished to establish the world, He made Avraham in the mystery of wisdom, Yitzchak in the mystery of understanding, and Yaakov in the mystery of knowledge. Thus it is called, “Through knowledge the chambers are filled.” At that time the whole world was perfected. When the twelve tribes were born to Yaakov, everything was perfected in the like

Therefore a person must delight at these three times, for the supernal faith depends upon this: the Holy Ancient One, the Small Countenance, and the field of apples. A person must delight in them and rejoice in them. Whoever omits one of these meals displays a deficiency above, and that person’s punishment is great.

There are three levels, and all are called Shabbat: the supernal Shabbat, the Shabbat of day, and the Shabbat of night. All are one, and the whole is called Shabbat. Each, when it rules, takes its companions and invites them to be with it in its dominion. When this one comes into the world, all come and are invited along with it.

As soon as Israel leave exile as the holy people alone, immediately the river that had been dried and parched is described by, “A river goes out from Eden”—this is the letter vav—“to water the garden.” The river is the central pillar. “Goes out from Eden”: this is the supernal Mother. “To water the garden”: this is the lower Divine Presence.
A river goes out from Eden to water the garden; from there it divides and becomes four heads.

In the teaching of the school of Rav Yeiva Sava we learned: Why are Vav and Dalet included in Yod? The planting of this garden is called Vav. There is another garden, which is Dalet, and from this Vav the Dalet is watered. This is the mystery of “A river goes forth from Eden.” What is Eden? It is supernal wisdom, and it is Yod. “To water the garden”: this is Vav. “From there it divides and becomes four heads”: this is Dalet. Everything is included in Yod.

Delight is “a river going forth from Eden to water the garden,” which is the delight of souls. Vav is the river that goes forth from Eden, from between Yod and He. Eden is none other than the supernal crown, which is wondrous and concealed. Therefore it is said of Eden, “No eye has seen, God, besides You.” “To water the garden”: this is the lower He.
From ancient times they have not heard or given ear; no eye has seen a God besides You who acts for the one who waits for Him.

Bereshit bara: “house” and “head,” which are Father and Mother. Bara, in Aramaic, means “son”; this is the middle pillar, of which it is said, “A river goes forth from Eden.” There is Eden and there is Eden, as it is written, “You give them drink from the stream of Your delights”—Your Edens, indeed. The upper Eden is the supernal crown; the Eden below it is Yod. There is also an Eden below, the supernal Mother, who is Dalet. She is Eden in relation to the river below her, as it is written, “A river goes forth from Eden to water the garden.”

What is the difference between the lower Eden and the upper? Like the advantage of light over darkness. The lower Eden is called feminine delight; the upper Eden is called masculine Eden, of which it is written, “No eye has seen, God, besides You.” This lower Eden is called a garden in relation to the Eden above it, and this garden is called Eden in relation to the garden below it. Those who are in the lower garden delight in this Eden above them every Shabbat and every new moon, as it is written, “From new moon to new moon, and from Shabbat to Shabbat.”

Therefore the Divine Presence is bound to Avraham, Yitzchak, Yaakov, and Yosef. They are together and have one likeness, as it is written, “These are the generations of Yaakov: Yosef.” Hence “from all the merchant’s powders,” for from the place of the river that flows and goes forth everything is watered, and all faces shine.

“These are the generations of Yaakov: Yosef.” As explained, Yaakov’s entire image was within Yosef, and everything that happened to one happened to the other; both go together as one. This is the mystery of the letter Vav [spelled with two vavs], in which both go together as one, for they are one mystery and one image.

Come and see: “Blessed is Adonai, day by day He bears us.” “Blessed is Adonai”—with the letters alef, dalet, nun, and yod. This verse is a mystery of wisdom. “Day by day”: these are the two years, as it says, “At the end of two years, Pharaoh dreamed, and behold, he stood by the river.” This is a mystery, as has been explained: this is Yosef, for this river is Yosef the righteous.
To all of them, to each man, he gave changes of clothing; but to Binyamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothing.
He sent portions to them from before him, and Benjamin’s portion was five times as large as any of theirs. They drank and became intoxicated with him.

“The men took… Yosef saw Binyamin with them… and prepare.” “Prepare” refers to Shabbat, as it says, “On the sixth day they shall prepare…” This teaches that Yosef observed Shabbat before it was given.

“Remember the Shabbat day”: in the mystery of the covenant, which is Yesod, to which Yosef cleaves. Therefore it is called Shabbat, for Yosef is called “all,” and Shabbat is also called “all,” because all delight and pleasure issue from it to sustain all the worlds. Therefore Shabbat includes positive and negative commandments, for Yosef too is the firstborn, who receives two portions.
Remember the Shabbat day, to sanctify it.

Come and see: corresponding to those seven righteous ones, the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded in the Torah that an additional offering be brought on seven occasions in the year, to add delights and pleasures for them from the King’s house, so that the fathers may first be satisfied, and afterward the children. These are seven occasions, and no more. On Shabbat it corresponds to the righteous one, the foundation of the world, who is called “all” and called Shabbat, to add delights for him from the concealed mind. On the new moon it corresponds to the congregation of Israel, who is called th
When the storm passes, the wicked one is no more; but the righteous one is the foundation of the world.

Therefore Yosef and Binyamin are two righteous ones. Yosef merited to be the righteous one above because he guarded the sign of the covenant. Binyamin is the righteous one below, so that the Shemittah may be crowned between the two righteous ones, Yosef the righteous and Binyamin the righteous. Was Binyamin righteous? Yes, for all his days he never sinned against this sign of the covenant, although a trial like Yosef’s did not come his way. If so, why is he called righteous? Rather, throughout all the days that Yaakov mourned for Yosef, he did not engage in marital relations. If you say that w
Light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright of heart.

The Holy One, blessed be He, sowed this light in the garden of His delights and made it into rows through this righteous one, who is the gardener of the garden. He takes this light, sows it as a true planting, and arranges it in rows within the garden. It produces, grows, and bears fruit, and from those fruits the world is sustained, as it is written, “Light is sown for the righteous.”

“To all of them, to each man, he gave changes of clothing, and to Binyamin he gave five changes.” Could that righteous person stumble over the very matter through which he had suffered? For Rava bar Machseya said in Rav Chama bar Gurya’s name, in Rav’s name: Because of the weight of two sela of fine wool that Yaakov gave Yosef beyond his brothers, events developed until our fathers descended to Egypt. Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet said: He hinted to him that a descendant would emerge from him who would go out from before the king in five royal garments, as it says, “Mordechai went out in royal clot
For Yehudah prevailed among his brothers, and a leader came from him, but the birthright belonged to Yosef.
Yehudah, your brothers shall acknowledge you; your hand shall be on your enemies’ neck. Your father’s sons shall bow before you.
Yisrael loved Yosef more than all his sons, for he was a son of his old age, and he made him a coat of many colors.

Come and see: At first yod comprises everything, concealed on all sides, with its paths unopened, encompassing male and female. The upper point of the yod alludes to Ayin, Nothingness. Afterward the yod brings forth the river that flows and issues from it, from which the heh is conceived. Of this it is written, “A river goes out from Eden”—“goes out,” not “went out.” Therefore she must not separate from it, and therefore it is written, “My companion.”

Five names are given to the soul: nefesh, ruach, neshamah, yechidah, and chayah. Nefesh is the blood, as it says, “For the blood is the nefesh.” Ruach ascends and descends, as it says, “Who knows the spirit of human beings, whether it ascends above?” Neshamah is the disposition, as people say, “A good disposition.” Chayah: all the limbs die, while it lives within the body. Yechidah: all the limbs come in pairs, while it is unique in the body.
For wisdom provides shelter, as money provides shelter; but the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom gives life to those who possess it.

“He hinted to him that a descendant would…”: He hinted that Benjamin, his maternal brother, would equal him in greatness. Just as Joseph became second to the king and was clothed in royal clothing, so in the future the king would make Mordechai second to him, and he would go out in royal clothing. You may ask: There should still be jealousy over his giving Benjamin three hundred pieces of silver without giving the same to the other brothers, and no hint is mentioned concerning this. One may answer, as above, that giving more to Benjamin, his brother also through his mother, caused no jealousy.
It is good to give thanks to Hashem, and to sing praise to Your name, Most High.

“It is good to acknowledge Hashem.” Adam said: Let all generations learn from me that whoever acknowledges his transgressions and abandons them is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom, as it says, “It is good to acknowledge Hashem.”

Adam met him [Kayin] and asked, “What happened in your judgment?” He answered, “I repented and reached a settlement.” Adam began striking his face and said, “Such is the power of repentance, and I did not know!” Immediately Adam stood and said, “A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day.” Rabbi Levi said: Adam composed this psalm, but it was forgotten by his generation. Moshe came and renewed it in his name: “A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day. It is good to acknowledge Hashem.”
A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day.

Rabbi Yehudah opened: “Serve Hashem with joy.” We have learned that every service a person wishes to perform for the Holy One, blessed be He, requires joy and heartfelt willingness, so that his service may be complete. If you say that the service of an offering is like this, that seems impossible. The person has transgressed his Master’s command, a command of the Torah, and returned before his Master. With what face can he stand before Him? Certainly with a broken spirit, with a sorrowful spirit. Where is joy? Where is song?
On the day Hashem gives you rest from your pain, from your turmoil, and from the hard labor that was imposed upon you.

Rabbi Shimon said further: We learned that Shabbat is a likeness of the World to Come; it is certainly so. Therefore the sabbatical year and the Jubilee correspond to one another, as do Shabbat and the World to Come. That additional soul comes from the mystery of “Remember” upon this shelter of peace, which receives from the World to Come and gives this addition to the holy people. They rejoice in that addition, and all weekday matters, all sorrow, and all distress are forgotten, as it says, “On the day Hashem gives you rest from your sorrow, from your agitation, and from the hard labor…”
Now, do not be distressed or angry with yourselves that you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.

When Rabbi Akiva reached this verse, he would weep: If someone who intended to obtain pork but instead obtained lamb requires atonement and forgiveness, how much more so someone who intended to obtain pork and actually obtained pork.
From ancient times they have not heard or given ear; no eye has seen a God besides You who acts for the one who waits for Him.
Rabbi Abbahu said: In the place where penitents stand, the completely righteous do not stand, as it says, “Peace, peace to the far and to the near”—first “to the far,” and afterward “to the near.”

Reish Lakish said: Great is repentance, for deliberate sins become inadvertent sins, as it says, “Return, Israel, to Hashem your God, for you have stumbled through your sin.” “Sin” denotes a deliberate act, yet it calls it a stumbling. Is that so? Did Reish Lakish not say: Great is repentance, for deliberate sins become merits, as it says, “When the wicked turns from his wickedness and practices justice and righteousness, he shall live by them”? There is no contradiction: one concerns repentance from love, and the other repentance from fear.

An action removes the effect of an action or an intention; an intention does not remove the effect of either an action or another intention. It is understandable that it does not remove an action, for speech does not come and nullify an action. But why should it not at least remove an intention?

There is no light except that which emerges from darkness. When this side is subdued, the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted on high and honored in His glory. There is no service of the Holy One except from within darkness, and no good except from within evil. When a person enters a bad path and abandons it, then the Holy One is exalted in His glory. Therefore the perfection of everything is good and evil together, followed by ascent in goodness. There is no good except that which emerges from evil; through this good His glory is exalted, and this is complete service.

Ben Azzai says: Run to a minor mitzvah as to a major one, and flee from a transgression. For a mitzvah draws another mitzvah, and a transgression draws another transgression. The reward of a mitzvah is a mitzvah, and the reward of a transgression is a transgression.
They said to one another, ‘Indeed, we are guilty concerning our brother, for we saw the distress of his soul when he pleaded with us, and we did not listen. Therefore this distress has come upon us.’

“And now, lest he stretch out his hand.” Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: This teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, opened for him an opening for repentance. “And now” signifies repentance, as it says, “And now, Israel, what does Hashem your God ask of you?”
They told him: Yosef is still alive, and he rules over all the land of Egypt. His heart grew numb, for he did not believe them.

Why does it say “like years [kashanim]”? It should say “like scarlet [kashani]”! Rabbi Yitzchak said: The Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: “Even if your sins are like these years, which have been ordered and have come from the six days of creation until now, they will become white as snow.”
Come now, let us reason together, says Hashem. Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall become white as snow; though they are red like crimson, they shall become like wool.

Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said in the name of Chilfa bar Agra, who said in Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri’s name: One who tears his garments in anger, breaks his utensils in anger, or scatters his money in anger should be considered in your eyes like an idolater. For this is the craft of the evil inclination: today it tells him, “Do this,” and tomorrow it tells him, “Do that,” until it tells him, “Worship an idol,” and he goes and worships it. Rabbi Avin said: What verse teaches this? “There shall be no foreign god within you.” What foreign god is within a person’s body? This is the evil inclination.
He sent his brothers away, and they went. He said to them: Do not become agitated on the way.

“The men took… Yosef saw Binyamin with them… and prepare.” “Prepare” refers to Shabbat, as it says, “On the sixth day they shall prepare…” This teaches that Yosef observed Shabbat before it was given.

Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said: All the words you read that Yehudah spoke to Yosef before his brothers, until you reach “Yosef could not restrain himself,” contained conciliation for Yosef, conciliation for his brothers, and conciliation for Binyamin. For Yosef: “See how he gives his life for Rachel’s children.” For his brothers: “See how he gives his life for his brothers.” For Binyamin, he said: “Just as I have given my life for you, so I give my life for your brother.”
Joseph could not restrain himself before all those standing by him, and he cried, ‘Send everyone out from before me!’ No one stood with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
Happy is the person who does this, and the son of man who holds fast to it: who guards Shabbat from desecrating it and guards his hand from doing any evil.

Perhaps you will say: What reward does one who observes Shabbat receive? Scripture teaches: “Happy is the person who does this, and the one who holds fast to it: who keeps Shabbat from profaning it and keeps his hand from doing any evil.” Thus we learn that whoever observes Shabbat even under difficult circumstances is saved from transgression.

A tanna taught before Rabbi Yochanan: All kinds of drinks are favorable in a dream except wine: some drink it and it is good for them, while others drink it and it is bad for them. Some drink it and it is good for them, as it says, “Wine gladdens the heart of man.” Others drink it and it is bad for them, as it says, “Give strong drink to one who is perishing, and wine to the embittered in spirit.”
Let Yisrael rejoice in its Maker; let the children of Zion exult in their King.
And wine gladdens the human heart, making the face shine more than oil; and bread sustains the human heart.
To his father he sent the following: ten donkeys carrying the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys carrying grain, bread, and food for his father on the journey.

“To his father he sent the following: ten donkeys carrying the good of Egypt.” What is “the good of Egypt”? Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet said in Rabbi Elazar’s name: He sent him aged wine, which is pleasing to the minds of elders.

“He sent the following”: this amount. What was the amount? “Ten donkeys…” [The gloss explains in the name of Maharshal: The extra word kezot, with the comparative kaf, indicates that he did not actually send ten male and ten female donkeys, but that the verse describes that quantity of their loads.]
Rabbi Chanin said: Wine was created only to comfort mourners and to pay the wicked their reward, as it says, “Give strong drink to one who is perishing.”

“When he sets his eye upon the cup, he walks on level ground.” Rabbi Ammi and Rabbi Assi differed: one said, “Whoever sets his eye upon his cup—all forbidden sexual relations appear to him like level ground.” The other said, “Whoever sets his eye upon his cup—the whole world appears to him like level ground.”
He says to her: “My daughter, much can wine cause; much can levity cause; much can youth cause; much can bad neighbors cause.”
Rabbi says: Why was the passage of the nazir placed next to the passage of the sotah? To tell you that anyone who sees a sotah in her degradation should abstain from wine.
He said to Avram: Know with certainty that your seed will be strangers in a land that is not theirs, and they will enslave them and afflict them for four hundred years.
But I will also judge the nation they serve; afterward they will go out with great wealth.

You alone are Hashem. You made the heavens, the highest heavens and all their host, the earth and all that is upon it, the seas and all that is in them; You give life to them all, and the host of heaven bows before You.
Go and proclaim in the ears of Jerusalem: Thus says Hashem: I remember for you the kindness of your youth, the love of your bridal days, your following Me in the wilderness, in a land not sown.
She lusted after their paramours, whose flesh is like the flesh of donkeys and whose flow is like the flow of horses.
Take your father and your households and come to me. I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat the fat of the land.
“The good of the land of Egypt”: the land of Goshen. He prophesied without knowing what he prophesied: they would ultimately make it like a depth containing no fish.
Your palate is like the finest wine, flowing smoothly to my beloved, making the lips of sleepers stir.

“Making the lips of sleepers move”: Rabbi Yochanan ben Torta said: Even after he has died, his lips move in the grave. What is the reason? “Making the lips of sleepers move.” Shmuel said: Like a vat of grapes that flows of itself. Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa and Rabbi Simon differed: one said, like someone drinking spiced wine; the other said, like someone drinking aged wine—even after he has drunk it, its taste and fragrance remain in his mouth.
The child grew and was weaned, and Avraham made a great feast on the day Yitzchak was weaned.

“I rejoice”: The Midrash [Shocher Tov] explains “For the leader, upon the eighth” as referring to circumcision, which is on the eighth day. Likewise they say in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer, chapter 29: “Avraham made a great feast on the day of higamel Yitzchak”—on the day of heh-gimel, he circumcised Yitzchak; that is, the eighth day of circumcision, equal to the numerical value of heh and gimel. Rabbeinu Tam.

Rabbi Yishmael says: Avraham did not delay anything he had been commanded. When Yitzchak was eight days old, he brought him for circumcision, as it says, “Avraham circumcised his son Yitzchak at eight days old.” He brought him as an offering upon the altar, and made a celebration and feast. From here the Sages said: A person is obligated to make a celebration and feast on the day he merits to circumcise his son, like Avraham our father, as it says, “Avraham made a great feast on the day Yitzchak was weaned.”

“I also established My covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan”—because they were circumcised. For everyone who is circumcised inherits the land, since only a righteous one inherits the land, and everyone who is circumcised is called righteous, as it says, “Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.” Everyone who is circumcised and guards this sign of the covenant is called righteous. See Yosef: throughout his life he was not called righteous until he guarded that covenant, the sign of the holy covenant. Once he guarded it, he was called righteous—Yosef the

Rav Yosef said: Had Acher expounded this verse like Rabbi Yaakov, his daughter’s son, he would not have sinned. What did he see? Some say he saw an incident of this kind. Others say he saw the tongue of Rabbi Chutzpit the interpreter lying in the refuse. He said: “Shall a mouth that produced pearls lick the dust?” He did not know that “so it may be well with you” refers to the world that is entirely good, and “so your days may be long” to the world that is entirely long.
Yours, Hashem, are greatness, might, splendor, victory, and majesty, for everything in the heavens and on the earth is Yours. Yours, Hashem, is kingship, and You are exalted as head over all.

“The child grew and was weaned.” Rabbi Hoshaya the Great said: He was weaned from the evil inclination. The Rabbis said: He was weaned from his mother’s milk. “Avraham made a great feast”: Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Simon said: The Great One of the worlds was there.
Now, Yisrael, what does Hashem your God ask of you, except to fear Hashem your God, to walk in all His ways, to love Him, and to serve Hashem your God with all your heart and all your soul?

“Open for Me an opening like the point of a needle, and I will open supernal gates for you. Open for Me, My sister, for the opening through which to enter to Me is in you. My children enter before Me only through you; you are the opening through which to enter to Me. If you do not open your entrance, I remain closed, so that they cannot find Me. Therefore, open for Me.” Thus David, when he wished to enter before the King, said, “Open for me the gates of righteousness; I will enter them and thank God. This is the gate to Hashem.” This is certainly the opening through which to enter before the K

Rabbi Shimon says: Why did the Torah say, “When a man takes a woman,” rather than “When a woman is taken by a man”? Because it is a man’s way to seek a woman, and not a woman’s way to seek a man. It is like a person who has lost an object: who seeks whom? The owner of the lost object seeks his lost object.

These three mouths were created on the eve of Shabbat at twilight. When the day becomes sanctified, the mouth appointed over all the other mouths ascends. What is it? That day which ascended and became sanctified in all respects, which is called “the mouth of Hashem.” On the eve of Shabbat at twilight the other mouths were created; when the day becomes sanctified, the mouth that rules over all ascends: “the mouth of Hashem.”

This speech is called Shabbat. Because Shabbat is called speech, weekday speech is forbidden on Shabbat, for this speech must rule, and no other. This speech, which comes from the side of darkness, reveals depths from within it. This is the meaning of “from darkness”: that which comes from the side of darkness, as the word “from” precisely indicates.
By the word of Hashem the heavens were made, and by the breath of His mouth all their host.
He made the letter tav king, bound a crown upon it, and formed through it the moon in the universe, the Shabbat day in the year, and the mouth in the person.

God said: Let us make man in our image, according to our likeness, and let them rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of the heavens, the cattle, all the earth, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth.

Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: In all my days I have not seen a deer gathering figs, a lion carrying burdens, or a fox keeping a shop, yet they earn their livelihood without suffering. They were created only to serve me, while I was created to serve my Maker. If those who were created only to serve me earn their livelihood without suffering, should I, who was created to serve my Maker, not earn my livelihood without suffering? Rather, I have corrupted my deeds and impaired my livelihood, as it says, “Your sins have turned these things away.”

Rabbi Elazar said: Every person was created for toil, as it says, “Man is born for toil.” I do not know whether he was created for the toil of the mouth or for physical labor. When it says, “His mouth urges him on,” you must say that he was created for the toil of the mouth. I still do not know whether for the toil of Torah or for conversation. When it says, “This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth,” you must say that he was created for the toil of Torah. This is what Rava said: All bodies are made for toil; fortunate is the one who merits that his toil is in Torah.
Yaakov drew near to his father Yitzchak, who felt him and said: The voice is the voice of Yaakov, but the hands are the hands of Esav.

Rabbi Yitzchak said: Whoever recites Shema upon his bed is as though he holds a double-edged sword in his hand, as it says, “The praises of God are in their throats, and a double-edged sword in their hands.” How does this indicate it? Mar Zutra—or, according to others, Rav Ashi—said: From the beginning of the passage, for it says, “Let the pious exult in glory; let them sing upon their beds,” and afterward it says, “The praises of God are in their throats, and a double-edged sword in their hands.”

“I am a worm and not a man.” Just as a worm strikes cedars only with its mouth, and though soft strikes what is hard, so Israel have only their mouths and their prayer, through which they strike the nations, who are compared to cedars, as it says, “Behold, Assyria was a cedar in Lebanon.” When the nations overpower them, they return in repentance and cry out in prayer, as it says, “Hear, Hashem, the voice of Yehudah.” Likewise it says, “These with chariots and those with horses, but we invoke the name of Hashem our God.” Therefore Israel hold to their fathers’ craft, as it says, “You shall see
Do not fear, worm of Yaakov, people of Yisrael. I will help you, says Hashem, and your redeemer is the Holy One of Yisrael.
You will plant vineyards and work them, but you will not drink wine or gather the grapes, for the worm will consume them.
The exalted praises of God are in their throats, and a double-edged sword is in their hands.
And this is for Yehudah. He said: Hear, Hashem, the voice of Yehudah, and bring him to his people; let his hands contend for him, and be a help against his adversaries.
He sent and brought him. He was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and a good appearance. Hashem said: Rise, anoint him, for this is the one.

Rabbi Huna said in Rabbi Acha’s name: Although ten people composed the book of Psalms, it was attributed to none of their names, but to David king of Israel. They gave a parable: A group of men wished to sing a hymn to the king. The king said, “You are all pleasant, all pious, all praiseworthy in singing a hymn before me; but let this particular man sing on behalf of all of you, because his voice is sweet.” So, when ten righteous men wished to compose the book of Psalms, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: “You are all pleasant, pious, and praiseworthy in singing a hymn before Me; but David sha
Hashem God created man from dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and it became in man a speaking spirit.
Hashem God formed man from dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living being.
On the third day Joseph said to them, ‘Do this and live, for I fear God.’
Rabbi Chelbo said in Rav Huna’s name: Whoever has fear of Heaven—his words are heard, as it says, “The end of the matter, everything is heard: fear God…”

A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If I am a father, where is My honor? If I am a master, where is the fear of Me?—says Hashem of hosts to you, the priests who despise My name. Yet you say, ‘How have we despised Your name?’
He raised his voice in weeping; Egypt heard, and Pharaoh’s household heard.
The report was heard in Pharaoh’s house: Yosef’s brothers have come. It was good in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of his servants.
Take your father and your households and come to me. I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat the fat of the land.
“For it is my mouth speaking to you”: in the holy tongue.
Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Binyamin, that it is my mouth speaking to you.
Joseph could not restrain himself before all those standing by him, and he cried, ‘Send everyone out from before me!’ No one stood with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.

Rabbi Yochanan said in Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s name: If Israel were to observe two Shabbatot according to their laws, they would immediately be redeemed, as it says, “Thus says Hashem to the eunuchs who keep My Shabbatot,” and afterward it says, “I will bring them to My holy mountain.”
I spoke with my heart, saying: Behold, I have increased and added wisdom beyond all who were before me over Jerusalem, and my heart has seen much wisdom and knowledge.

“Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Binyamin.” Rabbi Elazar said: He told them, “Just as I bear no resentment in my heart toward my brother Binyamin, who did not participate in selling me, so I bear none toward you.” “For it is my mouth speaking to you”: as my mouth, so is my heart.
Rabbi Yitzchak said: Sunshine on Shabbat is charity for the poor, as it says, “For you who fear My name, a sun of righteousness will shine, with healing in its wings.”
God spoke to Yisrael in visions of the night, saying: Yaakov, Yaakov. He said: Here I am.
They told him all the words Yosef had spoken to them, and he saw the wagons Yosef had sent to carry him; then the spirit of Yaakov their father revived.
Yisrael said: It is enough; my son Yosef is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.
Yisrael said to Yosef: Now let me die, after I have seen your face, for you are still alive.
Yosef harnessed his chariot and went up to meet his father Yisrael in Goshen. He appeared to him, fell upon his neck, and wept upon his neck still more.
“To the God of his father Yitzchak”: A person is obligated to honor his father more than his grandfather. Therefore he associated [the sacrifice] with Yitzchak and not with Avraham.

Rav Huna said: When Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi came to Tiberias, he asked Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish [why Yaakov offered sacrifices specifically to the God of his father Yitzchak]. Rabbi Yochanan said: A person is obligated to honor his father more than his grandfather. Reish Lakish said: He offered them on account of the covenant of the tribes.
Yisrael journeyed with all that he had and came to Beersheva, and he offered sacrifices to the God of his father Yitzchak.

“God appeared to Yaakov again upon his return.” Rabbi Yitzchak opened: “You shall make Me an altar of stones.” This is an argument from the lesser to the greater: If I reveal Myself and bless someone who builds an altar for My name, how much more so Yaakov, whose likeness is fixed upon My throne!

“My days are fulfilled”: the days my mother told me. Also, my days are fulfilled, for I am eighty-four years old—when will I establish the twelve tribes? This is why he said, “That I may come to her.” Even the most frivolous person would not speak this way! Rather, he said it in order to produce descendants.
Jacob said to Laban, “Give me my wife, for my days have been fulfilled, so that I may come to her.”

Rabbi Acha said: So it is: the Holy One, blessed be He, will awaken the desire needed for union, but it will not be constantly present in a person as it is now, when it is always present and people sin through it. It will exist only for that union, and that awakening will come from the Holy One. This is what is written, “I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.” What is a heart of flesh? Rabbi Yehudah said: A heart for producing flesh, and for nothing else.
I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you. I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh, and give you a heart of flesh.

Rav Acha said: When the righteous sit in tranquility and seek to dwell tranquilly in this world, the Accuser comes and prosecutes: “Is what is prepared for them in the World to Come not enough, that they also seek tranquility in this world?” Know that this is so: because Yaakov our father sought to dwell tranquilly in this world, the adversary of Yosef’s affair confronted him. “Yaakov dwelled”—“I was not at ease, nor was I quiet.” I was not at ease from Esav; I was not quiet from Lavan; I did not rest from Dinah; “and agitation came”—the agitation of Yosef came upon me.

Rabbi Yirmeyah ben Elazar said: During all the years when Adam was under a ban, he begot spirits, demons, and night spirits, as it says, “Adam lived one hundred and thirty years and begot in his likeness, according to his image”—implying that until then he did not beget according to his image. An objection was raised: Rabbi Meir used to say that Adam was exceedingly pious. When he saw that death had been decreed because of him, he fasted for one hundred and thirty years, separated from his wife for one hundred and thirty years, and wore girdles of fig leaves upon his flesh for one hundred and

“He sent Yehudah ahead of him”: to establish a house of study for him, where he would give instruction and teach the tribes. Know that it was so: when Yosef left him, he knew the passage in which they had parted, for he had been teaching him. When Yosef’s brothers came and said, “Yosef is still alive,” his heart grew faint, for he did not believe them. Yaakov remembered that they had parted while studying the passage of the heifer whose neck is broken, and said: “Let him give you a sign of the passage in which we parted, and I will believe you.” Yosef too remembered it and gave them wagons. Wh
He sent Yehudah ahead of him to Yosef, to give direction before him toward Goshen, and they came to the land of Goshen.

We learned: A person should always arouse the good inclination against the evil inclination and exert himself against it. If it departs from him, well and good; if not, let him engage in Torah, for there is nothing that breaks the evil inclination except Torah. If it departs, good; if not, let him remind it of the day of death in order to break it.

So the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: “My children, I created the evil inclination, and I created Torah as its antidote. If you engage in Torah, you are not delivered into its hand, as it says, ‘If you do well, will there not be elevation?’ But if you do not engage in Torah, you are delivered into its hand, as it says, ‘Sin crouches at the entrance.’ Moreover, all its dealings are with you, as it says, ‘Its desire is toward you.’ Yet if you wish, you can rule over it, as it says, ‘And you shall rule over it.’”

A student was following Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei in the marketplace of Zion. [Rabbi Yishmael] saw that he was afraid and told him: “You are a sinner, for it is written, ‘Sinners in Zion are afraid.’” He replied: “But it is written, ‘Fortunate is the person who always fears’!” He answered: “That verse is written concerning matters of Torah.”
Fortunate is the person who is always fearful, but one who hardens his heart will fall into evil.
Sinners in Zion are afraid; trembling has seized the godless. Who among us can dwell with consuming fire? Who among us can dwell with everlasting burning?

“Tell My people their transgression”: these are Torah scholars, whose inadvertent sins are reckoned as deliberate. “And the house of Yaakov their sins”: these are the unlearned, whose deliberate sins are reckoned as inadvertent. This is what we learned: Rabbi Yehudah says, “Be careful in study, for an error in study is reckoned as deliberate wrongdoing.”
Call out with the throat; do not hold back. Raise your voice like a shofar, and tell My people their transgression, and the house of Yaakov their sins.

The choicest of the prophets was Moshe, as it says, “Had not Moshe, His chosen one…” The Holy One, blessed be He, told him, “I will be with you,” yet ultimately he feared, as it says, “Hashem said to Moshe: Do not fear him.” He says “Do not fear him” only to someone who has become afraid.
He said: I am God, the God of your father. Do not fear going down to Egypt, for there I will make you into a great nation.
I will go down with you to Egypt, and I will also surely bring you up; and Yosef will place his hand upon your eyes.
Go and proclaim in the ears of Jerusalem: Thus says Hashem: I remember for you the kindness of your youth, the love of your bridal days, your following Me in the wilderness, in a land not sown.

“You shall not commit adultery”—“Do not stray after your hearts and after your eyes.” Rabbi Levi said: The heart and the eye are the two agents of sin. It is written, “My son, give Me your heart, and let your eyes guard My ways.” The Holy One, blessed be He, said: “If you give Me your heart and your eyes, I know that you are Mine.”

It was taught: “After your hearts”—this is heresy, as it says, “The fool said in his heart: There is no God.” “After your eyes”—this is a thought of sexual transgression, as it says, “Shimshon said to his father: Take her for me, for she is right in my eyes.” “After which you stray”—this is a thought of idolatry, as it says, “They strayed after the Baalim.”

Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: Sarah went down to Egypt and guarded herself against sexual immorality, and all the women guarded themselves through her merit. Yosef went down to Egypt and guarded himself against sexual immorality, and all the men guarded themselves through his merit. Rabbi Pinchas said in Rabbi Chiya’s name: The restraint against sexual immorality was itself sufficient for Israel to be redeemed from Egypt through its merit. What is the reason? “A locked garden is my sister, my bride.” What is written afterward? “Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates.”

Another interpretation: “He sent Yehudah ahead of him.” Rabbi Chanina son of Rabbi Acha and Rabbi Chanina differed: one said, to prepare a dwelling for him; the other said, to prepare a house of assembly where he would teach words of Torah and where the tribes would study.
He sent Yehudah ahead of him to Yosef, to give direction before him toward Goshen, and they came to the land of Goshen.

You alone are Hashem. You made the heavens, the highest heavens and all their host, the earth and all that is upon it, the seas and all that is in them; You give life to them all, and the host of heaven bows before You.

Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: Sarah went down to Egypt and guarded herself against sexual immorality, and all the women guarded themselves through her merit. Yosef went down to Egypt and guarded himself against sexual immorality, and all the men guarded themselves through his merit. Rabbi Pinchas said in Rabbi Chiya’s name: The restraint against sexual immorality was itself sufficient for Israel to be redeemed from Egypt through its merit. What is the reason? “A locked garden is my sister, my bride.” What is written afterward? “Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates.”

“Not one of them was found to be promiscuous”: Know that this was so, for there was one woman, and Scripture publicized her, as it says, “His mother’s name was Shelomit daughter of Divri, of the tribe of Dan.” Shelomit: Rabbi Levi said that she was always chattering in greetings: “Peace to you; peace to you all.” “Daughter of Divri”: Rabbi Yitzchak said that she brought pestilence upon her son. “Of the tribe of Dan”: disgrace to his mother, disgrace to him, disgrace to his family, and disgrace to the tribe from which he came.

“The sister of Lavan”: the sister of the deceitful evil inclination. As we learned: At first, when it was defiled by sins in this world, it was called Lot. In the future, when it is no longer defiled as before, like someone who washes and immerses himself from his impurity, it will be called Lavan [white]. Nevertheless, the evil inclination will not disappear from the world.

Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Yosei was coming from Cappadocia to Lod when Rabbi Yehudah met him. Rabbi Yitzchak said to him: “Would you say that our companions, the sages of the Mishnah, have explained that the evil inclination will be removed from the world except at the time of union?” He answered: “By your life, the evil inclination is needed in the world like rain is needed in the world. Without the evil inclination there would be no joy in discussing a teaching. But it will no longer be defiled as before, so that people sin through it. Thus it is written, ‘They will not harm or destroy thr
Hashem, God of Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yisrael, our fathers, preserve this forever in the formation of the thoughts of Your people’s heart, and direct their heart toward You.
To all of them, to each man, he gave changes of clothing; but to Binyamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothing.
Rather, whose view is this? It is Rabbi Akiva’s, for he said: “Make your Shabbat like a weekday, and do not depend upon other people.”

“To sanctify it”: How do you sanctify it? With food, drink, and clean clothing. Rabbi Chanan said: From here a person must have two wraps, one for weekdays and one for Shabbat. When he expounded this in Tiberias, they said, “Our wrap on Shabbat is the same as our wrap during the week.” He told them: “You must make a change, as it says, ‘Wash, anoint yourself, and put on your garments.’ Was she naked? Rather, she told her: Put on your Shabbat garments.”

Rabbi Tanchum son of Rabbi Chiya said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: It is written, “Sanctify My Shabbatot.” With what do you sanctify it? With food and drink and clean clothing. What is written there? “They shall be a sign between Me and you, that you may know that I am Hashem your God.” “I am Hashem”—I am faithful to pay you your reward. Thus, “He is entirely delightful.”

“Remember the Shabbat day”: in the mystery of the covenant, which is Yesod, to which Yosef cleaves. Therefore it is called Shabbat, for Yosef is called “all,” and Shabbat is also called “all,” because all delight and pleasure issue from it to sustain all the worlds. Therefore Shabbat includes positive and negative commandments, for Yosef too is the firstborn, who receives two portions.
To his father he sent the following: ten donkeys carrying the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys carrying grain, bread, and food for his father on the journey.
On a day of good, be in good; and on a day of evil, consider: God has made the one corresponding to the other, so that a person will find nothing that comes after him.

Rav Adda son of Rabbi Chanina said: Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Yehoshua, which records the arrangement of the land of Israel. What is the reason? “For with much wisdom comes much anger.”

“To his father he sent the following: ten donkeys carrying the good of Egypt.” What is “the good of Egypt”? Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet said in Rabbi Elazar’s name: He sent him aged wine, which is pleasing to the minds of elders.

The Rabbis taught: “Before gray hair you shall rise.” Could this mean even before an unworthy elder? Scripture says “an elder,” and an elder means a sage, as it says, “Gather for Me seventy men from the elders of Israel.” Rabbi Yosei the Galilean says: An elder is only one who has acquired wisdom, as it says, “Hashem acquired me at the beginning of His way.”
Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine I have mixed.

Meanwhile an elder came to him and said: “Faithful Shepherd, prepare a table for your Master, for Him and for the Matron, with every kind of delight, to fulfill ‘This is the table before Hashem.’ Until now, all have enjoyed the King’s table, as it says, ‘Come, eat of My bread.’ This is the bread of the Written Torah and the wine of the Oral Torah. There are many delicacies there—the many meanings of Torah, sweeter than all the foods and delights of the world and of the king.”

Rabbi Chanina said: I asked Rabbi Eliezer in the great assembly house: “How are firstborn donkeys different from firstborn horses and camels?” He told me: “It is a decree of Scripture. Moreover, they assisted Israel when they left Egypt, for not a single Israelite lacked ninety Libyan donkeys loaded with the silver and gold of Egypt.”
She lusted after their paramours, whose flesh is like the flesh of donkeys and whose flow is like the flow of horses.
But I will also judge the nation they serve; afterward they will go out with great wealth.
“The good of the land of Egypt”: the land of Goshen. He prophesied without knowing what he prophesied: they would ultimately make it like a depth containing no fish.
Take your father and your households and come to me. I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat the fat of the land.

Rather, anyone who is able to engage in Torah but does not do so—the Holy One, blessed be He, brings severe sufferings upon him, which trouble him, as it says, “I was mute in silence; I held back from good, and my pain was troubled.” “Good” means only Torah, as it says, “For I have given you a good teaching; do not abandon My Torah.”
For I have given you a good teaching; do not abandon My Torah.
The Torah of Your mouth is better to me than thousands of gold and silver.
“They emptied Egypt”: Rabbi Ammi said: This teaches that they made it like a trap with no grain in it. Reish Lakish said: They made it like a depth with no fish in it.
Hashem gave the people favor in the eyes of Egypt, and they granted their requests; so they emptied Egypt.

Just as these fish grow in water, yet when a single drop falls from above they receive it thirstily, as though they had never tasted water in their lives, so Israel grow in water—in Torah—yet when they hear something new from the Torah, they receive it thirstily, as though they had never heard a word of Torah in their lives.

“I sojourned with Lavan”: Lavan, who is the master of deceivers—I brought him into my grasp; how much more so that man [Esav]! Why did he say, “I sojourned with Lavan and delayed until now”? Because that man’s adversary had not yet been born; now his adversary has been born. Rabbi Pinchas said in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name: It is a tradition that Esav falls only into the hands of Rachel’s children, as it says, “Surely the youngest of the flock will drag them away.” Why are they called the youngest of the flock? Because they are the youngest of the tribes.

Rabbi Levi said: [Yaakov had] six hundred thousand dogs. The Rabbis said: one million two hundred thousand. They do not disagree: according to the one who says six hundred thousand, each flock had one dog; according to the one who says one million two hundred thousand, each flock had two dogs.

“They called his name Esav”: This is the vanity that I created in My world. Rabbi Yitzchak said: “You gave a name to your swine; I too give a name to My firstborn son”—“Thus says Hashem: My firstborn son is Israel.”
Yitzchak loved Esav because game was in his mouth, but Rivkah loved Yaakov.
Your seed shall be like the dust of the earth, and you shall spread out westward, eastward, northward, and southward; through you and through your seed all the families of the earth shall be blessed.

“Until I come to my lord at Seir”: Rabbi Abahu said: We searched all of Scripture and never found that Yaakov our father went to Esav at Mount Seir in his lifetime. Is it possible that Yaakov was truthful yet deceived him? Rather, when would he come to him? In the future, as it is written, “Saviors will ascend Mount Zion to judge the mountain of Esav.”
Please let my lord pass before his servant, while I move along slowly, at the pace of the work before me and at the pace of the children, until I come to my lord at Seir.
Saviors shall ascend Mount Zion to judge the mountain of Esav, and kingship shall belong to Hashem.

Reish Lakish said: May I be an atonement for Rabbi Chiya and his sons! For at first, when Torah was forgotten from Israel, Ezra came up from Babylonia and established it. It was forgotten again; Hillel the Babylonian came up and established it. It was forgotten again; Rabbi Chiya and his sons came up and established it.

Rabbi Abba said: Come and see what is written: “Avraham listened to Efron, and Avraham weighed out the silver for Efron.” This is the great longing of those worlds and yearnings. “Four hundred shekels of silver”: four hundred worlds, delights, and yearnings. “Current with the merchant”: Rav Nachman said that [the soul] passes through all the gates of heaven and the Jerusalem above, and none prevents her.
Avraham listened to Ephron, and Avraham weighed out for Ephron the silver he had named in the hearing of the children of Chet: four hundred silver shekels, current with the merchant.

Rabbi Yehudah asked Rabbi Chiya: “We learned that the Holy One, blessed be He, will prepare a feast for the righteous in the future. What is it?” He answered: “Before I went before those holy angels, the masters of the Mishnah, this is what I heard. When I heard Rabbi Elazar’s teaching, it became settled in my heart. Rabbi Elazar said: The feast of the righteous in the future is like ‘They beheld God, and ate and drank.’ This is what we learned: they are sustained. In one place we learned ‘they enjoy,’ and elsewhere ‘they are sustained.’ What is the difference? His father explained: The righte

Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will bequeath to every righteous person three hundred and ten worlds, as it says, “To bequeath substance to those who love Me, and I will fill their treasuries.”
To cause those who love me to inherit substance, and I will fill their treasuries.

Rava said: When a person is brought to judgment, they ask him: “Did you conduct business faithfully? Did you set fixed times for Torah? Did you engage in procreation? Did you await salvation? Did you reason deeply in wisdom? Did you infer one thing from another?” Even so, if “the fear of Hashem is his treasury,” yes; if not, no. It is like a person who told his agent, “Bring a kor of wheat up to the loft for me.” He brought it up. The owner asked, “Did you mix a kav of preservative into it?” He said, “No.” He replied, “It would have been better had you not brought it up.”
The faithfulness of your times will be a store of salvations, wisdom, and knowledge; fear of Hashem is his treasure.

David said, “The fear of Hashem is pure, enduring forever.” What does this mean? You may find a person who studies midrash, laws, and aggadot; if he has no fear of sin, he has nothing. It is like a person who tells his friend, “I have a thousand measures of grain, a thousand measures of oil, and a thousand of wine.” His friend asks, “Do you have storehouses in which to put them? If you do, everything is yours; if not, you have nothing.” So, when a person studies everything, they tell him: “If you have fear of sin, everything is yours,” as it says, “The faithfulness of your times shall be… the

A bent tzadi and a straight tzadi signify a bent righteous person and a straight righteous person. But this is the same as a bent faithful person and a straight faithful person! Scripture adds further bending to his bending. From here we learn that Torah was given with the head bowed.
Your people are all righteous; they will inherit the land forever—the shoot of My planting, the work of My hands, in which to be glorified.
On the third day Joseph said to them, ‘Do this and live, for I fear God.’
How great is Your goodness that You have stored away for those who fear You, that You have worked for those who take refuge in You, before the children of man.
“A load of three hundred”: This is not exact, and so it is with every instance of three hundred in the Talmud.
He made the letter tav king, bound a crown upon it, and formed through it the moon in the universe, the Shabbat day in the year, and the mouth in the person.

He blessed it through the light of a person’s face; He sanctified it through the light of a person’s face. The light of a person’s face throughout the days of the week is unlike its appearance on Shabbat.
God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on it He rested from all His work that God created to do.

Reish Lakish said in Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya’s name: The rounded part of Adam’s heel eclipsed the orb of the sun—how much more so the appearance of his face! Do not be surprised: ordinarily, when a person makes two salvers, one for himself and one for his household, which does he make more beautiful? His own. So Adam was created to serve the Holy One, blessed be He, while the orb of the sun was created to serve the creatures.

This follows the Rabbis and does not follow Rabbi Ammi, for Rabbi Ammi said: Adam’s glory did not remain with him overnight. What is the reason? “Man does not lodge in splendor; he is likened to the beasts that perish.” The Rabbis said: His glory did remain with him overnight; at the end of Shabbat his radiance was taken from him, and he was driven from the Garden of Eden, as it is written, “You change his face and send him away.”
You overpower him forever, and he goes; You change his face and send him away.

Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai said: The Holy One, blessed be He, does not attach His name to the righteous during their lifetimes, but only after their deaths, as it says, “To the holy ones who are in the earth.” When are they holy? When they are buried in the earth. As long as they live, the Holy One does not attach His name to them. Why? Because He does not trust them that the evil inclination will not mislead them. Once they die, He attaches His name to them.
Behold, He does not trust in His holy ones, and the heavens are not pure in His eyes.

When [Rabbi Bena’ah] reached Adam’s burial cave, a heavenly voice went forth and said: “You have looked upon the likeness of My image; do not look upon My image itself.” He said, “But I need to mark the cave!” It answered: “The dimensions of the inner cave are the same as those of the outer one.” According to the view that there were two chambers, one above the other: “The dimensions of the lower chamber are the same as those of the upper one.”

God said: Let us make man in our image, according to our likeness, and let them rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of the heavens, the cattle, all the earth, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth.

Rabbi Yudan said: Great is the power of the prophets, who compare the form to its Maker, as it says, “I heard a human voice between the banks of Ulai.” Rabbi Yehudah bar Simon said: We have another verse clearer than this: “Upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness with the appearance of a human being upon it, above.”

Above the expanse over their heads was the likeness of a throne, like the appearance of sapphire stone; and above the likeness of the throne was a likeness like the appearance of a man upon it, above.

“God appeared to Yaakov again upon his return.” Rabbi Yitzchak opened: “You shall make Me an altar of stones.” This is an argument from the lesser to the greater: If I reveal Myself and bless someone who builds an altar for My name, how much more so Yaakov, whose likeness is fixed upon My throne!

Rabbi Yosei said: “How is it possible that Yaakov’s beauty was Adam’s beauty? We learned that the rounded part of Adam’s heel eclipsed the orb of the sun! Would you say that Yaakov was like that?” Rabbi Elazar replied: “Certainly it was so. At first, before Adam sinned, no creatures could look upon his beauty. Once he sinned, his beauty changed, his height was diminished, and he became one hundred cubits tall. Come and see: Adam’s beauty is a mystery upon which supernal faith depends. Therefore, ‘May the pleasantness of Hashem our God be upon us,’ and ‘To behold the pleasantness of Hashem.’ Th

The truth of the matter is that Yaakov was a supernal image and a holy body. Since the day of Adam, there had been no body like Yaakov’s body. The very beauty of Adam was Yaakov’s beauty, and Yaakov’s image was the very image of Adam.

A certain noblewoman said to Rabbi Yehudah: “A teacher—and drunk?” He told her: “By my faith, woman, I taste wine only for kiddush, havdalah, and the four cups of Pesach, and I must bind my temples from Pesach until Shavuot. Rather, ‘A person’s wisdom lights up his face.’”
Who is like the wise person, and who knows the interpretation of a matter? A person’s wisdom lights up his face, and the sternness of his face is changed.
A joyful heart makes the face good, but through sorrow of heart the spirit is broken.

“God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it.” It is written, “The blessing of Hashem makes rich, and He adds no sorrow with it.” “The blessing of Hashem makes rich”: this is Shabbat, as it says, “God blessed the seventh day.” “He adds no sorrow with it”: this is mourning, as it says, “The king was grieved over his son.”
The blessing of Hashem makes rich, and He adds no sorrow with it.
When he sees his children, the work of My hands, in his midst, they will sanctify My name; they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob and stand in awe of the God of Israel.

King David further said: “My fear arose from my joy, my joy arose from my fear, and my love surpassed them all. Therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, made a covenant with me that I would be proficient in Scripture and Mishnah, laws and aggadot, as it says, ‘Is not my house thus with God? For He established an everlasting covenant for me, arranged in everything and preserved; for all my salvation and all my desire—will He not make it grow?’” A covenant means Torah, as it says, “My covenant was with him, life and peace.” “Arranged in everything”: in Scripture, Mishnah, laws, and aggadot. “Prese

“Israel loved Yosef”: Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Nechemyah differed. Rabbi Yehudah said that the radiance of his face resembled his father’s. Rabbi Nechemyah said that all the laws Shem and Ever had transmitted to Yaakov, he transmitted to Yosef.
Yisrael loved Yosef more than all his sons, for he was a son of his old age, and he made him a coat of many colors.

Yosef saw his brothers and recognized them, but he acted as a stranger toward them and spoke harshly with them. He said to them: Where have you come from? They said: From the land of Canaan, to buy food.
“He acted as a stranger toward them”: He made himself like a stranger to them in his words, speaking harshly.

Rashi wrote: “He made himself like a stranger to them in his words, speaking harshly to them.” According to his view, “he acted as a stranger” would mean that he spoke like a foreign man. This is not correct.
Yosef said to his brothers: I am Yosef. Is my father still alive? His brothers could not answer him, for they were overwhelmed before him.
Yosef harnessed his chariot and went up to meet his father Yisrael in Goshen. He appeared to him, fell upon his neck, and wept upon his neck still more.

I do not know the reason for “he appeared to him,” since it is obvious that they saw one another when he fell upon his neck. Moreover, it is not respectful for Yosef to fall upon his father’s neck; he should bow to him or kiss his hands, as it says, “Yosef brought them out from between his knees and bowed with his face to the ground.” This occasion was even more fitting for bowing to him.

“He wept upon his neck still more”: This denotes abundant weeping. Likewise “For He does not place upon a person more” uses “more” as an expression of addition: He does not place charges upon him beyond his sins. Here too, he wept greatly and added tears beyond the usual measure. But Yaakov did not fall upon Yosef’s neck or kiss him. Our Rabbis said that he was reciting Shema.
Rami bar Abba said: A wild animal does not gain power over a human being until he appears to it like an animal, as it says, “Man does not lodge in splendor; he is likened to the beasts that perish.”
He recognized it and said: It is my son’s coat. A wild animal has devoured him; Yosef has surely been torn apart.

Rabbi Elazar said: Even though the soul is no longer within them, the righteous do not change from the image they originally had. But when a person does not walk in the paths of Torah, that holy image changes in him. Then the beasts of the field and birds of heaven can gain power over him: because that holy image has changed, his human image has changed.
All his sons and all his daughters rose to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. He said: For I will go down to my son mourning, to the grave. And his father wept for him.
Yisrael said: It is enough; my son Yosef is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.

The Rabbis taught: Three people were given a taste of the World to Come by the Holy One, blessed be He, in this world: Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov. Of Avraham it is written “with everything”; of Yitzchak, “of everything”; of Yaakov, “everything.” Three people were not ruled by the evil inclination: Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov, of whom it is written “with everything,” “of everything,” and “everything.” Some say David as well, for it is written, “My heart is emptied within me.” The other opinion understands him to be recalling his suffering.
Please take my blessing that has been brought to you, for God has favored me, and I have everything. He urged him, and he took it.

Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi raised a contradiction: It is written, “Behold, I am with you, and I will guard you wherever you go,” yet it is written, “Yaakov was greatly afraid.” He said: “Perhaps sin will cause [the promise not to be fulfilled].”
I am diminished by all the kindnesses and all the truth that You have done with Your servant, for with my staff I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.
He does not fear evil tidings; his heart is firm, trusting in Hashem.
One thing I have asked of Hashem, that I seek: to dwell in the house of Hashem all the days of my life, to behold the pleasantness of Hashem, and to contemplate in His sanctuary.
Yisrael said to Yosef: Now let me die, after I have seen your face, for you are still alive.

Therefore a person should not make his voice heard in prayer, but should pray in a whisper, with that voice which is not heard. This is the prayer that is always accepted. Your sign is “The voice was heard”: kol, written without a vav, is heard. This is prayer in silence, as it is written of Channah, “Her voice was not heard.” This is the prayer the Holy One, blessed be He, accepts when it is offered with desire, intention, and proper order, and to unify the unity of one’s Master properly every day.
The report was heard in Pharaoh’s house: Yosef’s brothers have come. It was good in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of his servants.
But God has indeed heard; He has attended to the voice of my prayer.
Therefore it says, “The voice was heard in Pharaoh’s house.” This voice is none other than Yehudah’s voice, as it says, “Hear, Hashem, the voice of Yehudah.”
And this is for Yehudah. He said: Hear, Hashem, the voice of Yehudah, and bring him to his people; let his hands contend for him, and be a help against his adversaries.

“Yehudah approached him.” Rabbi Yehudah, Rabbi Nechemyah, and the Rabbis differ. Rabbi Yehudah says: an approach for battle, as in “Yoav and the people with him approached for battle.” Rabbi Nechemyah says: an approach for conciliation, as in “The children of Yehudah approached Yehoshua,” to conciliate him. The Rabbis say: an approach for prayer, as in “Eliyahu the prophet approached and said: Hashem, God…” Rabbi Elazar explained it to them: “If for battle, I am coming; if for conciliation, I am coming; if for prayer, I am coming.”
Yehudah approached him and said: Please, my lord, let your servant speak a word in my lord’s ears, and do not let your anger burn against your servant, for you are like Pharaoh.
“The good of the land of Egypt”: the land of Goshen. He prophesied without knowing what he prophesied: they would ultimately make it like a depth containing no fish.
Take your father and your households and come to me. I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat the fat of the land.
Let your eyes not spare your possessions, for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.

“To his father he sent the following: ten donkeys carrying the good of Egypt.” What is “the good of Egypt”? Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet said in Rabbi Elazar’s name: He sent him aged wine, which is pleasing to the minds of elders.
To his father he sent the following: ten donkeys carrying the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys carrying grain, bread, and food for his father on the journey.

“Making the lips of sleepers move”: Rabbi Yochanan ben Torta said: Even after he has died, his lips move in the grave. What is the reason? “Making the lips of sleepers move.” Shmuel said: Like a vat of grapes that flows of itself. Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa and Rabbi Simon differed: one said, like someone drinking spiced wine; the other said, like someone drinking aged wine—even after he has drunk it, its taste and fragrance remain in his mouth.

“He sent Yehudah ahead of him”: to establish a house of study for him, where he would give instruction and teach the tribes. Know that it was so: when Yosef left him, he knew the passage in which they had parted, for he had been teaching him. When Yosef’s brothers came and said, “Yosef is still alive,” his heart grew faint, for he did not believe them. Yaakov remembered that they had parted while studying the passage of the heifer whose neck is broken, and said: “Let him give you a sign of the passage in which we parted, and I will believe you.” Yosef too remembered it and gave them wagons. Wh
He sent Yehudah ahead of him to Yosef, to give direction before him toward Goshen, and they came to the land of Goshen.

“He sent Yehudah ahead of him.” This is what Scripture says: “Dominion and dread are with Him; He makes peace in His heights.” “Dominion” is Michael, and “dread” is Gabriel. Michael is of water and Gabriel of fire, yet they stand before the Divine Presence and do not harm one another. Thus, “He makes peace in His heights.”
Dominion and dread are with Him; He makes peace in His heights.

The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: If this despicable one [the evil inclination] encounters you, draw him into the house of study. If he is stone, he will dissolve; if he is iron, he will shatter. If he is stone, he will dissolve, for it is written, “Ho, everyone who thirsts, go to water,” and “Water wears away stones.” If he is iron, he will shatter, for it is written, “Is not My word like fire, says Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters rock?”
Is not My word like fire, says Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters rock?

Rabbi Oshaya said: Why are words of Torah compared to these three liquids—water, wine, and milk—as it says, “Ho, everyone who thirsts, go to water,” and “Go, buy and eat; go, buy wine and milk without money and without price”? To tell you: Just as these three liquids are preserved only in the lowliest vessels, so words of Torah are preserved only in someone whose mind is humble.
Ho, all who thirst, go to water; and the one who has no money, go, buy and eat. Go, buy wine and milk without money and without price.

“The spirit of God hovered”: this is the spirit of the Messiah, as it says, “The spirit of Hashem will rest upon him.” Through what merit does it approach and come? “Hovering over the face of the waters”: through the merit of repentance, which is compared to water, as it says, “Pour out your heart like water.”

Rise, cry out at night, at the beginning of the watches; pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord. Lift your hands to Him for the life of your young children, who faint from hunger at the head of every street.

“He sent Yehudah ahead of him.” Let our teacher instruct us: When do we recite the blessing over the lamp at the end of Shabbat? Our Rabbis taught: We do not bless over the lamp until we benefit from its light. From whom did they learn this? From the Holy One, blessed be He, for it says, “God saw the light, that it was good,” and afterward, “God separated the light from the darkness.” Rabbi Zeira bar Abahu said: From here we learn that we bless over the lamp at the end of Shabbat once we benefit from its light.
He fell upon the neck of his brother Benjamin and wept, and Benjamin wept upon his neck.

The Rabbis taught: An incident occurred with Miriam daughter of Bilgah, who abandoned her religion and married an officer of the Greek kings. When the Greeks entered the Sanctuary, she struck the altar with her sandal and said: “Wolf, wolf! How long will you consume Israel’s wealth without standing by them in their hour of distress?” When the Sages heard of it, they fixed her priestly watch’s ring in place and sealed its window.

“Behold, we heard of it in Efratah; we found it in the fields of the forest.” “In Efratah”: this is Yehoshua, who came from Ephraim. “We found it in the fields of the forest”: this is Binyamin, of whom it is written, “Binyamin is a wolf that tears.”
Binyamin is a wolf that tears: in the morning he consumes prey, and in the evening he divides spoil.
Behold, we heard of it in Efratah; we found it in the fields of the forest.

“He fell upon the necks of his brother Binyamin.” How many necks did Binyamin have? Rabbi Elazar said: He wept over the two Temples that would be in Binyamin’s portion and would be destroyed. “Binyamin wept upon his neck”: he wept over the Tabernacle of Shiloh, which would be in Yosef’s portion and would be destroyed.
Joseph saw Benjamin with them and said to the one in charge of his house, ‘Bring the men into the house, slaughter an animal, and prepare, for the men will eat with me at noon.’
Yosef hurried, for his compassion was stirred toward his brother, and he sought a place to weep. He entered the inner room and wept there.

The woman saw that the tree was good for food, that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was desirable for gaining understanding. She took of its fruit and ate, and she gave also to her husband with her, and he ate.

When the serpent came upon Chavah, he introduced impurity into her. Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai—their impurity ceased. The nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai—their impurity did not cease. Rav Acha son of Rava asked Rav Ashi: “What of converts?” He answered: “Although they were not present, their spiritual roots were present, as it says, ‘Those who are here with us, standing today before Hashem our God, and those who are not here…’”

Therefore Yosef and Binyamin are two righteous ones. Yosef merited to be the righteous one above because he guarded the sign of the covenant. Binyamin is the righteous one below, so that the Shemittah may be crowned between the two righteous ones, Yosef the righteous and Binyamin the righteous. Was Binyamin righteous? Yes, for all his days he never sinned against this sign of the covenant, although a trial like Yosef’s did not come his way. If so, why is he called righteous? Rather, throughout all the days that Yaakov mourned for Yosef, he did not engage in marital relations. If you say that w

Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah said: Woe to us from the day of judgment! Woe to us from the day of rebuke! If Yosef the righteous, who was flesh and blood, rebuked his brothers and they could not withstand his rebuke, how much more so the Holy One, blessed be He, who is judge and litigant, sits upon the throne of judgment, and judges each person—no flesh and blood can withstand Him!

When Rabbi Elazar reached this verse, he wept: “His brothers could not answer him, for they were overwhelmed before him.” If the rebuke of flesh and blood is so, how much more so the rebuke of the Holy One, blessed be He!
Yosef said to his brothers: I am Yosef. Is my father still alive? His brothers could not answer him, for they were overwhelmed before him.

“Let us appoint Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah: he is wise, wealthy, and a tenth-generation descendant of Ezra. He is wise, so if someone challenges him, he can answer; wealthy, so if service at Caesar’s court is needed, he too can go and serve; and a tenth-generation descendant of Ezra, so he has ancestral merit and cannot readily be punished.” … His wife told him: “You have no white hair.” He was eighteen years old that day; a miracle occurred, and eighteen rows of white hair appeared. This is why Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah said, “I am like a seventy-year-old,” rather than “seventy years old.”

Rabbi Yochanan said: Woe to us from the day of judgment! Woe to us from the day of rebuke! When Yosef said to his brothers, “I am Yosef,” their souls departed. When the Holy One, blessed be He, stands in judgment—of whom it is written, “Who can endure the day of His coming, and who can stand when He appears?” and “A person cannot see Me and live”—how much more so! If his brothers were overwhelmed before Yosef, how much more so when the Holy One comes to demand an account for the dishonor of the commandments and the transgression against Torah!
Who can endure the day of His coming, and who can stand when He appears? For He is like a refiner’s fire and like launderers’ soap.
He said: You cannot see My face, for a human being cannot see Me and live.

“I have placed Hashem before me always” is a great principle in Torah and in the virtues of the righteous who walk before God. A person’s sitting, movements, and affairs when alone in his house are unlike his sitting, movements, and affairs before a great king. Nor are his speech and free expression with his household and relatives like his speech in the king’s presence. How much more so when a person takes to heart that the great King, the Holy One, blessed be He, whose glory fills the whole earth, stands over him and sees his deeds, as it says, “Can a person hide in secret places and I not s

They said to [Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai]: “Our teacher, bless us.” He told them: “May it be His will that the fear of Heaven be upon you like the fear of flesh and blood.” His students asked: “Only to this extent?” He answered: “If only! Know that when a person commits a transgression, he says: Let no person see me.”

Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, fills the entire world, so the soul fills the entire body. Just as the Holy One sees but is not seen, so the soul sees but is not seen. Just as the Holy One sustains the whole world, so the soul sustains the whole body. Just as the Holy One is pure, so the soul is pure. Just as the Holy One dwells in the innermost chambers, so the soul dwells in the innermost chambers. Let that which possesses these five qualities come and praise Him who possesses these five qualities.

Therefore the masters of the Mishnah taught: “Study is not the essential thing, but action.” Since the Holy One, blessed be He, is hidden in the mysteries of Torah, through what is He known? Through the commandments, which are His Shechinah, His image. Just as He is humble, His Shechinah is humility. He is pious, and she is piety. He is mighty, and she is mistress over all the nations of the world. He is truth, and she is faith.
You will give truth to Jacob and kindness to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from days of old.

Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: “Yaakov called his sons and said: Gather, and I will tell you.” Yaakov wished to reveal the final end to his sons, but the Divine Presence departed from him. He said: “Perhaps, Heaven forbid, there is a flaw among my children, as Yishmael came from Avraham and Esav came from my father Yitzchak?” His sons said to him: “Hear, Israel: Hashem our God, Hashem is One.” They said: “Just as there is only One in your heart, so there is only One in our hearts.” At that moment Yaakov our father began and said: “Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.”

It was taught: “So that His fear should be upon your faces”—this is shame. “So that you do not sin”—this teaches that shame leads to fear of sin. From here they said: It is a good sign in a person that he is bashful. Others say: Anyone who feels shame will not readily sin. Whoever has no shame—it is known that his ancestors did not stand at Mount Sinai.
Moshe said to the people: Do not fear, for God has come to test you, and so that His fear may be upon your faces, so that you do not sin.
Face to face Hashem spoke with you on the mountain, from within the fire.
