I said: My God, I am ashamed and humiliated to raise my face to You, my God, for our iniquities have multiplied above our heads, and our guilt has grown to the heavens.
“They were overwhelmed before him”: because of shame.
Rabbi Yitzchak said: Sunshine on Shabbat is charity for the poor, as it says, “For you who fear My name, a sun of righteousness will shine, with healing in its wings.”

The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: Did I not write for you in My Torah, “This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth”? Although you work during all six days, let Shabbat be devoted entirely to Torah. Hence they said: A person should rise early and study on Shabbat, go to the synagogue and house of study, read the Torah and study the Prophets, and afterward go home to eat and drink, fulfilling “Go, eat your bread with joy and drink your wine with a good heart.” For the Holy One has rest only with those who practice Torah, as it says, “My hand made all these… But to this one I
Thus says Hashem: The heavens are My throne and the earth is My footstool. What house could you build for Me, and where is the place of My rest?
My hand made all these things, and so all these things came to be, says Hashem. But to this one I will look: to the poor and broken in spirit, who trembles at My word.

“Fortunate is the man who fears Hashem.” Is a man fortunate, but not a woman? Rav Amram said in Rav’s name: Fortunate is one who repents while still a vigorous man. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Fortunate is one who masters his inclination like a man.
Praise Yah. Fortunate is the person who fears Hashem, who greatly desires His commandments.

“It is good to acknowledge Hashem.” Adam said: Let all generations learn from me that whoever acknowledges his transgressions and abandons them is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom, as it says, “It is good to acknowledge Hashem.”
It is good to give thanks to Hashem, and to sing praise to Your name, Most High.
One who conceals his transgressions will not succeed, but one who acknowledges and abandons them will receive mercy.

Adam met him [Kayin] and asked, “What happened in your judgment?” He answered, “I repented and reached a settlement.” Adam began striking his face and said, “Such is the power of repentance, and I did not know!” Immediately Adam stood and said, “A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day.” Rabbi Levi said: Adam composed this psalm, but it was forgotten by his generation. Moshe came and renewed it in his name: “A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day. It is good to acknowledge Hashem.”
A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day.

He opened: “May Hashem bless you from Zion, and see the good of Jerusalem.” “May Hashem bless you from Zion”: from there blessings emerge to water the garden. It comprises all blessings and gives them to her; afterward, “See the good of Jerusalem.” This shows that all blessings come from male and female. Similarly, “May Hashem bless you and guard you”: “May Hashem bless you”—from the male; “and guard you”—from the female. “May Hashem bless you”—from Remember; “and guard you”—from Guard. It is all one matter, for from both of them blessings emerge to the worlds. Therefore, “He blessed them, eac
May Hashem bless you and guard you.

Rabbi Elazar said: They went out into the wilderness to look, but the Holy One, blessed be He, had removed the radiance of His glory from there; they went to look upon Him but did not find Him. We learned that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called Torah; water means Torah, and Torah is none other than the Holy One, blessed be He.

Act from love and act from fear. Act from love, so that if you come to hate, know that you love, and one who loves does not hate. Act from fear, so that if you come to rebel, know that you fear, and one who fears does not rebel.
God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.

There is no light except that which emerges from darkness. When this side is subdued, the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted on high and honored in His glory. There is no service of the Holy One except from within darkness, and no good except from within evil. When a person enters a bad path and abandons it, then the Holy One is exalted in His glory. Therefore the perfection of everything is good and evil together, followed by ascent in goodness. There is no good except that which emerges from evil; through this good His glory is exalted, and this is complete service.

Rabbi Elazar opened: “Because you have become precious in My eyes, you have been honored, and I have loved you; I will give people in your place, and nations in place of your life.” “You have become precious”: it should have said “precious”—“because you are precious in My eyes.” What is “you have become precious”? It implies that he made himself precious. This is certainly so: anyone who is guilty before the Holy One, blessed be He, is at first held in contempt and is an abomination before Him. After he reconsiders and repents of his sin, he has now made himself precious. The Holy One proclaim
Because you have become precious in My eyes, you have been honored, and I have loved you. I will give people in your place, and nations in place of your life.

Fortunate are the masters of repentance, for in one hour, in one day, in one moment they draw close to the Holy One, blessed be He, in a way that even the completely righteous did not attain except by drawing close to Him over many years. Avraham did not enter those supernal days until he was old, as explained. Likewise David, as it says, “King David was old, advanced in days.” But the master of repentance immediately enters and cleaves to the Holy One, blessed be He.
This day is a day of souls, not a day of the body, for the bundle of souls holds dominion. All those above and below stand in a single union, crowned with the additional supernal holy spirit.

So too, the Holy One, blessed be He, brings the soul and places it within the body, and judges them together, as it says, “He calls to the heavens above, and to the earth, to judge His people.” “He calls to the heavens above”—this is the soul. “And to the earth, to judge His people”—this is the body.
He calls to the heavens above, and to the earth, to judge His people.
Of David, a psalm. The earth and its fullness belong to Hashem, the world and those who dwell in it.

So too Torah scholars, the children of the King and the Matron, are called Shabbatot and festivals. They have nothing of their own, for they do not practice trades like the other servants, the children of weekdays. Their reward in this world and the World to Come is that they be given delight with all kinds of food and drink and honored with beautiful garments, like Shabbat, of which it is said: Honor it with clean clothing. Everything a person does for Shabbatot and festivals must be done for them.
Only this have I found: God made man upright, but they sought many schemes.

Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: In all my days I have not seen a deer gathering figs, a lion carrying burdens, or a fox keeping a shop, yet they earn their livelihood without suffering. They were created only to serve me, while I was created to serve my Maker. If those who were created only to serve me earn their livelihood without suffering, should I, who was created to serve my Maker, not earn my livelihood without suffering? Rather, I have corrupted my deeds and impaired my livelihood, as it says, “Your sins have turned these things away.”
By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread, until you return to the ground, for from it you were taken. For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.

Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says: Can a person plow at plowing time, sow at sowing time, reap at reaping time, thresh at threshing time, and winnow when the wind blows—what will become of Torah? Rather, when Israel do the will of the Omnipresent, their labor is done by others, as it says, “Strangers will stand and tend your flocks.” When Israel do not do the will of the Omnipresent, their labor is done by themselves, as it says, “You shall gather your grain.” Moreover, the labor of others is done by them, as it says, “You shall serve your enemies.”
I will give the rain of your land in its season, the early rain and the late rain, and you shall gather your grain, your wine, and your oil.
Jacob lived in the land of Egypt for seventeen years; the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were one hundred and forty-seven years.

Why were Ishmael’s years enumerated? To establish Jacob’s years by means of them. For it is written: “These are the years of Ishmael’s life: one hundred and thirty-seven years.” How much older was Ishmael than Isaac? Fourteen years, for it is written: “Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram,” and: “Abraham was one hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.” It is also written: “Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them.” How old was Ishmael when Jacob was born? Seventy-four. How many of his years remained? Sixty-three. It was taught: Our father Jacob was

Jacob said to Pharaoh: “The days of the years of my sojournings are one hundred and thirty years. Few and troubled have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not reached the days of the years of my fathers’ lives in the days of their sojournings.”

Here it says, “He lived.” Throughout all his earlier days it had not been called “he lived,” because all his days had been spent in suffering. Of him it is written: “I was not at ease, I was not quiet, I had no rest, and turmoil came.” After he went down to Egypt it says, “He lived.” He saw his son a king; he saw all his sons worthy and righteous, all enjoying the world’s delights and comforts, while he sat among them like good wine resting on its lees. Then it says, “Jacob lived.” There is no separation between “they were fruitful and multiplied greatly” and “Jacob lived,” and so it should be

Immediately the mercy of the Holy One, blessed be He, was stirred, and He gave Jacob seventeen good years near his old age, resembling the World to Come. From here they said: Whoever experiences one good year near his old age has a favorable sign; whoever experiences one bad year near his old age has an unfavorable sign. Our father Jacob enjoyed goodness during the seventeen years he was in Egypt, and the Holy One, blessed be He, accounted it to him as though all his days had been good, as it says: “Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years.”

Hashem said to Abram: “Go forth from your land, your birthplace, and your father’s house to the land that I will show you. I will make you a great nation; I will bless you and make your name great, and you shall be a blessing.”
Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and bless you; for to you and your descendants I will give all these lands, and I will fulfill the oath that I swore to your father Abraham.

Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Abbahu: Did Rabbi Yochanan really say this? Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Nechunya of the valley of Beit Chortan: The laws of ten saplings, the willow, and the water libation are laws given to Moses at Sinai! Rabbi Abbahu was silent for a time and answered: They forgot them, and the prophets reestablished them. But did Rabbi Yochanan say this? Rabbi Yochanan said: “I had said it was yours; it is theirs!” There is no difficulty: one statement concerns the Temple, the other places outside the Temple.

Reish Lakish said: May I be an atonement for Rabbi Chiyya and his sons. At first, when Torah was forgotten from Israel, Ezra came up from Babylonia and established it. It was again forgotten; Hillel the Babylonian came up and established it. It was again forgotten; Rabbi Chiyya and his sons came up and established it.

Rabbi Levi said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said: In her desolation she raised righteous people for Me, while in her flourishing she raised wicked people for Me. In her desolation she raised righteous people: Daniel and his companions, Mordechai and his companions, Ezra and his companions. In her flourishing she raised wicked people, such as Ahaz and his companions, Manasseh and his companions, Amon and his followers. Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, concerning Rabbi Levi’s teaching: “For the children of the desolate one are more numerous than the children of the married

Twelve simple letters: heh, vav, zayin, chet, tet, yod, lamed, nun, samekh, ayin, tzadi, and qof. He engraved them, hewed them, weighed them, combined them, exchanged them, and formed through them twelve constellations in the universe. Their sign is Aries, Taurus, Gemini; Cancer, Leo, Virgo; Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius; Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces. These are the twelve months in the year: Nisan, Iyar, Sivan, Tammuz, Av, Elul, Tishrei, Marcheshvan, Kislev, Tevet, Shevat, and Adar. These are the twelve governing organs in the soul: two hands, two feet, two kidneys, the spleen, liver, gallbladder

Another interpretation: Amon means ‘craftsman.’ The Torah says: I was the instrument of the Holy One’s craftsmanship. Ordinarily, when a human king builds a palace, he does not build it according to his own understanding, but according to an architect’s understanding. The architect, too, does not proceed solely from his own understanding: he has plans and notebooks showing how to make rooms and doorways. So the Holy One, blessed be He, looked into the Torah and created the world. The Torah says, ‘In the beginning God created.’ ‘Beginning’ means Torah, as it says, ‘The Lord acquired me at the b

Rabbi Simon said: Light is mentioned here five times, corresponding to the five books of the Torah. ‘God said, Let there be light’ corresponds to Genesis, with which the Holy One, blessed be He, occupied Himself in creating His world. ‘And there was light’ corresponds to Exodus, in which Israel emerged from darkness into light. ‘God saw that the light was good’ corresponds to Leviticus, which is filled with many laws. ‘God separated the light from the darkness’ corresponds to Numbers, which distinguishes those who left Egypt from those who entered the Land. ‘God called the light day’ correspon

“Isaac again dug.” How many wells did our father Isaac dig in Beersheba? Rabbi Yehudah said: Four, corresponding to the four divisions into which his children were arranged in the wilderness. The Rabbis said: Five, corresponding to the five books of the Torah. “He called the well Esek” corresponds to Genesis, in which the Holy One, blessed be He, occupied Himself with creating the world. “He called it Sitnah” corresponds to Exodus, because “they embittered their lives with hard labor.” “They found there a well of living water” corresponds to Leviticus, which is filled with many laws. “He calle

‘Jacob lived in the land of Egypt.’ Why is this section closed, unlike the other Torah sections? Once our father Jacob died, Israel’s enslavement in Egypt began. Another interpretation: Why is it closed? Because our father Jacob wished to reveal the end of the exile, but it was concealed from him. Another interpretation: Why is it closed? Because God closed off from him all the troubles of the world.

What purpose did the breaks serve? To give Moses room to reflect between one passage and another, and between one subject and another. Is this not an argument from the lesser to the greater? If someone who hears from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, and speaks through the Holy Spirit needs to reflect between one passage and another and between one subject and another, how much more must an ordinary person learning from another ordinary person do so!

Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years, and the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were one hundred and forty-seven years. The days of Israel drew near to die, and he called his son Joseph and said to him: “If I have found favor in your eyes, place your hand under my thigh and deal with me in kindness and truth; please do not bury me in Egypt.”

Why did Jacob merit life in this world without suffering and without the evil inclination, like what the Holy One, blessed be He, will give the righteous in the future? Because he sat in the house of study from youth to old age, proficient in Scripture, Mishnah, laws, and aggadot, as it says, “Jacob was a wholehearted man, dwelling in tents”; also, “Like arrows in a warrior’s hand are the sons of youth; fortunate is the man…”; and, “To whom shall he teach knowledge?… Those weaned from milk, withdrawn from the breast.” When he left his father’s house for Laban’s, the Divine Presence stood above

Here it says, “He lived.” Throughout all his earlier days it had not been called “he lived,” because all his days had been spent in suffering. Of him it is written: “I was not at ease, I was not quiet, I had no rest, and turmoil came.” After he went down to Egypt it says, “He lived.” He saw his son a king; he saw all his sons worthy and righteous, all enjoying the world’s delights and comforts, while he sat among them like good wine resting on its lees. Then it says, “Jacob lived.” There is no separation between “they were fruitful and multiplied greatly” and “Jacob lived,” and so it should be

“The days of Israel drew near to die.” It was taught: Rabbi Chiyya said: It is written, “Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years.” There, during his life, he is called Jacob; here, at his death, he is called Israel, for it says: “The days of Israel drew near to die.” Rabbi Yosei said: It is indeed so. It does not say “the day of Israel drew near to die,” but “the days.” Does a person die over several days? He dies and departs from the world in a single hour, a single instant. Rather, we learned: When the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to take a person’s spirit back to Himself, all th

The Sages taught: There were three to whom the Holy One, blessed be He, gave a taste of the World to Come in this world: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Concerning Abraham it is written “with everything”; concerning Isaac, “of everything”; concerning Jacob, “everything.” There were three over whom the evil inclination had no dominion: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, as it is written concerning them, “with everything,” “of everything,” and “everything.” Some say that David was also included, as it is written: “My heart is slain within me.” The other opinion understands David to be speaking of his sufferi
“Please accept my blessing that has been brought to you, for God has favored me and I have everything.” He pressed him, and he accepted.

Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Ilai expounded: What does “Declare to My people their transgression, and to the house of Jacob their sins” mean? “Declare to My people their transgression” refers to Torah scholars, whose inadvertent sins are counted as deliberate ones. “To the house of Jacob their sins” refers to the unlearned, whose deliberate sins are counted as inadvertent ones. This accords with the Mishnah: Rabbi Yehudah says, “Take care in your learning, for an error in learning is counted as deliberate wrongdoing.”
He said: “Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel, for you have striven with divine beings and with men, and have prevailed.”

God spoke to Israel in visions of the night and said: “Jacob, Jacob!” He said: “Here I am.” He said: “I am God, the God of your father. Do not fear going down to Egypt, for there I will make you into a great nation.”

During his lifetime Rabbi lived in Tzippori for seventeen years. He would apply to himself the verse “Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years,” saying: “Judah lived in Tzippori seventeen years.” Our Rabbi suffered from his teeth for thirteen years, and throughout those thirteen years no animal died in the Land of Israel and no pregnant woman in the Land of Israel miscarried.
Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will awaken: some to everlasting life, and some to reproach and everlasting abhorrence.
Your dead will live; my dead bodies will arise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust, for Your dew is a dew of lights, and the earth will bring forth the departed.

Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: There was a gang of lawless men in Kefar Chittaya who would eat and drink in the synagogue every Shabbat evening. After eating, they would take the bones and throw them at the schoolteacher. One of them lay dying. They asked him: “To whom do you entrust your son, to look after him?” He answered: “To the schoolteacher.” Did he not have many friends, yet he said “to the schoolteacher”? He knew their conduct, and knew that the schoolteacher was better than they.

Further, words of Torah become settled only there. There is no light except what emerges from darkness: when this side is subdued, God is exalted above and honored in His glory. Service of God comes only from darkness, and goodness only from evil. When a person enters an evil path and abandons it, God is exalted in His glory. Thus the perfection of everything is good and evil together, afterward rising through good. There is no good except what emerges from evil. Through this good His glory rises; this is complete service.
“To inquire of Hashem”: so that He would tell her what would become of her in the end.

“Jacob lived in the land of Egypt.” Why is this passage closed? Rabbi Yaakov said: When Jacob died, the eyes of Israel were closed. Rabbi Yehudah said: Then they descended into exile and were enslaved. Rabbi Shimon said: What is written above? “Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen; they took possession of it and were fruitful and multiplied greatly.” Then it is written: “Jacob lived,” for it is not fitting to separate the two. Just as they enjoyed royal comforts, receiving delights and desirable things for themselves, so Jacob too enjoyed royal comforts, delights, and desir

What purpose did the breaks serve? To give Moses room to reflect between one passage and another, and between one subject and another. Is this not an argument from the lesser to the greater? If someone who hears from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, and speaks through the Holy Spirit needs to reflect between one passage and another and between one subject and another, how much more must an ordinary person learning from another ordinary person do so!

For we must surely die, and are like water spilled on the ground that cannot be gathered again. Yet God does not take away life, but devises plans so that the banished one will not remain banished from Him.
Joseph died at the age of one hundred and ten years. They embalmed him, and he was placed in a coffin in Egypt.
God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.
Another interpretation: “The fruit of a beautiful tree”—these are Israel. Just as the etrog has both flavor and fragrance, so Israel includes people who possess both Torah and good deeds.

The Sages taught: The compounding of the incense: balsam, onycha, galbanum, and frankincense, each weighing seventy maneh; myrrh, cassia, spikenard, and saffron, each weighing sixteen maneh; costus, twelve; aromatic bark, three; and cinnamon, nine.

“There is a time for everything, and a season for every purpose under heaven.” Abraham had a time when circumcision was given to him, as it says: “On that very day Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised.” His children had a time when they were circumcised twice, once in Egypt and once in the wilderness, as it says: “All the people who came out were circumcised.” Why was Abraham not circumcised at forty-eight, when he recognized his Creator? So as not to close the door before converts. Should you say that he ought to have been circumcised at eighty-five, when God spoke with him at the cov

“The angel who redeems me from all evil.” Rabbi Yosei bar Chalafta said: Earning a livelihood is twice as hard as childbirth. Of childbirth it is written, “In pain you shall bear children”; of livelihood, “In toil you shall eat from it all the days of your life.” Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman differed. Rabbi Elazar said: Scripture links redemption with livelihood and livelihood with redemption: just as redemption is twofold, livelihood is twofold; just as livelihood is needed every day, redemption is needed every day. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said: Livelihood is greater than redemp

Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: A person’s evil inclination grows stronger against him every day and seeks to kill him, as it says: “The wicked watches the righteous and seeks to kill him.” If the Holy One, blessed be He, did not help him, he could not overcome it, as it says: “Hashem will not leave him in its hand, nor condemn him when he is judged.”

Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: One who delights in Shabbat is saved from the subjugation of exile. Here it is written, “I will make you ride upon the heights of the earth,” and there it is written, “You shall tread upon their heights.”
Happy is the person who does this, and the son of man who holds fast to it: who keeps Shabbat from profaning it and keeps his hand from doing any evil.

Perhaps you will say: What reward does one who observes Shabbat receive? Scripture teaches: “Happy is the person who does this, and the one who holds fast to it: who keeps Shabbat from profaning it and keeps his hand from doing any evil.” Thus we learn that whoever observes Shabbat even under difficult circumstances is saved from transgression.

quote: Thus there is no person who does not receive an addition to his nefesh, ruach, and neshamah, according to the portion allotted to him. A person must direct his intention so that some of this addition will remain with him for the weekdays. Through this his ways will be established, if he directs his intention properly; he is assured that he will not sin, that sins will not come about through him, and that the evil inclination will not accuse him. Everything depends upon his intention.
Then you shall delight in Hashem. I will make you ride upon the heights of the earth, and I will feed you the inheritance of your father Jacob, for the mouth of Hashem has spoken.

Rabbi Shimon said: Whoever completes the three meals on Shabbat, a voice goes forth and proclaims concerning him: “Then you shall delight in Hashem”—this is one meal, corresponding to the Holy Ancient One, holiest of all. “I will make you ride upon the heights of the earth”—this is the second meal, corresponding to the field of holy apples. “I will feed you the inheritance of your father Jacob”—this is the completion fulfilled in Zeir Anpin. In correspondence with them a person must complete his meals, delight in all the meals, and rejoice in each one, for this is complete faith. Therefore Sha

ref: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath 17
quote: From the companions: At each Shabbat meal, including the meal after Shabbat, one should say: “These are meals of complete faith.” On Friday night one arranges twelve loaves upon the table and says: “This is the meal of the field of apples; Zeir Anpin and the Holy Ancient One come to dine with her.” This meal belongs to Isaac, who is the master of the meal and directs them. Whoever delights in this meal is saved from the birth pangs of Mashiach.

Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s name, in the name of Bar Kappara: Whoever fulfills the three meals on Shabbat is saved from three calamities: the birth pangs of Mashiach, the judgment of Gehinnom, and the war of Gog and Magog. From the birth pangs of Mashiach: here it is written “day,” and there, “Behold, I send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the day.” From the judgment of Gehinnom: here it is written “day,” and there, “That day is a day of wrath.” From the war of Gog and Magog: here it is written “day,” and there, “On the day that Gog comes.”

He began: “The angel who redeems me from all evil.” This verse requires reflection. Why does it say “who redeems,” rather than “who redeemed”? Because he is constantly present with human beings and never departs from a righteous person. Come and see: “The angel who redeems me” is the Shekhinah, which accompanies a person continually and does not leave him when he keeps the Torah’s commandments. Therefore a person must take care not to set out on a journey alone. What does “alone” mean? He should take care to keep the Torah’s commandments, so that the Shekhinah does not depart from him and he i

When the Matron travels, they all travel with her, as it is written: “The angel of God traveled.” Is she called “the angel of God”? Rabbi Abba said: Yes. Come and see: Rabbi Shimon said: The Holy One, blessed be He, established before Him a holy palace, a supernal palace, a holy city, a supernal city, called Jerusalem, the holy city. Whoever enters before the King enters only from that holy city, taking the path to the King, for the path is established from there. This is what is written: “This is the gate to Hashem; the righteous shall enter through it.” Every mission the King desires goes fo

He afflicted you and made you hungry, and fed you the manna that neither you nor your fathers had known, in order to teach you that a person does not live by bread alone, but by everything that proceeds from the mouth of Hashem does a person live.
You shall serve Hashem your God; He will bless your bread and your water, and I will remove illness from your midst.

May the angel who redeems me from all evil bless the lads. May my name be called upon them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac, and may they multiply abundantly like fish in the midst of the earth.

Rabbeinu Tam says: In the first chapter of Berakhot, concerning the blessing over Torah, the text reads, “Rabbi Yochanan concludes it as follows: ‘Make pleasant, please.’” It is a single blessing, for if these were two blessings, the latter would need to open with “Blessed,” even though it immediately follows another blessing, since the preceding blessing is short. Afterward the text reads, “Therefore let us recite both of them,” and we do not read “all of them,” for that would imply that there are three blessings.
“There was famine in all the lands”—in three lands: Phoenicia, Arabia, and Palestine.
Rabbi Elazar HaKappar says: Jealousy, desire, and honor remove a person from the world.
I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will make myself like the Most High.
For God knows that on the day you eat from it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like divine beings, knowing good and evil.
“For Hashem listens to the needy”—these are Israel. For Rabbi Yochanan said: Wherever Scripture says “lowly,” “poor,” or “needy,” it is speaking of Israel.
He blessed Joseph and said: “The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has shepherded me from my beginning until this day.”
Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: Israel knew that there was no reality in idol worship; they worshiped idols only so as to permit themselves sexual immorality openly.

Rav Nachman said: The arrogance within Jeroboam drove him from the world, as it says: “Jeroboam said in his heart: Now the kingdom will return to the house of David. If this people goes up to offer sacrifices in the House of Hashem in Jerusalem, the heart of this people will return to their lord Rehoboam king of Judah; they will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah.” He said: We have a tradition that no one may sit in the Temple courtyard except the kings of the house of Judah. When they see Rehoboam sitting and me standing, they will think: This one is the king, and that one is the se

Rabbi Shalmoni said in the name of Reish Lakish: He showed him a chair with three legs. Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin said in Rabbi Levi’s name: You are the third leg. This accords with Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin in Rabbi Levi’s name: “For Hashem’s portion is His people; Jacob is the cord of His inheritance.” Just as a cord is not twisted from fewer than three strands, so there are no fewer than three patriarchs.
Come and see: Jacob is the glory of the patriarchs, and he encompasses them all. Because he encompasses everything, he stands to illuminate the moon; Jacob stands to establish the evening prayer.
I will give grass in your field for your cattle, and you shall eat and be satisfied. Take care lest your hearts be enticed, and you turn aside and serve other gods and bow down to them.

“You shall eat and be satisfied”; “Take care lest your heart be enticed.” He said to them: Take care lest you rebel against the Omnipresent, for a person rebels against the Omnipresent only from satiation. As it says: “Lest you eat and be satisfied, build good houses and dwell in them, and your cattle and sheep multiply and your silver and gold increase.” What does it say afterward? “Your heart will be exalted and you will forget Hashem your God.” Similarly, “When I bring them to the land that I swore to their fathers, flowing with milk and honey”—what follows? “They will turn to other gods.”

Rav Acha son of Rav Huna said in Rav Sheshet’s name: This is what people say: A full belly is a kind of evil, as it says: “When they grazed they were satisfied; they were satisfied and their hearts were exalted, therefore they forgot Me.” Rav Nachman said: It is learned from here: “Your heart will be exalted and you will forget Hashem.” The Rabbis said: From here: “They will eat, be satisfied, grow fat, and turn away.”

Rabbi Avdimi of Haifa said: Before a person eats and drinks, he has two hearts; after he eats and drinks, he has only one heart, as it says: “An empty man will gain a heart.” And it is written, “Hollow boards,” which we translate as “hollow planks.”

A person must bless for adversity as he blesses for good, as it says: “You shall love Hashem your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.” “With all your heart”—with both your inclinations, the good inclination and the evil inclination. “With all your soul”—even if He takes your soul. “With all your might”—with all your wealth. Another interpretation of “with all your might”: Whatever measure He metes out to you, give thanks to Him exceedingly.
Come, eat of my bread and drink of the wine that I have mixed.
To the woman He said: “I will greatly multiply your travail and your pregnancy; in pain you shall bear children. Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you.”

“The angel who redeems me from all evil.” Rabbi Yosei bar Chalafta said: Earning a livelihood is twice as hard as childbirth. Of childbirth it is written, “In pain you shall bear children”; of livelihood, “In toil you shall eat from it all the days of your life.” Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman differed. Rabbi Elazar said: Scripture links redemption with livelihood and livelihood with redemption: just as redemption is twofold, livelihood is twofold; just as livelihood is needed every day, redemption is needed every day. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said: Livelihood is greater than redemp

To Adam He said: “Because you listened to your wife’s voice and ate from the tree concerning which I commanded you, ‘You shall not eat from it,’ cursed is the ground because of you; in toil you shall eat from it all the days of your life.”
Rabbi Yochanan said: A person’s sustenance is twice as difficult as childbirth. Concerning childbirth it is written “in pain,” while concerning sustenance it is written “in toil.”
Guard me like the pupil of the eye; hide me in the shadow of Your wings.

“Guard me like the pupil of the eye”—as a person guards the pupil of his eye, the black part through which light is seen. It is called ishon because the form of an ish, a person, appears in it. The vav and nun make it diminutive, since the form is small.
By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread, until you return to the ground, for from it you were taken; for you are dust, and to dust you shall return.
The people went about and gathered it, ground it in mills or pounded it in a mortar, cooked it in a pot, and made cakes from it; its taste was like the taste of fresh oil.

Of those who were not people of faith, what is written? “The people went about and gathered.” What does “went about” mean? They took foolishness upon themselves because they were not people of faith. What is written of them? “They ground it in mills or pounded it in a mortar.” Who caused them all this toil? It was because they were not people of faith.
It shall be on the day that Hashem gives you rest from your sorrow, your agitation, and the hard service that was imposed upon you.

Rabbi Shimon said further: Concerning this we learned that Shabbat resembles the World to Come. It is indeed so. Just as the sabbatical year and the Jubilee resemble one another, so do Shabbat and the World to Come. That addition to the soul comes from the mystery of “Remember” to this shelter of peace, which receives from the World to Come; it gives this addition to the holy world. Through that addition they rejoice, and all weekday affairs, all sorrow, and all distress are forgotten, as it says: “On the day that Hashem gives you rest from your sorrow, your agitation, and the hard service.”
To Him who alone performs great wonders, for His kindness is everlasting.

“In toil,” and so forth: This was explained above, in chapter 20 of Bereishit. There the reading is: “Just as redemption involves wonders, so does livelihood,” and this is also the reading in the Yalkut. Its meaning is that concerning redemption it says, “To Him who alone performs great wonders,” and near it, “He rescued us.” Similarly, concerning redemption from Egypt, it says, “Awesome in praises, performing wonders.” According to the text of our book, one may explain that we find repeated expressions concerning redemption—“Comfort, comfort,” “I, I,” and many others—and this indicates its di
He rescued us from our adversaries, for His kindness is everlasting. He gives bread to all flesh, for His kindness is everlasting.

“In toil you shall eat from it.” Rav Asi said: Livelihood is twice as difficult as childbirth. Of childbirth it is written, “In pain you shall bear children,” and of livelihood, “In toil you shall eat from it.” Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman differed. Rabbi Eliezer said: Scripture links redemption with livelihood and livelihood with redemption, as it says, “He rescued us from our adversaries,” followed by “He gives bread to all flesh.” Just as redemption involves wonders, so does livelihood; just as livelihood is needed every day, so is redemption. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said: Li
Moses said to the people: “Do not fear. Stand firm and see the salvation of Hashem that He will perform for you today. For as you have seen Egypt today, you will never see them again.”

Rav Nachman said: Reading the Megillah is itself its Hallel. Rava said: There, at the Exodus, “Praise, servants of Hashem” properly means servants of Hashem and no longer servants of Pharaoh. But here, can “Praise, servants of Hashem” mean no longer servants of Ahasuerus? We are still servants of Ahasuerus.
As in the days of your departure from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders.

Rabbi Yitzchak said: When Israel encamped beside the sea, they saw many multitudes, armies, and camps, above and below, all gathering against Israel. In their distress they began to pray. At that moment Israel saw distress on every side: the sea with its waves rising before them; behind them all the multitudes and camps of Egypt; above them many accusers. They began to cry out to the Holy One, blessed be He. Then it is written, “Hashem said to Moses: Why do you cry out to Me?” It was taught in the Book of Concealment: “To Me,” specifically; everything depends upon Atika. At that moment the Hol
Who is like You among the mighty, Hashem? Who is like You, majestic in holiness, awesome in praises, performing wonders?
Rabbi Yosei found Rabbi Abba sitting and reading this verse: “Cast your burden upon Hashem.” The word al, “upon,” is precise, for sustenance depends upon mazala.
I said: You are divine beings, and all of you are children of the Most High.

It was taught: Rabbi Yosei says: Israel received the Torah only so that the Angel of Death would have no dominion over them, as it says, “I said: You are divine beings, and all of you are children of the Most High.” But you corrupted your deeds: “Nevertheless, like man you shall die.”
The sea saw and fled; the Jordan turned backward.
Shimon of Kitron said: In the merit of Joseph’s bones the sea was split for Israel. Thus it is written, “The sea saw and fled”—in the merit of “He left his garment in her hand and fled.”

Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: Sarah went down to Egypt and fenced herself off from sexual immorality, and all the women were protected in her merit. Joseph went down to Egypt and fenced himself off from sexual immorality, and all the men were protected in his merit. Rabbi Pinchas said in the name of Rabbi Chiyya: Guarding against sexual immorality was itself sufficient for Israel to be redeemed from Egypt in its merit. What is the proof? “A locked garden is my sister, my bride.” What is written afterward? “Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates.”
Your people are all righteous; they will inherit the land forever—the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, in which I take glory.
He will swallow up death forever. The Lord Hashem will wipe tears from every face and remove the disgrace of His people from all the earth, for Hashem has spoken.

quote: From the companions: at every Shabbat meal, including the meal after Shabbat, one should declare, ‘These are meals of complete faith.’ On Friday night one arranges twelve loaves and says, ‘This is the meal of the Field of Apples; Ze‘ir Anpin and the Holy Ancient One come to feast with her.’ This is Isaac’s meal: he is its master and guides it. Whoever delights in it is saved from the birth pangs of the Messiah. At the morning meal one arranges eight loaves and says, ‘This is the meal of the Holy Ancient One; Ze‘ir Anpin and the Field of Holy Apples come to feast with Him.’ It corresponds to Ab

“Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it”—this is the mystery of the holy covenant. Just as all the sources of the body’s limbs are sustained in this covenant, which includes them all, so Shabbat comprises the Torah, and all the mysteries of Torah depend upon it. Keeping Shabbat is like keeping the entire Torah; whoever observes Shabbat is as though he observed the entire Torah.

We learned: Rabbi Yehudah said: There is no sin in the world for which there is no repentance, except this one. There are no sinners who do not see the face of the Shekhinah, except this one, for it is written, “Evil shall not dwell with You”—not at all. Rabbi Yitzchak said: Fortunate are the righteous, in this world and in the World to Come! Of them it is written, “Your people are all righteous; they will inherit the land forever.” What does “they will inherit the land forever” mean? Rabbi Yehudah said: As it is written, “I will walk before Hashem in the lands of the living.”

Come and see: All a person’s sins, all the damage he has caused, depend upon repentance. But the sin of spilling seed upon the ground, corrupting his way and emitting seed upon the ground, harms him and harms the earth. Of him it is written, “Your iniquity remains stained before Me,” and, “For You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You”—except through great repentance. It is written, “Er, Judah’s firstborn, was evil in the eyes of Hashem, and Hashem put him to death,” as has been explained.
Even if you wash with natron and use much soap, your iniquity remains stained before Me, declares the Lord Hashem.

He opened and said: “For I know my transgressions, and my sin is before me always.” How greatly people must guard themselves against their sins before the Holy One, blessed be He! After a person sins, his sin is inscribed above and is not erased except through the power of great repentance, as it says, “Even if you wash with natron and use much soap, your iniquity remains stained before Me.” Come and see: When a person sins before the Holy One, blessed be He, once, he makes an impression. When he sins a second time, that impression grows stronger. If he sins a third time, the stain spreads fro
Come now, let us reason together, says Hashem: Even if your sins are like scarlet, they will become white as snow; even if they are red as crimson, they will become like wool.
These are David’s last words: The declaration of David son of Jesse, the declaration of the man raised on high, the anointed one of the God of Jacob, the sweet singer of Israel.

Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: What is the meaning of “The declaration of David son of Jesse, the declaration of the man raised on high”? It means the declaration of David son of Jesse, who raised the yoke of repentance.
Purify me with hyssop and I will be clean; wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.

Why does the verse say ka-shanim, which can mean “like years”? It should say ka-shani, “like scarlet.” Rabbi Yitzchak said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: Even if your sins are like these years that have been arranged and have unfolded from the six days of creation until now, they will become white as snow.
Chokhmah is the brain, the thought within. Binah is the heart, and through it the heart understands. Of these two it is written: “The concealed things belong to Hashem our God.”
Then you will understand the fear of Hashem and find the knowledge of God.
Rav and Shmuel differed. One said: Fifty gates of understanding were created in the world, and all of them were given to Moses except one, as it says: “You made him lack little of the divine.”

“She saw that he was good.” It was taught: Rabbi Meir says: His name was Tov. Rabbi Yehudah says: His name was Toviyyah. Rabbi Nechemyah says: He was fit for prophecy. Others say: He was born circumcised. The Sages say: When Moses was born, the entire house filled with light. Here it says, “She saw that he was good,” and there it says, “God saw that the light was good.”

Rabbi Abbahu and Rabbi Chiyya Rabbah taught. Rabbi Abbahu said: From the beginning of the world’s creation, the Holy One, blessed be He, foresaw the deeds of the righteous and the deeds of the wicked, as it is written: “For Hashem knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked will perish.” “The earth was desolate and empty”—these are the deeds of the wicked. “God said: Let there be light”—these are the deeds of the righteous. But I do not know which He desires, the deeds of these or the deeds of those. Once it says, “God saw that the light was good,” it is clear that He desires the

Reish Lakish said: Great is repentance, for deliberate sins become like unwitting sins, as it says, “Return, Israel, to Hashem your God, for you have stumbled in your iniquity.” Iniquity is deliberate, yet it is called a stumbling. Is that so? Did Reish Lakish not say: Great is repentance, for deliberate sins become merits, as it says, “When the wicked turns from his wickedness and practices justice and righteousness, by them he shall live”? There is no difficulty: the latter refers to repentance from love, and the former to repentance from fear.

Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: Whoever observes Shabbat according to its law is forgiven, even if he worshiped idols like the generation of Enosh, as it says, “Happy is the person who does this … who keeps Shabbat from profaning it.” Do not read me-challelo, “from profaning it,” but machul lo, “he is forgiven.”

‘Jacob lived in the land of Egypt.’ Why is this section closed, unlike the other Torah sections? Once our father Jacob died, Israel’s enslavement in Egypt began. Another interpretation: Why is it closed? Because our father Jacob wished to reveal the end of the exile, but it was concealed from him. Another interpretation: Why is it closed? Because God closed off from him all the troubles of the world.

“Jacob lived in the land of Egypt.” Why is this passage closed? Rabbi Yaakov said: When Jacob died, the eyes of Israel were closed. Rabbi Yehudah said: Then they descended into exile and were enslaved. Rabbi Shimon said: What is written above? “Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen; they took possession of it and were fruitful and multiplied greatly.” Then it is written: “Jacob lived,” for it is not fitting to separate the two. Just as they enjoyed royal comforts, receiving delights and desirable things for themselves, so Jacob too enjoyed royal comforts, delights, and desir

What purpose did the breaks serve? To give Moses room to reflect between one passage and another, and between one subject and another. Is this not an argument from the lesser to the greater? If someone who hears from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, and speaks through the Holy Spirit needs to reflect between one passage and another and between one subject and another, how much more must an ordinary person learning from another ordinary person do so!

“The years of Levi’s life”: Why were Levi’s years enumerated? To make known the length of the enslavement, for as long as any one of the tribal ancestors remained alive there was no enslavement, as it says, “Joseph died, and all his brothers,” and afterward, “A new king arose.” Levi lived longer than all of them.
“Joseph died, and all his brothers, and all that generation.” This teaches that as long as any one of those who had descended to Egypt remained alive, the Egyptians did not enslave Israel.

Joseph died, and all his brothers, and all that generation. The children of Israel were fruitful, increased abundantly, multiplied, and became exceedingly mighty; the land was filled with them. A new king arose over Egypt, who did not know Joseph.

“The angel who redeems me from all evil.” Rabbi Yosei bar Chalafta said: Earning a livelihood is twice as hard as childbirth. Of childbirth it is written, “In pain you shall bear children”; of livelihood, “In toil you shall eat from it all the days of your life.” Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman differed. Rabbi Elazar said: Scripture links redemption with livelihood and livelihood with redemption: just as redemption is twofold, livelihood is twofold; just as livelihood is needed every day, redemption is needed every day. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said: Livelihood is greater than redemp

“Jacob lived”: Why is this passage closed? Because when our father Jacob died, Israel’s eyes and hearts were closed by the distress of enslavement, for the Egyptians began to enslave them. Another interpretation: Jacob wished to reveal the end to his sons, but it was closed off from him. This is in Bereishit Rabbah.

“Jacob lived in the land of Egypt.” Why is this passage closed? Rabbi Yaakov said: When Jacob died, the eyes of Israel were closed. Rabbi Yehudah said: Then they descended into exile and were enslaved. Rabbi Shimon said: What is written above? “Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen; they took possession of it and were fruitful and multiplied greatly.” Then it is written: “Jacob lived,” for it is not fitting to separate the two. Just as they enjoyed royal comforts, receiving delights and desirable things for themselves, so Jacob too enjoyed royal comforts, delights, and desir

Some say that this is what Bava ben Buta told Herod: He blinded the eye of the world, as it is written, “If it was done unwittingly away from the eyes of the congregation.” Let him go and occupy himself with the eye of the world, as it is written, “Behold, I am profaning My sanctuary, the pride of your strength, the desire of your eyes.”
Chokhmah is the brain, the thought within. Binah is the heart, and through it the heart understands. Of these two it is written: “The concealed things belong to Hashem our God.”

According to the view that Job lived in the days of Moses, should Job not be placed first? We do not begin with calamity. But Ruth also concerns calamity! It is calamity that has a future. For Rabbi Yochanan said: Why was she called Ruth? Because David descended from her, and he saturated the Holy One, blessed be He, with songs and praises.
For I know the thoughts that I think concerning you, declares Hashem—thoughts of peace and not of evil, to give you a future and hope.
“To give you a future and hope.” Rav Yehudah, son of Rav Shmuel bar Shilat, said in Rav’s name: These are date palms and linen garments.

“He said”—what is meant by “he said”? We have explained it, as in “You will say in your heart”: speech in a whisper. “Gather yourselves”: should it not say “Gather,” as in “Gather My faithful ones to Me”? Rather, we know that “Gather yourselves” comes from the place above: gather yourselves in a complete bond, in a single unity. “I will tell you”—what does “I will tell” mean? It is a mystery of wisdom. Rabbi Yosei asked Rabbi Shimon: We learned that “I will tell,” “he told,” “they will tell,” and similar forms are a mystery of wisdom. Why does this expression embody a mystery of wisdom? He ans

Further, words of Torah become settled only there. There is no light except what emerges from darkness: when this side is subdued, God is exalted above and honored in His glory. Service of God comes only from darkness, and goodness only from evil. When a person enters an evil path and abandons it, God is exalted in His glory. Thus the perfection of everything is good and evil together, afterward rising through good. There is no good except what emerges from evil. Through this good His glory rises; this is complete service.

“This is my God.” Rabbi Eliezer says: How do we know that a maidservant at the sea saw what Isaiah and Ezekiel did not see? It says, “Through the prophets I use likenesses,” and, “The heavens opened, and I saw visions of God.” To what may this be compared? To a mortal king who entered a province, surrounded by a retinue, with warriors to his right and left and troops before and behind him. Everyone asked, “Which one is the king?” because he was flesh and blood like them. But when the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself at the sea, none needed to ask, “Which one is He?” As soon as they sa

Rabbi Abba said: What is the meaning of “Is Hashem in our midst, or ayin?” Were Israel foolish, not knowing this matter? They saw the Shekhinah before them and the clouds of glory above them, surrounding them, yet they said: “Is Hashem in our midst, or ayin?” People who saw the radiance of their King’s glory at the sea—and we have learned that a maidservant at the sea saw what Ezekiel did not see—were they found to be foolish, saying: “Is Hashem in our midst, or ayin?”

Five things are one-sixtieth: fire, honey, Shabbat, sleep, and a dream. Fire is one-sixtieth of Gehinnom; honey is one-sixtieth of manna; Shabbat is one-sixtieth of the World to Come; sleep is one-sixtieth of death; and a dream is one-sixtieth of prophecy.
It shall be on the day that Hashem gives you rest from your sorrow, your agitation, and the hard service that was imposed upon you.

Rabbi Shimon said further: Concerning this we learned that Shabbat resembles the World to Come. It is indeed so. Just as the sabbatical year and the Jubilee resemble one another, so do Shabbat and the World to Come. That addition to the soul comes from the mystery of “Remember” to this shelter of peace, which receives from the World to Come; it gives this addition to the holy world. Through that addition they rejoice, and all weekday affairs, all sorrow, and all distress are forgotten, as it says: “On the day that Hashem gives you rest from your sorrow, your agitation, and the hard service.”
The blessing of Hashem makes one rich, and He adds no sorrow with it.
Of Naphtali he said: “Naphtali, satisfied with favor and full of the blessing of Hashem, possess the sea and the south.”

Come and see: All the supernal blessings were entrusted to this level, to bless everything. Although it has no light of its own, all blessings, all joy, and all goodness abide in it and issue from it. Therefore it is called “the cup of blessing,” and it is called blessing itself, as it is written, “The blessing of Hashem makes one rich.” Thus it is written, “Full of the blessing of Hashem, possess the sea and the south.” Therefore it has a share in all of them, is filled from all of them, and contains something of all of them. It is blessed from all those supernal blessings, and the blessings
God saw that the light was good, and God separated the light from the darkness.

How many are “many”? Rav Nachman said: Three. Rabbi Yitzchak said: Ten. Rav Nachman said three because “days” means two, while “many” adds a third. Rabbi Yitzchak said ten because it says “congregation.”

Rava said: Length of life, children, and sustenance do not depend upon merit, but upon mazal. For Rabbah and Rav Chisda were both righteous sages: one prayed and rain came, and the other prayed and rain came. Rav Chisda lived ninety-two years; Rabbah lived forty. In Rav Chisda’s household there were sixty weddings; in Rabbah’s household, sixty bereavements. In Rav Chisda’s household there was fine flour for the dogs, and it was not needed; in Rabbah’s household, barley bread for people could not be found.
Cast your burden upon Hashem, and He will sustain you; He will never allow the righteous to falter.
Rabbi Yosei found Rabbi Abba sitting and reading this verse: “Cast your burden upon Hashem.” The word al, “upon,” is precise, for sustenance depends upon mazala.
She was bitter of soul, and she prayed to Hashem and wept greatly.

It was taught: ‘The Shabbat burnt offering on its Shabbat, above the continual burnt offering.’ One must direct the heart higher and higher, more than on other days. Hence precisely ‘above the continual burnt offering.’ Of Hannah it says, ‘She prayed above the Lord’—precisely ‘above,’ since children depend upon the holy mazal, as explained. No word of Torah, nor even a small letter, fails to allude to upper Wisdom; heaps upon heaps of its secrets depend on each, as in ‘His locks are curled in heaps.’

Come and see: At first, yod contains everything, closed on every side; the paths have not opened, and it includes male and female. The upper tip of the yod alludes to Ayin. Afterward, the yod brings forth the river that flows and goes out from it, so that the heh is conceived from it. Of this it is written, “A river goes out from Eden”—“goes out,” not “went out,” for it never wishes to be separated from it. Therefore it is written, “My beloved.”

In this arrangement they are called: Chesed, the right arm; Gevurah, the left arm; Tiferet, the torso; Netzach and Hod, the two legs; Yesod, the body’s extremity, the sign of the holy covenant; Malchut, the mouth, which we call the Oral Torah. Chokhmah is the brain, inward thought. Binah is the heart, through which the heart understands. Of these two it is written, ‘The concealed things belong to the Lord our God.’ The upper Keter is the royal crown, of which it says, ‘Declaring the end from the beginning.’ It is the skull of the tefillin; another reading says, the skull that does not put on t
Look to Abraham your father and to Sarah who bore you, for I called him when he was one; I blessed him and multiplied him.

Rabbi Ammi said: Abraham and Sarah were tumtumin, their sexual organs concealed, as it says, “Look to the rock from which you were hewn, and to the hollow of the pit from which you were dug,” and it says, “Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who bore you.”
Isaac sowed in that land and found a hundredfold yield that year, and Hashem blessed him. The man grew great, and continued to grow greater, until he became very great.
“The man grew great and continued to grow greater.” Rabbi Chanin said: Until people would say: “The dung of Isaac’s mules is preferable to Abimelech’s silver and gold.”
Behold, I am with you. I will guard you wherever you go and bring you back to this land, for I will not leave you until I have done what I have spoken to you.

Reish Lakish said: Satan, the evil inclination, and the Angel of Death are one. He is Satan, as it is written, “Satan went out from before Hashem.” He is the evil inclination: there it is written, “Only evil all day,” and here, “Only do not stretch out your hand against him.” He is the Angel of Death, as it is written, “But preserve his life,” implying that his life was in Satan’s power.

God appeared to Jacob again when he came from Paddan Aram, and blessed him. God said to him: “Your name is Jacob; your name will no longer be called Jacob, but Israel shall be your name.” And He called his name Israel.
He said: “Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel, for you have striven with divine beings and with men, and have prevailed.”

After they had eaten, Rabbi Yitzchak said to Rav Nachman: Rabbi Yochanan said: Our father Jacob did not die. Rav Nachman asked: Was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized him, the embalmers embalmed him, and the buriers buried him? He answered: I am expounding Scripture, for it says: “Do not fear, My servant Jacob, declares Hashem, and do not be dismayed, Israel, for I will save you from afar and your descendants from the land of their captivity.” Scripture compares Jacob to his descendants: just as his descendants are alive, so he is alive.

“If You will surely bless me”—with Torah; “and enlarge my border”—with students; “and Your hand will be with me”—so that my learning will not be forgotten from my heart; “and keep me from harm”—so that I will find companions like myself; “that I may not be pained”—so that the evil inclination will not overpower me and prevent me from learning. If You do this, well and good; if not, I go in my sorrow to the grave. Immediately, “God granted what he had asked.”

To the woman He said: “I will greatly multiply your travail and your pregnancy; in pain you shall bear children. Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you.” To Adam He said: “Because you listened to your wife’s voice and ate from the tree concerning which I commanded you, ‘You shall not eat from it,’ cursed is the ground because of you; in toil you shall eat from it all the days of your life.”
When it had finished eating the grass of the land, I said: “Lord Hashem, please forgive! How will Jacob stand, for he is small?”
Hashem reigns; He is clothed in majesty. Hashem is clothed in strength and has girded Himself; the world is firmly established and will not be moved.

God said: “Let us make man in our image, according to our likeness, and let them rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of the heavens, the livestock, all the earth, and every creeping creature that creeps upon the earth.”

Rabbi Yosei bar Zimra said: Three things were said of that tree: it was good for food, beautiful to the eyes, and increased wisdom. All three were said in one verse: “The woman saw that it was good”—from here, that it was good; “and that it was a delight to the eyes”—from here, that it was beautiful to the eyes; “and that the tree was desirable for gaining wisdom”—from here, that it increased wisdom, as in “A maskil of Ethan the Ezrachite.” “She took of its fruit and ate.” Rabbi Aivu said: She pressed grapes and gave him their juice. Rabbi Simlai said: She approached him with a considered argu

“To the woman He said: I will greatly multiply”—these are two kinds of blood, menstrual blood and the blood of virginity. “Your travail”—this is the pain of raising children. “Your pregnancy”—this is the pain of pregnancy. “In pain you shall bear children”—as it plainly means.
The man said: “The woman whom You gave to be with me—she gave me from the tree, and I ate.”
Light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright of heart.

There is no honor except Torah, as it says, “The wise will inherit honor,” and, “The blameless will inherit good.” There is no good except Torah, as it says, “For I have given you a good teaching; do not forsake My Torah.”
For the commandment is a lamp and Torah is light, and the reproofs of discipline are the path of life.

Moses began grieving over the breaking of the tablets. The Holy One, blessed be He, told him: Do not grieve over the first tablets, which contained only the Ten Commandments. In the second tablets I give you, there will be laws, midrash, and aggadot, as it is written, “He will tell you wisdom’s hidden things, for sound wisdom is doubled.” Moreover, you receive the tidings that I have forgiven your sin, as it says, “Know that God remits some of your iniquity.”

The Holy One, blessed be He, said: You suffered; by your life, you will not lose! The first tablets contained only the Ten Commandments. Now that you have suffered, I give you laws, midrashim, and aggadot, as it says, “Write for yourself these words.” Why did the Holy One, blessed be He, say “Write for yourself,” when it is written, “The writing was God’s writing, engraved upon the tablets,” and, “He wrote upon the tablets like the first writing”? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, told him: Write Torah, Prophets, and Writings, so that they shall be written; but laws, midrash, aggadot, and t
He would tell you the secrets of wisdom, for wisdom is twofold; know that God has overlooked some of your iniquity.

What is Shabbat? If you say it denotes cessation, as in ‘For on it He ceased,’ that is correct. But its inner mystery is this: when this point rises and light shines, she is crowned with the patriarchs. Once crowned with them, she joins and unites with them as one, and everything is called Shabbat. Shabbat: shin-bat. Shin, as explained, is the mystery of the three patriarchs united with the only daughter. She is crowned with them, and they with the world to come. All is one. This is shin-bat, that everything become one.

On the seventh day God completed the work that He had done, and He rested on the seventh day from all the work that He had done. God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on it He rested from all His work that God had created to be done.

Rabbi Chama bar Chanina and Rabbi Yonatan taught. Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said: A king built a palace, saw it, and was pleased with it. He said: “Palace, palace, may you always find favor before me as you have found favor before me at this moment.” So the Holy One, blessed be He, said to His world: “My world, My world, may you always find favor before Me as you have found favor before Me at this moment.”
The glory of Hashem will endure forever; Hashem will rejoice in His works.

As it were, the Holy One, blessed be He, has not rejoiced in His world. It does not say, “Hashem rejoiced in His works,” but, “He will rejoice”: in the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will rejoice in the deeds of the righteous.
It shall be on the day that Hashem gives you rest from your sorrow, your agitation, and the hard service that was imposed upon you.

“They rose before Moses.” The companions have explained this verse. Rabbi Shimon said: “Those summoned to the assembly”—keri’ei is written without a yod. Why keri’ei? Rather, earthly kingship is like heavenly kingship. Its mystery is this: all those supernal crowns to which the holy Name is joined are summoned from the place called Holiness, as it is written: “Holy convocations.” When? When a festival is appointed in the world. Just as those supernal crowns are summoned from the upper Holiness, so the lower Holiness summons its hosts, to crown and elevate them. The upper Holiness is known; the

Rabbi Simon said: Light is mentioned here five times, corresponding to the five books of the Torah. ‘God said, Let there be light’ corresponds to Genesis, with which the Holy One, blessed be He, occupied Himself in creating His world. ‘And there was light’ corresponds to Exodus, in which Israel emerged from darkness into light. ‘God saw that the light was good’ corresponds to Leviticus, which is filled with many laws. ‘God separated the light from the darkness’ corresponds to Numbers, which distinguishes those who left Egypt from those who entered the Land. ‘God called the light day’ correspon

Everyone agrees that the Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat. Here it is written, “Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it,” and there it is written, “Moses said to the people: Remember this day.” Just as there it means the very day on which he was speaking, so here it means the very day.

“God completed on the seventh day”—this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day. Through it the world was perfected, for it sustains everything. “His work that He had done,” not “all His work,” for the Written Torah brought everything forth through the power of the writing that issues from Wisdom. “The seventh day” appears here three times: “God completed on the seventh day”; “He rested on the seventh day”; “God blessed the seventh day”—three times. “God completed on the seventh day”—this is the Oral Torah, for through this seventh day the world was perfected, as we have said.

In this arrangement they are called: Chesed, the right arm; Gevurah, the left arm; Tiferet, the torso; Netzach and Hod, the two legs; Yesod, the body’s extremity, the sign of the holy covenant; Malchut, the mouth, which we call the Oral Torah. Chokhmah is the brain, inward thought. Binah is the heart, through which the heart understands. Of these two it is written, ‘The concealed things belong to the Lord our God.’ The upper Keter is the royal crown, of which it says, ‘Declaring the end from the beginning.’ It is the skull of the tefillin; another reading says, the skull that does not put on t

“A great light”—the light created on the first day, which the Holy One, blessed be He, concealed for those who labor in the Oral Torah day and night. Through their merit the world endures, as it says, “Thus says Hashem: Were it not for My covenant by day and night, I would not have established the laws of heaven and earth.” Which covenant applies both by day and by night? The study of Talmud. It also says, “Thus says Hashem: If you break My covenant of the day and My covenant of the night, then My covenant with My servant David will also be broken.” And it says, “His desire is in the Torah of

Five things are one-sixtieth: fire, honey, Shabbat, sleep, and a dream. Fire is one-sixtieth of Gehinnom; honey is one-sixtieth of manna; Shabbat is one-sixtieth of the World to Come; sleep is one-sixtieth of death; and a dream is one-sixtieth of prophecy.
Everything created during the six days of creation requires further work: mustard needs sweetening, lupines need sweetening, wheat needs grinding; even a human being requires rectification.

“Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it.” Rabbi Yitzchak said: It is written, “God blessed the seventh day,” yet concerning manna it is written, “Six days you shall gather it, but on the seventh day, Shabbat, there will be none.” Since no sustenance is found on that day, what blessing is found in it? Rather, we learned: All blessings above and below depend upon the seventh day. Why was no manna found on the seventh day? Because from that day all six supernal days receive blessing. Each gives its sustenance below, each on its own day, from the blessing with which they were blessed on the seven
For six days Hashem made the heavens and the earth, the sea and all that is in them, and He rested on the seventh day. Therefore Hashem blessed the Shabbat day and sanctified it.
Hashem has established His throne in the heavens, and His kingdom rules over all.
Your eyes saw my unformed body, and in Your book they were all written: days were formed, and one of them is His.

“Days were formed, and one of them is His”—this is the day of Shabbat for Israel. How so? A person works for six days and rests on the seventh, finding reconciliation with his children and household. Again, a person works in the presence of his enemies for six days and rests on the seventh, forgetting all the suffering he endured. Such is human nature: a good day causes one to forget a bad day, and a bad day causes one to forget a good day. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: Did I not write for you in My Torah, “This book of the Torah shall not depart from your mouth”? Although you w

It was taught: They said of Shammai the Elder that all his days he ate in honor of Shabbat. If he found a fine animal, he said, “This is for Shabbat.” If he found another finer than it, he set aside the second and ate the first. But Hillel the Elder had a different practice, for all his deeds were for the sake of Heaven, as it says, “Blessed is the Lord day by day.” It was likewise taught: Beit Shammai say: From the first day of your week, prepare for your Shabbat. Beit Hillel say: “Blessed is the Lord day by day.”
Blessed is the Lord day by day; He bears our burden, the God who is our salvation. Selah.

What is Rabbi Yehudah’s reason? Scripture says, “Blessed is the Lord day by day.” Do we bless Him by day but not by night? Rather, this teaches you: Each day, give Him the blessings appropriate to that day. Here too, for each kind of produce, give Him the blessing appropriate to its kind.
You will grant truth to Jacob and kindness to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from days of old.

The Holy One, blessed be He, said: How long will the world conduct itself in darkness? Let the light come! “God said: Let there be light”—this is Abraham, as it is written, “Who awakened righteousness from the east?” Do not read he’ir, “awakened,” but he’ir, “illuminated.”

Bereshit contains Tishrei. This is the second arm, the second day: “He made darkness His hiding place.” The letter resh remains: it is the “head,” rosh, of the year. There is the separation between good and evil. On Rosh Hashanah the King is judgment, and all the sefirot are called judgments and ordinances from His side. All the hosts of heaven stand beside Him, on His right and His left: these incline to the side of merit, and these incline to the side of guilt. When Israel awaken through shofar blasts and raise the Shekhinah there—she is “the King’s teruah”—through ten shofar verses, for she

“Ask for yourself a sign”—literally a letter, for all of them acted through the mystery of the letters. Likewise, what is written concerning Rahab? “Give me a true sign.” This is the letter vav, which is called the letter of truth. Should you say that the other letters are not true? They are, but this letter is called the letter of truth.
Jacob traveled to Sukkot and built himself a house, and made shelters for his livestock. Therefore he called the name of the place Sukkot.

Therefore the Shekhinah is bound to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph. They are as one, and have one likeness. Thus it is written: “These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph.” Therefore, “from all the merchant’s powders,” for everything is watered from the place of the river that flows and goes forth, and all faces shine.

“These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph”—as has been said, Jacob’s entire likeness was in Joseph. Whatever happened to one happened to the other, and both go together. This is the mystery of the letter vav, spelled vav-vav: both go together, because they are one mystery and one likeness.

Do you wish to understand? Go and learn from the vessels of service. Moses sanctified the Tabernacle, but who sanctified all its vessels? Could Moses come and sanctify them? Rather, what did they do? A priest received something holy into a vessel, and the vessel became sanctified. Just as Moses sanctified through the blood of the altar, so too, when wine for a libation or a meal offering is poured into an ordinary vessel, the ordinary vessel becomes sanctified. If an ordinary vessel becomes sanctified when filled with something holy, how much more so Israel, who are holy and sanctify the new m
Speak to the children of Israel, saying: “You must keep My Shabbatot, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”
After these things, Joseph was told: “Behold, your father is ill.” He took his two sons with him, Manasseh and Ephraim.

The days of Israel drew near to die, and he called his son Joseph and said to him: “If I have found favor in your eyes, place your hand under my thigh and deal with me in kindness and truth. Please do not bury me in Egypt. When I lie with my fathers, carry me from Egypt and bury me in their burial place.” He said: “I will do as you have said.”

The days of Israel drew near to die. He called his son Joseph and said to him: “If now I have found favor in your eyes, place your hand under my thigh and deal with me in kindness and truth; please do not bury me in Egypt.”
Light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright of heart.
Yours, Hashem, are greatness, might, splendor, eternity, and majesty, for everything in the heavens and on the earth is Yours. Yours, Hashem, is the kingdom, and You are exalted as head over all.

Scripture specifies these six supernal days, as it is written: “Yours, Hashem, are greatness, might, beauty,” and so forth. “For all”—this is the Righteous One; “in the heavens”—this is Tiferet; “and in the earth”—this is the Congregation of Israel. As the Targum renders it: “Who joins heaven and earth.” That is, the foundation of the world, called “all,” joins Tiferet, called “heavens,” and the earth, called the Congregation of Israel.
She opens her mouth with wisdom, and the Torah of kindness is on her tongue.

Rabbi Elazar said: What is the meaning of “She opens her mouth with wisdom, and a Torah of kindness is upon her tongue”? Is there a Torah of kindness and a Torah that is not of kindness? Rather, Torah studied for its own sake is a Torah of kindness; Torah studied not for its own sake is a Torah that is not of kindness. Some say: Torah studied in order to teach it is a Torah of kindness; Torah studied without the intention of teaching it is a Torah that is not of kindness.
Abraham was old, advanced in years, and Hashem had blessed Abraham with everything.

It was taught: Rabbi Yitzchak said: It is written, “A joyful mother of children, hallelujah.” The mother is known; who are the children? Rabbi Shimon said: We learned that the Holy One, blessed be He, has two children, one male and one female. He gave the male to Jacob, as it is written, “Israel is My son, My firstborn,” and, “Israel, in whom I will be glorified.” He gave the daughter to Abraham, as it is written: “Hashem blessed Abraham with all.” Abraham had a daughter, and her name was Bakol, “with all.”

Rav Adda son of Rabbi Chanina said: Had Israel not sinned, only the five books of the Torah and the book of Joshua would have been given to them, because it contains the arrangement of the Land of Israel. What is the reason? “For with much wisdom comes much anger.”
Ten measures of wisdom descended to the world. The Land of Israel took nine, and the entire rest of the world took one.
You will grant truth to Jacob and kindness to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from days of old.

Rabbi Yochanan said to him: Torah and acts of kindness are understandable, for it is written: “Through kindness and truth, sin is atoned.” “Kindness” means acts of kindness, as it says: “One who pursues righteousness and kindness will find life, righteousness, and honor.” “Truth” means Torah, as it says: “Acquire truth, and do not sell it.”

Rabbi Elazar said: They went out into the wilderness to gaze. The Holy One, blessed be He, withdrew the radiance of His glory from there; they went to gaze upon Him and did not find Him. We learned that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called Torah; water means Torah, and Torah means the Holy One, blessed be He.

We learned: A person should always stir the good inclination against the evil inclination and strive against it. If it departs from him, well and good.
