If not, he should engage in Torah, for nothing breaks the evil inclination except Torah. If it departs, well and good; if not, he should remind it of the day of death, in order to break it.

Reish Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya: The rounded part of Adam’s heel dimmed the orb of the sun; how much more so the radiance of his face! Do not wonder: Ordinarily, when a person makes two salvers, one for himself and one for his household, whose does he make finer? Surely his own. So Adam was created to serve the Holy One, blessed be He, and the orb of the sun to serve created beings.

“He said”—what is meant by “he said”? We have explained it, as in “You will say in your heart”: speech in a whisper. “Gather yourselves”: should it not say “Gather,” as in “Gather My faithful ones to Me”? Rather, we know that “Gather yourselves” comes from the place above: gather yourselves in a complete bond, in a single unity. “I will tell you”—what does “I will tell” mean? It is a mystery of wisdom. Rabbi Yosei asked Rabbi Shimon: We learned that “I will tell,” “he told,” “they will tell,” and similar forms are a mystery of wisdom. Why does this expression embody a mystery of wisdom? He ans

Rabbi Yehudah says: When Israel heard “I am Hashem your God,” Torah study was fixed in their hearts; they would learn and not forget. They came to Moses and said: “Moses our teacher, become an emissary and intermediary between us,” as it says, “You speak with us and we will hear,” and, “Now, why should we die?” What benefit would there be in our destruction? They returned to learning and forgetting. They said: Just as Moses is flesh and blood and passes away, so his teaching passes away. Immediately they returned to Moses and said: Moses our teacher, if only He would reveal Himself to us a sec

They said to Him: We are poor and have nothing with which to bring offerings. He answered: I seek words, as it says, “Take words with you and return to Hashem,” and I will forgive all your sins. “Words” means words of Torah, as it says: “These are the words that Moses spoke.”

Rabbi Shimon opened and said: “Hear, Israel: Hashem our God, Hashem is One.” The ayin is large, and so is the dalet; together they signify ed, “witness.” Thus it is written: “Hashem is a witness among you.” The letters shin-mem remain, with an open mem. Why is it not closed? Because the closed mem is the supernal King, while the open mem is the lower King. The other letters, alef-chet, remain. It is written: “The glory of God is to conceal a matter.”

Ulla Bira’a said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: In the future, the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a circle for the righteous, and He will sit among them in the Garden of Eden. Each one will point with his finger, as it says: “On that day they will say: Behold, this is our God; we hoped in Him and He saved us. This is Hashem; we hoped in Him. Let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation.”

“Yet all this is worth nothing to me”: This teaches that all the treasures of that wicked man were engraved upon his heart, and when he saw Mordechai sitting at the king’s gate, he said: “All this is worth nothing to me.”

Everyone agrees that the Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat. Here it is written, “Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it,” and there it is written, “Moses said to the people: Remember this day.” Just as there it means the very day on which he was speaking, so here it means the very day.

“God completed on the seventh day”—this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day. Through it the world was perfected, for it sustains everything. “His work that He had done,” not “all His work,” for the Written Torah brought everything forth through the power of the writing that issues from Wisdom. “The seventh day” appears here three times: “God completed on the seventh day”; “He rested on the seventh day”; “God blessed the seventh day”—three times. “God completed on the seventh day”—this is the Oral Torah, for through this seventh day the world was perfected, as we have said.
He blessed Joseph and said: “The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has shepherded me from my beginning until this day.”

“He blessed Joseph and said: The God before whom…” This verse requires examination. “He blessed Joseph”—we do not find a blessing here with which he blessed Joseph, but only his sons. If it refers to his sons, it should have said “he blessed them.” What does “he blessed Joseph” mean, when we do not find Joseph being blessed here? Rabbi Yosei said: The word et is precise. It says “et Joseph.” It was a blessing for his sons, and when his sons are blessed, he is blessed, for the blessing of a person’s children is his own blessing. Rabbi Elazar said: “He blessed et Joseph”—et is precise: he blesse
He approached and kissed him. He smelled the fragrance of his garments and blessed him, saying: “See, the fragrance of my son is like the fragrance of a field that Hashem has blessed.”

“He said: See, the fragrance of my son is like the fragrance of a field that Hashem has blessed.” “He said” is an unspecified expression. Some say that it was the Shekhinah, and some say that it was Isaac. “Like the fragrance of a field that Hashem has blessed”—which field? This is the field of apples, a field that the supernal patriarchs cherish and prepare.
“Of apples”: Some interpret “apples” to mean the fragrance of etrogim.
Another interpretation: “The fruit of a beautiful tree”—these are Israel. Just as the etrog has both flavor and fragrance, so Israel includes people who possess both Torah and good deeds.

Rav Yosef said: Shall we arise and learn from Abraham? Rava said: The tanna learns from Abraham, and shall we not learn from him? For it was taught: “On the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised” teaches that the entire day is fit for circumcision, but the zealous perform commandments early, as it says: “Abraham arose early in the morning and saddled” his donkey.
“Shall we arise and learn from Abraham?”—You have come to teach us to be zealous like Abraham.

Rav Tovi son of Rav Kisna raised a contradiction before Rava: We learned, “Whoever performs one commandment is treated well.” If he performed one, yes; if he did not, no. Yet it was taught: One who sat and did not transgress is given a reward as though he had performed a commandment! He answered: That refers to a case in which an opportunity to transgress came to him and he escaped it.
He blessed Joseph and said: “The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has shepherded me from my beginning until this day.”
House and wealth are an inheritance from fathers, but an understanding wife is from Hashem.

“The angel who redeems me from all evil, may he bless the lads.” Rabbi Chiyya opened and said: “House and wealth are an inheritance from fathers.” Are they an inheritance from fathers? Does not the Holy One, blessed be He, give everything to a person? Rather, when He grants a person a house and property, the person may bequeath everything to his son, and it becomes an inheritance from fathers. But “a discerning wife is from Hashem,” because when a person receives a wife, he receives her from the Holy One, blessed be He; the Holy One, blessed be He, does not grant her to a person until they pro
Prepare your work outside and make it ready for yourself in the field; afterward, build your house.

Another interpretation: “Prepare your work outside”—this is Scripture; “make it ready for yourself in the field”—this is Mishnah; “afterward build your house”—this is Gemara. Another interpretation: “Prepare your work outside”—this is Scripture and Mishnah; “make it ready for yourself in the field”—this is Gemara; “afterward build your house”—these are good deeds. Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says: “Prepare your work outside”—this is Scripture, Mishnah, and Gemara; “make it ready for yourself in the field”—these are good deeds; “afterward build your house”—expound and receive rewa
A man who loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but one who keeps company with prostitutes loses wealth.

Rava said to him: Why did the Master say this? Rabbi Acha son of Chanina said: What is the meaning of “One who keeps company with harlots loses wealth”? Anyone who says, “This teaching is fine, but this one is not fine,” loses the wealth of Torah! He answered: I retract my statement.
Through knowledge, rooms are filled with every precious and pleasant treasure.

May the angel who redeems me from all evil bless the lads. May my name be called upon them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac, and may they multiply abundantly like fish in the midst of the earth.

Just as these fish grow in water, yet when a single drop falls from above they receive it thirstily, as though they had never tasted water in their lives, so Israel grow in water—in Torah—yet when they hear something new from the Torah, they receive it thirstily, as though they had never heard a word of Torah in their lives.
He made darkness His hiding place, His shelter around Him: dark waters and thick clouds of the skies.
May my teaching fall like rain, my speech flow like dew, like showers upon grass and like abundant drops upon vegetation.
For I have given you a good teaching; do not forsake My Torah.
Your dead will live; my dead bodies will arise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust, for Your dew is a dew of lights, and the earth will bring forth the departed.

He said to him: I expound another verse, for it is written: “For Your dew is a dew of lights, and the earth will bring forth the departed.” Whoever makes use of the light of Torah—the light of Torah revives him; whoever does not make use of the light of Torah—the light of Torah does not revive him.

Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: With every utterance that issued from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, the souls of Israel departed, as it says: “My soul departed when He spoke.” Since their souls departed at the first utterance, how did they receive the second? He brought down the dew with which He will revive the dead and revived them, as it says: “You showered a generous rain, O God; when Your inheritance was weary, You restored it.”

Within the skull dwell thirteen thousand myriads of worlds, which lift their feet upon it and rest upon it. From this skull dew drips to the one outside, filling its head each day, as it says: “My head is filled with dew.” From that dew that the one outside shakes from its head, the dead will awaken in the World to Come, as it says: “For Your dew is a dew of lights.” “Lights” means the white radiance of Atika. The supernal holy ones are sustained from that dew; it is the manna ground for the righteous in the World to Come. That dew drips into the field of holy apples, as it says: “The layer of

“He was there with Hashem forty days and forty nights.” How did Moses know when it was day? When the Holy One, blessed be He, taught him the Written Torah, he knew it was day; when He taught him orally, Mishnah and Talmud, he knew it was night. For day and night are equal before the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says, “Light dwells with Him,” and, “Even darkness is not dark for You; night shines like day; darkness is like light.” How else did he distinguish day from night? When he saw the constellations kneeling and bowing, he knew it was day; when he saw the sun bowing, he knew it was night,

“God completed on the seventh day”—this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day. Through it the world was perfected, for it sustains everything. “His work that He had done,” not “all His work,” for the Written Torah brought everything forth through the power of the writing that issues from Wisdom. “The seventh day” appears here three times: “God completed on the seventh day”; “He rested on the seventh day”; “God blessed the seventh day”—three times. “God completed on the seventh day”—this is the Oral Torah, for through this seventh day the world was perfected, as we have said.

When the sun set on Shabbat evening, the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to conceal the light, but He showed honor to Shabbat. Thus it is written: “God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it”—He blessed it with light. When the sun set on Shabbat evening, the light began to shine and continued serving; everyone began to praise, as it says: “Under all the heavens He directs it, and His light to the ends of the earth.” Why “His light to the ends of the earth”? Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Simon said: With the light that the Holy One, blessed be He, created on the first day, Adam could look and s

What does “Babel” signify? Rabbi Yochanan said: It is blended with Scripture, blended with Mishnah, and blended with Talmud. “He has made me dwell in dark places, like those long dead”—Rabbi Yirmeyah said: This is the Talmud of Babylonia.

Further, words of Torah become settled only there. There is no light except what emerges from darkness: when this side is subdued, God is exalted above and honored in His glory. Service of God comes only from darkness, and goodness only from evil. When a person enters an evil path and abandons it, God is exalted in His glory. Thus the perfection of everything is good and evil together, afterward rising through good. There is no good except what emerges from evil. Through this good His glory rises; this is complete service.

Rav Adda son of Rabbi Chanina said: Had Israel not sinned, only the five books of the Torah and the book of Joshua would have been given to them, because it contains the arrangement of the Land of Israel. What is the reason? “For with much wisdom comes much anger.”

Rabbi Abba said: Blessing is made ready for those supernal days, which are blessed from this day. This day fills the head of Zeir Anpin with the dew that descends from the Holy Ancient One, concealed beyond everything, and He casts it into the field of holy apples three times from the entrance of Shabbat, so that all will be blessed together. Therefore a person must take delight at these three times, for the faith above depends upon this: the Holy Ancient One, Zeir Anpin, and the field of apples. A person must delight in them and rejoice in them. Whoever omits one of these meals displays a def
It shall be on the day that Hashem gives you rest from your sorrow, your agitation, and the hard service that was imposed upon you.

Rabbi Shimon said further: Concerning this we learned that Shabbat resembles the World to Come. It is indeed so. Just as the sabbatical year and the Jubilee resemble one another, so do Shabbat and the World to Come. That addition to the soul comes from the mystery of “Remember” to this shelter of peace, which receives from the World to Come; it gives this addition to the holy world. Through that addition they rejoice, and all weekday affairs, all sorrow, and all distress are forgotten, as it says: “On the day that Hashem gives you rest from your sorrow, your agitation, and the hard service.”
For I know the thoughts that I think concerning you, declares Hashem—thoughts of peace and not of evil, to give you a future and hope.
It is good to give thanks to Hashem, and to sing praises to Your name, Most High.
You are righteous, Hashem, when I contend with You; yet I would speak with You of justice. Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why are all who act treacherously at ease?

How great are Your works, Hashem! Your thoughts are exceedingly deep. An ignorant person does not know, and a fool does not understand this: when the wicked flourish like grass and all evildoers blossom, it is so that they may be destroyed forever.
The righteous will flourish like a date palm; like a cedar in Lebanon he will grow tall.
Now, if I have found favor in Your eyes, please make Your ways known to me, that I may know You and find favor in Your eyes. See that this nation is Your people.

Moses asked that the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, be made known to him, and He granted it, as it says: “Please make Your ways known to me.” He said before Him: Master of the world, why is there a righteous person who prospers and a righteous person who suffers, a wicked person who prospers and a wicked person who suffers? He answered: Moses, the righteous person who prospers is the righteous son of a righteous man; the righteous person who suffers is the righteous son of a wicked man. The wicked person who prospers is the wicked son of a righteous man; the wicked person who suffers is
He said: “Please show me Your glory.”

Another interpretation: “He said: Please show me Your glory.” He desired to understand the reward of the righteous and the tranquillity of the wicked. From where do we know that the reward of the righteous is called “glory”? It says: “The wise will inherit glory,” and likewise, “Glory before His elders.” From where do we know that the tranquillity of the wicked is called “glory”? It says: “After glory You will take me.” What does the Holy One, blessed be He, answer? “He said: You cannot see My face.” The word “My face” here refers to the tranquillity of the wicked, as it is written: “He repays
I will remove My hand, and you will see My back, but My face will not be seen.
I will remove the guidance of My glory, and you will see what is behind Me; what is before Me will not be seen.

Rav Huna said: It is written, “When I take the appointed time, I will judge uprightly,” and, “On that day there will not be light, precious things, and congelation”—yikpa’un. Things concealed from you in this world will be visible to you in the World to Come, like a blind person who gains sight, as it says: “I will lead the blind on a way they did not know; on paths they did not know I will guide them.” It also says: “These things I have done.” It does not say “I will do,” but “I have done”: I have already done them for Rabbi Akiva and his companions. Another interpretation: Things not reveale
He cuts channels through the rocks, and his eye sees every precious thing.

“They shall take for you a red cow.” Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: To you I reveal the reason for the cow, but for another it is a statute. For Rav Huna said: It is written, “When I take the appointed time, I will judge uprightly,” and, “On that day there will not be light, precious things, and congelation”—the written form is yikpa’un. Things concealed from you in this world will be visible in the World to Come, like a blind person who gains sight, as it says: “I will lead the blind on a way they did not know.” It also says: “These things I
He said: “You cannot see My face, for a human being cannot see Me and live.”
In the year of King Uzziah’s death, I saw the Lord sitting upon a high and exalted throne, and the skirts of His robe filled the Temple.

Rava said: Manasseh judged Isaiah and killed him. He said to him: Moses your teacher said, “A human being cannot see Me and live,” but you said, “I saw the Lord sitting upon a high and exalted throne.” Moses your teacher said, “Who is like Hashem our God whenever we call to Him,” but you said, “Seek Hashem when He is found.” Moses your teacher said, “I will fulfill the number of your days,” but you said, “I will add fifteen years to your days.” … “I saw the Lord”—as it was taught: All the prophets looked through a mirror that did not shine; Moses our teacher looked through a mirror that shone.

Moses returned and came before the Holy One, blessed be He. He said before Him: Master of the world, You have a man like this, yet You give the Torah through me? He answered: Be silent; thus it arose in thought before Me. He said before Him: Master of the world, You have shown me his Torah; show me his reward. He answered: Turn around. He turned around and saw them weighing Rabbi Akiva’s flesh in the butcher’s market. He said before Him: Master of the world, is this Torah and this its reward? He answered: Be silent; thus it arose in thought before Me.

Rabbi Simon said: Light is mentioned here five times, corresponding to the five books of the Torah. ‘God said, Let there be light’ corresponds to Genesis, with which the Holy One, blessed be He, occupied Himself in creating His world. ‘And there was light’ corresponds to Exodus, in which Israel emerged from darkness into light. ‘God saw that the light was good’ corresponds to Leviticus, which is filled with many laws. ‘God separated the light from the darkness’ corresponds to Numbers, which distinguishes those who left Egypt from those who entered the Land. ‘God called the light day’ correspon

Rabbi Shimon said: Fortunate is the portion of the righteous person who merits that of which it is written: “Then you shall delight above Hashem.” It does not say “with Hashem,” but “above Hashem.” What is “above Hashem”? The place from which the higher and lower beings are drawn, and for which they yearn, as it is written: “From where will my help come?” and, “He reached the Ancient of Days, and they brought him before Him.” The yearning and delight of the righteous is to gaze upon that radiance from which all radiance issues and from which all those crowns are drawn.
Then you shall delight in Hashem. I will make you ride upon the heights of the earth, and I will feed you the inheritance of your father Jacob, for the mouth of Hashem has spoken.

It was taught: ‘The Shabbat burnt offering on its Shabbat, above the continual burnt offering.’ One must direct the heart higher and higher, more than on other days. Hence precisely ‘above the continual burnt offering.’ Of Hannah it says, ‘She prayed above the Lord’—precisely ‘above,’ since children depend upon the holy mazal, as explained. No word of Torah, nor even a small letter, fails to allude to upper Wisdom; heaps upon heaps of its secrets depend on each, as in ‘His locks are curled in heaps.’
She was bitter of soul, and she prayed to Hashem and wept greatly.
The woman conceived and bore a son. She saw that he was good, and she hid him for three months.

“She saw that he was good.” It was taught: Rabbi Meir says: His name was Tov. Rabbi Yehudah says: His name was Toviyyah. Rabbi Nechemyah says: He was fit for prophecy. Others say: He was born circumcised. The Sages say: When Moses was born, the entire house filled with light. Here it says, “She saw that he was good,” and there it says, “God saw that the light was good.”
God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.

Rabbi Nachman son of Shmuel bar Nachman said in the name of Rav Shmuel bar Nachman: “Behold, it was very good”—this is the good inclination; “and behold, it was very good”—this is the evil inclination. Is the evil inclination very good? Rather, without the evil inclination a person would not build a house, marry, have children, or conduct business. Thus Solomon says: “For it is a person’s jealousy of his neighbor.” Rav Huna said: “Behold, it was very good”—this is the measure of good; “and behold, it was very good”—this is the measure of suffering. Is the measure of suffering very good? Rather

If so, concerning “Who makes peace and creates evil,” do we say it just as it is written? Rather, “evil” is written, but we say “everything,” as a refined expression. Here too, let us say “brightness,” as a refined expression!

Rav Huna said in the name of Rav, in the name of Rabbi Meir, and it was likewise taught in the name of Rabbi Akiva: A person should always accustom himself to say, “Everything the Merciful One does, He does for the good.” Rabbi Akiva was once traveling. He reached a town and sought lodging, but they did not give him any. He said: “Everything the Merciful One does is for the good.” He went and slept in the open country, with a rooster, a donkey, and a lamp. A wind came and extinguished the lamp; a cat came and ate the rooster; a lion came and ate the donkey. He said: “Everything the Merciful On
You shall love Hashem your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.

When Rabbi Akiva was taken out to be executed, it was the time for reciting the Shema. They were combing his flesh with iron combs, and he was accepting upon himself the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven. His disciples said to him: Our teacher, even to this extent? He answered: All my days I was troubled by this verse, “With all your soul”—even if He takes your soul. I said: When will the opportunity come to me, so that I may fulfill it? Now that it has come to me, shall I not fulfill it? He prolonged the word “One” until his soul departed with “One.” A heavenly voice went forth and said: Fortunat

Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish interpreted the verse as referring to the exiles. “The earth was tohu”—this is the Babylonian exile, as it says: “I looked at the earth, and behold, it was tohu.” “And bohu”—this is the exile of Media: “They hastened to bring Haman.” “And darkness”—this is the Greek exile, which darkened Israel’s eyes through its decrees, telling them: Write upon the horn of an ox that you have no share in the God of Israel. “Upon the face of the deep”—this is the exile under the wicked kingdom, whose depths cannot be fathomed, like the deep. Just as the deep cannot be fathomed, so too
My God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions, and they did not harm me, because innocence was found in me before Him; and before you too, O king, I have done no harm.
The soul of man is the lamp of Hashem, searching all the chambers of the belly.
They shall be holy to their God and shall not profane the name of their God, for they offer the fire offerings of Hashem, the bread of their God, and they shall be holy.

Come and see: When nourishment is found below, nourishment is found above. This is like a king who prepared his own meal but did not prepare one for his servants. When he prepared one for his servants, he ate his meal and they ate theirs. Thus it is written: “I ate my honeycomb with my honey”—this is the King’s meal. “Eat, friends; drink and become intoxicated, beloved ones”—this is their meal, from the fragrance of the offering when its fragrance ascended. It is therefore called “a pleasing fragrance to Hashem”: fragrance for His servants, satisfaction for Hashem, from the place where the del
Your throne is established from of old; You are from eternity.

“Then Moses sang”—this is what is written: “Your throne is established from then.” Rabbi Berechyah said in the name of Rabbi Abbahu: Although You are from eternity, Your throne was not settled and You were not made known in Your world until Your children sang. Therefore it says: “Your throne is established from then.” This is like a king who fought and won a war, and they made him Augustus. They said: Before you fought the war you were a king; now we have made you Augustus. What distinction in honor is there between a king and Augustus? The king stands upon the platform, while Augustus sits. S

God blessed them, and God said to them: “Be fruitful and multiply, fill the earth and subdue it; rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of the heavens, and every living thing that moves upon the earth.”
The blessing of Hashem makes one rich, and He adds no sorrow with it.
You shall serve Hashem your God; He will bless your bread and your water, and I will remove illness from your midst.

Rava said: Length of life, children, and sustenance do not depend upon merit, but upon mazal. For Rabbah and Rav Chisda were both righteous sages: one prayed and rain came, and the other prayed and rain came. Rav Chisda lived ninety-two years; Rabbah lived forty. In Rav Chisda’s household there were sixty weddings; in Rabbah’s household, sixty bereavements. In Rav Chisda’s household there was fine flour for the dogs, and it was not needed; in Rabbah’s household, barley bread for people could not be found.
Rabbi Yosei found Rabbi Abba sitting and reading this verse: “Cast your burden upon Hashem.” The word al, “upon,” is precise, for sustenance depends upon mazala.

It was stated: Rabbi Chanina says: The constellation makes one wise, the constellation makes one wealthy, and Israel is subject to the constellations. Rabbi Yochanan said: Israel is not subject to the constellations. Rabbi Yochanan follows his own view, for Rabbi Yochanan said: From where do we know that Israel is not subject to the constellations? It says: “Thus said Hashem: Do not learn the way of the nations, and do not be terrified by the signs of heaven, for the nations are terrified by them.” They will be terrified, but Israel will not.
God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on it He rested from all His work that God had created to be done.

“Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it.” Rabbi Yitzchak said: It is written, “God blessed the seventh day,” yet concerning manna it is written, “Six days you shall gather it, but on the seventh day, Shabbat, there will be none.” Since no sustenance is found on that day, what blessing is found in it? Rather, we learned: All blessings above and below depend upon the seventh day. Why was no manna found on the seventh day? Because from that day all six supernal days receive blessing. Each gives its sustenance below, each on its own day, from the blessing with which they were blessed on the seven
He blessed them on that day, saying: “By you Israel will bless, saying: ‘May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh.’” He placed Ephraim before Manasseh.

Rabbi Yehudah opened and said: “He blessed them on that day, saying: Through you Israel will bless.” “He blessed them on that day”—what does “on that day” mean? It would have been enough to say “he blessed them.” Moreover, everywhere leimor is written defectively, but here it is written with a vav. Why the difference? Rather, it is a mystery. “He blessed them on that day”—this is the mystery of the degree appointed over blessings above. “That day”—a day from the supernal place called “He.” In “that day” there is no separation between “day” and “He”; wherever “that day” occurs, these are two de
Judah, your brothers will acknowledge you; your hand will be on the neck of your enemies; your father’s sons will bow down to you.
The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh comes, and to him will be the gathering of peoples.

Rabbi Abba said: Blessing is made ready for those supernal days, which are blessed from this day. This day fills the head of Zeir Anpin with the dew that descends from the Holy Ancient One, concealed beyond everything, and He casts it into the field of holy apples three times from the entrance of Shabbat, so that all will be blessed together. Therefore a person must take delight at these three times, for the faith above depends upon this: the Holy Ancient One, Zeir Anpin, and the field of apples. A person must delight in them and rejoice in them. Whoever omits one of these meals displays a def

“Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it”—this is the mystery of the holy covenant. Just as all the sources of the body’s limbs are sustained in this covenant, which includes them all, so Shabbat comprises the Torah, and all the mysteries of Torah depend upon it. Keeping Shabbat is like keeping the entire Torah; whoever observes Shabbat is as though he observed the entire Torah.

“Bless et Hashem”—et is precise, as we have said: this is Shabbat at the entrance of Shabbat. “Blessed is Hashem, the blessed One”—this is the drawing forth of blessings from the source of life, the place from which all watering issues to irrigate everything. Because it is the source, in the mystery of the sign of the covenant, we call it “the blessed One.” It is the spring of the well. Once they reach there, the well is certainly filled, and its waters never cease.

This wisdom is called Eden, and this Eden is drawn from the supernal Eden, the most concealed of all concealed things. From this Eden a beginning is spoken of. In Atika there is no such designation, and there is neither beginning nor end. Because there is neither beginning nor end in it, it is not called “You,” for it is hidden and unrevealed; it is called “He.” From the place where a beginning is found, it is called “You” and “Father,” as it is written: “For You are our Father.” In the aggadah of the school of Rav Yeiva Sava, the general rule is: Zeir Anpin is called “You”; Atika Kadisha, whi
Do not defile the land in which you dwell, in whose midst I dwell, for I, Hashem, dwell among the children of Israel.

Another interpretation: “Guard my soul, for I am pious.” Why? So that I may act kindly with Ani, “I,” of which it is said “Ani va-ho.” Woe to one who separates “I” from “He,” of which it is said: “He made us, and not we,” for all is one without separation. Thus it is written: “See now that I, I am He; I put to death and bring to life, I wounded and I will heal, and none can rescue from My hand.” “I am Hashem”—I am He and no other. This Ani is from Adonai; Havayah is the middle pillar.
May my teaching fall like rain, my speech flow like dew, like showers upon grass and like abundant drops upon vegetation.
I said in my heart: “Come now, I will test you with joy; experience good.” But behold, this too was vanity.
Haman entered, and the king said to him: “What should be done for the man whom the king desires to honor?” Haman said in his heart: “Whom would the king desire to honor more than me?”

“He said”—what is meant by “he said”? We have explained it, as in “You will say in your heart”: speech in a whisper. “Gather yourselves”: should it not say “Gather,” as in “Gather My faithful ones to Me”? Rather, we know that “Gather yourselves” comes from the place above: gather yourselves in a complete bond, in a single unity. “I will tell you”—what does “I will tell” mean? It is a mystery of wisdom. Rabbi Yosei asked Rabbi Shimon: We learned that “I will tell,” “he told,” “they will tell,” and similar forms are a mystery of wisdom. Why does this expression embody a mystery of wisdom? He ans

“Ask for yourself a sign”—literally a letter, for all of them acted through the mystery of the letters. Likewise, what is written concerning Rahab? “Give me a true sign.” This is the letter vav, which is called the letter of truth. Should you say that the other letters are not true? They are, but this letter is called the letter of truth.

“Bless et Hashem”—et is precise, as we have said: this is Shabbat at the entrance of Shabbat. “Blessed is Hashem, the blessed One”—this is the drawing forth of blessings from the source of life, the place from which all watering issues to irrigate everything. Because it is the source, in the mystery of the sign of the covenant, we call it “the blessed One.” It is the spring of the well. Once they reach there, the well is certainly filled, and its waters never cease.
I have given you one portion beyond your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorite with my sword and my bow.

Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Nechemiah: Rabbi Yehudah said: “I have given you one portion”—this is the birthright and the garment of Adam the first man. “Which I took from the hand of the Amorite”—this is Esau. Was Esau an Amorite? Rather, he acted like an Amorite. “With my sword and with my bow”—through commandments and good deeds.

You have declared Hashem this day to be your God, to walk in His ways, to keep His statutes, commandments, and ordinances, and to listen to His voice. Hashem has declared you this day to be His treasured people, as He spoke to you, and to keep all His commandments.

Who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth, whom God went to redeem as His people, to make Yourself a name through great and awesome deeds, driving out nations before Your people whom You redeemed from Egypt?

Does the Holy One, blessed be He, take pride in the praises of Israel? Yes, as it is written: “You have declared Hashem this day,” and, “Hashem has declared you this day.” The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: You have made Me a single, distinct entity in the world, and I will make you a single, distinct entity in the world. You have made Me a single, distinct entity in the world, as it is said: “Hear, Israel: Hashem our God, Hashem is One”; and I will make you a single, distinct entity in the world, as it is said: “Who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth?”
When it had finished eating the grass of the land, I said: “Lord Hashem, please forgive! How will Jacob stand, for he is small?”
“For Hashem listens to the needy”—these are Israel. For Rabbi Yochanan said: Wherever Scripture says “lowly,” “poor,” or “needy,” it is speaking of Israel.
Yet I destroyed the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of cedars and who was strong as oaks; I destroyed his fruit above and his roots below.

“The city of Sihon”: if a person makes himself like this young donkey that follows pleasant talk, what is written afterward? “For fire has gone forth from Heshbon.” Fire will go forth from those who reckon their deeds and consume those who do not reckon them.
For the lips of a strange woman drip honey, and her palate is smoother than oil.

In the World to Come, when the Holy One, blessed be He, exacts payment from Esau, what does Esau do? He wraps himself in his tallit like an elder, comes, and sits beside Jacob. From where is this known? It is written: “Though you set your nest among the stars.” The stars mean Israel, as it is said: “Look now toward the heavens,” and, “So shall your offspring be.” What does Jacob say to him? My brother, you will not be my brother, equal to me, as it is said: “I will be your plagues, death; I will be your destruction, Sheol; consolation will be hidden from My eyes.” “I will be your plagues, deat
He approached and kissed him. He smelled the fragrance of his garments and blessed him, saying: “See, the fragrance of my son is like the fragrance of a field that Hashem has blessed.”

Rabbi Yehudah said: It is written, “He smelled the fragrance of his garments and blessed him.” “His garments”—it should have said “Esau’s garments,” for they were not his; those garments belonged to Esau, as it is written: “Rebecca took the precious garments of Esau, her elder son.” There it says “Esau’s garments,” while here “the fragrance of his garments” implies Jacob’s. Rather, we explained it thus: “He smelled”—he looked beyond and perceived the fragrance of his garments in that world, and then he blessed him. Therefore it says: “See, the fragrance of my son is like the fragrance of a fie

Esau used to keep those garments with Rebecca, and would go out hunting in them. On that day he did not take them; he went out into the field and remained there. When Esau wore them, no fragrances rose at all. Once Jacob wore them, the lost object returned to its place and fragrances rose, because Jacob’s beauty was Adam’s beauty. Therefore at that moment they returned to their place, and fragrances rose.

The sword of the Holy One, blessed be He: yod is the point of the sword; vav is its body; the two letters heh are its two edges. “Justice, justice shall you pursue”—they pronounce two judgments, the judgment of the heavenly court and the judgment of the earthly court. From here it is known that a person does not bruise a finger below unless permission has been given from above. The sword’s sheath is Adonai; there judgment is found. In the Shema, Havayah is the sword of the Holy One, blessed be He, of which it is said: “The exalted praises of God are in their throats, and a two-edged sword is i

“Ask for yourself a sign”—literally a letter, for all of them acted through the mystery of the letters. Likewise, what is written concerning Rahab? “Give me a true sign.” This is the letter vav, which is called the letter of truth. Should you say that the other letters are not true? They are, but this letter is called the letter of truth.
You will grant truth to Jacob and kindness to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from days of old.

Rabbi Yochanan said to him: Torah and acts of kindness are understandable, for it is written: “Through kindness and truth, sin is atoned.” “Kindness” means acts of kindness, as it says: “One who pursues righteousness and kindness will find life, righteousness, and honor.” “Truth” means Torah, as it says: “Acquire truth, and do not sell it.”

Rava was accustomed to say: The purpose of wisdom is repentance and good deeds, so that a person should not read Scripture and study Mishnah while rebelling against his father, mother, teacher, or one greater than himself in wisdom or in number. For it is said: “The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem; good understanding belongs to all who perform them.” It does not say “for those who perform,” but “for those who perform them”—for those who act for the sake of the mitzvot, and not for those who act for an ulterior purpose. Whoever acts for an ulterior purpose would have been better off n
Why is there a price in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, when he has no heart?

Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: What is the meaning of “Why is there a price in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, when he has no heart”? Woe to the enemies of Torah scholars, who engage in Torah but possess no fear of Heaven.

Rabbi Yitzchak said: Whoever recites the Shema upon his bed is as though he holds a two-edged sword in his hand, as it is said: “The exalted praises of God are in their throats, and a two-edged sword is in their hand.” How does this imply it? Mar Zutra, or some say Rav Ashi, said: From the beginning of the passage, where it is written: “Let the pious rejoice in glory; let them sing upon their beds.” Afterward it is written: “The exalted praises of God are in their throats, and a two-edged sword is in their hand.”

Elazar ben Achui said: From here Israel merited the recitation of the Shema. When our father Jacob was departing from the world, he called his twelve sons and said to them: Hear the God of Israel in heaven, your Father. Is there perhaps a division in your hearts concerning the Holy One, blessed be He? They said to him: Hear, Israel our father: just as there is no division in your heart concerning the Holy One, blessed be He, so there is no division in our hearts; rather, “Hashem our God, Hashem is One.” He too pronounced with his lips: “Blessed be the name of the glory of His kingdom forever a

The sword of the Holy One, blessed be He: yod is the point of the sword; vav is its body; the two letters heh are its two edges. “Justice, justice shall you pursue”—they pronounce two judgments, the judgment of the heavenly court and the judgment of the earthly court. From here it is known that a person does not bruise a finger below unless permission has been given from above. The sword’s sheath is Adonai; there judgment is found. In the Shema, Havayah is the sword of the Holy One, blessed be He, of which it is said: “The exalted praises of God are in their throats, and a two-edged sword is i

Rabbi Yochanan said: An anonymous Mishnah is Rabbi Meir; an anonymous Tosefta is Rabbi Nechemiah; an anonymous Sifra is Rabbi Yehudah; an anonymous Sifrei is Rabbi Shimon; and all of them follow Rabbi Akiva’s opinion.

He sent Nero Caesar against them. As he was coming, he shot an arrow toward the east, and it landed in Jerusalem. Toward the west—it landed in Jerusalem. Toward all four directions—it landed in Jerusalem. He said to a child: Recite your verse for me. The child said to him: “I will place My vengeance upon Edom by the hand of My people Israel.” He said: The Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to destroy His house and wishes to wipe His hands on that man. He fled, went away, and converted, and Rabbi Meir descended from him.

So too Esau, throughout all forty years, hunted married women and violated them. When he reached forty years, he likened himself to his father, saying: Just as my father married at forty years old, so I will marry at forty years old. Thus it is written: “Esau was forty years old.”

Moreover, the Shema is a spear, romach, comprising the six words of the declaration of unity and the two hundred and forty-eight words, including “Hashem your God is true.” It is also a sling. We have explained the five stones, heh, which became one stone in the letter yod, with which one kills the evil inclination. Where is the sling? In the tefillin: the sling’s cord wrapped around the hand is the strap of the hand tefillin, like the cord of the cantillation mark zarqa. The Shema is also a bow that shoots arrows, from the side of “Blessed be the name of the glory of His kingdom,” and “Blessi
On the third day Joseph said to them, ‘Do this and live, for I fear God.’
His delight will be in the fear of Hashem; he will not judge by what his eyes see, nor decide by what his ears hear.
Rava expounded: What is the meaning of “The mandrakes have given their fragrance”? These are the young men of Israel who have not tasted the taste of sin.

Rav Huna found a fragrant hinnunita date, took it, and wrapped it in his headcloth. His son Rabba came and said to him: I smell the fragrance of hinnunita. He said to him: My son, there is purity in you. He gave it to him. Meanwhile, Rabba’s son Abba came, and Rabba took it and gave it to him. Rav Huna said to him: My son, you have gladdened my heart and set my teeth on edge. This is what people say: A father’s compassion is for his children; his children’s compassion is for the children they have.
The fear of Hashem is pure, enduring forever; the judgments of Hashem are truth, righteous altogether.

“Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it”—this is the mystery of the holy covenant. Just as all the sources of the body’s limbs are sustained in this covenant, which includes them all, so Shabbat comprises the Torah, and all the mysteries of Torah depend upon it. Keeping Shabbat is like keeping the entire Torah; whoever observes Shabbat is as though he observed the entire Torah.

Adam the first man was the firstborn of the world. When he offered his sacrifice, as it is said, “It will please Hashem more than an ox, a bull with horns and hooves,” he put on the garments of the High Priesthood, as it is said: “Hashem God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife, and clothed them.” They were garments of glory, and the firstborn would use them.
You shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother, for honor and splendor.

It is forbidden to afflict oneself on Shabbat. Rather, a Jew must delight in it through food and drink, and honor it through fine clothing and covering, as it is written: “You shall call Shabbat a delight.” “And honor it”—your clothing for Shabbat should not be like your clothing for a weekday. Rabbi Yochanan called the garments he wore on Shabbat “those that honor me.” Rav Huna said: Whoever has clothes to change into should change; whoever has none should let his garments hang lower. It was taught: Rabbi Yochanan said: A person should have two wraps, one for a weekday and one for Shabbat.

If you restrain your foot because of Shabbat, from pursuing your affairs on My holy day, and call Shabbat a delight, Hashem’s holy day honored, and honor it by refraining from your own ways, from seeking your affairs and speaking of them.

“And you shall honor it, refraining from your own ways.” “And you shall honor it”—your clothing for Shabbat should not be like your clothing for a weekday. This accords with Rabbi Yochanan, who called his garments “those that honor me.”

From where do we know the rule concerning a priest lacking the required garments? Rabbi Abbahu said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, and some trace it to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon: “You shall gird them with a sash.” While their garments are upon them, their priesthood is upon them; when their garments are not upon them, their priesthood is not upon them. They are then like non-priests, and the master said: A non-priest who performs the Temple service is liable to death.

Do you think that perhaps I gave you Shabbat for your harm? I gave it to you only for your good. How? Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said: You sanctify Shabbat with food, drink, and clean clothing, and give yourself pleasure, and I give you reward. From where is this known? “You shall call Shabbat a delight.” What is written afterward? “Then you shall delight in Hashem,” and, “He will grant you your heart’s requests.”

When the Tree of Good and Evil rules, comprising the profane that is pure and the profane that is impure, those sages who resemble Shabbat and festivals have only what those of the profane realm give them, just as Shabbat has only what is prepared for it during the weekdays.

Ameimar said: Who are the “ministering angels”? The sages. For if you say that they are actual ministering angels, why did Rabbi Yochanan say that the law does not follow Yochanan ben Dahabai? They are surely more knowledgeable about the formation of the child! Why, then, were the sages called ministering angels? Because they are distinguished like ministering angels.
Show me the Torah scholars of Babylonia. They resemble ministering angels.

“They resemble ministering angels”—dressed in white and wrapped like ministering angels, as it is written: “The man clothed in linen.” Likewise, in Bameh Madlikin we say of Rabbi Yehudah that he would wrap himself and sit in linen garments with fringes, resembling an angel. In Nedarim too we say: Who are the ministering angels? The sages. Why are they called ministering angels? Because they are distinguished like ministering angels, in fine garments.
Sudara, a headcloth—“The secret of Hashem is for those who fear Him.”

This is like Rav Kahana, who took a headcloth in payment for the redemption of a firstborn son and said: For me it is worth five selaim. Rav Ashi said: We stated this only in a case like Rav Kahana, who is a distinguished person and needs a headcloth upon his head; it does not apply to everyone. Likewise, Mar son of Rav Ashi bought a headcloth worth ten for thirteen from the mother of Rava of Kubi.

A certain town official went and stood near a sorb tree close to the town. Sixty demons entered him, and he was endangered. He came to a certain sage who did not know that the sorb tree was the abode of sixty demons, and the sage wrote an amulet for one demon. He heard them celebrating within the man and singing: “The master’s headcloth is like that of a Torah scholar, but we have examined the master and found that he does not know ‘Blessed.’” A sage who knew that the sorb tree had sixty demons came and wrote an amulet for sixty demons. He heard them say: “Remove your belongings from here.”
For the lips of a priest should guard knowledge, and Torah should be sought from his mouth, for he is a messenger of Hashem of hosts.

Rav Acha said: It does not say here “and sustain your hearts,” levavkhem, but “and sustain your hearts,” libkhem. This teaches that the evil inclination does not rule over angels. This accords with Rabbi Chiyya’s view, for Rabbi Chiyya said: It does not say “Set your hearts,” levavkhem, “upon her rampart,” but libkhem. This teaches that the evil inclination will not rule in the future.

Again, what is written in it? “You shall not murder,” “You shall not commit adultery,” “You shall not steal.” Is there jealousy among you? Is there an evil inclination among you? Immediately they acknowledged the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said: “Hashem, our Lord, how mighty is Your name”; but it does not say here, “Place Your glory upon the heavens.”
My covenant with him was life and peace; I gave them to him for reverence, and he feared Me and stood in awe before My name.

Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: This was Rabbi Yehudah bar Ilai’s practice. On Shabbat eve they would bring him a basin filled with hot water. He would wash his face, hands, and feet, wrap himself, and sit in linen garments with fringes, resembling an angel of Hashem of hosts.

“God completed on the seventh day”—this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day. Through it the world was perfected, for it sustains everything. “His work that He had done,” not “all His work,” for the Written Torah brought everything forth through the power of the writing that issues from Wisdom. “The seventh day” appears here three times: “God completed on the seventh day”; “He rested on the seventh day”; “God blessed the seventh day”—three times. “God completed on the seventh day”—this is the Oral Torah, for through this seventh day the world was perfected, as we have said.

Come and see: “From Asher, his bread is rich.” This is the place that all call blessed. What is it? The World to Come, which those above and below call blessed and long for. “His bread is rich”—whose? Until now the place has not been specified. Rather, there is bread and there is bread, just as there is a tree and there is a tree: a Tree of Life, and a tree on which death depends. There is bread called “bread of poverty,” and bread called “bread of delight.” What is it? This is vav: lachmo, “his bread,” is lechem-vav, “bread of vav.” Thus it is written, “Behold, I am raining bread for you from

You shall not eat leaven with it. For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread with it, bread of poverty, for you left the land of Egypt in haste, so that you may remember the day you left the land of Egypt all the days of your life.

Another Shabbat, which had not been mentioned, remained and was ashamed. She said before Him: “Master of the world, from the day You made me I have been called Shabbat; and a day does not exist without a night.” He said to her: “My daughter, you are Shabbat, and Shabbat I call you; but now I crown you with a still higher crown.” He issued a proclamation and said, “You shall fear My sanctuary.” This is the Shabbat of Shabbat eve: she is fear, and fear rests in her.
From your dwelling places you shall bring two loaves as a wave offering. They shall be made of two tenths of an ephah of fine flour, baked leavened, as firstfruits to Hashem.
The Sages taught: Three things are harmful in excess and beneficial in small measure: leaven, salt, and refusal.

Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Yose was coming from Cappadocia to Lod when Rabbi Yehudah met him. Rabbi Yitzchak said: “Would you say that our companions, the masters of the Mishnah, have considered this matter—that the evil inclination will be removed from the world except at the time of union?” He answered: “By your life, the evil inclination is as necessary to the world as rain. Without it, there would be no joy in Torah learning. But it will not be debased as formerly, so that people sin through it.” Thus it is written, “They shall neither harm nor destroy in all My holy mountain.” Rabbi Shim
From Asher, his bread shall be rich, and he shall provide royal delicacies.

Therefore, “From Asher, his bread is rich”—lechem-vav, “bread of vav”—for this tree is nourished from it, and it crowns him, as it is written, “With the crown with which his mother crowned him.” When he receives, certainly “he will provide royal delicacies.” Who is the king? The Congregation of Israel, for she is nourished from him, and he gives to her through the Righteous One, the holy degree, the sign of the covenant. From here it reaches the other degrees below, all of them corresponding to what is above.

Come and see: From the World to Come, a flow extends to this Righteous One, to give delights and pleasures to this earth, which is “bread of poverty,” so that it becomes “bread of delight.” This is the meaning of “From Asher, his bread is rich, and he will provide royal delicacies”—certainly, as we have explained.

The highest nourishment of all is the nourishment of the companions who occupy themselves with Torah. They eat the nourishment of spirit and soul, and do not eat bodily nourishment at all. It comes from the exalted place, more precious than all, called Chokhmah. Therefore the companions’ bodies are weaker than those of other people, for they do not eat bodily nourishment at all; they eat the nourishment of spirit and soul from a distant, exalted place, more precious than all. That nourishment is therefore subtler than subtle, beyond all others. Happy is their portion! Thus it is written, “Wisd
For wisdom provides shelter, as money provides shelter; but the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom gives life to those who possess it.
On the sixth day they gathered a double portion of bread, two omers for each person. All the leaders of the congregation came and told Moses.

In the book of Rav Hamnuna the Elder it says: “From Asher, his bread is rich”—this is Shabbat bread, which is delight, two for one, as it is written, “They gathered double bread.” What is “double bread”? Two kinds of bread: bread from heaven and bread from the earth. One is bread of delight, and the other is the poor person’s bread. On Shabbat the lower bread is included in the upper bread; the former is blessed because of the latter, and it is double bread.

At that time it will be said of Moses and Israel, “Then you shall delight in Hashem,” with oneg: ayin—Eden; nun—river; gimel—garden. The verse “Then Moses will sing” will be fulfilled: it does not say “sang,” but “will sing.” For the mixed multitude and the idolatrous nations, oneg, “delight,” will turn into nega, “affliction,” as with Pharaoh and the Egyptians, upon whom blistering boils erupted. But for Israel there will be delight.
A river goes out from Eden to water the garden; from there it divides and becomes four heads.

The words of Amos, who was among the shepherds of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
Are you not like the children of the Cushites to Me, children of Yisrael? says Hashem. Did I not bring Yisrael up from the land of Egypt, the Philistines from Kaftor, and Aram from Kir?
He left all that he had in Yosef’s hand, and with him there he concerned himself with nothing except the bread that he ate. Yosef was handsome in form and handsome in appearance.

Why are the nations tainted? Because they did not stand at Mount Sinai. When the serpent came upon Eve, it implanted pollution in her. Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, had their pollution cease; the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai, did not have their pollution cease. Rav Aha, Rava’s son, asked Rav Ashi: What about converts? He answered: Though they themselves were not there, their heavenly roots were there, as it says, “Those standing here with us today before the Lord our God, and those who are not here.” This disagrees with Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, who said: The pollution did not ce

Rabbi Yirmeyah ben Elazar said: During all the years when Adam was under a ban, he begot spirits, demons, and night spirits, as it says, “Adam lived one hundred and thirty years and begot in his likeness, according to his image”—implying that until then he did not beget according to his image. An objection was raised: Rabbi Meir used to say that Adam was exceedingly pious. When he saw that death had been decreed because of him, he fasted for one hundred and thirty years, separated from his wife for one hundred and thirty years, and wore girdles of fig leaves upon his flesh for one hundred and

Er, Judah’s firstborn, was evil in Hashem’s eyes, and Hashem put him to death. Judah said to Onan: Go in to your brother’s wife, perform the duty of a brother-in-law toward her, and raise up offspring for your brother. Onan knew that the offspring would not be his; whenever he went in to his brother’s wife, he wasted his seed on the ground, so as not to give offspring to his brother. What he did was evil in Hashem’s eyes, and He put him to death as well.

Therefore he said, “The dead do not praise Yah.” “The dead do not”—for the living must praise the Living One; the dead cannot do so. “But we shall bless Yah,” for we are alive and have no share whatever in the side of death. Hezekiah said, “The living, the living, he shall thank You, as I do,” because the living draw near to the Living One. King David is alive, and his nearness is to the Life of the worlds. Whoever draws near to Him is alive, as it is written, “You who cleave to Hashem your God are all alive today,” and, “Benaiah son of Jehoiada, son of a living man, great in deeds, of Kabzeel
He will swallow up death forever. The Lord Hashem will wipe tears from every face, and He will remove His people’s disgrace from all the earth, for Hashem has spoken.
“Joab sent to Tekoa and took from there a wise woman.” What is distinctive about Tekoa? Rabbi Yochanan said: Because they are accustomed to olive oil, wisdom is found among them.

The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: If this repulsive one encounters you, draw him into the house of study. If he is stone, he will dissolve; if iron, he will shatter. If he is stone, he will dissolve, for it is written, “Ho, everyone who thirsts, go to water,” and it is written, “Water wears away stones.” If he is iron, he will shatter, for it is written, “Is not My word like fire, declares Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters rock?”

So the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: “My children, I created the evil inclination, and I created Torah as its seasoning. If you occupy yourselves with Torah, you will not be handed over to it, as it is said, ‘If you do well, you shall be lifted up.’”
On a day of good, be in good; and on a day of evil, consider: God has made the one corresponding to the other, so that a person will find nothing that comes after him.

Rabbi Avira expounded—and some say Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: The evil inclination has seven names. The Holy One, blessed be He, called it “evil,” as it is written, “For the inclination of a person’s heart is evil from his youth.” Moses called it “uncircumcised,” as it is written, “Circumcise the foreskin of your heart.” David called it “impure,” as it is written, “Create for me a pure heart, O God”—implying that there is an impure heart.
All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is what their father spoke to them when he blessed them: each according to his blessing, he blessed them.

“He blessed them.” It should have said, “Each according to his blessing, he blessed him.” Why does it say “he blessed them”? Since he gave Judah the strength of a lion, Benjamin the ravenousness of a wolf, and Naphtali the swiftness of a deer, you might think he did not include them all in all the blessings. Therefore it says, “He blessed them.”
May Hashem bless you and guard you.
Remember the Shabbat day, to sanctify it.

He opened and said: “May Hashem bless you from Zion, and may you see the good of Jerusalem.” “May Hashem bless you from Zion”—from there blessings emerge to water the garden. He comprises all blessings and gives them to her; afterward, “may you see the good of Jerusalem.” This shows that all blessings come from male and female. Likewise, “May Hashem bless you and guard you”: “May Hashem bless you”—from the male; “and guard you”—from the female. “May Hashem bless you”—from “Remember”; “and guard you”—from “Keep.” It is all one matter, because from both of them blessings issue to the worlds. The
Keep the Shabbat day to sanctify it, as Hashem your God commanded you.

“You shall keep My commandments and perform them.” We have learned concerning the Master of the world’s commandments: it is written, “You shall keep My commandments and perform them.” If keeping is what is required, why is performance needed? Furthermore, all the Torah’s commandments have two aspects that are one: “Remember” and “Keep.” “Remember” belongs to the male; “Keep” to the female, and all form one unity. If “Keep” belongs to the female, why is it written, “You shall keep My commandments”?
Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it.

The angel who redeems me from all evil, may he bless the lads; may my name and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac be called upon them, and may they multiply abundantly in the midst of the earth.

He opened and said: “The angel who redeems me from all evil.” This verse must be examined. Why does it say “who redeems,” rather than “who redeemed”? Because he is constantly present with people and never departs from a righteous person. Come and see: “The angel who redeems me”—this is the Shechinah, which goes with a person continually and does not depart when he keeps the Torah’s commandments. Therefore a person must take care not to go alone on the road. What does “alone” mean? He must take care to keep the Torah’s commandments, so that the Shechinah will not depart from him and leave him t

Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: What is the meaning of “Why is there a price in the fool’s hand to acquire wisdom, when he has no heart”? Woe to those Torah scholars who occupy themselves with Torah but have no fear of Heaven.
Why is there payment in a fool’s hand to acquire wisdom, when he has no heart?
To declare Your kindness in the morning and Your faithfulness in the nights.

For this reason the masters of the Mishnah taught, “Study is not the main thing, but action.” The Holy One, blessed be He, is concealed in the Torah’s mysteries. Through what does He become known? Through the commandments, which are His Shechinah, His likeness. As He is humble, His Shechinah is humble. He is pious, and she is pious; He is mighty, and she rules over all the world’s nations. He is truth, and she is faith. He is a prophet, and she a prophetess; He is righteous, and she is righteous. He is King, and she is kingship. He is wise, and she is wisdom. He understands, and she is His und
A wise person’s heart is at his right, and a fool’s heart at his left.
God called the light day, and the darkness He called night. There was evening and there was morning: one day.
For a mitzvah is a lamp, and Torah is light, and the reproofs of discipline are the way of life.
From where is the blessing before Torah study derived from the Torah? From “For I shall proclaim the name of Hashem; ascribe greatness to our God.”
For I shall proclaim Hashem’s name; ascribe greatness to our God.

On the seventh day God completed His work that He had done, and on the seventh day He ceased from all His work that He had done. God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, for on it He ceased from all His work that God had created to do.
The children of Yisrael shall keep Shabbat, to observe Shabbat throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant.

In Bereshit are trei, “two,” and Shabbat, thus: bet, reshit; bara shit. These are two Shabbatot, concerning which it is said, “The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat, to make Shabbat.” Shabbat is mentioned here twice, corresponding to the upper and lower Shechinah. “Throughout their generations”—what is ledorotam? Happy is the one who makes them a dwelling on Shabbat in the heart’s two chambers, and removes from there the evil inclination, which is desecration of Shabbat. “An everlasting covenant”—this is the Righteous One, upon whom both dwell: one to fill him, and one to be filled from hi

Come and see: All the supernal blessings have been entrusted to this degree, to bless everything. Although she has no light of her own, all blessings, all joy, and all goodness abide in her and issue from her. Therefore she is called the “cup of blessing,” and she is called blessing itself, as it is written, “Hashem’s blessing makes rich.” Thus it is written, “Full of Hashem’s blessing, inherit the sea and the south.”
The blessing of Hashem makes rich, and He adds no sorrow with it.
Of Naphtali he said: Naphtali, satisfied with favor and filled with Hashem’s blessing, take possession of the sea and the south.

Therefore it is a priest, and no other: a priest, so that through him his crown of Chesed will be aroused, for he is called pious, as it is written, “To Your pious man,” and he comes from the side of Chesed. It is written, “Your pious ones shall bless You”—do not read yevarkhukhah, “shall bless You,” but yevarkhu koh, “shall bless Koh.” “Thus shall you bless”—with the explicit Name; “Thus shall you bless”—in the holy tongue.
All Your works shall thank You, Hashem, and Your faithful ones shall bless You.

The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: “Wicked one, do you think that through you a blessing upon My children will come to pass, or its opposite? They have no need of you, as people say to the wasp. Rather, return to Balak. When you open your mouth it will not be under your control, and speech will not depend upon your mouth. Instead, ‘Thus [Koh] shall you speak.’ Koh is ready to bless them. Koh will speak My children’s blessing: when you open your mouth, she will speak the words that are to be fulfilled upon My children, for I will not leave the words to you.”
Speak to Aaron and his sons, saying: Thus shall you bless the children of Israel; say to them:
A river goes out from Eden to water the garden; from there it divides and becomes four heads.
God saw the light, that it was good, and God separated the light from the darkness.
Light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright of heart.
The light of the righteous rejoices, but the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.

Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: I too say that not all are destined for light, and not all for joy. The righteous are destined for light, and the upright for joy. The righteous for light, as it says, “Light is sown for the righteous”; the upright for joy, as it says, “And joy for the upright of heart.”

In Bereshit are trei, “two,” and Shabbat, thus: bet, reshit; bara shit. These are two Shabbatot, concerning which it is said, “The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat, to make Shabbat.” Shabbat is mentioned here twice, corresponding to the upper and lower Shechinah. “Throughout their generations”—what is ledorotam? Happy is the one who makes them a dwelling on Shabbat in the heart’s two chambers, and removes from there the evil inclination, which is desecration of Shabbat. “An everlasting covenant”—this is the Righteous One, upon whom both dwell: one to fill him, and one to be filled from hi
Sweet is the worker’s sleep, whether he eats little or much, but the rich man’s satiety does not let him sleep.

They said to him: “But you said, ‘The abundance of the rich does not allow him to sleep.’ What does this mean? Surely it allows him to sleep, for anyone who is sated is brought to sleep by his food!” He told them: “I speak of those rich in Torah, not of those rich in money.” How so? A great person, rich in Torah, taught many students, spread Torah publicly, and was sated with Torah. Even after he dies, the students he established do not let him sleep. They sit and occupy themselves with Torah, Talmud, halakhot, and aggadot; they state laws and teachings in his name, mention his name continuall
The rich and poor meet; Hashem is the Maker of them all.

Likewise it says, “The poor man and the man of intrigues meet; Hashem gives light to the eyes of both.” When a student goes to his teacher and says, “Teach me Torah,” if he teaches him, “Hashem gives light to the eyes of both.” If not, “The rich and poor meet; Hashem makes them all”: He who made this one wise makes him foolish, and who made that one foolish makes him wise. This is Rabbi Natan’s teaching.

‘God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it.’ It is written, ‘The Lord’s blessing brings riches, and He adds no sorrow with it.’ ‘The Lord’s blessing brings riches’ refers to Shabbat, as it says, ‘God blessed the seventh day.’ ‘He adds no sorrow with it’ refers to mourning, as in the verse, ‘The king was grieved over his son.’

All agree that the Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat. Here it is written, “Remember the day of Shabbat to sanctify it,” and there it is written, “Moses said to the people: Remember this day.” Just as there it means that very day, so here it means that very day.

“God completed on the seventh day”—this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day. Through it the world was completed, for it sustains everything. “His work which He had made,” and not “all His work,” for the Written Torah brings everything forth through the power of writing, which issues from wisdom.

Come and see: corresponding to those seven righteous ones, the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded in the Torah that an additional offering be brought on seven occasions in the year, to add delights and pleasures for them from the King’s house, so that the fathers may first be satisfied, and afterward the children. These are seven occasions, and no more. On Shabbat it corresponds to the righteous one, the foundation of the world, who is called “all” and called Shabbat, to add delights for him from the concealed mind. On the new moon it corresponds to the congregation of Israel, who is called th

A psalm of David. Hashem is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing. He makes me lie down in grassy pastures; He leads me beside restful waters. He restores my soul; He guides me in paths of righteousness for His name’s sake. Even when I walk in the valley of the shadow of death, I shall fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff comfort me.

He blessed Joseph and said: The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has shepherded me from my beginning until this day; the angel who redeems me from all evil, may he bless the lads; may my name and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac be called upon them, and may they multiply abundantly in the midst of the earth.

Rabbi Elazar said: He compared redemption to sustenance, and sustenance to redemption: just as redemption is doubled, so sustenance is doubled; just as sustenance is daily, so redemption is daily. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said: Sustenance is greater than redemption, for redemption is through an angel, whereas sustenance comes through the Holy One, blessed be He. Redemption through an angel: “The angel who redeems me”; sustenance through the Holy One, blessed be He: “You open Your hand and satisfy every living thing.”

Rabbi Yochanan said: Providing a person’s sustenance is more difficult than redemption. Concerning redemption it is written, “The angel who redeems me from all evil”—merely an angel. But concerning sustenance it is written, “The God who shepherds me.”

“Moses was shepherding the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, priest of Midian.” Rabbi Chiyya opened and said: “A psalm of David. Hashem is my shepherd; I shall not lack.” That is, Hashem is the shepherd who tends me. Just as a shepherd leads the sheep and brings them to good pasture, rich pasture, beside streams of water, and directs their movement in righteousness and justice, so too the Holy One, blessed be He—as it is written, “He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside restful waters; He restores my soul.”
I will give grass in your field for your animals, and you will eat and be satisfied. Guard yourselves, lest your heart be enticed and you turn aside, serve other gods, and bow down to them.

“You shall eat and be satisfied”; “Take care lest your heart be enticed.” He said to them: Take care lest you rebel against the Omnipresent, for a person rebels against the Omnipresent only from satiation. As it says: “Lest you eat and be satisfied, build good houses and dwell in them, and your cattle and sheep multiply and your silver and gold increase.” What does it say afterward? “Your heart will be exalted and you will forget Hashem your God.” Similarly, “When I bring them to the land that I swore to their fathers, flowing with milk and honey”—what follows? “They will turn to other gods.”
Keep falsehood and lying words far from me; give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me my allotted bread.

“He restores my soul”—through Your Torah, as it says, “The Torah of Hashem is perfect, restoring the soul.” “He guides me in paths of righteousness”—through the manna, the well, the quail, and the clouds of glory; not because I possess merit, but for His name’s sake. “Even when I walk through the valley of the shadow of death”—in the heart of the wilderness. “I shall fear no evil, for You are with me”: “Hashem went before them by day.” “Your rod”—these are sufferings; “Your staff”—this is Torah. “They comfort me.” Could it mean without sufferings? Scripture says, “Only goodness and kindness sh
Happy is the person who does this, and the son of man who holds fast to it: who guards Shabbat from desecrating it and guards his hand from doing any evil.

Perhaps you will say: What reward does one who observes Shabbat receive? Scripture teaches: “Happy is the person who does this, and the one who holds fast to it: who keeps Shabbat from profaning it and keeps his hand from doing any evil.” Thus we learn that whoever observes Shabbat even under difficult circumstances is saved from transgression.

It was taught: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehudah says: Two ministering angels accompany a person on Friday evening from the synagogue to his home, one good and one evil. When he comes home and finds a lamp lit, a table arranged, and his bed prepared, the good angel says, “May it be so on another Shabbat,” and the evil angel answers “Amen” against his will. If not, the evil angel says, “May it be so on another Shabbat,” and the good angel answers “Amen” against his will.

When does a person come to be purified? When he is thirteen years old. Then he is joined by both: one on the right and one on the left—the good inclination on the right and the evil inclination on the left. These are literally two appointed angels, and they are constantly present with the person.

Rabbi Levi bar Chama said in Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish’s name: A person should always stir the good inclination against the evil inclination, as it says, “Tremble, and do not sin.” If he defeats it, well and good; if not, he should occupy himself with Torah, as it says, “Speak within your hearts.” If he defeats it, well and good; if not, he should recite the Shema, as it says, “Upon your beds.” If he defeats it, well and good; if not, he should remember the day of death, as it says, “And be silent, selah.”

We have been taught that it behoves man always to rouse the good prompter against the evil prompter; if the latter departs, well and good, but if not, the man should study the Torah, as there is nothing so well calculated to crush the evil prompter as the Torah; if he departs, well and good, but if not, let the man remind him of the day of death so as thereby to subdue him.

Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: A person’s evil inclination grows stronger against him every day and seeks to kill him, as it says: “The wicked watches the righteous and seeks to kill him.” If the Holy One, blessed be He, did not help him, he could not overcome it, as it says: “Hashem will not leave him in its hand, nor condemn him when he is judged.”

The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: If this repulsive one encounters you, draw him into the house of study. If he is stone, he will dissolve; if iron, he will shatter. If he is stone, he will dissolve, for it is written, “Ho, everyone who thirsts, go to water,” and it is written, “Water wears away stones.” If he is iron, he will shatter, for it is written, “Is not My word like fire, declares Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters rock?”

“Israel saw Joseph’s sons and said: Who are these?” Rabbi Yehudah bar Shalom said: Did he not recognize them? Every day they sat and studied Torah before him, and now he asks, “Who are these?” After they had served him for the seventeen years he spent in Egypt, did he not recognize them? Rather, he saw Jeroboam son of Nebat and Ahab son of Omri arising from Ephraim as idolaters, and the holy spirit departed from him. When Joseph saw this, he immediately prostrated himself on the ground and pleaded for mercy before the Holy One, blessed be He: “Master of the world, if they are worthy of blessin
