Another explanation: “Behold, I send an angel.” This is what is written, “The angel of Hashem encamps around those who fear Him and rescues them.” When a person performs one mitzvah, the Holy One, blessed be He, gives him one angel to guard him, as it says, “The angel of Hashem encamps.” If he performs two mitzvot, He gives him two angels to guard him, as it says, “For He will command His angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways.” If he performs many mitzvot, the Holy One, blessed be He, gives him half His camp, as it says, “A thousand shall fall at your side, and ten thousand at y

Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says: One who performs one mitzvah acquires one advocate; one who commits one transgression acquires one accuser. Repentance and good deeds are like a shield against calamity.

The angel of Hashem called to Abraham a second time from heaven and said: By Myself I have sworn, declares Hashem, because you have done this thing and have not withheld your son, your only one, I shall surely bless you and greatly multiply your offspring like the stars of heaven and like the sand on the seashore. Your offspring shall possess the gate of their enemies. All the nations of the earth shall bless themselves through your offspring, because you have listened to My voice.
He blessed them that day, saying: Through you Israel shall bless, saying, May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh. He placed Ephraim before Manasseh.
I am Hashem your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slaves. You shall have no other gods before Me.

Rabbi Yehuda says: When Israel heard “I am the Lord your God,” Torah study became fixed in their hearts. They learned without forgetting. They came to Moses and said: Moses our teacher, become an intermediary between us, as it says, “You speak with us, and we shall hear,” and, “Now, why should we die? What benefit is there in our destruction?” They reverted to learning and forgetting. They said: As Moses is flesh and blood and passes away, so his teaching passes away. They immediately returned to Moses, saying: Moses our teacher, would that He reveal Himself to us a second time! “Would that He
In return for my love they accuse me, but I am prayer.

Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: What does “The utterance of David son of Yishai, the utterance of the man raised on high” mean? It is the utterance of David son of Yishai, who established the yoke of repentance.
These are David’s last words: the utterance of David son of Yishai, the utterance of the man raised on high, the anointed of the God of Yaakov and the sweet singer of Yisrael.

Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to Hashem. He said: Please, Hashem, remember how I have walked before You in truth and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in Your eyes. Hezekiah wept greatly.
What does “I have done what is good in Your eyes” mean? Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: He joined redemption to prayer. Rabbi Levi said: He put away the book of remedies.

Moreover, the Shechinah does not rest upon him at all. Then it is written, “Hezekiah turned his face to the wall.” We have learned that he directed his thoughts and resolved to take a wife, so that the Shechinah—the mystery of “wall”—would rest upon him. Therefore it is written afterward, “He prayed to Hashem.” From here we learn: Whoever has a sin and wishes to seek mercy must first direct his purpose and thoughts toward repairing that sin, and afterward pray. As it is said, first, “Let us search our ways and examine them,” and afterward, “and return.” Here too, when Hezekiah knew his sin, “H

Come and see what is written in his prayer: “Please, Hashem, remember how I have walked before You.” He hinted here that he guarded the holy covenant, did not defile it, and guarded it properly. Here it says, “I have walked before You,” and there, “Walk before Me and be whole, and I shall place My covenant between Me and you”—he guarded the holy covenant properly. “In truth and with a whole heart”—he directed his intention to all the mysteries of faith contained in truth. “I have done what is good in Your eyes”—he joined redemption to prayer, as we have explained. The companions explained that
When Abram was ninety-nine years old, Hashem appeared to Abram and said to him: I am El Shaddai; walk before Me and be whole.
Against You alone have I sinned, and what is evil in Your eyes I have done, so that You are justified when You speak and blameless when You judge.

Come and see: It is written, “Woe to the wicked—evil!” Since it says “Woe to the wicked,” why add “evil”? As we said: he made himself evil. It is written, “Evil shall not dwell with You.” All others ascend, but this one does not ascend. If you ask about other sinners who killed people: all of them ascend, but he does not. Why? They killed other people, whereas this one kills his own children and sheds much blood. Of other sinners in the world it is not written, “It was evil in Hashem’s eyes,” but here it is written, “What he did was evil in Hashem’s eyes.” Why? Because it is written, “He waste

Rabbi Elazar said: Even for one righteous person the world was created, as it says, “God saw the light, that it was good.” “Good” means none other than a righteous person, as it says, “Say of the righteous that he is good.”
Say of the righteous that it is good, for they shall eat the fruit of their deeds.

He said to him: “Why is this so severe?” He answered, “Because you did not engage in being fruitful and multiplying.” He said, “Because I saw through the holy spirit that unworthy children would issue from me.” He answered him: “Why concern yourself with the Merciful One’s hidden matters? You must do what you were commanded, and let the Holy One, blessed be He, do what is pleasing before Him.”

“Israel saw Joseph’s sons and said: Who are these?” Rabbi Yehudah bar Shalom said: Did he not recognize them? Every day they sat and studied Torah before him, and now he asks, “Who are these?” After they had served him for the seventeen years he spent in Egypt, did he not recognize them? Rather, he saw Jeroboam son of Nebat and Ahab son of Omri arising from Ephraim as idolaters, and the holy spirit departed from him. When Joseph saw this, he immediately prostrated himself on the ground and pleaded for mercy before the Holy One, blessed be He: “Master of the world, if they are worthy of blessin

This Messiah is from the tribe of Ephraim and from the seed of Jeroboam son of Nebat, through Abijah, who died in his youth. On the day he died, a son was born to him and was taken from Jeroboam’s house to the wilderness. One hundred and seventy warriors went there, all righteous men from the tribe of Ephraim who had no part in Jeroboam’s sin. From this son of Abijah will emerge this Messiah. Therefore it is written, “All Israel shall mourn him and bury him.” This conceals both a prophecy for that time and a prophecy for the future: “For he alone of Jeroboam’s house shall come to the grave, be
He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for Ahab’s daughter was his wife; he did what was evil in Hashem’s eyes.
Come now, let us reason together, says Hashem. Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall become white as snow; though they are red like crimson, they shall become like wool.

Why does the verse say ka-shanim, which can mean “like years”? It should say ka-shani, “like scarlet.” Rabbi Yitzchak said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: Even if your sins are like these years that have been arranged and have unfolded from the six days of creation until now, they will become white as snow.

Reish Lakish said: Great is repentance, for deliberate sins become like unwitting sins, as it says, “Return, Israel, to Hashem your God, for you have stumbled in your iniquity.” Iniquity is deliberate, yet it is called a stumbling. Is that so? Did Reish Lakish not say: Great is repentance, for deliberate sins become merits, as it says, “When the wicked turns from his wickedness and practices justice and righteousness, by them he shall live”? There is no difficulty: the latter refers to repentance from love, and the former to repentance from fear.

Rabbi Nachman bar Shmuel bar Nachman said in Rav Shmuel bar Nachman’s name: “Behold, it was very good”—this is the good inclination; “and behold, it was very good”—this is the evil inclination. Is the evil inclination very good? Rather, without the evil inclination a person would not build a house, marry a wife, have children, or conduct business. Thus Solomon says, “It is a man’s envy of his fellow.”
God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.

Then, when Scripture says “He makes peace and creates evil,” do we say it exactly as written? Rather, it is written “evil,” and we say “everything,” using a favorable expression. Here too, let us say “radiance,” using a favorable expression!
I form light and create darkness; I make peace and create evil. I, Hashem, do all these things.
A river goes out from Eden to water the garden; from there it divides and becomes four heads.
Please take my blessing that has been brought to you, for God has favored me, and I have everything. He urged him, and he took it.

Scripture specifies these six supernal days: “Yours, Hashem, are greatness, might, beauty,” and so forth. “For all”—this is the Righteous One. “In heaven”—this is Tiferet; “and on earth”—this is the Congregation of Israel. As the Targum renders it, “who joins heaven and earth”: the foundation of the world, called “All,” joins Tiferet, called heaven, with the earth, called the Congregation of Israel.
Yours, Hashem, are greatness, might, splendor, victory, and majesty, for everything in the heavens and on the earth is Yours. Yours, Hashem, is kingship, and You are exalted as head over all.
Joseph died at the age of one hundred and ten years. They embalmed him, and he was placed in a coffin in Egypt.

How did Moses our teacher know where Joseph was buried? They said: Serach daughter of Asher remained from that generation. Moses went to her and said, “Do you know where Joseph is buried?” She told him, “The Egyptians made a metal coffin for him and fixed it in the Nile so that its waters would be blessed.” Moses went and stood at the bank of the Nile. He said, “Joseph, Joseph! The time has arrived of which the Holy One, blessed be He, swore, ‘I will redeem you,’ and the time has arrived for the oath you imposed upon Israel. If you reveal yourself, well and good; if not, we are released from y

Joseph’s coffin traveled with the Ark of the Testimony in the wilderness. The nations of the world asked, “What is the nature of these two arks?” Israel answered, “This is the coffin of the dead, and this is the Ark of the Life of the worlds.” They asked, “Is it usual for a dead person to travel with the Ark of the Life of the worlds?” They answered them, “The dead person lying in this coffin fulfilled all that is written in that Ark.”

We have learned: Why are there two yods? Joseph guarded the covenant below and guarded the covenant above. When he departed from the world, he was placed in two arks: an ark below and an ark above. What is the ark above? As it is written, “Behold, the Ark of the Covenant of the Master of all the earth.” The upper ark is called the Ark of the Covenant, for only one who guards the covenant inherits it. Because Joseph guarded the covenant, he was placed in two arks.
Joseph made the children of Israel swear, saying: God will surely attend to you, and you shall bring my bones up from here.

The Sages taught: There are three partners in a person: the Holy One, blessed be He, his father, and his mother. His father supplies the white substance, from which come the bones, sinews, nails, the brain in his head, and the white of the eye. His mother supplies the red substance, from which come skin, flesh, hair, and the black of the eye. The Holy One, blessed be He, gives him spirit, soul, facial appearance, sight, hearing, speech, walking, understanding, and intelligence.

Antoninus said to Rabbi: “From when does the evil inclination rule over a person—from the time of formation or from the time of emergence?” He answered, “From the time of formation.” He said, “If so, he would kick within his mother’s womb and emerge! Rather, it is from the time of emergence.” Rabbi said: Antoninus taught me this, and Scripture supports it, for it says, “Sin crouches at the opening.”

“Jacob sent angels.” Rabbi Yehudah opened: “For He will command His angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways.” The companions have explained this verse: when a person comes into the world, the evil inclination immediately joins him and continually accuses him, as it is written, “Sin crouches at the opening.” “Sin crouches”—this is the evil inclination. David also calls it “sin”: “My sin is always before me,” because every day it causes a person to sin before his Master. This evil inclination never departs from a person from the day he is born; the good inclination comes from the da

Was Benjamin righteous? Yes: throughout his life he did not sin against this sign of the covenant, although an event like Joseph’s did not befall him. If so, why is he called righteous? Throughout the time that Jacob mourned Joseph, Benjamin did not have marital relations. If you say that when Joseph was taken from Jacob he was a boy and not married, yet you say he refrained from marital relations: even though he subsequently married, he did not wish to have marital relations.
When the storm passes, the wicked one is no more; but the righteous one is the foundation of the world.

Ulla of Bira said in Rabbi Elazar’s name: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a circle for the righteous, and He will sit among them in the Garden of Eden. Each one will point with his finger, as it says, “On that day one shall say: Behold, this is our God, for whom we hoped, and He will save us; this is Hashem, for whom we hoped; let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation.”
Yah is my strength and song, and He has become my salvation. This is my God, and I shall glorify Him; my father’s God, and I shall exalt Him.

Therefore the Shechinah is bound to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph. They are as one and have one form, as it is written, “These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph.” Therefore, “from all the merchant’s powders”: from the place of the river that flows forth, everything is watered and all faces are illuminated.
Joseph died at the age of one hundred and ten years. They embalmed him, and he was placed in a coffin in Egypt.
Joseph remembered the dreams he had dreamed about them and said to them: You are spies; you have come to see the nakedness of the land.
She lusted after their paramours, whose flesh is like the flesh of donkeys and whose flow is like the flow of horses.
Six things are said of the horse: it loves sexual activity, loves war, is haughty in spirit, despises sleep, eats much, and excretes little. Some say: It also seeks to kill its master in war.

Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: Sarah went down to Egypt and fenced herself off from sexual immorality, and all the women were protected in her merit. Joseph went down to Egypt and fenced himself off from sexual immorality, and all the men were protected in his merit. Rabbi Pinchas said in the name of Rabbi Chiyya: Guarding against sexual immorality was itself sufficient for Israel to be redeemed from Egypt in its merit. What is the proof? “A locked garden is my sister, my bride.” What is written afterward? “Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates.”

Joseph’s coffin traveled with the Ark of the Testimony in the wilderness. The nations of the world asked, “What is the nature of these two arks?” Israel answered, “This is the coffin of the dead, and this is the Ark of the Life of the worlds.” They asked, “Is it usual for a dead person to travel with the Ark of the Life of the worlds?” They answered them, “The dead person lying in this coffin fulfilled all that is written in that Ark.”
Shimon of Kitron said: In the merit of Joseph’s bones the sea was split for Israel. Thus it is written, “The sea saw and fled”—in the merit of “He left his garment in her hand and fled.”
The sea saw and fled; the Jordan turned backward.
She seized him by his garment, saying: Lie with me. He left his garment in her hand, fled, and went outside.
This is the burnt offering of each Shabbat, in addition to the continual burnt offering and its libation.
When you acquire a Hebrew servant, he shall serve for six years, and in the seventh he shall go free without payment.

Concerning the well-known Shovavim: Israel has an ancient custom of fasting forty consecutive days, from the first day of the week of Shemot through Terumah and part of Tetzaveh. The mnemonic ‘Return, wayward children’ uses the initials of Shemot, Va’era, Bo, Beshalach, Yitro and Mishpatim. These forty days of fasting were instituted principally for the sin of seminal emission; this period is more suited to fasting for that sin than the rest of the year. The reason follows our explanation of Egypt’s exile through mortar and bricks. Those enslaved in Egypt were the sparks of souls that Adam emi
For the children of Israel are servants to Me; they are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am Hashem your God.

Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai expounded this verse in the manner of a parable: Why is the ear singled out from all the body’s limbs? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: “The ear that heard My voice at Mount Sinai when I said, ‘For the children of Israel are servants to Me’—and not servants to servants—and this person went and acquired a master for himself: let it be pierced.”

Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: Whoever recites Havdalah over wine at the conclusion of Shabbat has male children, for it is written, “To distinguish between the holy and the ordinary,” and elsewhere, “To distinguish between the impure and the pure,” adjacent to “When a woman conceives.” Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Children fit to issue rulings, for it is written, “To distinguish … and to instruct.”
To distinguish between the holy and the ordinary, and between the impure and the pure; and to teach the children of Israel all the statutes that Hashem spoke to them through Moses.
And wine gladdens the human heart, making the face shine more than oil; and bread sustains the human heart.
Of laughter I said, It is madness; and of joy, What does it accomplish?

The wicked Turnus Rufus also asked Rabbi Akiva this question. He said to him, “What distinguishes one day from other days?” He answered, “What distinguishes one man from other men?” He said, “My master desires it.” “Shabbat too—its Master desires it.”

Rabbi Yudan said: One recites the established blessing and then makes Havdalah. This accords with Rabbi, for Rabbi said: “I wonder how they omitted ‘Who graciously grants knowledge’ on Shabbat. If there is no knowledge, whence comes prayer?” Here too: if there is no knowledge, whence comes distinction? Rabbi Yitzchak bar Elazar said: One makes Havdalah and then recites the established blessing.
I have loved you, says Hashem. But you say: How have You loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother, declares Hashem? Yet I loved Jacob.
Now, if you truly listen to My voice and keep My covenant, you shall be My treasured possession from among all the peoples, for all the earth is Mine.
Of the children of Issachar, men who understood the times, to know what Israel should do: their chiefs were two hundred, and all their brothers were at their command.
To distinguish between the impure and the pure, and between the living creature that may be eaten and the living creature that may not be eaten.

“To distinguish”: not merely to repeat the laws, but to know, recognize, and be proficient in them. “Between the impure and the pure”: Must it tell you to distinguish between a donkey and a cow? They are already expressly identified! Rather, between what is impure for you and what is pure for you—between an animal whose trachea was half slaughtered and one whose trachea was mostly slaughtered.

“What my soul still sought and did not find: one man out of a thousand I found.” In the usual course of the world, a thousand people enter to study Scripture; a hundred of them go on to Mishnah; ten of them go on to Talmud; and one of them emerges qualified to issue rulings. This is what is written: “One man out of a thousand I found.”
He sent Yehudah ahead of him to Yosef, to give direction before him toward Goshen, and they came to the land of Goshen.
“He sent Judah ahead of him”—to establish a house of study, where he would issue rulings and teach the tribes.

If one vows, “Benefit from the uncircumcised is forbidden to me,” he may benefit from uncircumcised Israelites, but may not benefit from circumcised members of the nations. If he vows against benefit from the circumcised, he may not benefit from uncircumcised Israelites, but may benefit from circumcised members of the nations. For “uncircumcised” is applied to the nations, as it says, “All the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in heart.” It also says, “This uncircumcised Philistine,” and, “Lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice; lest the daughters

Rav Chana bar Bizna said in Rabbi Shimon Chasida’s name: Yosef, who sanctified Heaven’s name in private, had one letter of the Holy One’s name added to his name. Yehudah, who sanctified Heaven’s name publicly, was named entirely after the name of the Holy One, blessed be He.

Behold, I am sending My messenger, and he shall clear the way before Me. Suddenly the master whom you seek shall come to his Temple, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire—behold, he is coming, says Hashem of hosts.

Come and see: At first it is written, “What are you doing here, Elijah?” and, “I have been exceedingly zealous for Hashem, for the children of Israel have abandoned Your covenant.” He said to him: “By your life, wherever My children mark this holy sign in their flesh, you shall be present. The mouth that testified that Israel abandoned the covenant shall testify that Israel upholds it.” We have learned why Elijah was punished before the Holy One, blessed be He: because he accused His children.
Your people are all righteous; they will inherit the land forever—the shoot of My planting, the work of My hands, in which to be glorified.

Israel has already been assured that Elijah will come neither on the eve of Shabbat nor on the eve of a festival, because of the trouble involved. One might therefore think that, since Elijah does not come, Mashiach also does not come; let the person be permitted wine on Friday! Elijah does not come, but Mashiach may come, for once Mashiach comes, all are servants to Israel.
Strangers shall stand and pasture your flocks, and foreigners shall be your plowmen and vinedressers.

Rabbi Simon said: Light is mentioned here five times, corresponding to the five books of the Torah. ‘God said, Let there be light’ corresponds to Genesis, with which the Holy One, blessed be He, occupied Himself in creating His world. ‘And there was light’ corresponds to Exodus, in which Israel emerged from darkness into light. ‘God saw that the light was good’ corresponds to Leviticus, which is filled with many laws. ‘God separated the light from the darkness’ corresponds to Numbers, which distinguishes those who left Egypt from those who entered the Land. ‘God called the light day’ correspon
God said, Let there be light; and there was light.
Joseph died at the age of one hundred and ten years. They embalmed him, and he was placed in a coffin in Egypt.

Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: I too say that not all are destined for light, and not all for joy. The righteous are destined for light, and the upright for joy. The righteous for light, as it says, “Light is sown for the righteous”; the upright for joy, as it says, “And joy for the upright of heart.”
Light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright of heart.
When the storm passes, the wicked one is no more; but the righteous one is the foundation of the world.
Your people are all righteous; they will inherit the land forever—the shoot of My planting, the work of My hands, in which to be glorified.

The Holy One, blessed be He, sowed this light in the garden of His delights, arranging it in rows through the Righteous One, the garden’s gardener. He takes this light and sows it as a true seed, arranging it in rows in the garden. It produces, grows, and bears fruit, from which the world is nourished. Thus it is written, “Light is sown for the righteous.”
He sent a man before them: Joseph was sold as a slave.
Whoever disqualifies others is himself disqualified, and he never speaks in their praise. Shmuel said: He disqualifies others with his own blemish.

Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: Sarah went down to Egypt and fenced herself off from sexual immorality, and all the women were protected in her merit. Joseph went down to Egypt and fenced himself off from sexual immorality, and all the men were protected in his merit. Rabbi Pinchas said in the name of Rabbi Chiyya: Guarding against sexual immorality was itself sufficient for Israel to be redeemed from Egypt in its merit. What is the proof? “A locked garden is my sister, my bride.” What is written afterward? “Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates.”

Joseph’s coffin traveled with the Ark of the Testimony in the wilderness. The nations of the world asked, “What is the nature of these two arks?” Israel answered, “This is the coffin of the dead, and this is the Ark of the Life of the worlds.” They asked, “Is it usual for a dead person to travel with the Ark of the Life of the worlds?” They answered them, “The dead person lying in this coffin fulfilled all that is written in that Ark.”

“He blessed them.” It should have said, “Each according to his blessing, he blessed him.” Why does it say “he blessed them”? Since he gave Judah the strength of a lion, Benjamin the ravenousness of a wolf, and Naphtali the swiftness of a deer, you might think he did not include them all in all the blessings. Therefore it says, “He blessed them.”
All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is what their father spoke to them when he blessed them: each according to his blessing, he blessed them.

Concerning the well-known Shovavim: Israel has an ancient custom of fasting forty consecutive days, from the first day of the week of Shemot through Terumah and part of Tetzaveh. The mnemonic ‘Return, wayward children’ uses the initials of Shemot, Va’era, Bo, Beshalach, Yitro and Mishpatim. These forty days of fasting were instituted principally for the sin of seminal emission; this period is more suited to fasting for that sin than the rest of the year. The reason follows our explanation of Egypt’s exile through mortar and bricks. Those enslaved in Egypt were the sparks of souls that Adam emi
Er, Judah’s firstborn, was evil in Hashem’s eyes, and Hashem put him to death.
Hashem’s eyes are toward the righteous, and His ears are toward their cry.

Hashem’s face is against evildoers, to cut off their memory from the earth. They cried out and Hashem heard, and He rescued them from all their troubles. Hashem is close to the brokenhearted, and He saves those crushed in spirit.

The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: “Did I not write for you in My Torah, ‘This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth’?” Although you work during all six days, let Shabbat be entirely Torah. From here they said: A person should rise early and study on Shabbat, go to the synagogue and the house of study, read Torah and study the Prophets. Afterward he should go home, eat, and drink, fulfilling “Go, eat your bread with joy and drink your wine with a good heart.” For the Holy One, blessed be He, has rest only with those who practice Torah, as it says, “All these My hand has made

Thus says Hashem: Heaven is My throne, and the earth is My footstool. What house could you build for Me, and what place could be My resting place? My hand made all these things, and all these things came into being, declares Hashem. But to this one I shall look: to the poor and broken in spirit, who trembles at My word.
For they are life to those who find them, and healing to all his flesh.
This shall be his impurity through his discharge: whether his flesh runs with its discharge or his flesh is obstructed by its discharge, this is his impurity.
What has My beloved to do in My house, when she practices wickedness with many? Holy flesh shall pass away from you, for in your evil you rejoice.
She lusted after their paramours, whose flesh is like the flesh of donkeys and whose flow is like the flow of horses.
Yaakov drew near to his father Yitzchak, who felt him and said: The voice is the voice of Yaakov, but the hands are the hands of Esav.

Why? Because prayer is not the audible voice; that audible voice is not prayer. What is prayer? Another voice, dependent upon the audible voice. What is the audible voice? Kol spelled with vav; the voice dependent on it is kol without vav. Therefore a person should not make his voice heard in prayer, but should pray quietly, with the inaudible voice. This is the prayer that is always accepted. Your sign is “The voice was heard”: kol without vav is heard. This is silent prayer, as it is written of Hannah, “Her voice was not heard.” This is the prayer that the Holy One, blessed be He, accepts, w

Rabbi Yochanan said to him: Torah and acts of kindness are understandable, for it is written, “Through kindness and truth iniquity is atoned.” “Kindness” is acts of kindness, as it says, “One who pursues righteousness and kindness will find life, righteousness, and honor.” “Truth” is Torah, as it says, “Acquire truth and do not sell it.” But from where is the burial of one’s children derived?

“Ask for yourself a sign”—literally a letter, for they all moved within the mystery of the letters. Similarly, what is written concerning Rahab? “Give me a sign of truth”—this is the letter vav, which is called the sign of truth. If you say, “Are the other letters not truth?”—yes, but this letter is called the sign of truth.

All agree that the Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat. Here it is written, “Remember the day of Shabbat to sanctify it,” and there it is written, “Moses said to the people: Remember this day.” Just as there it means that very day, so here it means that very day.
On the seventh day God completed His work that He had done, and on the seventh day He ceased from all His work that He had done.

“God completed on the seventh day”—this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day. Through it the world was completed, for it sustains everything. “His work which He had made,” and not “all His work,” for the Written Torah brings everything forth through the power of writing, which issues from wisdom.
Rabbi Yitzchak said: Sunshine on Shabbat is charity for the poor, as it says, “For you who fear My name, the sun of righteousness shall shine, with healing.”
For you who fear My name, a sun of righteousness shall shine, with healing in its wings. You shall go out and leap like calves from the stall.
“Those who fear My name”—those who keep Shabbat.

Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Ilai expounded: What does “Hear the word of Hashem, you who tremble at His word” mean? These are Torah scholars. “Your brothers”—these are masters of Scripture; “those who hate you”—these are masters of Mishnah; “those who exclude you”—these are the unlearned.

Hear Hashem’s word, you who tremble at His word: Your brothers who hate you and cast you out have said, For My name’s sake, let Hashem be glorified, and let us see your joy. But they shall be put to shame.

Five things are one-sixtieth: fire, honey, Shabbat, sleep, and a dream. Fire is one-sixtieth of Gehinnom; honey is one-sixtieth of manna; Shabbat is one-sixtieth of the World to Come; sleep is one-sixtieth of death; and a dream is one-sixtieth of prophecy.
